items.statement: Capital allocation policy changed to distribute at least 85% of free cash flow over five years via dividends or buyback
items.quote: In the go forward policy, we have an endeavour to distribute at least 85% of our free cash flow generated over a period of five years to shareholders in the form of dividends or buyback.

items.statement: No transformational M&A planned; focus on organic growth and integrating existing portfolio companies
items.quote: In a sense, yes. In a sense, the focus will very much be on organic growth. Never say no to really compelling opportunities. But we are not in the market for a transformational M&A at this time.

items.statement: No active divestiture plan for acquired portfolio companies; focusing on front-end and back-end integration
items.quote: We have obviously worked to closely integrate all of the portfolio companies much more closely into our service line structure. And because we have said that we are not going to be hugely acquisitive anymore, it gives us the ability to drive synergies, including front-end integration and including back-end integration, a lot more effectively over time. But there is no active disposition plan at th

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth 25-30%, EBITDA margin 17-18%, net debt INR225-250 cr, capex INR250-300 cr, DI pipe production >4 lakh tons
items.quote: For FY '25, we anticipate revenue growth in the region of 25% to 30%, EBITDA margins of around 17% to 18% and the net debt to be reduced to a range of around INR225 to INR250 crores. The capital expenditure is also expected to be in the range of INR300 to INR250 crores and we expect the ductile iron pipe production to exceed INR4 lakh tons.

items.statement: DI pipe margin 22-25%, specialised ferroalloy margin ~20%, group EBITDA margin 18-20% post expansion
items.quote: In terms of margin you asked, in percentages, in ductile pipes we have a margin of around 20% to 25% and in Ferroalloys, specialized Ferroalloys, we have a margin of around 25%.

items.statement: INR1,000 cr capex plan; INR497 cr incurred, balance INR503 cr over next 15 months via internal accruals
items.quote: you all on Page 2 o f 19 the capacity expansion and the capex plan of the company, we had earlier announced a capex plan of around INR1,000 crores and out of this, around INR497 crores has already been incurred and the balance INR503 crores is expected to be incurred in the next 15 months. All this capex is being done through internal accruals only

items.statement: FY25 capex INR250-300 cr; CWIP capitalisation over three quarters
items.quote: Around INR300 crores of capex will be done in the current financial year.

items.statement: DI pipe order book 10-12 months of current capacity; ~35% government orders
items.quote: See, the order book currently for ductile iron pipes, it is in the region of around 10-12 months of the current capacity. And out of this, around 35% would be government orders.

items.statement: Q4 DI pipe margin 20-25%, specialised ferroalloy margin ~25%; Q3 DI pipe margin 20-21%
items.quote: Q3 the margins cost saving in the region of around 20% 21%.

items.statement: Steady-state group EBITDA margin guidance 18-20% for next 4-5 years; margins insulated from steel price falls
items.quote: We've been repeating this continuously, is that we're looking at expanding our margins to 18% to 20% by the time the entire capex plan is completed over the next 15 to 18 months. So this is the guidance for the future.

items.statement: DI pipe industry CAGR 13-15%; Jal Jeevan Mission & AMRUT driving demand; target market share 18-20% from 9-10%
items.quote: We expect that the DI pipe industry to go at 13% to 15% CAGR in the near future. The Jal Jeevan Mission and Mission Amrut Sarovar Infrastructure Development Plan which has been promoted by the government has led to an increased demand of these pipes and Jai Balaji is also contributing to the same.

items.statement: Value-added products share rose from 25% to 50% in FY24; target 80-90% by FY25-26; DI pipes 45-50%, ferroalloys ~35% of volumes
items.quote: With a focus on increasing the contribution of value-added products for margin expansion, we expect DI to contribute 45% to 50% and Ferroalloys to contribute around 35% of our total volumes by FY '25 '26.

items.statement: No further capex plans until current INR1,000 cr programme completed and benefits realised
items.quote: See what is happening is that currently the management is very focused to complete this particular capex plan. So, as of now, we would not like to give any guidance of further capex till the time this particular project are completed and the company is able to reap the fruits and the benefits of this particular capex.

items.statement: Net debt fell 54% to INR398 cr in FY24; net debt/EBITDA 0.4x vs guidance 0.6x; target net debt free in 15 months
items.quote: In FY '24, the net debt decreased to INR398 crores from INR871 crores, marking a reduction of 54%. It's worth noting that our current net debt to EBITDA ratio stands only at 0.4 as of March 31, 2024, thus performing better than our guidance of maintaining 0.6 net debt EBITDA.

items.statement: DI pipe capacity: 3.0 lakh tons (FY24) -> 4.4 lakh (FY25 Phase 1) -> 6.6 lakh (FY26 Phase 2); ferroalloy 1.3 -> 1.66 lakh tons (FY25); blast furnace 5.0 -> 6.3 lakh tons (FY24) -> full by FY25; sinter 6 -> 9 -> 12 lakh tons (FY25)
items.quote: Capacity of DI pipes has been expanded 3 lakh tons compared to 2.4 lakh tons last year. Furthermore, 1.4 lakh metric tons that is the balance of Phase 1 and 2.2 lakh metric tons that is Phase 2 is expected to be commissioned in FY '25 and FY '26 respectively. The capacity of ductile pipes will finally reach 6.6 lakh tons in the immediate future.

items.statement: FY24 revenue INR6,414 cr (+5% YoY), EBITDA INR375 cr (+71%), PAT INR880 cr (+1,422%); Q4 revenue INR1,846 cr (+7%), adj EBITDA INR257 cr (-3%), PAT INR273 cr
items.quote: Revenue for this year increased by 5% year over year to INR6414 crores and INR375 crores up 71% year over year. EBITDA margin also increased to 15% compared to 9% last year. PAT also showed a very significant increase of 1422% to INR880 crores compared to only INR58 crores earned last year.

items.statement: Cost saving initiatives target INR3,000-4,000 per ton on hot metal via blast furnace efficiency, sinter, green power (BFG boiler INR30 cr, 50% done)
items.quote: In incremental what we are talking about is that on the metals produced entirely, we are looking at a cost saving of approximately INR3000 to INR4000 per ton on the hot material.

items.statement: Ferroalloy FY24 production: special grade 34,350 t, normal grade 81,000 t; FY25 capacity +30,000 t, utilisation ~76%; special grade share rising Q-o-Q
items.quote: In Ferroalloys, we'll be increasing capacity by around 30,000 this year. So, roughly the same level of capacity utilization. Last year, we achieved around 76%. We'll achieve the same level.

items.statement: DI pipe FY25 production target ~4 lakh tons, FY26 ~6 lakh tons; ferroalloy FY25 ~1.5 lakh tons, FY26 ~1.8-1.9 lakh tons
items.quote: For ductile alloys, we are looking to produce around 4 lakh tons in the forthcoming year there is FY '25. And in FY '26, we are looking to produce around 6 lakh tons. And as far as Ferroalloys are concerned, we are looking to produce around 1.5 lakh tons in the forthcoming year.

items.statement: Industry DI pipe capacity ~35 lakh tons, expected ~45 lakh tons in 2 years; bid pipeline 50-60% above demand; export focus after 18-24 months
items.quote: The current capacity, operating capacity, it is around 35 lakh tons approximately. So, different manufacturers are adding different capacities in different timelines. So, we are expecting over the next 2 years, this capacity to grow to approximately around 4.5 lakh tons t o . Sorry, to around 45 lakh tons.

items.statement: FY25 USD constant currency revenue growth guidance of 8-10%
items.quote: Factoring the current economic scenario, our guidance for FY25 is for a USD constant currency revenue growth of 8-10%.

items.statement: Aspiration to reach $1.5 Bn revenue run rate by FY25 exit
items.quote: Our aspirations to touch the $1.5 Bn run rate in FY25 remains.

items.statement: FY25 EBIT margin expected at 16% levels due to reorganization investments and macro factors
items.quote: This will lead to softness in EBIT margin for FY25 ranging at 16% levels while our endeavour will be to achieve higher levels in the medium term.

items.statement: Margin trajectory: Q1-Q2 lower, Q3-Q4 higher, averaging 16% for FY25
items.quote: So, when I look at 16% levels take that to be an average across the year, with Q1, Q2 to be lower and Q3, Q4 to be higher.

items.statement: Investments in people and technology front-ended in FY25 for new segment structure
items.quote: The reorganization will entail investments in people and new technologies, which will be front-ended beginning start of FY25.

items.statement: Reorganization into three segments: Mobility, Sustainability, Hi-Tech with three horizontals
items.quote: Under this 'Go Deeper to Scale' strategy we will have 3 segments – Mobility, Sustainability and Hi-Tech.

items.statement: Transportation expects strong rebound in Q1 and strong growth prospects in FY25
items.quote: Overall, while we had a soft Q4 as some of our deal decisions were delayed, we see a strong rebound in Q1. Transportation gre w 12% in FY24 and we continue to see strong growth prospects strong in this business in FY25.

items.statement: Plant Engineering optimistic of strong growth in Q1 and FY25 driven by capex and modernization
items.quote: New capex and plant modernization will continue to drive demand and we are optimistic of strong growth in Plant Engineering in Q1 and for FY25.

items.statement: Industrial Products expects growth pickup in second half of FY25
items.quote: We expect growth to pick up second half of FY25.

items.statement: Telecom & Hitech optimistic about FY25 with semiconductor and ISV rebound, though Q1 may see weakness
items.quote: Overall, we remain optimistic about FY25, given the rebound in Semiconductor and ISV, although we may see some weakness in Q1.

items.statement: Medical expects momentum pickup from Q2 onwards and better FY25
items.quote: We do expect the momentum to pick up from Q2 onwards and a better FY25.

items.statement: Q4 large deal wins: one $100M, one $30M, two $20M, two $10M deals plus O&G empanelment
items.quote: Large deal wins have been strong with one USD 100 million, one USD 30 million, two USD 20 million and two USD 10 million deals, in the quarter. Additionally, we won one significant empanelment in the O&G sector.

items.statement: FY24 closed 25 deals >$10M TCV including one $100M, three $30-50M, nine $15-20M plus three empanelments
items.quote: In FY24, we closed a total of 25 deals greater than $10M in TCV, which includes 1 $100M deal, 3 in the $30M - 50M range and 9 in the $15M - 20M range. In addition, we had 3 significant empanelment agreements.

items.statement: Cybersecurity deal is software-led with home-grown solutions, not traditional SI, enabling global scaling
items.quote: I can confidently tell you that cybersecurity will be $100M business with us in the next few years annually.

items.statement: Decision-making delays and geopolitical risks factored into FY25 guidance
items.quote: In the immediate near term, we are dealing with decision making delays and rising geopolitical risks.

items.statement: M&A actively pursued in ISV, MedTech, Europe Auto but no pressured acquisitions
items.quote: We are actively looking for targets in ISV, Med tech and Europe Auto.

items.statement: Expect to grow balance sheet around 25% annually over next 3 years
items.quote: We will continue to grow our balance sheet by maybe around 25% annually over the next 3 years.

items.statement: Target high ROA assets to reach 70-75% of portfolio by FY27
items.quote: We are confident to grow these segments to approximately 70% to 75% of our portfolio, up from current 70% by '27.

items.statement: Aim to defend 1.6% ROA in FY25 including merger integration costs
items.quote: So, we want to defend 1.6% ROA next year too.

items.statement: Steady state credit cost expected at 1-1.1% on advances and 0.75% on total assets
items.quote: So, I think anything about 1% to 1.1% on overall advances and anything around about 70 to 75 basis points on total assets is where we should work with.

items.statement: Incremental MFI credit cost of 1-1.5% to be provided in FY25 on Rs 8,000 cr portfolio
items.quote: Correct. Absolutely right.

items.statement: Endeavor to protect margins on merged basis for FY25 despite 40-45 bps cost of funds increase
items.quote: On a merge basis, our endeavor would be to protect the margins on the overall level for next financial year, at least.

items.statement: Disbursement yields increased 8 bps in Q4; Wheels up 27 bps, MBL up 20 bps QoQ
items.quote: The overall disbursement yield for the entire business for the full quarter went up by 8 basis points.

items.statement: Target 75% of disbursements from high ROA assets (Wheels, MBL, MFI, gold, NBFC funding)
items.quote: Our own estimation says that our 75% of disbursement this year would be from high-yield assets.

items.statement: Moderate credit card issuance to FY24 levels (~6 lakh cards) to control acquisition costs
items.quote: We'll not be issuing more than 6 lakh credit cards this year, too.

items.statement: AD1 license capex ~Rs 20 cr incurred; no major further capex expected
items.quote: So, we incurred around Rs. 20 crores.

items.statement: Merger integration BAU expenses of Rs 50-60 cr over next 1-2 years
items.quote: Overall, Rs. 50 crores, Rs. 60 crores in maybe 1 to 2 years.

items.statement: Combined customer base nearly 1.1 crore; 2,383 touchpoints across 21 states and 4 UTs
items.quote: With a combined customer base of nearly 1.1 crores and an employee strength of over 46,000 dedicated employees, the merger positions us a formidable financial entit y. Our physical presence expands to 2,383 touchpoints across 21 states and 4 union territories, giving us a pan -India

items.statement: No material impact on FY25 from general elections; Q1 may see some business continuity break
items.quote: There could be some break in business continuity during quarter 1 due to multiphase election s, but we don’t see the impact to be material in our annual FY ‘25

items.statement: AML and cybercrime/identity theft are major risks; robust systems implemented
items.quote: The major risk nowadays is coming from the AML side and has attained prominence with increased cybercrime and identity theft. We remain vigilant and have implemented robust systems and processes to effectively mitigate this risk associated including our AD1 business.

items.statement: Merged entity Tier-1 capital ~19-20%; total capital ~Rs 14,981 cr
items.quote: So, it will be around 20% to 21% (Corrected 19%-20%).

items.statement: Target current account share of deposits at least 7.5% by FY27 from ~5% currently
items.quote: We aim to achieve a healthy current account book targeting at least 7.5% of deposits from approximately 5% currently.

items.statement: Aiming to hit 35-40% growth trajectory within next two years
items.quote: as a company, we are aiming to hit between 35-40% growth. At least, we want to set the trajectory for that within the next two years.

items.statement: FY25 growth will be higher than FY24
items.quote: our goal next year is to show definitely more growth than what we have seen this year

items.statement: Targeting customer acquisition run rate of 1.5-2 lakh per month
items.quote: I want to get that to about 1.5 lakhs, 2 lakhs.

items.statement: Expect to operate within same EBITDA margin range including investment costs
items.quote: we can assume that we will always operate within that same EBITDA margin, of course, but this time, including those costs, that is it.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin range expected to continue in coming quarters
items.quote: considering the investment and this other one-off cost, the current margin that we have seen in Q4, that is the range we might be looking at in coming quarter.

items.statement: Regulatory scrutiny increasing costs like 2x infrastructure redundancy
items.quote: our infrastructure cost went up this quarter, because we had to build 2x redundancy. Now, this is a new change that came from the exchange.

items.statement: Expect some extra hit to profitability from regulatory penalties and compliance costs
items.quote: I expect that there will be some extra hit to profitability, but it's not very material.

items.statement: Focus on building products for high-end traders via API and digital platforms
items.quote: we are investing heavily, heavily in our digital acquisition businesses and also digital fulfilling businesses, which means the API business, the programming business and so on.

items.statement: Cash and derivative market share currently 2-3%
items.quote: currently our cash and derivative market share stands between 2% and 3%.

items.statement: Reinvesting profits to scale growth and build new products
items.quote: We are going to be reinvesting our profits to support growth.

items.statement: Customer acquisition cost recovered within first year
items.quote: We are able to recover the customer acquisition cost in the first year itself, and thereby we can attain better revenue multiples in the future.

items.statement: Lifetime value of customers 5-7x of acquisition cost, in line with top peers
items.quote: look at the cohort system, if you look at the lifetime value for the three brokers who are ahead of us, the India's largest three, and you compare their LTV to my LTV, it is exactly the same. In fact, for some cohorts, my LTV goes up to 7x

items.statement: Equity and hybrid fund yield improved by 5 bps sequentially to ~76 bps, driven by commission overestimation reversal and B30 trail commission cessation.
items.quote: We are continuing with the same rate. So, almost 76 bps will be there for equity and hybrid funds. So, we start the year with the same rate.

items.statement: Cash and arbitrage fund yields improved from 9 to 11 bps; fixed income yields improved from 21 to 22 bps.
items.quote: So, cash and arbitrage, yields have improved from 9 to 11 bps, and on the fixed income from 21 to 22 bps.

items.statement: Standalone blended yield benchmark for Q1 FY25 is 34 bps after normalizing for commission estimation adjustments.
items.quote: Yes, the 34 bps is the right benchmark, and this yield estimation and comparison is being done on a quarterly basis itself.

items.statement: International business yield expected to improve due to new higher-margin product launches (India Innovation Fund, Private Credit Real Estate Fund).
items.quote: Both of these funds have a slightly better margin, so we do believe that overall revenue as well as the margin number should improve for UTI International as well going forward.

items.statement: Employee cost increased ~10% QoQ and YoY due to one-time gratuity expense of ₹5.5 crore, insurance cost increase of ₹2.5 crore, and UTI International expansion (~₹3 crore QoQ).
items.quote: there has been an increase in the employee cost by close to ~10%, both on a sequential as well as on a year-on-year basis. It is primarily because of two factors. One is the one-time expense on account of gratuity. B ecause of actuarial valuation, it increased was by around ₹ 5.5 crore. Also, the insurance cost also has marginally gone up by ₹ 2.5 crore during this quarter

items.statement: Standalone employee cost growth guided at 2-3% for FY25; consolidated growth 100-150 bps higher due to investments in International, Alternatives, and RSL.
items.quote: Very similar to whatever the growth rate has been there for the current year, maybe on a standalone basis, the increase could be around 2 %-3%. On a consolidated basis, the increase could be slightly higher because we are investing in all three lines of business.

items.statement: Tax rate guided at 22-23% for FY25.
items.quote: I think it should be in the range of 22%-23%.

items.statement: Plan to launch Multi Cap Fund, and innovate in passively managed and thematic funds during FY25.
items.quote: We are planning to launch a Multi Cap Fund during the year, and we are also looking to further innovate in the passively managed space as well as thematic funds.

items.statement: SIP AUM grew 42.95% YoY to ₹30,747 crore; SIP inflows for FY24 were ₹6,767 crore, up 5% YoY.
items.quote: Our SIP AUM witnessed growth of 42.95% over the corresponding quarter of the last year, reaching to ₹ 30,747 crore as of March 2024.

items.statement: Equity and hybrid gross sales in Q4 FY24 were ₹2,981 crore; redemptions from banks and national distributors offset by inflows in other products.
items.quote: So, gross sales for Q4 FY24 were ₹ 2,981 crore in equity and hybrid category.

items.statement: UTI RSL AUM grew 25.74% YoY to ₹3.03 lakh crore, managing 25.8% of NPS industry AUM.
items.quote: Our 100% owned subsidiary, UTI Retirement Solutions Ltd., has recorded a growth of 25.74% YoY in its AUM, reaching ₹ 3.03 lakh crore in Q4 FY24, and currently manages 25.8% of the NPS industry AUM.

items.statement: UTI International AUM grew 27.4% YoY to ₹27,645 crore; IDEF AUM at USD 951.77 million.
items.quote: UTI International, which represents our international business interest, has an AUM of ₹ 27,645 crore as of March 31st, 2024, up by 27.4% YoY.

items.statement: UTI International obtained French regulator license for Paris office operations in Europe; UTI RSL obtained PFRDA POP license and SEBI NOC; UTI Alternatives received SEBI approval for GIFT City operations; UTI AMC and UTI Investment America
items.quote: UTI International obtained license from the French regulators for business operations in the European region through our Paris office. This will give us an on-ground presence in Continental Europe and create significant business opportunities in this market.

items.statement: Dividend policy maintained at minimum 50% payout; FY24 payout at 66-67% plus additional dividend distributing 100% of profit.
items.quote: As far as dividend is concerned, w e have a policy that we always pay a minimum 50% dividend to our investors. Last year, we paid around 66%. This year, 66% or 67% we have maintained for the current financial year, and we have given an additional dividend and 100% of our profit we have distributed to our investors

items.statement: Liquid fund outflows due to bank quarter-end exits; flows return in first 1-2 days of next quarter.
items.quote: For liquid funds, most of the banks go for the exit and therefore there was an outflow. It comes back on the first or second day of the next financial year. So, it is a quarter on quarter problem, and which all AMCs face.

items.statement: ESOP cost FY24: ₹13.14 crore standalone, ₹16.8 crore consolidated; FY25 estimated at ₹4.5 crore standalone, ₹5 crore consolidated if no new grants.
items.quote: For the next year, as of now, if you don't issue any further ESOP, the next-year cost will be ₹ 4.5 crore on the AMC and roughly around ₹ 5 crore at the consolidated level.

items.statement: Expect gross loan book growth of around 30% for FY25
items.quote: We expect gross loan book growth of around 30%, deposit growth to be higher by at least 3% to 5% vs. loan book growth and with the target to reduce CD ratio further in FY25.

items.statement: Target credit cost at around 2% for FY25 including additional floating provision
items.quote: Focus on maintaining strong asset quality with nil net NPAs and credit costs at around 2%. Credit cost guidance includes an additional floating provision which the Bank will build in

items.statement: Target ROA of more than 2% and ROE of more than 18% for FY25
items.quote: On profitability – return on assets of more than 2% and return on equity of more than 18% and cost income ratio in the range of 54% to 57%.

items.statement: NIM to remain above 9% in medium term (2-3 years)
items.quote: I think margins NIM will always be above 9%. That is what we have given guidance earlier also and that remains today also.

items.statement: Expect write-off collections of Rs. 65-80 crores for FY25
items.quote: So, overall, maybe in the range of say Rs. 65 to Rs. 80 crores is what we expect overall write off collections will happen . Again, as I mentioned is indicative or guidance from our side.

items.statement: Cost of funds may increase by 10-15 basis points in FY25 if market rates stay same
items.quote: So, our perspective maybe it can go up at the most maybe 10 to 15 basis point s, not more than that and during this financial year if the market remains the same level where it is today, it might go up around 10 to 15 basis points, not beyond that.

items.statement: Plan to open around 150 branches in FY25 (60 general banking, 90+ micro-banking)
items.quote: So, this year we have a plan for opening around 150 odd branches. I mean, the number could be plus minus based on getting property, getting property in time and those type of things. But around 150 odd branches we expect this year . Out of that general banking branches around 60 odd will be general banking branches and the next 90 plus will be our micro-banking branches across the country.

items.statement: Board guided to make 2% floating provision on JLG book in FY25
items.quote: This year the board has directed us or guided us to make 2% floating provisions on our JLG book and the way we had told in past also we intend to create a sizable floating provision, so that any issue we are able to withstand.

items.statement: Technology and business transformation project underway to strengthen technology architecture
items.quote: We are also undertaking technology and business transformation project to strengthen our technology architecture to make it future growth ready.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 NIM at 9.86%, full year FY24 NIM at 9.44%
items.quote: We ended NIM of 9.86% for Q4 and for the full financial year our NIM was 9.44%.

items.statement: Expect FY25 NIM around 9.35-9.4% as 9.9% not sustainable
items.quote: Obviously 9.9 will not be sustainable, but if you look at next year, maybe 9.4 or 9.35 type of margins are certainly there and in medium term, it will always be (+9%).

items.statement: Implementing differential rate of interest for JLG customers based on asset quality and vintage from current quarter
items.quote: From the current quarter , w e are planning to introduce a differential rate of interest for our JLG customers basis asset quality, vintage curve etc., which will help us implement risk-based pricing in micro-banking lending more effectively.

items.statement: Differential pricing to offer 1-2% lower than card rate for better quality vintage customers
items.quote: So, what we are planning, I mean we are still assessing, but our sense is that we would be doing let us say 1% to 2% lower than our card rate for select better quality customers, better vintage customers and so on.

items.statement: Healthy new customer acquisition in micro-banking; subsequent cycle disbursements good
items.quote: In micro-banking lending, we continue to witness healthy new customer acquisition. Subsequent cycle disbursements have also been good.

items.statement: Micro-banking share to decline 3-5% to 57-59% in FY25; MSME, housing, wheels to grow; wholesale at 10-11%
items.quote: This is our expectation for financial year 25 as well , so maybe share of micro -banking will come down by 3 % to 5% anywhere between 57% to 59% for financial year 25 and businesses, I mean in terms of let us say MSME, Govind sir had talked about Micro LAP, housing and wheels are the businesses which will increase in terms of size. Wholesale lending, which is at about 10% now would remain at about

items.statement: No specific geographic stress; few districts in Jharkhand, UP, Haryana have minor issues
items.quote: We don't have any specific area, but we have few districts and few states like there are two three districts in Jharkhand, there are 4 -5 districts in UP , again 2-3 districts in Haryana. Otherwise , we don't have any specific geography where we are facing any such problem which can affect our credit cost.

items.statement: Management guides sustainable credit cost of 80 basis points
items.quote: The impairment cost, we believe, on a sustainable basis will be something like 80 basis points. So, that's what we are comfortable guiding ahead.

items.statement: Management guides AUM growth of 25% plus for FY25
items.quote: We believe that from where we are, we should be able to comfortably grow at a rate of 25% plus. And we will take advantage of any tailwinds that the environment affords us from time to time.

items.statement: Small mortgage share of on-book AUM rose from 24% to 29% and will continue to dominate
items.quote: As a percentage of on-books, the small mortgage business is up from 24% to 29% in the current year, and that trajectory should continue in the foreseeable future.

items.statement: NIMs expected to stay constant in FY25 with potential upside from gold co-lending and short-term rate easing
items.quote: We believe that our spread will stay constant. The only thing that will increase the spread is that if we do more co-lending for gold, which is what we are in a quest for, our spreads might increase from here on.

items.statement: Plan to open 50 gold loan branches and 30 small mortgage locations in FY25
items.quote: In the coming years we want to open about 50 gold loan branches and 30 small mortgage locations. So, that is the plan for the year, and we will execute it, try and front-end that during the course of the year.

items.statement: Cost-to-AUM guided to improve by 30-40 bps in FY25 from 5.2% in FY24
items.quote: For the year gone by, we had a cost-to-AUM of 5.2%. We believe that in the coming year it should be better by between 30 basis points and 40 basis points.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded to AA+ by CARE and India Ratings; CRISIL assigned AA with positive outlook
items.quote: We have received a rating upgrade. We are rated AA+ by CARE and India Ratings, and CRISIL has assigned us a long-term credit rating of AA with a positive outlook.

items.statement: Gold loan regulatory compliance robust; all recent regulator concerns addressed pre-COVID
items.quote: All of what the regulator has said and which has been in the public domain in the months of Feb and March is really quite old hat for us, okay? And we are reasonably robust from that standpoint.

items.statement: Blended cost of funds increased 10-12 bps in Q4 due to RBI risk weight hike; incremental borrowing costs lower post rating upgrade
items.quote: In quarter three RBI had increased risk weights on bank lending to NBFCs. As a result of that, there has been a small increase in our cost of about 10 bps, 12 bps in terms of the blended cost of funds. But that being said, post our credit rating upgrade, we have been able to tie up incremental commitments at rates reasonably lower than the blended cost of funds.

items.statement: Applied for corporate agency license to cross-sell insurance; expect approval in May-June
items.quote: Yes, we have applied for a corporate agency, we will get our license hopefully in the month of May or June. And at that point in time, we will use our distribution network of gold and non-gold branches to also sell insurance.

items.statement: Gold loan co-lending AUM grew from Rs 176 cr to Rs 522 cr in Q4 FY24
items.quote: This quarter's off-book was largely gold loan co-lending, and that went up from Rs. 176 crores at the end of Q3 to Rs. 522 crores at the end of Q4, so that's about Rs. 350-ish crores that we have added to our co-lending book in the quarter.

items.statement: CPCL expects to maintain operational performance and harness market opportunities for shareholders
items.quote: CPCL is very focused and very committed to operational performance. We will continue to do this so that whenever the market gives that opportunity, the opportunity will be hamessed for the benefit of sharcholders.

items.statement: FY25 capex budget is INR600-650 crores, mostly for maintenance and profitable projects, not CBRPL
items.quote: I think the budget is around INR600 to INR650 crores.

items.statement: CBRPL project revised cost INR36,354 crores, CPCL equity share INR3,000 crores (25%), INR1,000 crores spent, balance INR2,000 crores over 2-3 years
items.quote: So the revised project cost is INR36,354 crores. CPCL share is 25%. Debt is 2:1. So, total equity will be INR12,000 Crore, 25% of that is INR3.000 crores. That is CPCL's contribution.

items.statement: CBRPL timeline 39 months from CCEA approval (36 months mechanical completion + 3 months commissioning), reduced from earlier 45 months
items.quote: Thus, the project takes 39 months from CCEA approval which is 36 months for mechanical completion and 3 months for commissioning.

items.statement: Evaluating profitable projects: LOBS grade 2/3, de-bottlenecking, propylene capacity addition, niche products, sustainability capex; individual projects INR200-700 crores, one INR1,700 crores
items.quote: So, first on kind of capex, so, one of the project is LOBS, grade 2, grade 3 LOBS project, which will help us move in the value chain from petroleum liquid fuels to lube-based, products. So, that is one that we are looking into. Others are like de-bottlenecking, some addition in propylene capacity and again, some niche products, those are the items on radar.

items.statement: RLNG long-term contract revised from 1.08 to 1.3 MMSCD, actual usage over 2.0 MMSCD when economics permit
items.quote: Actually we had a long term contract of 1.08. The unit was MMSCD which now we have revised upwards to 1.3. But Imust tell you, even though my new long-term arrangement is 1.3, I have been using more than 2.0 MMSCD.

items.statement: FY24 GRM $8.64/bbl vs Singapore $6.61/bbl; Q4 FY24 GRM $7.71/bbl vs Singapore $7.32/bbl; consistently beating benchmark
items.quote: The gross refining margin, GRM, for FY full year, 2023-2024, was $8.64 per barrel. If you benchmark it against Singapore GRM, which was $6.61 per barrel.

items.statement: Windfall tax impact ~INR900 crores (~$1.5/bbl) in FY24, applied product-wise and fortnightly, not on entire volume uniformly
items.quote: IfT theoretically calculate the impact of windfall tax, it will be around INR90O crores this year, and INR900 crores which will translate to about $1.5 per barrel.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 inventory loss $0.59/bbl (INR112 crores); Q3 FY24 inventory gain $0.35/bbl (INR80-90 crores); FY24 net inventory gain $0.43/bbl (INR300 crores)
items.quote: Q4 current year, that is '23 24, was a loss of $ 0.59/bbl, and that translates to INR112 crores.

items.statement: Arab Mix premium Q4 FY24 $1.81/bbl vs $3.50/bbl in Q3 FY24 vs $5.18/bbl in Q4 FY23; full year FY24 $2.50/bbl vs $5.18/bbl FY23; Basra Medium FY24 $0.50/bbl vs $2.80/bbl FY23
items.quote: The Arab mix last quarter Q423-24 the premium was 1.81 $/bbl as compared to 1.53 $/bbl of the corresponding quarter of previous year. But if you compare with Q3 it has come down. Q3 Arab mix premium was 3.5 $/bbL. Q4 was 1.818/bbl.

items.statement: Crude throughput 11.64 MMT (111% capacity utilization) in FY24, highest ever; 8 of 12 months crossed 1 MMT; expect similar 11-12 MMT volumes for next 2-3 years until CBRPL commissioning
items.quote: CPCL achieved highest ever crude throughput of 11.64 million metric tons (which is 111% of installed capacity i.c 10.5 million ) as against previous best of 11.32 MMT, that is 2022-2023.

items.statement: FY24 distillate yield 76.2% (up from 76% FY23); fuel & loss 8.81% (can maintain/improve without M&I shutdowns); no significant product slate change expected FY25
items.quote: 23-24 full year distillate yield is 76.2, and that is over 76 in the previous year.

items.statement: Forex loss FY24 ~INR70 crores vs INR500+ crores FY23; natural hedge via RTP formula; future forex volatility unpredictable
items.quote: Last year this was significant, little over INR500 crores loss on our P&L. This time it is around INR70-odd crores as the rupee remained stable.

items.statement: Russian crude ~30% of basket; discount narrowed last 3-4 months; will maximize profits by switching to opportunity crudes if economics favor
items.quote: Again, broadly we have maintained it around 30%, because there are term crudes, there are other opportunity crudes, so we have to make a balance between all this.

items.statement: Debt reduced to INR2,700 crores (0.32x debt/equity) from INR4,200 crores (0.67x); no immediate debt requirement; will maintain manageable levels while funding profitable projects
items.quote: As on March 31, 2024, it is 0.32 times as compared to 0.67 times previous year end. Borrowing stands at INR2,762 crores as against INR4,235 crores in the previous year end.

items.statement: Board recommended highest ever dividend INR55/share (550%) for FY24 vs net profit INR2,711 crores; sustainable per DIPAM guidelines balancing retention and distribution
items.quote: Our Board recommended highest ever dividend of INRSS per equity share, i.e., 550%, on a face value of INR10 for the current year, i.e., 2023- 2024, certainly which is subject to approval of shareholders in the AGM, and this is against a net profit of INR2,711 crores posted in the current year.

items.statement: Order book looks promising; plan to maintain average exports through the year
items.quote: So, the order book looks promising at this point of time. We plan to maintain the average through the year.

items.statement: Capex commitment of INR 1,500 crores over three years; third year ongoing, full year may exceed INR 500 crores but no annual guidance given
items.quote: As we had committed that in three years, we will do INR 1,500 crores and this is the third year, and we will be keeping our promise.

items.statement: Q1 CY24 capex INR 173 crores vs INR 118 crores YoY; capex-to-sales at 7%
items.quote: And clearly in line with that strategy, even in this quarter, we have been able to invest INR 173 crores as against INR 118 crores in the same period last year. This has taken our CAPEX as a percentage-to-sales to 7%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 18.3% in Q1 CY24 vs 17.9% QoQ; sustained near 18% despite >7% inflation due to localization
items.quote: So, it is already impacting and that's why see we are able to sustain our EBITDA margins close to 18% despite having last year inflation averaged above 7% in the prices, personnel cost, fuel, etc., but we still registered EBITDA margin over 18%.

items.statement: Auto/industrial pricing linked to commodity indices; aftermarket prices increased annually to cover inflation
items.quote: Pricing is always on a comparative level. That's the first point I want to make. It's related. Second is, yes, you're right, the commodity prices have stabilized, and our pricing is always linked to the commodity price movement and so our contractual agreements with the customers are always linked with the price of the commodities at the global level.

items.statement: Wind gearbox demand up ~70% YoY in Q1 CY24; wind equipment recovery slower; two-wheeler and power transmission strong
items.quote: Coming into Q1'2024, what we have seen is a very strong uptick compared to the Q1 '2023; if we go back four quarters, we have seen a very strong uptick, almost 70% growth in demand we have seen come back.

items.statement: Restructured into four divisions: E-Mobility, Powertrain & Chassis, Vehicle Lifetime Solutions, Bearings & Industrial Solutions effective 1 April 2024
items.quote: Globally, Schaeffler has restructured the divisions which we were having three divisions earlier, have now been split into four divisions. Now, why has this been done? Considering or emergence into the electric mobility play, it has become relevant and important for us to create a new business division called E-Mobility.

items.statement: Export recovery seen across Europe, Americas, Asia Pacific and China; Europe stock optimization driving orders; Asia Pacific efforts adding new order book
items.quote: If we see our performance on exports, Q1 vis-à-vis Q4 of last year, that is quarter-on-quarter, we have seen the uptick from all the markets, Europe, America, Asia Pacific , also China, we have PUBLIC seen order book improving

items.statement: Localization at 77% in Q1 CY24 vs 75% YoY; focus on component-level localization of high-specialty imports from Europe
items.quote: localization percentage as of Q1 was at 77% and last year it was at around 75%. So, we will continue to localize more and more and now our effort is also on to localize more and more at a component level for the automotive applications where we continue to import some high specialty products from Europe

items.statement: Vitesco India integration under evaluation; full integration into listed entity will take more time due to due diligence; no timeline disclosed

items.statement: Domestic revenue grew 12.4% YoY in Q1 CY24; QoQ flat; tractor and MHCV segments weak, PV and 2W strong
items.quote: In the domestic Indian market, our growth was 12.4%, and this has come from across sectors, barring a couple of sectors which I will talk about.

items.statement: E-axle project progressing per committed timelines; phased investments on track; localization actions started
items.quote: On the e-axle business, what I can say is that the project is progressing very well with our customer, and it is according to the timelines that we have committed, yes. Rightfully, our phased investments also is on track.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 17.8% in Q1 CY24 including Koovers; Koovers revenue up 24.6% YoY but EBITDA negative in ramp-up
items.quote: So, as a consolidated unit, Schaeffler India Limited, we have been able to close the quarter with INR 1,873 crores on the revenue and our EBITDA stands at 17.8% consolidated.

items.statement: Working capital at INR 1,352 crores; target range 17-19% of sales; inventory built to service recovering demand
items.quote: Our working capital went up to INR 1,352 crores in the quarter, which was an increase compared to the Q1, but however we believe that with demand that we see coming in from many of these sectors recovering, we believe that this kind of inventory need to be there to service our customer needs, and this is an optimum level of working capital that we would definitely want to operate with in the 17% t

items.statement: Free cash flow negative INR 25.6 crores in Q1 CY24 vs positive INR 177 crores QoQ; typical Q1 pattern; focus on consistent quarterly recovery
items.quote: We did have some challenges on the free cash flow. As you can see here, we have delivered a negative cash flow of INR 25.6 crores, which if one were to compare to last quarter, it was a whopping INR 177 crores coming in, in Q4'2023.

items.statement: FY25 fertilizer EBITDA per ton expected at Rs 4,500-5,000, up Rs 1,500-2,000 from new NBS rates
items.quote: In terms of margins for next year, we are expecting in the range of Rs. 4,500 to Rs. 5,000 per ton in terms of EBITDA. This considers the NBS rates that have been announced by the government, we expect an uptick of about Rs. 1,500 to Rs. 2,000 coming out of it.

items.statement: FY25 capex estimated at Rs 1,200-1,500 Cr across businesses
items.quote: We have for FY '25 estimated between Rs. 1,200 Cr to Rs. 1,500 Cr overall in terms of capex investment. This is across the multiple businesses that we have.

items.statement: New phosphoric and sulphuric acid complex at Kakinada with Rs 1,030 Cr capex, completion in couple of years
items.quote: Company has just commenced work on the new phosph oric acid and sulphuric acid complex plants at Kakinada with an estimated capex of about Rs. 1,030 crores. These plants are expected to come up in couple of years' time

items.statement: Debottlenecking granulation capacity at Kakinada and Vizag adding 3.5 lakh tons
items.quote: During the year the business is looking at debottlenecking the capacity which will add further 3.5 lakh tons to the existing capacity which means from the current 34.5 we are expecting another 3,-3.5 lakh tons to get added to the granulation capacity.

items.statement: Dhaksha drone order book at Rs 250 Cr, to be executed in H1 FY25
items.quote: Dhaksha's order book stands at around Rs. 250 Cr, and the company plans to service the same in the first half of the year.

items.statement: Crop protection margin pressure persists due to high global inventory; WoW and I Care initiatives strengthening cost position
items.quote: However, the margin pressure persists due to higher inventor y in the global markets. The business focus ed on several WoW and I Care initiatives, which helped in strengthening its cost position to offset some of the pricing pressures in the

items.statement: IMD and Skymet forecast normal to above normal rainfall for kharif 2024, boding well for agriculture season
items.quote: On a positive note, the recent forecast by IMD and Skymet have estimated normal to above normal rainfall for kharif 2024, which bodes well for the upcoming agriculture season.

items.statement: Crop protection introduced 7 new products in FY24, new product turnover index at 15%
items.quote: The business introduced 7 new products during the year and it is partnering with innovative companies to launch in-licensing products. The new products turnover index for the year was at 15%.

items.statement: Nano DAP commercial sales started H2 FY24, targeting 20-25% import replacement over 3-4 years
items.quote: We hope to see a 20% to 25% replacement happening over the next 3, 4 years and Coromandel is rightfully positioned to take advantage of this opportunity.

items.statement: New Urea SSP product approved by FCO under NBS, facility at Nimrani, first full year of operation in FY25
items.quote: Company plans to introduce new Urea SSP product, which has recently been approved by the FCO and brought under NBS. This innovative product will provide sources of N added to the traditional SSP.

items.statement: Ennore plant NGT hearing concluded, orders reserved and expected soon
items.quote: On the Ennore plant, the NGT has concluded the hearing and the matter is reserved for orders. we expect the orders to come in soon.

items.statement: Retail stores revenue ~Rs 1,700 Cr in FY24, 750 stores, adding 50 in FY25 to reach ~850, expanding to Tamil Nadu
items.quote: Last year, I would say that we had somewhere close to Rs. 1,700 Cr of revenue from all our retail centers. We have about 750-odd stores. We're planning to expand by 55 stores in last year, an additional 50 stores in FY '25. That means that the overall number of stores will go about 850 or so.

items.statement: CDMO in advanced discussions with three innovator companies, traction expected to build in FY25
items.quote: Efforts in CDMO is progressing well, and Coromandel is in advanced stages of discussion with three innovator companies. This being a two to three year journey, company expects additional traction to build up during the coming year.

items.statement: Company expects 25% volume growth in plastic piping systems and 20% overall volume growth in FY25
items.quote: The Company expects that the plastics piping system business will grow by 25% in Volume Terms and the overall growth by 20% in Volume Terms this year.

items.statement: Forecasting 15.5% gross margin for FY25
items.quote: We are forecasting this year also 15.5%.

items.statement: Adding 5 new plastic piping systems in FY25: Acoustic PP, PE Gas, PERT, PE single wall corrugated, Rainwater Harvesting
items.quote: The Company currently has 36 plastic piping Systems in the division and plans to add another 5 new systems viz. Acoustic PP Pipe System in collaboration with Poloplast GmbH of Austria, Polyethylene Gas Piping System, PERT Piping System, PE single wall corrugated Pipes, and Rainwater Harvesting System (Infiltration modules for ground recharge and storage) during the current year.

items.statement: PVC raw material prices expected to remain range-bound around Rs 50,000/ton; pricing to follow raw material trends
items.quote: The raw material price is going to remain at the same level , range bound of 50,000 plus , 50,000 minus. So, we will maintain the same way pricing , if there will be any upside on the raw material price.

items.statement: JNPT protective packaging plant investment in FY25 but production likely only in FY26
items.quote: The new plant what we are going to put up in JNPT may not go in production also in this year. It requires some time now, the investment we will be making which will be in operation fully in '25-'26.

items.statement: Packaging segment EBITDA margin improved to 18% in Q4; management hopes to maintain or improve annual average margin
items.quote: We are making average. We hope to maintain or improve the average margin back to last year because we are introducing so many product ranges also and we are growing more and more in export markets.

items.statement: Non-piping segments (packaging, industrial, material handling) expected to grow ~10% in FY25; furniture flat
items.quote: You see when we are saying 20% growth for the Company, it means we are talking of about 125,000 metric tons for the Company as a whole and maximum it is coming from piping. So, other than piping, it will be a single digit, about 10% growth you can say.

items.statement: Inventory loss of Rs 50 crore in FY24 due to lower resin prices; no inventory gain in Q4
items.quote: For full year, there was around Rs. 50 crore. The sto ck which was valued as on 31st March 2023 has been valued at 51 crore lower on 31st March 2024. So, there is no gain

items.statement: Cash surplus increased to Rs 1,178 crore as of March 2024 from Rs 738 crore a year earlier
items.quote: The Company has total Cash Surplus of Rs. 1178 crores as on 31 st March, 2024 as against Cash Surplus of Rs. 738 crores as on 31st March, 2023

items.statement: Net interest margin guidance kept at 2.90% for the year
items.quote: Net interest margin, we have kept a guidance of 2.90%.

items.statement: Annual slippage ratio guidance was 1.25% for FY24, actual came at 1.27%
items.quote: And if we look at overall annual slippage ratio of the bank that we had given a guidance of 1.25%, it is at 1.27%.

items.statement: ROA improvement targeted quarter-on-quarter but reaching 1% in FY25 seen as challenging
items.quote: Maybe. It will be challenging. It may not be easy going. It may be challenging. But yes, definitely the effort will be to improve on ROA on a quarter-to-quarter basis.

items.statement: Approximately Rs.1,000 crore of IT and digital transformation spend planned for the year
items.quote: So all these are planned, approximately 1000cr. of spend we have planned for this year and that trend will continue as and when we go ahead.

items.statement: Total recovery pool around Rs.28,000 crore with Rs.18,400 crore in NCLT
items.quote: I think total return of pool is around 28,000cr. and out of that, NCLT is Rs.18400 crore.

items.statement: Domestic NIM improved to 3.25% in Q4 FY24 from 3.03% previous quarter
items.quote: For domestic, the net interest margin for the quarter was 3.25%, and on a global basis it was 3.03%.

items.statement: Cost of deposits declined Q-o-Q from 4.91% to 4.82% due to excess SLR liquidation and overseas borrowing
items.quote: Cost of deposit ratio of the bank improved in this quarter over the previous quarter from 4.91% to 4.82%.

items.statement: NBFC lending rates increased 50 bps on average case-to-case; some exposures called back when borrowers did not accept
items.quote: So, it can't be quantified that 25 bps across, but 50 bps across it was increased on a case-to-case basis.

items.statement: Similar recovery levels of around Rs.3,000 crore expected in FY25 as achieved in FY24
items.quote: So similar level of recoveries we are expecting in the next year as well as we did last year.

items.statement: Forward-looking provisions of Rs.1,100 crore held in addition to mandated Rs.1,400 crore to prepare for ECL implementation
items.quote: As far as provisions, we are holding provisions, forward-looking provisions around Rs.1,100 crores, in addition to the mandated provision of Rs.1,400 crores.

items.statement: Board approved raising capital via issue of 400 crore equity shares of Rs.10 face value, subject to AGM approval
items.quote: The bank has taken approval for raising capital during the year from the board, which will go to the AGM for further approvals. That is around issue of 400 crore equity shares for the face value of Rs.10 each.

items.statement: CASA ratio improved to 39% in FY24 from typical 37-38%; target is to sustain and improve further
items.quote: In the current year, our CASA ratio is around 39pc which we have achieved. Generally, it is 37-38pc. Now we have achieved 39pc.

items.statement: HTM proportion of SLR investments to be maintained around 75-80% of Rs.66,000 crore SLR book
items.quote: Out of 66,000 crores, I think around 75-80% is in HTM. So, I think going forward also, that same ratio will be maintained.

items.statement: Investment book reclassification impact on CET-1 minimal at around 4-5 basis points positive
items.quote: Hardly it will be around 4-5 basis points on the CET-1 ratio. So, that is there.

items.statement: Dividend of 2.8% declared for first time in nine years due to consistent profits
items.quote: And bank has also declared dividend for the first time after nine years; 2.8% dividend because of th e consistent profit for the last three years bank has been making

items.statement: FY25 capex planned at INR 250-275 crores for ~100 stores and store innovations
items.quote: During this yea r, we are planning to spend INR 275 crores in opening circa 100 stores and innovating some of our top stores

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance INR 250-275 crores funded from internal accruals
items.quote: For FY '25, we are planning to spend INR250 crores to INR275 crores and we are reasonably confident we will show this from our internal accruals.

items.statement: Plan to open 15 department stores, 60 Intune stores and new beauty stores in FY25
items.quote: So I think we are -- at this point of time, we are very, very confident of sticking to our guidance, which is 15 new stores in departmental stores and around 60 Intune stores and new stores.

items.statement: Expect gross margin improvement in FY25 driven by lower private brand inventory write-offs
items.quote: You are absolutely spot on, Ankit. When we did the budgeting exercise during for FY '25, we have factored the increase in margin in private brands.

items.statement: Beauty distribution business targeting 7-9% EBITDA margins by year 4
items.quote: So the margin should be in the range of between 7% and probably 9%. That's a range we are expecting it right now.

items.statement: Apparels poised for recovery in FY25 with strong women's ethnic wear performance
items.quote: We believe that apparels are poised for recovery in FY '25, and the women's ethnic wear line has shown some very, very strong performances across the board, and we are very confident about that.

items.statement: Premium plus portfolio grew 25% in Q4 with 10+ new brands added driving ATV up 8% and ASP up 4%
items.quote: During the quarter, our premium plus portfolio grew by 25% and we added more than 10 new brands such as Dockers, Beverly Hills Polo Club, GANT, Salt Attire, Saundh, Ancestory and Folksong.

items.statement: Private brand turnaround expected in Q2 FY25 with 500 new options launched in April
items.quote: We see the likely turnaround of private brands apparel business sometime in Q2.

items.statement: Election-related store closures and heat wave causing near-term slowness in April-May
items.quote: Once the elections have started, I think the mixture of election and the heat wave which we are all witnessing, there has been certain markets where there has been slowness.

items.statement: Intune capex per sq ft sustained at INR 1,550 with payback period of 2.5-3 years
items.quote: The capex per square feet is sustained at INR1,550 per square feet. This will help us to improve the overall return on capital employed.

items.statement: Intune store-level EBITDA positive in first year with mature stores at 12,000+ sales per sq ft and 36% delivered margins
items.quote: mature stores are consistent ly hovering in north of 12,000 as far as sales per square foot on an annualized basis is concerned. So that's the start point of the economics. We have clarified that our delivered margins would be in the range of 36

items.statement: Beauty distribution revenue target INR 250 crores in FY25, INR 400 crores in FY26, INR 550 crores in FY27
items.quote: We are forecasting next year to double this current run rate. We intend to reach around INR250 crores. And what was very important for us is to be EBITDA positive from year 1.

items.statement: Private brand inventory reduced by INR 56 crores vs FY23 to INR 134 crores, targeting 14-16 weeks inventory
items.quote: We have been successful in reducing the inventory to INR134 crores, a reduction of more than INR50-plus crores versus last year.

items.statement: Intune inventory at 12-16 weeks with 22 stores, expected to improve to 12-14 weeks with scale
items.quote: On the Intune, again, we are between 12 and 16 weeks with just 22 stores opened. So, with the additional stores, I do expect the working capital in terms of weeks should come down probably between 12 and 14 weeks.

items.statement: Like-for-like costs flat in Q4; 10% cost increase from new stores, new businesses, and tech investments
items.quote: I'm happy to infor m you like-to-like costs were almost flat. The increase in cost is due to three reasons. One due to new stores opened in the last one year. Secondly, new business such as SSBeauty.com and Intune; and thirdly investments in technology

items.statement: Like-for-like expense growth target at half of inflation (2-3%) for FY25 with new store costs additional
items.quote: This year, as we start, we want to have like-for-like expenses of probably half the inflation between 2 and 3 percentage. And any new stores, obviously, will have the additional expenses.

items.statement: Management does not provide specific numerical guidance on member additions or inventory additions for FY25, but aims to double inventory to 10,000 rooms by FY30.
items.quote: Normally, we never give guidance on what numbers we will sort of deliver. But definitely, you can see that we have already delivered approximately 400 rooms. And if we have to double from 5,000 to 10,000, obviously, the rate of room additions itself will accelerate.

items.statement: INR 835 crores of capex is currently underway for 5 greenfield, 1 brownfield and acquisition projects, adding ~690 keys.
items.quote: All of these actions lead to INR835 crores of capex, which is underway right now for 5 greenfield, 1 brownfield and acquisition projects, and with the total estimated keys that will come through this would be about 690.

items.statement: Management aims to spend about INR 2,500 crores in capex by 2030 to double inventory.
items.quote: our aim, and I mentioned this earlier, is that we are going to spend about INR2,500 crores in capex over the next -- by 2030.

items.statement: Deferred revenue increased by INR 269 crores to INR 5,595 crores as of March 31, 2024.
items.quote: Our deferred revenue has increased by INR269 crores to INR5,595 crores.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin expanded 90 bps to 28.5% in FY24; consolidated EBITDA margin not explicitly stated but consolidated EBITDA grew 3.3% to INR 623 crores.
items.quote: EBITDA margin up by 90 basis points and stands at 28.5%.

items.statement: Sales and marketing expense as % of sales value improved to ~22.8-23% in FY24 from 25.1% in FY23, driven by digital/referral mix and productivity.
items.quote: For this full year, we are at about 22.8%, 23%. And last year, we were at 25.1%. So you can see there's already something has come in.

items.statement: 59% of member additions in Q4 FY24 and 57% in FY24 came through digital and referral channels; online booking at 82% (76% via app).
items.quote: 59% of the member additions through the referral and digital routes in Q4 and 57% in FY '24.

items.statement: HCR annual capex is EUR 3-4 million, primarily for IT and refurbishment; timeshare apartment build is treated as inventory, not capex.
items.quote: is EUR3 million to EUR4 million. Kavinder Singh: EUR3 million to EUR4 million. It's pretty basic just to get some -- a little bit of some improvement in some resorts, and IT capex is quite big

items.statement: Inventory additions depend on approvals and execution, not capital; some projects may slip from FY25 to FY26.
items.quote: The constraint is approvals. The constraint is the execution on the ground. So some things will come, if not in FY '25, they'll come in FY '26.

items.statement: Resort income expected to grow faster in FY25 (targeting 12-13% CAGR) as new inventory ramps up and F&B spend per room night increases.
items.quote: I am very confident that the resort revenue, if you look at a CAGR for a certain period, I think, say, a five year period or something like that, we may be upwards of 12%, 13%.

items.statement: Cash position INR 1,383 crores as of March 31, 2024; received INR 66 crores income tax refund (incl. INR 6.5 crores interest).
items.quote: Our cash position stands at INR1,383 crores as on 31 st March 2024. We have received income tax refund of INR66 crores, which includes interest of INR6.5 crores.

items.statement: Member-to-room ratio currently ~56; management comfortable with ratio falling to 50-53 as inventory additions run ahead of member additions.

items.statement: No specific FY25 room addition guidance given; inventory additions depend on project approvals and execution across greenfield, brownfield, lease, PPP, and acquisition channels.
items.quote: As I mentioned to Himanshu earlier, neither on the member additions nor on the inventory additions we give any guidance.

items.statement: Targeting spread of 2.5% and NIM of 3.5% for FY25
items.quote: in terms of the spread, we would look at about 2.5% and 3.5% NIM is what we would be targeting.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio guidance of 18% maintained for FY25
items.quote: we will continue with the 18% guidance for cost-to-income ratio in FY '25.

items.statement: Expect to exceed FY24 organic growth of 12.5-13% in FY25
items.quote: So, for FY'25, we believe that our aspirations of course to do better than that and we think that we can exceed that number in FY '25 in terms of full year numbers.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin was 16% in Q4, down 100 bps quarter-on-quarter due to revenue shortfalls with costs incurred
items.quote: Our operating EBITDA for the quarter was at 16%. It declined 100 bps quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Target to return to 17% EBITDA margin quickly; medium-term trajectory remains 17-19%
items.quote: Our endeavor is to first reach 17%, which we are very confident about, we will reach to that number, as I said, because revenue loss has reflected into the margin profile because cost was incurred, so we should be able to come back to 17% very quickly.

items.statement: US Healthcare order book grew 250% in FY24; won USD 17 million five-year deal and USD 8 million deal
items.quote: While we don't report TCV order book, just to give you some flavor, while on a small base, the Healthcare order book in US grew 250% in FY'24.

items.statement: UK and Europe projected to deliver at least double-digit year-on-year growth in FY25
items.quote: So, all in all, our UK and Europe will definitely deliver double-digit, in FY'25.

items.statement: Middle East and APAC expected to continue double-digit growth in FY25
items.quote: But geography will continue to grow double-digits.

items.statement: US expected to bounce back in Q1 FY25 and grow much faster than company average
items.quote: US which we had a challenge in Q4, like we said will bounce back in Q1, and will grow much faster compared to the entire company.

items.statement: Declared dividend of INR 12 per share for FY24
items.quote: We declared a dividend of INR 12 per share.

items.statement: Three specific client situations in US impacted Q4 revenue by over USD 1 million each; two expected to recover in Q1
items.quote: Just ballpark, each of these three very specific situations that I talked about, right, give or take each of them created a little over a million each of impact and so you can kind of do the rough math there.

items.statement: Top 30 accounts now contribute 57% of revenue, up from ~50% range; focus on mining existing accounts
items.quote: The identified top 30 accounts globally in Mastek now contribute roughly about 57% of our overall revenue.

items.statement: Borrowings at INR 487 crores as of March 31, 2024; planned repayment over next 2-3 years
items.quote: Our borrowings now stood at INR 487 crores as of 31st March 2024 and we have a detailed installment plan agreed with banks as part of loan borrowing and we are meeting all our installments commitment as we have said and will continue to discharge this borrowing in next two to three years as planned.

items.statement: BizAnalytica acquisition impacted margins by 30-40 bps for full year FY24
items.quote: BizAnalytica impact would be broadly in the range of 30 to 40 bps for a full year basis.

items.statement: Selected as key supplier in UK Defense Department DIP framework with addressable market of ~USD 400 million; expect USD 50-60 million revenue over 4 years
items.quote: Over the period of the four years, we expe ct roughly about USD 50 to 60 million worth of revenue coming from this particular framework

items.statement: Talent costs remain high due to cloud/digital skill demand; investing in growth across regions and verticals
items.quote: The talent cost because 90%-plus of our business is cloud and digital. While there is an attrition which is coming down for the industry, but the kind of talent we operate with, very less legacy business, the talent is always at the high demand.

items.statement: Expect 10%-12% value growth and 15%-18% volume growth for FY25
items.quote: We feel that going forward also in the year coming we should have a healthy growth, both in terms of value and volume close to about 10%-12% on the value basis as well as 15% to 18% on the volume basis.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 18%-20% for FY25
items.quote: Probably 10% to 12% with regard to value, broad guidelines with regard to the margins per se , yes, you can expect anywhere between 18 % and 20% to sustain.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity target of 1x-1.05x and debt/EBITDA below 3x for next 3-5 years
items.quote: As I said the guidance for equity could be 1x-1.05x max. If I'm talking about debt and equity prima facie at least for the next 3 to 5 years or so. And a debt EBITDA should be less than 3x most of the time.

items.statement: Capex turnaround 14-16 months; planning expansion for Dihydromyrcenol, Amber Fleur, CST capacity and new products like Menthol, Peppermint oil
items.quote: We are contemplating possibly some fundraising for some of our very high value dream project of menthol and peppermint oil and a few other CAPEX, possibly some expansion on our very important products like Dihydromyrcenol, Amber Fleur. Maybe there could be a capacity expansion of CST.

items.statement: Aroma chemical demand robust driven by FMCG/fragrance brands and premiumization; Europe biggest market, then US; developing economies (Africa, Middle East) long-term growth
items.quote: the demand for aroma chemicals has remained robust as prominent FMCG and fragrance brands continue to enjoy robust demand from their end customers. The demand has been further propelled by the ongoing premi umization trend in the cosmetics and personal care industry

items.quote: Despite this, freight costs have been increasing significantly due to the impact of the Red Sea crisis and obviously there's been an escalation in the shipping cost which has compressed our margins otherwise the results could have read better.

items.statement: Biotech R&D progressing but commercialization timeline uncertain; focus on cost parity with existing processes; sharing trial results with interested customers under NDA
items.quote: Our challenge is not to get the biotechnology piece right but it is also important to get the costing right because we want to ensure that in the ecosystem in which we operate, even if there is a new technology which is breakthrough and a game changer, it is either affordable, on par or at best an affordable premium.

items.statement: Givaudan JV phase 1 capex done; phase 2 under exploration with potential for further expansion and margin change
items.quote: Yes, in the first phase the capex that we have indicated is the first phase capex. And once the first phase capex rolls out then in the second phase which is still work in progress, there will be opportunities and scope to explore for further capex.

And we hold on to that aspiration of double-digit kind of EBITDA margin for the coming year, with improvement also in profit after tax.

items.statement: Lighting segment targets 20% revenue growth in FY25 and aims to reach breakeven
items.quote: we feel that it would be reasonable to aspire for a 20% growth in lighting in the coming year.

items.quote: So, number one, we are banking on a 2x growth for the current year from the -- as I said, we are on a small base. So, we plan to grow 100%.

items.statement: Flashlight segment overall growth estimated at 10-12% in FY25 despite battery-operated degrowth
items.quote: we estimate that we will be growing between 10% and 12% in the coming year in the overall flashlight segment.

items.quote: I would say we would go on to say about INR 1,800 crore in the next 3 years on these three categories, including FY25.

items.quote: If that happens, we have a decent period of time to plan things and to mitigate that. And obviously, the only mitigation would be that we tak e price increases, for which we will have adequate time

items.quote: The Bank continues to hold contingency provisions of Rs. 13,100 crore at March 31, 2024.

items.quote: It's very difficult to forecast what is going to happen in the future and we don't really kind of forecast. For us maintaining liquidity is important as we reported. items.quote: We don't really give an outlook, Mahrukh, in terms of growth. I think we have our risk framework, our distribution and our delivery system, whatever passes through that we'll be happy to take.

items.quote: So I guess we could see some further moderation in the NIM, but I would expect it to be pretty range bound from here on for the next few quarters until a rate cut actually happens.

items.quote: I mean, we did raise deposit rates by 10 bps in February on the retail side, which was not there at the time when we had our last call. So, some impact will be there, but I guess that will go through, it wouldn't be a very large impact.

items.statement: Operating expense growth pace has moderated and expected to remain moderate; technology expense growth rate to moderate given large base
items.quote: So I think in totality, as I said, we would expect the pace of growth of opex to be more moderate than we have seen in the last couple of years.

items.statement: No particular growth challenge seen in current environment; sufficient room to grow given market share in micro markets
items.quote: I don't see any particular growth challenge sitting here today in the environment.

items.statement: Corporate portfolio growth at 10-11% for some time; less competitive in some pockets due to profitability view but open to opportunities passing risk filters
items.quote: On the corporate side, actually, our growth has been 10% to low double-digit kind of for some time. See, we are very open. I mean, we have strong corporate relationships and a strong funnel for business.

items.statement: Credit costs at sub-40 bps this quarter; may normalize upwards slightly but nothing dramatic expected
items.quote: I guess, looking at it in terms of credit costs, we are still at sub-40 basis points for this quarter. I think, if you kind of adjust out one offs or if you take a more adjusted view, we would still be under 50 basis points.

items.statement: Employee headcount additions slowing from Q3; expect stability to moderate increase going forward
items.quote: I would expect stability to moderate increase from here on.

items.statement: FY25 presales guidance of Rs. 2,500 crores for residential plus Rs. 500 crores from IC&IC, totaling Rs. 3,000 crores combined

items.statement: Long-term aspiration to reach Rs. 8,000-10,000 crores pre-sales by FY28
items.quote: Our aspiration to where we were in FY23 to 5X over which will mean we target a pre-sales scale of Rs. 8,000 crores to Rs. 10,000 crores.

items.statement: Estimated Rs. 7,000-7,500 crores capital needed to achieve 5X growth aspiration, half funded through internal accruals and IC&IC cash flows
items.quote: Our estimate is in order to achieve our aspiration, we will need something around Rs. 7,000 crores to Rs. 7,500 crores of capital. Half of that is available to us through our accruals, our IC business, our debt to equity.

items.statement: Actively discussing platform-level fundraise with parent Mahindra Group open to participate; open to QIP, products, or external partners
items.quote: We are in the process of doing some discussions, fundraise at a platform level where even our parent is quite open to participating given their desire to grow Mahindra Lifespaces into a growth gem and support our growth aspiration.

items.statement: Healthy business development pipeline of Rs. 5,000-6,000 crores GDV in addition to Rs. 4,400 crores acquired in FY24 and Thane project of Rs. 7,000-8,000 crores
items.quote: We continue to have a very healthy BD pipeline, anywhere from Rs. 5,000 crores to Rs. 6,000 crores. This is in addition to the Rs. 4,400 crores that we acquired last year. It is in addition to Thane which is around Rs. 8000 crores.

items.statement: Targeting project-level pre-tax IRR north of 20% across portfolio; not guiding on EBITDA margins due to accounting complexity
items.quote: Our goal is to be always north of 20% IRR and that's project IRR, pretax if you do equity IRR with the right debt to equity, capital structure, post-tax it'll come out to be a couple of percentage points higher.

items.statement: Residential demand remains buoyant driven by per capita income growth and home ownership desire across urban and non-urban centers
items.quote: The Resi segment will continue to have lot of buoyancy driven by per capita income, driven by the desire to own home across urban and non-urban centers.

items.statement: FY28 presales mix aspiration: Rs. 5,000-6,000 crores from Mumbai, couple thousand crores each from Pune and Bangalore
items.quote: Ideally it will be somewhere around Rs. 6,000 crores from Mumbai, let's say Rs. 5,000 crores to Rs. 6,000 crores and couple of thousand crores each from Pune and Bangalore.

items.statement: Acquiring land at peak cycle but pricing captures cost; maintaining deal discipline with IRR guardrails, walking away from deals below financial parameters
items.quote: Anytime we are acquiring a piece of land we are very diligent about the economic assessment related to that acquisition. We do lots and lots of market intelligence gathering to ensure that we are able to make our business case work.

items.quote: The biggest thrust area for me going forward is going to be project execution, especially cost of construction, the procurement, the design specs, the procurement excellence because that's where you will end up losing a couple of basis points, a couple of percentage points of margin.

items.quote: We get a lot of requests Shreyans for Ahmedabad which are small 1-2-3 acres kind of you know demand from them. But we want to get to anchor client which is at least 40 acres - 50 acres plus.

items.statement: Operating costs to reduce by INR200-300 per ton over next three years driven by controllable efficiency levers
