items.statement: UK soda ash contribution margin compressed to USD 30-40 per ton; expected to remain under pressure
items.quote: It has broadly been in the range of about USD 30 to USD 40-odd per ton and that's created a pressure on the financial numbers to do the impairment charge.

items.statement: Export NSR down ~$60 per ton QoQ; export prices fell $100-120 per ton YoY; domestic prices stable with only $2-8 movement
items.quote: the current quarter, the NSR is down from the previous quarter in export to almost $60 -odd. And the fall between the same quarter last year, beca use last ye ar, this quarter was a peak because the prices were reset down by $150 broadly on the export side

items.statement: European soda ash demand destruction of 1-1.2 million tons due to high energy costs; Chinese demand grew ~15% in Jan-Feb 2024
items.quote: the broad oversupply, demand supply mismatch is about 1 million to 1.2 m illion tons in the European market because that's the demand destruction has happened and the supplies have remained

items.statement: India soda ash demand stable at 4.056 million tons in FY24 vs 4 million tons in FY23; imports rose 500,000 tons to 1-1.1 million tons
items.quote: the marke t demand in India has been fairly stable last year, compared to the year end ed '23, w here the demand was 4 million tons, the demand this year has been 4.056 tons

items.statement: UK strategy shifting to value-added products: bicarb, salt, pharma salt; soda ash plant at Lostock impaired
items.quote: U.K. will continue to focus on the more value-added space of bi-carbonate, salt and pharmaceutical salt. They will continue to run them very efficiently, and they are profitable.

items.statement: European oversupply driven by Turkish capacity displacement and Red Sea freight issues; Chinese demand risk if real estate weakens
items.quote: The key challenge continues to be the European market where because of the loss of market, the Turkish capacity is moving to the rest of the world.

items.statement: India 250,000 ton brownfield expansion commissioning in May 2024; full capacity utilization expected within 90 days
items.quote: Once the capacity is hooked up, I think we would probably tend to sort of see full capacity reaching in about 90-odd days or so, not more than that.

items.statement: US debt paydown may extend from 3 to 4 years; paid $110M vs $100M target in year 1
items.quote: The maximum we see it increasing instead of being 3-year pay down, it may have become 4-year pay down. Our calculations are landing somewhere there.

items.statement: US domestic EBITDA stable with only $4-5 change YoY; export EBITDA main driver of margin decline
items.quote: We have not seen anything more than $4 or $5 change in the EBITDA number compared to last year. The biggest fall has been on the export side.

items.statement: US domestic volumes growing; record production in Feb-Mar 2024; shipments to LATAM, APAC, Europe, China
items.quote: the plant has had record numbers , actually in the month of Feb ruary and March, and the op erations continue to post record production numbers

items.statement: UK Lostock soda ash plant impaired (non-cash) under IND-AS 36 due to lower future cash flows; other UK plants unaffected
items.quote: This plant in Lostock has been impaired as per IND-AS 36 as required, because these future cash flows at this point of time are lower than what we are holding value of the assets are.

items.statement: Early summer onset in South, East, Maharashtra driving excellent demand across models; North yet to fire but expected soon
items.quote: Starting March 24, it has seen a decent summer. There has been all around phenomenal demand and summer set s in early in South ern India, Eastern India and Maharashtra, and we are witnessing excellent demand across all these regions across the

items.statement: Aspire to restore historical EBITDA margin of 32% over next 2-3 years; not expected in FY25
items.quote: Our endeavour and our aspiration is to be back to that level. It might not happen this year, but in the next 2 years or 3 years or so, that is where we aspire to be back again.

items.statement: Minor price hikes of 1-2% in current quarter; significant price hikes not possible as prices already committed
items.quote: There will not be a significant price hike in this quarter. There will be some minor price hikes. But a lot of it is already sort prices already have been committed. So we will not be able to sort of change the price significantly.

items.statement: Climate Technologies Australia transitioning to fully outsourced model by Sep'25; portable coolers from India, other products from China
items.quote: Completely outsourced business model which is progressing well . Portable air coolers will be outsourced from India and Rest of their other products will be outsourced from China.

items.statement: Climate Technologies Australia cost of doing business reduced from ₹77 cr to ₹49 cr in FY24; targeting ₹38 cr next year
items.quote: When we acquired the company , its annual cost of doing business was ₹ 77 crores. In FY23-24, we reduced it to ₹ 49 crores and next year , it is likely to be around ₹ 38 crores.

items.statement: Climate Technologies Australia Q4 FY24 gross margin 40.4% vs negative 7% YoY; Q3 FY24 40.0% vs 27.9% YoY
items.quote: In Q4 FY24 gross profit margin percentage stood at 40.4% versus negative 7%. While in Q3 FY24, it was 40 .0% versus 27.9%.

items.statement: Stock-outs occurring in select models due to unprecedented demand; operations team working to fulfill orders
items.quote: To some extent, that is sort of happening in some select models in our case. However, our operations team is working day and night to meet with the demand.

items.statement: Modern retail, e-commerce, D2C, institutional channels contributed ~30% of FY24 sales; GT remaining 70%
items.quote: However, Y -o-Y and in absolute quantity, it is showing phenomenal growth. But all put together in FY23-24, it would have contributed almost 30% or one third of the sale which consists of large format stores, RCS, e-commerce, D2C, institution, etc.

items.statement: GSK China loan outstanding ~₹51.7 cr after ₹7.7 cr impairment; expect recovery and impairment reversal as profitability improves
items.quote: So overall loan, including outstanding interest was ~ ₹ 59.4 crores, out of which ₹7.7 crores impairment has been provided for. It doesn't mean it has been written off, it is provided for. So remaining is ~ ₹ 51.7 crores.

items.statement: Industrial cooling inquiries and orders rising sharply due to heat spike
items.quote: Yes, of course. Of course, because of the spike in heat, there is a much larger level of inquiries and orders. So of course, what we are seeing in domestic, is also something we are witnessing in industrial coolers.

items.statement: Standalone FY24 EBITDA margin flat at 20.2% vs 20% YoY; Q4 FY24 standalone EBITDA margin 25.3%
items.quote: EBITDA margin for FY24, on Y-o-Y basis almost remains the same, up from 20% to 20.2%.

items.statement: Overseas subsidiaries FY24 revenue ₹433 cr (up 13% YoY), EBITDA margin improved from -9.1% to +2.6%
items.quote: Overseas subsidiaries put together has registered a top line of ₹ 433 crores versus ₹ 385 crores in FY24 i.e. increase of 13% Y-o-Y, while for the Q4 FY24, sales has registered Y-o-Y growth of 15%.

items.statement: IMPCO Mexico and Symphony Brazil exceeded internal budgets; GSK China first positive EBITDA ₹5 cr
items.quote: IMPCO Mexico is concerned, for the quarter as well as for the year, it has registered highest ever top line as well as profitability. Summer has been a strong tailwind, and it has surpassed our internal budgeted financials.

items.statement: Target 20% market share by FY28 from current 14%+
items.quote: Adani Cement's current market share is about 14% plus with an internal target to hit 20% by FY28.

items.statement: Growth capex for FY25 estimated at INR 5,000-6,000 crores; total capex including efficiency around INR 7,500 crores
items.quote: I would say our total capex would be for growth alone, if you're asking, would be in the range of about INR5,000 crores to INR6,000 crores. Purely growth.

items.statement: Capacity to reach 86 mt in FY25, 100-120 mt in FY26, 140 mt in FY28
items.quote: FY '25, I will be exiting with capacity of almost 86 million tons. In '26, we should achieve 100, 120 in FY27 and finally 140 million tons in FY '28.

items.statement: Master Supply Agreement volume at 3.4 mt in Q4 FY24, up 42% YoY
items.quote: The Master Supply Agreement volume stood at 3.4 million tons against 2.4 million tons, an increase of 42%.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin expanded 3.5% to 19.1%; FY24 margin expanded 7.4% to 19.3%
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by 7.4% to 19.3%.

items.statement: Target INR 530/ton cost reduction by FY28 from FY24 base of INR 4,170/ton
items.quote: we have already targeted to achieve almost INR530 a ton further reduction for which we are investing and target to achieve by FY'28.

items.statement: Power cost to fall from INR 6.75/kWh to INR 4.50/kWh by FY28 saving ~INR 150/ton
items.quote: Today the power cost is about INR6.75 paisa. Over the next 5 years this will come down to about INR4.50 or so. And that itself you can work out is about INR150 a ton purely on cement.

items.statement: Logistics cost reduced 8% to INR 1,280/ton in Q4 FY24; targeting 40% of INR 530 saving from logistics
items.quote: Because of these initiatives, our logistics cost has been reduced by 8% to INR1,280 per ton in Q4 FY '24 from INR1,389 in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Expect cement demand growth of 8-9% annually, outpacing capacity additions
items.quote: We expect higher utilisation over the next five years since demand is expected to grow at a rate of 8% to 9% faster than the capacity expansion rate.

items.statement: Blended cement at 86% of sales; premium products at 24% of trade sales in Q4 FY24
items.quote: blended cement as a mix of total sales maintained at 86%, premium products as a percentage of trade sales increased to 24%.

items.statement: Clinker expansion of 12 mt (3 kilns) ready to order pending environmental clearance in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: Three locations, one in West, one in North and one in South, 4 million, 3 kilns we are ready to place orders as soon as we have the EC. And this is not so far in distant future. I'm talking of only a quarter or two at the most.

items.statement: Promoters infused INR 8,339 crores in April 2024 via warrants, total INR 20,000 crores; stake up 3.6% to 70.3%
items.quote: The promoters have fully subscribed to the warrants program in the company by further infusing INR8,339 crores in April 24, thereby i nfusing a total amount of INR20,000 crores. Promoters have further increased their stake in the company by 3.6% to 70.3

items.statement: Sanghi to produce minimum 5 mt clinker in FY25; kilns refurbished by H1, both running flat out in H2
items.quote: Yes, 5 million is something minimum we will do, number one. As you know, we have done an MSA with Sanghi in the current format and that MSA is in the public domain.

items.statement: Target 82 mt clinker capacity by FY28 (from ~54 mt); 80% brownfield, 20% greenfield
items.quote: our target is to reach almost 76 million tons of clinker by end of FY28 sorry 82 million tons of clinker when I look at 140 million tons.

items.statement: WHRS capacity to reach 186 MW by March 2025 (currently 134 MW); 1,000 MW RE by FY26 for 60% green power
items.quote: Our waste heat recovery capacity at the time of takeover was 40 MW in September '22, which we are now targeting to increase to 186 MW by March '25. Currently, the WHRS capacity is at 134 MW.

items.statement: Medium-term revenue growth guidance of 17%-20% reaffirmed with FY24 as new base
items.quote: Looking ahead, I would also like to reaffirm our revenue growth guidance. As previously stated, we expect to achieve a growth rate of 17%-20% in the medium term. However, we now use FY24 as our new base here for these projections.

items.statement: Planned Kolkata expansion of ~35 crores for infrastructure plus 10 crores routine capex, funded by internal accruals
items.quote: This expansion involves an investment of approximately 35 crores for the infrastructure. We plan to finance this expansion entirely through internal accruals underscoring our strong financial health and commitment to sustainable growth.

items.statement: Gujarat land expansion deferred by 1-2 years to prioritize Kolkata modernization
items.quote: In line w ith our strategic priorities , we have decided to defer the land expansion at our Gujarat facility by approximately 1-2 years. This decision allow us to focus on modernizing and enhancing our facilities in Kolkata first

items.statement: Gross margin expected to improve to 35%-36% over next 2-3 years from current ~32%
items.quote: So, we expect the margin to go up by say around 5%. So, maybe around 35%-36% over the next 2-3 years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 11.1% in FY24, down 150 bps YoY; room for improvement with revenue growth
items.quote: FY24 EBITDA margin at 11.1% underwent a reduction of 1 50 BPS from FY23 levels. This contraction stemmed from an increase of over 13% in overhead expenses as compared with 4% growth in revenue.

items.statement: Pentonic portfolio contribution to cross 50% of revenue in 2-3 years from 34% currently
items.quote: So, currently, as I mentioned that Pentonic, portfolio contributes about 34% to our overall revenue and going forward definitely in another 2-3 years' time it will easily cross 50% contribution.

items.statement: Industry volume growth estimated at 4-6%; value growth higher due to premiumization
items.quote: I think that in terms of volume, the growth rate is going to be around 5% or anything between 4-6%. But definitely, with the premiumization, it is possible to achieve a higher growth in terms of value.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 gross margin fell 178 bps YoY due to ~30% minimum wage hike in Gujarat
items.quote: The margin increased by 103 BPS over the previous quarter but fell by 178 BPS as compared to Q4 FY23. This fall was on account of rise in minimum wages in Gujarat leading to higher labor costs.

items.statement: Kenya subsidiary investment structured as $100 for 60% equity plus $350k loan; total expected investment ~$500k
items.quote: So, we expect our overall investment of around $5 lakh; half a million dollars in this Kenyan subsidy, which will be in form of loans only. Capital is right now invested at $100.

items.statement: Dividend of ₹5 per share announced (~22% payout) pending AGM approval
items.quote: Finally, I'm pleased to inf orm that our Board of Directors have announced a dividend of ₹5 per share maintaining our commitment to rewarding our shareholders. This represents a payout of about 22% pending approval at our upcoming AGM

items.statement: Q1 FY25 off to double-digit growth in first month despite high base; confident on new products and exports
items.quote: So, Q1 so far has been... I mean, it's just been one month, which is typically a low month for us. So we have a double-digit growth in the first month. We have a good task for Q1 because last year it had a high base. But yes, we are confident that with the help of the new products and increase in our exports, we'll definitely be able to deliver a good Q1.

items.statement: Adjacent categories (markers, highlighters, crayons, modeling dough) to launch in H1 FY25 as growth driver
items.quote: The second driver is going to be the adjacent categories, as I mentioned, that right now we Q4 FY24 & FY 24 Earnings Webinar 10 are largely in the popular category like ball pen and gel pens but we are absent in categories like children's markers, permanent markers, highlighters, and some such adjacent categories. So , which we are going to launch in the first half itself

items.statement: Mitsubishi Uni-Ball brand target of ₹100 crore revenue in next 2 years
items.quote: So we are doing good with the Mitsubishi Pencil Company and we are trying to grow the brand to a hundred crore level in next two years. So that's about the Uni-Ball brand.

items.statement: Corporate sales contribution erratic; long-term range estimated at 5-10% vs 18% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: But typically, the contribution from corporate, we estimate anything between 5 to 10% i.e. on a long term or on a yearly basis, you will see it will range in between 5 to 10%.

items.statement: Asset growth target of 12-13% for FY25, similar deposit growth, medium-term NIM target of 3.5%, ROA to stay near 1% in near term
items.quote: We would -- we want to grow at the rate at which we grew this year, which is about 12% on assets -- 12%, 13%, so either 12% or early teens on the asset side, and deposit side of a similar number

items.statement: CV/CE business target of INR 1,000-1,100 crores by end of FY25
items.quote: On the CV CE side, I think the thought process is that if we are able to get to about INR1,000 crores to INR1,100 crores of business by the end of the year, then I think we will be happy.

items.statement: New products (affordable housing, LAP, CV/CE) each targeting at least INR 1,000 crores, mortgage LAP aiming for a couple of thousand crores in FY25
items.value: INR 1,000+ crores each; LAP couple thousand crores
items.quote: Our aim -- ambition is to get at least INR1,000 crores in each one of these product categories if not more. So mortgage LAP, for instance, we want to do a couple of thousand crores during the year.

items.statement: Plan to launch 6-7 fully automated lending products by end of FY25 after first MSME product went live in Q4 FY24
items.quote: We have an agenda of installing 6 or 7 similar products before the year is out, which, in turn, will change the way we do business

items.statement: Q4 FY24 NIM at 3.38%, full year 3.31% (highest in 18 years); medium-term target 3.5% via balance sheet restructuring toward higher-yield assets
items.quote: We've hit about 3.38% NIM this quarter. In the medium term, we want to get to about 3.5%, so we are doing everything in our power to increase NIMs.

items.statement: Corporate yields improved via aggressive repricing on NBFC exposures post risk-weight changes and better pricing discipline
items.quote: We did go back and try and renegotiate wherever it is possible so that we got an incremental yield to cover for the incremental risk weights that RBI had prescribed for us.

items.statement: Retail disbursement momentum: home loans +26% QoQ, auto loans +23% QoQ; gold loans +12% YoY; personal loans ~INR 2,282 crores
items.quote: Home loan and auto loans, areas where we are trying to increase our focus, was able to grow 26% quarter-on-quarter for HL disbursals and 23% quarter-on-quarter for auto loan disbursals.

items.statement: Corporate book ~INR 32,000 crores (+INR 8,000 crores YoY); retail transformation underway with new MSME structure, sales value addition metric targeting 50% branch cost recovery
items.quote: Our corporate business continued to grow robustly, coming in at about INR32,000 crores at the end of this quarter. The total growth on the corporate side is approximately -- on a year-on-year basis, is approximately INR8,000 crores

items.statement: Credit card issuance halted per RBI direction; working on remediation, targeting restart next quarter subject to RBI approval
items.quote: Our current wishlist, and I'm not saying that it will happen in that form, but our current wishlist is that we should be in a position to have crossed all the T's and dotted all the I's and restart next quarter subject to RBI approval.

items.statement: PCR (RBI measure) at 79.1%, expected to improve 300-400 bps over next year; no aggressive technical write-offs planned given secured assets and ~70% PCR
items.quote: over the next year or so, we expect another 300, 400 basis points improvement on this number. At some point in time, we will need to take a management call on whether we need to aggressively do technica l write-offs

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio high vs peers; ~2/3 expenses uncontrollable; targeting ~1,000 bps reduction over multiple years via revenue growth and tight expense control
items.quote: Our ambition, we had actually disclosed in the last quarter. We said that we want to take off about 1,000 basis points from our revenue expense ratio.

items.statement: Rights issue completed in Q4 FY24; CAR 19.91%, Tier 1 17.65%; dividend ~INR 78 crores (30% payout)
items.quote: The bank successfully completed its rights issue during Q4 FY'24, taking the capital adequacy ratio of the bank to 19.91% and Tier 1 capital to 17.65%.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio INR 15,513 crores, avg LTV 74.92% (incl. buyout) / 70.73% (own); LTV trend expected to decline as own sourcing grows
items.quote: Including buyout, it's at 74.92%, so about 75%. And excluding buyout, which is basically our own portfolio, is at 70.73%. So the long-term trends are that it will continue to drop

items.statement: Co-lending partnerships actively being explored with multiple counterparties to accelerate retail growth
items.quote: We are in discussions with multiple counterparties as well as entities that can enable us to connect with multiple participants. So this is something that we are actively exploring.

items.statement: Branch sales value addition metric live since Jan 2024; 202 branches met 50% cost recovery target in Q4 vs ~100 expected; current account originations 4x, avg balances +70%
items.quote: When we built this metric, our expectation was roughly about 100 branches will meet it because that was the historical trend line. But last quarter, approxim ately 202 did meet it

items.statement: Board approved investment of up to USD 1 million to form an entity in Dubai DIFC for wealth management
items.quote: the Board has approved an investment of up to USD1 million to form an entity in Dubai.

items.statement: Brokerage income reduced to 45% of total revenue from 58% in FY20; distribution income crossed Rs 150 crores
items.quote: The brokerage income is 45% of the total revenue compared to 58% in FY20. Another highlight was the distribution income crosse d Rs. 150 crores, stands at Rs. 152 crores now

items.statement: Mutual fund equity AUM grew 46% in FY24, in line with industry growth of 48%
items.quote: The industry equity AUM grew 48% FY24 over FY23, we have grown 46%.

items.statement: Mutual fund distribution yield is 0.8%; PMS yield estimated at 2.2-2.4% including performance fees
items.quote: Yield on m utual fund is 0.8 and on PMS, it varies around we estimated around 2.2 – 2.4 percentage

items.statement: PMS AUM grew from Rs 450 crores to Rs 914 crores in FY24; aggressive focus to continue in FY25
items.quote: We have grown from Rs. 450 crores in FY23 to Rs. 914 crores and we have invested hugely in that business in terms of manpower cost.

items.statement: Insurance premium collected Rs 100 crores in FY24 vs Rs 76 crores in FY23; expects FY25 to be good without giving estimates
items.quote: For ‘23- 24, we have totally collected Rs. 100 crores of premium, which is compared to Rs. 76 crores for the previous financial year which includes, of course , Rs. 4 crores of general and health insurance. There is still lot of growth left in this business and we are hoping that ‘25 also should be good for

items.statement: Majority of group cash (Rs 750 crores) deployed in margin trading book and working capital; limited free cash for acquisitions
items.quote: On the group basis, the cash available is Rs. 750 crores. But as MD said, the majority of that is used for MTF books, lending, MT F and another major portion is used for the working capital requirements on a regular basis

items.statement: Software income declined 16% in FY24; no aggressive business plan but will consider growth over next 1-1.5 years
items.quote: At the moment we do not have an aggressive business plan on the software business, but over a period of next 1 year to 18 months, we will think about growing that business.

items.statement: Interest income increased to around Rs 110 crores in FY24
items.quote: But having said this, our interest income has gone up to around Rs. 110 crore last year.

items.statement: Inorganic acquisitions will be explored if opportunities align with culture and compliance standards
items.quote: Inorganic acquisition is an opportunity we will explore as and when we see opportunities that are aligning with our culture as well as the, you know, particularly on the compliance culture, etc.

items.statement: Targets 30% top-line growth in FY25 including Warner deal
items.quote: As committed earlier, this year for FY25 I feel 30% growth on top line is possible -- as you see in FY24 bottom line as compared to last year was up by 66%. But still we feel on 66% we will do another 30% this year i.e. in FY 25 as well.

items.statement: Targets 30% PAT growth in FY25 on FY24 base of INR127.2 cr
items.quote: FY 25 see now you can calculate whatever our entire year's bottom line you calculate 30% growth on that. Our target is to achieve that. So we will try and achieve that.

items.statement: Content investment budget of INR75-80 cr for FY25
items.quote: Yes, we have a budget of INR75 crores-INR80 crores. We have thought about it. Yes.

items.statement: Plans to acquire 8-10 films across languages (~50 songs) plus independent music in FY25
items.quote: I think our target is to at least acquire Hindi, Tamil, all languages put together, around eight to 10 films, yes. And average should be five songs per movie, so 50 songs we should get from film side. That's the idea.

items.statement: Will release ~150 songs in FY25 vs 733 in FY24, focusing on quality over quantity
items.quote: Maybe our target is, maybe we will reduce further, and maybe this year we will do only between 150, approximately 150 songs. So we are not going to reduce amount, but we are improving our quality and going for bigger numbers, bigger artists and bigger those things.

items.statement: Content cost target 25-30% of revenue; will invest up to 30% if quality content available
items.quote: Actually, still, if we get a good content, then we will do 30% also. We will go for 30%. 25%-30% is our target. We will invest that much money.

items.statement: Warner deal: fixed MG for 4 years with 85:15 overflow split; first-year advance higher
items.quote: MG is constant. MG is constant. It is fixed. We have taken it from them according to the projection of 4 years. And if we surpass that MG there will be an immediate kick-in of overflow.

items.statement: Paid streaming growing but will take 2-3 more years for meaningful numbers; Spotify targets 60-70% paid conversion in 5 years
items.quote: I think that's a good thing for the industry, but as mentioned earlier it will still take 2 years, 3 years more to have very good numbers to see.

items.statement: Client concentration risk with Warner mitigated by content ownership and upfront MG; Warner negotiation power stronger
items.quote: No, there won't be any revenue loss. I think Warner being an international big player, their negotiation power is better than us. It is not less than us. So, you can rest assured that we took this decision very carefully.

items.statement: Group company Tips Films to supply 30-35% of content acquisition budget in FY25
items.quote: I think maximum it can be 30%-35% from our own company. We acquire content. I think it will be that much. And that is the target we have kept for this year.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 75% digital streaming, 25% non-streaming; YouTube ~45-50% of total revenue
items.quote: That is same, 75%-25%. So 75% is digital and 25% is online.

items.statement: Content cost written off fully in quarter of release; expects investment recovery in 4-5 years
items.quote: We don't carry forward anything. We just write off everything in the quarter we release our content. So, we don't have any liability. So that way, we feel safe. It's our kind of business.

items.statement: Non-current liability >INR70 cr from Warner MG advance; current liability INR64 cr
items.quote: Yes. I think it will be more than INR70 crores.

items.statement: Short-term investments INR91 cr in liquid and short-term debt mutual funds
items.quote: Yes. So, primarily it's into mutual funds, debt mutual funds. And towards, let's say, it's liquid and short-term funds.

items.statement: Employee cost to rise nominally for new hires in brands/sync team; hiring nearly complete
items.quote: Little bit will be here and there, very nominal. It won't affect much. But it will go up because we need a few expensive people. And with these new businesses, we are getting more aggressive in that.

items.statement: Management aims for industry-leading revenue growth in FY25 but will not provide specific guidance due to market volatility
items.quote: We will, of course, aim to deliver industry-leading growth. Now what that number is, we can't guide. It is very, very hard to guide.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to stay in a narrow band for next 24-36 months while investing 1-1.5% of revenue in capabilities
items.quote: For the next 24 to 36 months we will be in an investment mode and we would love to keep the margin in a ramp narrow band. And if you realize that when we invest we will invest upwards of 1% or 1.5% of revenue in our business.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin at 16.3%, up 31 bps QoQ, exceeding the 16% exit target set at start of FY24
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for quarter 4 stands at 16.3%, which is a 31 basis points growth quarter-over-quarter. You may recall at the start of the financial year, we have indicated that we would like to exit the year with 1 6% EBITDA margin, and I'm happy to note that we've been able to deliver above that number

items.statement: Pipeline at all-time high of $1.8 billion, targeting $2.4-2.5 billion; TCV signings flat YoY at $240M in Q4 with 45% from new deals
items.quote: Our pipeline is currently growing. The one thing however I will tell you Shradha is the decision-making is getting pushed out because the discretionary spends are getting pushed out. So I can't really comment in terms of what that growth number will be.

items.statement: Pipeline at $1.8 billion, target to improve to $2.4-2.5 billion over next 6-8 months with focus on order booking
items.quote: We've got about $1.8 billion worth of pipeline and we want to improve it to about $2.4 billion to $2.5 billion. We are working on it. Are we there yet? We are not. But yes, a lot of effort over the next 6 to 8 months will be on order booking.

items.statement: Demand environment remains challenging with slower client decision-making and discretionary spend push-outs; no material change from past 4-5 quarters
items.quote: The past few quarters the demand environment has been quite challenging and marked with a lot of uncertainty. And the situation going forward is not going to change. We see the situation in the market nothing different from what we saw in the past 4 or 5 quarters.

items.statement: Will continue investing in capabilities for long-term growth including Gen AI platform Cogito, ROW expansion, and Optimus efficiency program
items.quote: we will continue to make investments that are required to create and scale up our capabi lities for long -term growth, we will also be driving multiple initiatives across the company to increase our operational

items.statement: Two whistleblower complaints received, both behavioral in nature with no financial impropriety found so far; investigations ongoing

So if you load up the tax, we probably will be around 2.3 to 2.5 range. And then ROA is in the 19 % to 21% range.

First is the headline itself, which says that my Net NPA is INR130 crores, more than half of that - 55% is in the form of secured loans. And the linked second point I wanted to make there is that, these have an LTV of about 51% -- 52%.

items.statement: Net credit cost declining: 3.36% to 2.1% to 1.96% (Mar'24); includes accelerated provisions and recoveries
items.quote: The next slide is on credit cost. Again, the highlight I just wanted to make here was in terms of the reducing trends of credit cost. Net credit cost, 3.36% down to 2.1%, down to 1.96% in March 24.

items.statement: 17 new branches and 39 relocations added; measured branch expansion to balance cost; digital/robotics investment ongoing (120 robotic processes)
items.quote: So if you see the line here, 17 new branches and 39 relocations. Relocations are much cheaper. New branches are more expensive. Right? And I think so it's a conscious effort, saying listen, if we don't need, let's not spend the money, but if we need, we won't stop.

items.quote: Not mentioned as a milestone, but we have said it to a few press interviews that we will prepare this year for applying for a universal bank, which the RBI has come with a clear guideline on. items.quote: So Tier 2 capital for us is only 1.3% of our capital adequacy. So we have room to take more capital, but as of now, it is not required. We are adequately capitalized. items.statement: Cost of deposits increased due to marketing spend for quality deposits; cost income ratio slightly up but expected to decline to 52-53%
items.quote: We had to spend some dollars on marketing and get the good quality deposits, which we did over the last year. So that's the reason there is a slight increase in cost income ratio.

items.statement: Punjab/Haryana microfinance collections 99.5% in B0 bucket for March; no geography-specific stress observed
items.quote: So first is the favourite question is Punjab, Haryana. We don't have a Punjab, Haryana problem. Our collection in Punjab, Haryana on record for March for the B0 bucket was 99.5%.

items.statement: Opex growth expected at 8-10% annually, not 25% as in FY24
items.quote: So you don't expect a similar 25% growth in terms of opex the next year as well, because this has already been considered. So there's no every year growth of 25%. So more likely around 8% to 10% opex growth is expected, so not more than that.

items.statement: Cost-income ratio target 52-53% over three years from current 58%
items.quote: Over a period of time, like I said, 58% cost income, we're more closer to the 52 to 53 range. And we're talking about three -year timeframe.

items.statement: PAT growth guidance of 30-40% for next three years
items.quote: Gautam Jain: Okay. So, impact growth for next three years, 30% to 40%? Ajay Kanwal: Which is why I mentioned earlier, I didn't put a guidance here. I left guidance as a word.

items.statement: ROE guidance 19-21% without DTA benefit; DTA of INR800 cr to be absorbed by FY27
items.quote: Without taking into account the impending DTA benefit of INR800 crores plus, this is from Rajkumar. Rajkumar, so my CFO is challenging all of us. He's saying that the guidance we have given is without the DTA impact, so we have to work harder.

items.statement: NIM may drop 30-50 bps as secured mix rises to 60-80%, offset by CASA improvement
items.quote: So, in three years, the NIM drops by 50 basis points if I turn 60 to 80 basis points, 80% secured. But at the same time, if CASA goes from 20 to 30, then the NIM drop is only 30 basis points because the cost of funds will come down.

items.statement: Gold loan book to grow significantly; 350 branches doing gold, targeting INR1000-1500 cr
items.quote: If you did about INR3 crores to INR5 crores average per branch, INR1000 to INR1500 crores book he has to do.

items.statement: Secured book target 60-80% in three years from current level
items.quote: I should grow my secured business proportion each year. To me, that is more important than the 20% growth. If I have to grow 18%, I have to grow secured higher.

items.statement: Used two-wheeler and used car loans prioritized over new car loans
items.quote: Our bias is used two wheeler used car and then cars in that order, but we are also a bit conservative.

items.statement: Top risks: technology/cyber security, operational risk/fraud, monitored via monthly 40-50 page product decks
items.quote: Now specifically, we do what is the top five risk. So I think one is always technology. We haven't changed. We haven't had a problem. But it's never been out of my top five risk because that is one thing I can't predict.

items.statement: Branch relocation strategy: move underperforming urban branches to higher-potential areas; incremental rent cost ~INR1 lakh
items.quote: What happens is you're spending say INR50,000 in the rent. You move to a different you spend 1.5 lakh. So incremental cost is a lakh, but then all the network, etc. all the hardware gets used up.

items.statement: Universal bank application likely May-June next year after audited results
items.quote: So, like I said, we can only apply after next year's audited results. So more likely the May-June timeframe of next year, we'll apply for universal.

items.statement: Refinance from NHB/NABARD/SIDBI ~INR5,000 cr keeps CD ratio at 86% vs 102-103% reported
items.quote: National Housing Bank has given us refinance. They have given us 10 year loan at a price which is lower than a deposit price of a one year deposit. We tend to borrow from three refinance agencies, which is NABARD, SIDBI and NHB. And roughly that's about INR5,000 crores of my book.

items.statement: SR collections: oldest vintage 60% recovered/normalized in two years; LTV ~51-52%
items.quote: The oldest SR, in two years, we've collected about 60%. Collected or normalized. So we believe that that's the kind of collection trends that we are getting. Plus, most of the SRs are secured where my LTV is pretty much in line with the LTV on my NPA book, around 51%, 52%.

items.quote: As regards to 2G ethanol, we are looking into various options to make the project more viable. items.quote: You would have seen if you have been following the company that earlier on we had a lot of capex and loans which were there, and we were not in a position to pay dividends. items.statement: Margin outlook stable with no major change from current levels; willing to take short-term hit for RTM 2.0 and brand investments
items.quote: So I would say not a major change from what we've seen. Upside, I would not expect upsides on this, but not a major change from where we are today.

items.statement: Adjacencies gross margins slightly better than biscuits; net margins not better
items.quote: Average would be maybe slightly better, the gross margins. The net margins will not be, but the gross margins will be slightly better.

items.statement: Private consumption currently down but expected to improve through the year; GDP growth driven by gross fixed capital formation
items.quote: However, the only point to be made is that private consumption is down. The GDP numbers are looking good because of the gross fixed capital formation that's happening in the country. However, we are confident that as we go through this year, things will change on the private consumption side as well.

items.quote: also commercialized our cheese factory in Ranjangaon, and we've started to now make the products and supply to the market as well. Are they in the market yet? Vipin Kataria: Just moving into the trade

items.quote: see while the crop seems to be fine as far as wheat is concerned, the government holding has been reasonably low. So there is going to be a government buying because of their programs. So I would think that the wheat outlook is slightly inflationary during the year, while until the elections, things will not move. But beyond the elections, I think it will be slightly inflationary. Similarly, sugar

items.statement: Volume growth 2x revenue growth in Q4; volume and revenue growth nearly at par for full year FY24
items.quote: So the situation on volume and revenue for the last year has been, they are almost at par, right? So volume and revenue are the same. However, if you look at it by quarter, it's a very different story. So the last quarter, the volume growth is 2x the revenue growth, right?

items.statement: Direct distribution expanded from 26.8 lakh to 27.9 lakh outlets; rural distributors increased from 28,000 to 30,000
items.quote: We've expanded direct distribution from March '23, we were at 26.8 lakh outlets. In March '24, we are at 27.9 lakh outlets. We've strengthened our rural distribution by going from 28,000 rural distributors to 30,000 rural distributors.

items.statement: Service levels in modern trade and e-commerce up 15% to north of 90%; some accounts exceed 93%
items.quote: So our service levels have gone up by 15%. We are at north of 90%, which is best-in-class, both in modern trade as well as e-commerce. In some of the accounts, we are at service level, which is in excess of 93%.

items.statement: International business performed well led by GCC and Americas; Nepal business consistent and seen as replicable model
items.quote: The international business has performed well this quarter as well as this year, and this is led by the GCC as well as Americas. Nepal has been a very consistent performance, albeit at a very small base. But the fact is that this is an experiment, which we feel very proud of.

items.statement: Raised Rs 1,332 crore via CCDs (Rs 275 crore) and warrants (Rs 1,057 crore) to fund growth for current year and next two years.
items.quote: This total capital raise of 1,332 crores, of which is 275 crores in form of CCD and 1,057 crores in form of warrant fulfils our capital need for the year, and also for the next 2 years.

items.statement: AUM growth of minimum Rs 3,000 crore per year; targeting 30-35% AUM growth with focus on higher-yielding segments.
items.quote: First and foremost, we were at Rs 3,000+ in AUM in FY22, at Rs 6,000+ in FY23, and at a Rs 9,000+ in FY24, which means this company sees minimum of Rs 3,000 crore of AUM growth.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target of 40-45% over 6-8 quarters from current 54%.
items.quote: Cost to income ratio, as of now is closer to 54%, we'd like to take it to 45% which may be over 6 to 8 quarters from now, and ultimately we'll reach the desired ROA of 4%, which we believe may take around 8 quarters time.

items.statement: Micro-enterprise vertical expanding from 75 to 250 branches by year-end; micro loans at ~20% yield to drive yield expansion.
items.quote: We are going to increase that branch count to 150 now, and by end of the year it should be 250, and most of this portfolio of Rs 8 lakhs secured loans happens at around 20% yield.

items.statement: Intermediated channel share to reduce from ~50% to 40-35% over 8 quarters; direct channels (micro, machinery, retailer, digital) to increase.
items.quote: We see this going towards 40% or sub 40% in next 8 quarters.

items.statement: MyShubhLife acquisition expected to add Rs 1,500 crore AUM and Rs 100 crore incremental PAT over 3 years.
items.quote: This acquisition over the next 3 years potentially helps us acquire retailers as customers, and probably 1,500 cr in AUM at the end of 3rd year implementation, and roughly around 100 crore of incremental PAT.

items.statement: Rate reset on secured portfolio done on 25th January; full impact reflecting from March quarter.
items.quote: The reset was done on 25 th January. Since then, the entire book has been, almost the entire secured book has been reset so the numbers would continue to reflect the way they are in March.

items.statement: Expecting 50 bps cost of borrowing reduction from scale/vintage and 25-30 bps from rate cycle over 8-10 quarters.
items.quote: We are expecting that because of the increase in vintage and in scale and because of a very sizable capital raise nearly equal to our existing networth, a 50-basis point rate reduction would happen over 8 quarters, and hopefully, some bit of rate cycle change would give us additional 25 to 30 basis points decrease.

items.statement: Credit cost guided at 1.8-2% for FY25; Q4 blip due to one-off Rs 10 crore write-off on old unsecured loan.
items.quote: As per our plan and as per the way we have calibrated, we would be between for the next year we should be between 1.8% to 2% overall.

items.statement: On-book GNPA higher due to FLDG on co-origination; comfortable with on-book GNPA up to 5%.
items.quote: We are quite comfortable, and lot of our banks' covenants are basis that comfort, and we are quite comfortable to go up to 5%.

items.statement: No fresh capex needed; existing digital, physical infrastructure (105 branches to 400 in 2 years) and tech stack can support accelerated growth.
items.quote: Our existing physical infrastructure and digital infrastructure is sweating more multi products, our AUM is growing and our costs is not growing in proportion to AUM and that's the operating leverage of 50 basis point we are presuming.

items.statement: PAT growth to be significantly higher than AUM growth for next 3 years to achieve 4% ROA target.
items.quote: It's of course it is likely that our PAT growth will be higher than the AUM growth. Otherwise, this target of reaching 4% ROA cannot happen.

items.statement: Foreclosures higher than expected in Q4; quarterly AUM growth 8% vs 15% target; will correct with higher growth in high-yield segments.
items.quote: The foreclosure for us was a negative surprise, and higher than what we expected. Obviously, we'll correct that, and we will match that at higher growth rate. Quarterly growth coming at 8% rather than 15% was a function of that.

items.statement: Leverage capped at 4.5x for next 2-3 years; CRISIL upgraded rating to A/Stable in March; further upgrade expected post capital raise.
items.quote: Yeah, for next 2 to 3 years, we have not built ever more than 4 and a half times multiple leverage.

items.statement: Flares revenue expected to grow 2.5x to 3x FY24 level
items.quote: It should be anywhere in the ratio of 2.5x to 3x of what it was this year.

items.statement: Flares margin expected similar to prior expectation with slight dip due to cost overruns
items.quote: Very similar margin to what you had expected earlier. I'd say a slight dip because there are a few small cost overruns and stuff that they need to be looked at.

items.statement: Equipment margins target double-digit, can get close next year
items.quote: It will be a bit of a push, but we can get close to it. We can get close.

items.statement: Capex this year similar to last year at ~70% of prior plan, continuing for 18 months
items.quote: We have a little bit of capex, not a little bit we have. I would say 70% of the capex plan we did last year, we will have this year as well.

items.statement: Consumables volume growth ~10-12% in FY24, in line with market
items.quote: We've been seeing it in the region of 10%, 11%, 12% on the consumers front.
