items.quote: Exhibition we received very positive response and very robust demand was seen there and that is one of the reasons after visiting there, we had lot of request for collaboration and developing the product in, we went for this world differential in Saudi Arabia.

items.statement: New products to be announced in weeks/months; will enhance existing anti-drone and simulator lines or target adjacent markets
items.quote: We are going to announce in the next, few months, weeks and months some new product, very interesting range of products and that should the end users not only in India, but worldwide will find them very interesting.

items.statement: Working capital cycle sustainable at 140-160 days; Q4 FY24 at 148 days due to higher sales and inventory build for FY25 execution
items.quote: That we would say this is sustainable going forward also our working capital cycle will be in the range of 140 to 160 days, this is number one.

items.statement: Order book entirely from government (Indian or foreign); virtually no private orders
items.quote: It is completely from the government, either Indian government or foreign government. Almost everything is from the government, so no private orders in this, almost no private orders in this.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth expected at 20-25% and FY26 at 10-15% on current capacities
items.quote: for the FY25 also we can expect a similar revenue growth of approx. 20% to 25% and similarly for FY26, I think with the current capacities we can see a further 10% to 15 % increased

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin target maintained at 20-25% range
items.quote: for the current year, again on margin target of EBITDA margins, maintaining in the range of 20% to 25%, that's what we are looking at.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margins expected similar to FY25 at 20-25%
items.quote: I think similar EBITDA margins because honestly speaking, these margins look quite attractive and are pretty good and we are concentrating on volume growth by and revenue growth by maintaining similar margins.

items.statement: Vada expansion from 250,000 to 500,000 CBM per annum underway, 50,000 CBM started, remaining 200,000 CBM in 1.5-2 months
items.quote: Out of the 250,000-capacity expansion at Vada, 50,000 has already started and another 200,000 should start in the next 1 ½, two months at maximum.

items.statement: JV plant at Ramosadi commenced production March 30, 2024 with 250,000 CBM per annum capacity for AAC blocks and panels
items.quote: our JV Siam Cement - Big block construction Technologies Private Limited, which has its plant located at Ramosadi, Gujarat has commenced production of A AC blocks and ALC panels with a capacity of 250,000 cubic meters per annum since March 30th, 2024.

items.statement: Finalizing land for Greenfield plants near Chennai/Bangalore and in Northern/Central India, targeting closure in current financial year
items.quote: for southern India near Bangalore or Chennai, we are almost in the finalization phase of line and I think hopefully we should be able to close that in the next two to three months more or less. And, similarly we are also looking at opportunities in Northern as well as Central India for our upcoming expansions.

items.statement: Added new clients including Birla Estates, Afcons Infrastructure, Nyati Group, Symbiosis, JSW Steel, Reliance Life Sciences, Puravankara Group and others
items.quote: we have been concentrating on increasing our customer base and have added new clients like Birla Estates, Afcons Infrastructure, Nyati Group, Symbiosis, Educational institution , Vilas Saudagar, JSW Steel, Reliance Life Sciences, R.K Developers. Alembic Limited, Dorsi G roup, Sethia Infrastructure, Puravankara Group, N ew Consolidated Construction, WellSpan Group and many others

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 18.53% impacted by new market penetration costs and JV panel marketing expenses with no revenue yet
items.quote: the margins have been a little bit affected because as I mentioned that we have presented lots of different newer markets and plus in the last quarter we have also done a lot of marketing and, etc., activities of the JV Company for which we have just started production

items.statement: Realizations in new markets 3-5% lower than established markets, expected to reach parity over time
items.quote: the realizations are a little bit on the lower to a certain extent, but that is sort of 3% to 5%, which could be because of product introduction and market penetration.

items.statement: ALC blocks priced at Rs 3,800-4,000 per CBM vs red bricks at Rs 4,500-5,000 per CBM, pricing down 2-5% last year due to raw material cost declines
items.quote: I think currently red bricks are almost in the similar price range of almost Rs. 4500 to Rs. 5000 of cubic meters and ALC blocks are in the range of almost Rs. 3800 to Rs. 4000 cubic meters.

items.statement: Real estate demand remains strong, only temporary labor issues due to elections
items.quote: the demand frankly is looking fantastic, but yes, definitely this quarter I think major reason due to elections is there are definitely some labor issues at lot of construction site.

items.statement: Panel revenue contribution expected from Q3 FY25, initial margins 20-25% EBITDA with potential improvement after 6-12 months
items.quote: So, for panels, I think the panels will start contributing from Q3.

items.statement: Debt-equity rose to 1.3x from 0.5x due to consolidated JV debt and capex cycle, expected to return to 1:1 as new capacity generates revenue
items.quote: debt equity has gone up from almost 0.5 to 1.3 , but that is mainly because this is again on a consolidated level whereas the debt is completely on the books of the balance sheet, whereas 48% of the debt is belonging to the SCG Group also who is the venture partner in the JV project.

items.statement: Installed 450 kW solar at Umargam, installing 625 kW at Arvada, targeting rooftop solar at all factories in current year
items.quote: we have just completed a solar installation of 450 kilowatt at our Umargam plant in the year under review and are in the process of installing a solar plant of 625 kilowatts at Arvad a unit.

items.statement: FY25 capacity utilization target 75%+ on 1.3 million CBM installed capacity, FY26 target 80%+
items.quote: our installed capacity for FY25 will be approximately at around 1.3 million cubic meters, which will be completed in the next 2.5 to 3 months approximately. And I think similar utilization levels of almost 75% plus for this year can be targeted.

items.statement: Battery materials revenue target Rs 250-300 crore in FY26 with full utilization; FY25 revenue expected Rs 200-250 crore, Rs 100 crore+ likely
items.quote: So in FY26, we will have a minimum Rs. 250 crore to Rs. 300 crore revenue. On top of that, the capacity which is coming online during the year and coming in FY26, will also contribute.

items.statement: Neogen Chemicals standalone revenue target Rs 1,000 crore+ by FY26
items.quote: We are basically aiming for that to achieve by the end of at least the next financial year so that we are on track to get a Rs. 1,000 crore plus kind of revenue from Neogen Chemicals in FY26 as we have targetted earlier.

items.statement: Total CAPEX Rs 1,500 crore across sites; Rs 1,150 crore debt tied up via project finance; Rs 400-500 crore in FY25, balance in FY26
items.quote: The CAPEX of the total upcoming capacities at all sites is around Rs. 1,500 crore, and I am glad to inform you that we have already tied up majority of funds through existing bankers to fund this through project finance route.

items.statement: Pakhajan greenfield battery materials plant construction starting soon; inauguration targeted second half FY26 using MUIS technology
items.quote: Construction including related utilities is expected to start soon, keeping us on schedule to inaugurate this facility by second half of FY2026.

items.statement: Electrolyte salt trial shipments started; customer approvals expected end of Q2 FY25; 400 MT plant fully utilized by Q3-Q4 FY25
items.quote: And with that, we should start seeing permissions come by the end of Q2. Again, some customers will be a little bit higher, some will be lower. So, by the end of Q3 and Q4, we expect that this 400 metric tons will be used fully.

items.statement: India electrolyte demand estimated 160 GWh (120 GWh EV, 30-40 GWh storage); non-China lithium salt demand strong globally; only 2-3 active non-China manufacturers
items.quote: For the 160 gigawatt hour guidance we had given for India's electrolyte demand, roughly around 120 gigawatt of that was estimated to be EV and another 30 gigawatt to 40 gigawatt was likely to be the solar and wind energy storage.

items.statement: Board approved up to Rs 500 crore CCD infusion into Neogen Ionics over 3 years; Rs 220 crore already invested to be converted; 12-year term loans with 2-year interest moratorium secured
items.quote: The CCD was a way for us to basically put up equity or, quasi equity into the Ionics. Again, this is an enabling resolution up to Rs. 500 crore. We will be doing it gradually over 3 years of time.

items.statement: BuLi Chemicals amalgamation filing planned; synergies from common pharma/agro customers, internal organolithium use, by-product recycling, lower admin costs
items.quote: Based on the recommendation of our Board, we will file for amalgamation of BuLi Chemicals with Neogen Chemicals as now most of the customers have registered transfer from Livent to Neogen's ownership.

items.statement: Management expects to deliver EBITDA and net margins in FY25 similar to FY22 and FY23 levels, in line with volume growth.
items.quote: I can certainly confirm that we are on track to deliver the kind of EBITDA and the kind of net margins which we had shown in FY‘22 and FY‘23, which should happen in FY‘25, in line with the volume

items.statement: Branded edible oil volume growth expected at 9-10% in FY25, with overall edible oil volume around 2.7 million tons.
items.quote: Now, next year, we hope to have at least a double-digit figure somewhere in the range of 9-10%. If that happens, that should be good because our volumes are quite large. We did around 2.7 million ton in packed oil.

items.statement: Food and FMCG volume share targeted to reach 30% of total volume next year, up from 17% currently.
items.quote: Today, it is at 17% of volume. Two years back, it was 12-13%. And next year maybe, we are hopeful that it should touch 30% of our volume.

items.statement: Food segment EBITDA margin expected to exceed edible oil margins (3.5-4%) within two years as volumes cross 1.5 million tons.
items.quote: Edible oil margins can be ranged between 3.5% to 4%, but food can give double than this, and therefore we are moving on this trajectory. And I think we have no reasons to believe that in next two years of time, by the time when we will cross the volume of more than 1.5 million tons in food, we should have that pricing power in hand, which can give us a better margin than the edible oil.

items.statement: IPO-funded Gohana rice milling unit expected ready by November for the Basmati season.
items.quote: Second is that our Gohana unit, which is from the IPO investment we did, will be ready. Hopefully, the rice part should be ready by November as the season starts.

items.statement: Two 600-ton-per-day mustard crushing plants commissioned (one ready, one nearing completion) adding ~35% Kachi Ghani capacity.
items.quote: This year amongst the IPO project, one 600 ton crushing per day has been commissioned. So, that is now ready for operation in this season. In Gohana, we are coming up with another 600 ton plant, which will be ready by, say, another one month or so, and at least we can do crushing there. So, 1,200 ton of crushing should give you an additional around 35% of Kachi Ghani.

items.statement: Branded exports grew 72% in FY24 to nearly INR 200 crore across 30+ countries.
items.quote: On a branded export, which is again a focus area, we have more than doubled the sales which are growing by 72% and now close to 200 crore of turnover contributed by this channel, 30 plus countries, where we are exporting all the products on the brand name Fortune.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA run rate of ~INR 900 crore per half-year achieved in H2 FY24.
items.quote: EBITDA in H2 24 is close to INR 863 crores, so that run rate of INR 900 crores EBITDA in half is somewhere we are close to that, as compared to INR 962 crores of EBITDA in H2 of last year.

items.statement: Edible oil standard run rate gross profit INR 11,500-12,000 per ton and EBITDA ~INR 3,500 per ton.
items.quote: See, on edible oil, so for us the standard run rate for gross profit is anywhere between 11,500 to 12,000 per ton and the EBITDA margins of close to 3,500 metric tons per ton.

items.statement: Food segment delivered EBITDA of INR 170 crore on ~INR 5,000 crore turnover (3.5% margin) in FY24.
items.quote: For the Financial Year 24, food contributed an EBITDA of 170 crore on a turnover of 5,000 crores close to 3.5% of EBITDA, which is quite encouraging for us.

items.statement: Mustard oil provides stable margins; higher domestic production lowers input costs and improves brand margins.
items.quote: Higher production is good. The markets remain stable and when it remains stable, the brands get a lot of strength because volatility in prices brings a lot of fluctuation in MRP. So, for us, the lower prices give us higher margins and we would always like higher production because that is better for the country as well as for the brand.

items.statement: Rural per capita edible oil consumption below national average (17.5 kg) in states like Bihar, UP, Odisha; rural focus to drive growth.
items.quote: We are banking in rural market because in rural, there are many states which still consume less than average India, whether it is Bihar, UP, Orissa, parts of Bengal, parts of Rajasthan, Parts of Madha Pradesh where we have seen that consumption, per capita consumption much lower. And we see a good opportunity to improve our sales there.

items.statement: Food and FMCG domestic volumes grew ~40% in FY24; branded portion exceeds 80% of food business.
items.quote: In FY‘24, the domestic volume grew in the range of 40%, and that is very encouraging for us because most of the branded products are getting sold in domestic market for us

items.statement: Alternate channel revenue reached INR 2,700+ crore in FY24, growing 29% YoY with e-commerce up 42%.
items.quote: In our case, this channel has contributed now for revenue close to 2,700 crore plus of revenue. In this whole alternate channel piece, e-commerce is growing faster than the modern trade. The overall growth of alternate channel is 29%, whereas the e-commerce has grown by 42%.

items.statement: Bangladesh JV issues (FX crunch, price controls) resolved; no profitability drag expected in FY25.
items.quote: both this problem as we stand today, as we speak today are more or less got resolved. Bangladesh went into elections in January with a now fresh government coming in place. Most of the macros have been improving in Bangladesh. Availability of Fx is now there. Prices have cooled down. Government has also allowed us some free hand on the pricing and the business is now giving a good numbers in Bangl

items.statement: Inventory risk mitigated via revised risk management policy and just-in-time operations; no high-cost inventory buildup expected.
items.quote: Unlike last year, we have learnt certain things, and we have done corrective measures. We have changed our, tweaked our risk management policy to ensure that we remain tight on inventory and we have ensured that we are just in time managing, and hence we will not be saddled with any great inventory.

items.statement: EBIT margin guidance of 12% to 13% maintained for next 12-24 months
items.quote: we've been saying consistently. I think both Ashok and I and all of us have been saying that 12% to 13% is a reasonable expectation to have for the EBIT margin. And annually, I would still say we are staying with that point of view.

items.statement: Jewellery EBIT margin dropped 140 bps for full year and 110 bps in Q4 due to competitive intensity and gold price impact
items.quote: this year, yes, in the current quarter, there has been, let's say, a gross margin, which is lower than what we would usually deliver in a studded quarter, studded intensive quarter.

items.statement: Jewellery margin improvement expected from Q2 FY25 onwards as gold price impact corrects
items.quote: I'm hoping that from quarter 2 onwards, we'll start seeing some improvement because some of these efforts require -- take time.

items.statement: Watches margin decline due to wearables pricing pressure and higher advertising spend
items.quote: we did prioritize growth, and we have got 19% growth in sales and for doing that, I think we've invested a lot more in advertising, which is more than 40% growth.

items.statement: Watches margin expected to improve in FY25 as operating leverage flows through
items.quote: for this financial year, we continue to push the pedal on Revenue growth, but also put a lot of focus and attention on managing costs much better, so that the overall benefit and the operating leverage actually flows through to the profit line.

items.statement: Competitive intensity in jewellery to continue; consumer sentiment soft due to elevated gold prices
items.quote: competitive intensity will continue, and we will continue to invest in growth and respond accordingly in the marketplace to ensure that we continue to gain market share.

items.statement: Jewellery discounting driven more by gold price volatility than demand weakness
items.quote: I would say greater emphasis on the gold price increase because we didn't see it all the time, not the entire quarter. It is -- it became particular only when gold prices were jumping up significantly.

items.statement: Studded ratio stable at 33% in Q4 despite gold price inflation
items.quote: studded ratio being constant in spite of sharp inflation in gold prices. Because in Q3, there was a 200 bps drop. This time, it is stable at 33%.

items.statement: High value studded grew to 14% contribution in Q4 from 13% last year; targeting aggressive growth
items.quote: high value studded the way we've defined it has done well for us. The price bands that we look at consistently over the last several years, we have continued to gain. And even in the quarter, it was a 14% contribution compared to 13% last year in the same quarter.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamonds not yet significant in India; monitoring U.S. market stress and early adopters
items.quote: so far, we have not seen any significant traction, though there is some traction at the margin, but it is very small. In the 3 years period, how it will emerge is very difficult to conclude.

items.statement: Tanishq added 46-47 stores in FY24; sees opportunity to expand beyond 300 towns
items.quote: we have added in the current year several stores, in fact, 46 or 47 new stores in Tanishq. And of course, Mia, we've added 67 and CaratLane also has continued to add quite a few 50-odd stores.

items.statement: International jewellery targeting ~30 stores across North America and GCC from current 16
items.quote: from the 16 stores, we are looking to get to something like around 30 stores across both North America as well as the GCC region.

items.statement: Gold exchange contributed 31% of non-Tanishq gold sales in FY24; total exchange ~40-41% of sales
items.quote: Last year, gold exchange, excluding the -- this is the non-Tanishq gold, was 30% contributor to sales. This year, it was -- in FY24, it was 31%. So there was a 1% improvement. And Tanishq exchange also does pretty well. So at an overall level, exchange gold accounts were about 40% - 41% of our total sales.

items.statement: Long-term debt of INR 3,000 crores for CaratLane acquisition to be repaid in 18 and 24 months
items.quote: We have a long-term debt of about INR 3,000 crores, which is squarely linked to our acquisition of CaratLane balance stake. And if you would have noticed that the term for that NCD, which we took is 18 months and 24 months.

items.statement: Zoya MRP turnover just under INR 300 crores in FY24, up from INR 60-65 crores 4 years ago
items.quote: Zoya, we have ended the year with an MRP turnover, not NSV, MRP turnover of just under INR 300 crores. 4 years ago, it was around INR 60-65 crores.

items.statement: Demand growth in India for FY25 expected to be better than FY24's 2.7%
items.quote: We definitely see that next year '24-25 the demand growth will better as compared to '23-24.

items.statement: Greenfield soda ash project capex ~Rs 4,000 cr over next 3 years; vacuum salt ~Rs 150-170 cr and bromine ~Rs 115-120 cr
items.quote: If you look at the investment into the bromine project which is very hardly around 115-120 crores kind of a thing and in vacuum salt is roughly around 150 to 170 crores. So, put together both, we are talking about 300. So, the major growth investment which is coming into the greenfield project which is around 4,000 crores and that also will be happening in next 3 years of time.

items.statement: Maintenance and smaller expansion capex ~Rs 250 cr per year for FY25 and FY26 excluding greenfield
items.quote: Next year also '25-26 other than the greenfield project completion of vacuum salt and bromine and some maintenance. This will be in the range of around 250 crores kind of a situation every year kind of a situation.

items.statement: India soda ash demand projected to grow from ~4.3 mt to ~7 mt in next 5-7 years
items.quote: If you take that into account, there is a kind of a projection which we have is the demand which is around 4.3 million tons which is likely to be around 7 million tons in next 5 to 7 years of time.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 23.9% vs 20.3% in Q3 FY24; improvement due to higher volume and lower input cost
items.quote: For the quarter, the EBITDA margin came at 23.9% compared to 32.5% in the corresponding quarter of last year and 20.3% in Q3 of the current year.

items.statement: Realizations in Q4 FY24 lower than Q3 FY24; EBITDA per ton slightly better due to cost control
items.quote: In terms of the realization yes, the realization was lower as compared to the last quarter, Q3 of '24, it was lower. And EBITDA was slightly better because of the better cost control.

items.statement: Global soda ash demand ex-China fell 3.2% in CY23; CY24 likely similar growth ~2.5%; no major capacity additions in CY25-26
items.quote: Calendar Year 2024 is likely to be dull year, but I believe it should not be worse than Calendar Year 2023 and growth will be similar of Calendar Year 2023 at about 2.5%.

items.statement: Sodium bicarbonate capacity expanded; expect significant utilization growth in FY25 and possible further expansion
items.quote: You will see in '24-25, the demand expansion happening into the sodium bicarbonate. And probably '24-25 we will have a significant amount of growth into our utilization of '24-25 and hopefully the full utilization and probably maybe we will be looking at a few more expansion into the sodium bicarbonate in next year probably.

items.statement: Bromine project ~2,800 tpa capacity, ~Rs 120 cr capex, IRR 18-20%, revenue ~Rs 60-63 cr
items.quote: The preparation was going on in this and just to kind of give you like I said, approximately the investment is around 120 crores, and we will be producing something around 2,800 tons and our IRR will be roughly around 18% to 20% kind of IRR will be there.

items.statement: Turkey imports into India temporary; will redirect to Europe when European demand recovers
items.quote: Turkey supply which you are getting into the Indian market is a temporary phenomenon. Because for them the natural market is the Europe market. The moment the Europe recovers all the volume or majority of the volume of Turkey will go to that market.

items.statement: Prices have bottomed out; near-term range-bound realizations; upside possible if opportunity arises
items.quote: I think prices of that trajectory has bottomed out. This would be in the range bound kind of a situation on this pricing. This is a way we look at this point of time.

items.statement: Greenfield project timeline ~3 years from now; final approvals in last leg; physical activity to start in few months
items.quote: I think the projection at this point of a time is likely to take around 3 years of time from now onwards to complete this kind of a massive project.

items.statement: Net cash surplus ~Rs 701 cr at FY24 end; gross debt Rs 197 cr, cash Rs 898 cr; peak debt/equity <0.5x for greenfield
items.quote: We are a net debt-free Company and our gross debt stood at 197 crores with cash and cash equivalent of Rs. 898 crores resulting in a net cash surplus of around 701 crores at the year end.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend Rs 12/share (120% of face value, 20% of net profit)
items.quote: Board has recommended a dividend of Rs. 12 per equity share of Rs. 10 each which is 120% of the paid capital and 20% of our net profit.

items.statement: Salt yield improvement benefits accruing gradually over 3-4 years; some benefit in FY24, more in FY25
items.quote: No, it started happening like last year also we got some improvement, this year we will get another improvement on that, and this will be journey like I said in the past also 3-4 years of time.

items.statement: Expects telecom equipment revenue of ~Rs 2,000 cr in FY25 vs Rs 150 cr in FY24
items.quote: We expect the revenue from this segment during FY 25 will reach to approximately Rs.2000 Crores from Rs.150 Crores of FY 24.

items.statement: Expects optical fiber cable revenue of >Rs 2,000 cr in FY25
items.quote: we expect a revenue again more than INR2,000 crores in the current financial year from optical fibe r cable business

items.statement: Expects turnkey project revenue of Rs 1,750-2,000 cr in FY25
items.quote: current year, we are looking at turnkey projects of about INR1,250 crores plus INR500 crores, about INR1,750 crores to INR2,000 crores

items.statement: Expects OFC demand recovery from Q2 FY25
items.quote: We are confident that OFC demand will be restored from Q2 FY 25 onwards in both India and key global markets.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 7,685 cr as of 31 Mar 2024
items.quote: Our order book now stands at INR 7685 crs as of 31st March 2024 as compared to INR 7010 crs last year.

items.statement: Incremental order book added in FY24 ~Rs 3,725 cr
items.quote: During FY24, the Company added an incremental order book of ~INR 3725 Crores comprising of products orders worth more than ~INR 1500 Crores and System Integration orders worth ~INR 2225 Crores.

items.statement: Has >Rs 1,700 cr orders in hand for telecom equipment
items.quote: Of the INR2,000 crores revenue I'm expecting, we have more than INR1,500 worth of order already in our hands, more than that, about INR1,700 crores.

items.statement: Has ~Rs 1,200 cr turnkey orders in hand
items.quote: On turnkey business, we already have orders worth of about INR1,200 crores in hand.

items.statement: Poland OFC plant investment up to Euro 15.9 mn (Rs 144 cr) for 3.25 mn fkm capacity
items.quote: HFCL has committed an initial investment of up to Euro 15.9 million (INR 144 crores) for its Poland optical fiber cable manufacturing plant with an initial capacity of 3.25 million fiber km

items.statement: Poland plant targets production start from April next financial year
items.quote: 3.25 million capacity, we are targeting to start manufacturing from April of next financial year.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin 15-17% in FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margin would be something like, I would say, 15% or so. 15% to 17% depending upon order to order and the situation.

items.statement: BharatNet Phase III tender ~Rs 60,000 cr capex over 3 years + Rs 40,000 cr O&M over 10 years
items.quote: One of the most anticipated opportunitie s on the horizon is the government’s ambitious Bharat Net Phase III project under which BSNL has already floated approximately Rs.60,000 crore tender for capex to be incurred in next 3 years followed by additional O&M opportunity worth approximately Rs.40,000 crore over a period of 10 years

items.statement: Product revenue mix to shift to >2/3 of total revenue in FY25
items.quote: would mean that our revenue would consist of more than two third of the product driven and less than one third of project driven

items.statement: Debt-equity to stay 0.24-0.30; capex funded by internal accruals, equity raise done, and part debt
items.quote: debt equity ratio, which is currently 0.24, it will remain in the same range. I mean, 0.24 to maybe 0.27, and max it be will 0.30, not more than that.

items.statement: Expect 8-10% volume growth and 8-10% EBITDA per ton growth in FY25
items.quote: In terms of volume, we are expecting 8% to 10% growth. And in EBITDA per ton also, we are expecting an 8% to 10% growth next financial year.

items.statement: Mukutban volume target of 2.7 million tons for FY25
items.quote: In Mukutban, we are expecting to have a volume of about 2.7 million tons.

items.statement: Total incentives guided at INR 100-110 crores for FY25 including all plants
items.quote: Overall, incentives next year will be around INR100 crores -- INR110 crores, including the other plants.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR 800 crores for FY25 split across sustenance, coal mines, and Kundanganj line 3
items.quote: See, out of the INR800 crores, we plan to spend about INR400 crores on sustenance capex, about INR200 crores on the development of coal mines and another INR 200 crores on Kundanganj line three.

items.statement: Net debt expected to close below INR 3,000 crores by end of FY25
items.quote: And as a result, net debt number, we expect to close that number below INR3,000 by the end of next year.

items.statement: Premium sales grew from 51% to 54% of total volumes in FY24
items.quote: And certainly, in our premium sales, which is really a function of the trade sales, we have had a growth from 51% to 54% in terms of percenta ge growth

items.statement: Q4 demand driven by infra and commercial segments; trade segment grew only 2%
items.quote: Actually, in the quarter 4, if you look at the entire industry, the demand mostly came from the Infra and Commercial segments.

items.statement: Competition in central markets depends on capacity additions and player behavior; too early to predict
items.quote: This year, it's too early to predict. It all depends on how the growth happens in the next 2 quarters, especially the capacities having come up.

items.statement: Pricing discipline maintained due to 100% capacity utilization in core markets and premium focus
items.quote: Our strategy is very clear. We do not have in these markets any anxiety for volumes, because we do not -- our capacity utilization is 100% in the key markets, which are our core markets of Central India.

items.statement: Freight cost optimization is market-specific; focus on net realization rather than absolute freight reduction
items.quote: We look at our net realization. So if you see a Mukutban situation, obviously, there, we will have to now spread ourselves further. So you may not get a freight cost reduction in Mukutban.

items.statement: Bikram coal mine expected in Q4 FY25; Marki Barka in FY26/27
items.quote: See, Bikram, we are expecting in Q4 of FY '25. And Marki Barka, we are expecting in FY '26/'27.

items.statement: Bikram coal mine savings to start from FY26 after ramp-up phase
items.quote: In this year, we don't envisage much savings, because it is in a ramp-up phase. The savings will start acquiring from next financial year.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR 600 crores in FY24 to INR 3,003 crores
items.quote: About INR600 crores compared to last year.

items.statement: Fuel cost in Q4 was INR 1.56/Kcal, ahead of guidance
items.quote: And our fuel cost in Q4 was INR1.56/Kcal, of course, leading to your guidance.

items.statement: No clinker capacity expansion planned; only announced grinding unit expansion
items.quote: First of all, I would request you again to keep your questions to only one question because others don't get a chance. But since you have already asked it, we have stated that our clinker capacity expansion is not going to come just now. So there's no plan for clinker capacity.

items.statement: Price outlook uncertain due to elections, heat, and monsoon; last quarter saw unexpected price decline
items.quote: This quarter is affected by elections, extreme heat in most of the country. And once the elections and everything is over, it will probably take a little while for the economic condition to stabilize.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected in 16-17% range
items.quote: earlier were expecting it in the ran ge of 15, now we expect it will be in the range of —16- 17 because there are a lot of initiatives that is being taken on cost control, on cost reduction, on innovation, on improvement , productivity

items.statement: Volume growth expected at 10-15% for FY25
items.quote: It would be more modest; it will be more in the range of 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Capex budget for FY25 estimated at 500-600 crores
items.quote: We expect the CAPEX spends to be a modest 500-600 crores this year.

items.statement: Order book stands at $1.5 billion with 30% export and 70% domestic
items.quote: The order book is a robust $1.5 billion , out of which export is 30% , domestic 70%.

items.statement: ROCE improved to around 20%
items.quote: The ROCE has improved. The ROCE is now in the range of 20.

items.statement: Raw material prices expected to stay in current band: iron ore $100-120, coal around $250 for 6-8 months
items.quote: The raw material prices if you see we expect them to move in a current band, iron ore between 100 to 120 but we don't import any. Domestically we are able to source iron ore at $80, 5,000 to 6,000 which is a good thing for us and we expect we'll continue to do that. Coal will remain around 250 and that should continue at least for the next 6 to 8 months is what our understanding.

items.statement: Strong demand visibility for 3-5 years driven by water infra and industrial growth
items.quote: So next now 3 to 5 years we do have certain confidence, we have certain visibility of good performance moving forward.

items.statement: QIP of 1,000 crores unlikely; enabling resolution for 1,000 crores debt instrument approved
items.quote: I can let you know that now it looks like the QIP may not happen. On the contrary yesterday we have taken again an enabling resolution from the board and we are going to take it to the shareholders 1,000 crores of a debt instrument.

items.statement: Middle East conflict escalation could disrupt shipping and demand in the region
items.quote: Only point of concern is a Middle East conflict if it gets blown into a full-fledged war then there could be disruptions in the area.

items.statement: Successfully extruded 13 Chrome Inconel, only Indian company with this capability
items.quote: I am very happy to let you know that in our stainless , we have now successfully extruded 13 Chrome Inconel which are very exotic, and we would be the only one in the country who would be able to do that.

items.statement: Prepaying entire 1,000 crore acquisition loan for Sathavahana during calendar year 2024
items.quote: I am very happy to announce that this year , we are prepaying the entire loan of that 1,000 crores even though it was an acquisition funding long term. But now we have a strategy in place where we want to prepay, already the prepayment has started April onwards and during this calendar year we would prepay the entire 1,000 crores

items.statement: Consolidated ROC to incrementally keep growing and cross 20% mark in next 2 years
items.quote: I am confident that given the multiple growth engines, we should see strong growth for 25 and our ROC to incrementally keep growing and cross the 20% mark in the next 2 years.

items.statement: India operations CAPEX about Rs. 500 crores for FY25
items.quote: So, it would be about 500 crores.

items.statement: Overseas entities CAPEX about $65 million for FY25 mainly towards US Aluminum Phase 2 and maintenance CAPEX in Europe
items.quote: For the next year, the CAPEX for overseas entities would be about $65 million, which is mainly towards the US Aluminum Phase 2 and some maintenance CAPEX in Europe.

items.statement: Consolidated CAPEX for FY25 expected to be about Rs. 800 to 1,000 crores
items.quote: Yes, about I would say 800 to 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Defense order book Rs. 5,200 crores execution timeline 3 to 4 years
items.quote: Some of it is 3 years. Some of it is 4 years.

items.statement: New business secured worth almost Rs. 6,300 crores across all key businesses in FY24
items.quote: During the year, the company secured new business worth almost Rs. 6,300 crores across all key businesses including defense, traditional busine ss as well as the casting business

items.statement: European aluminum business will be profitable in 2025 at both EBITDA and PBT level
items.quote: So, I would say that the European aluminum business will be profitable in 2025, both at EBITDA and at PBT level.

items.statement: US operations to see positive EBITDA in Q4 FY25
items.quote: But I think we have a handle on that, and we should see even the US operations with the positive EBITDA in Quarter 4, healthy, profitable EBITDA in Quarter 4.

items.statement: Overseas subsidiaries to reach double-digit EBITDA margin by exit of FY25
items.quote: Definitely in a double digit. I would say definitely double digit at the EBITDA level, yes.

items.statement: US truck market outlook reasonably optimistic with stability expected
items.quote: And everybody is talking about a reasonably optimistic scenario, which does not mean necessarily growth, but stability. And that is what we are following. That is also what we are seeing in our order book.

items.statement: Domestic CV space expected to be flat compared to last year
items.quote: We are expecting it to be flat as compared to last year.

items.statement: JS Auto business to double over next 4 years with 30% YoY growth over last 2 years
items.quote: This business will double over the next four years, mo st probably double or more than double over the next 4 years

items.statement: Aerospace business expected to double in next 3-4 years from roughly Rs. 300 crores revenue
items.quote: So, I expect in the next 3-4 years or 3 years also to double this growth.

items.statement: Oil and gas contribution about Rs. 300 crores in FY24, expected to go up slightly in FY25 with new products
items.quote: It's about 300 crores right now. I think we expect this to go up a little bit this year because we have new products that we are developing which we haven't supplied before.

items.statement: Defense business moving entirely to 100% owned subsidiary KSSL in FY25 once new facilities commissioned and licenses transferred
items.quote: The defense business will move entirely into the 100% owned subsidiary K SSL in FY25 once the new facilities are fully commissioned and the licenses get transferred to those physical facilities

items.statement: Two new sunrise sectors identified, expected to ramp up from next year and become meaningful by FY27
items.quote: We have made initial breakthroughs in two new sunrise sectors, and we expect that these will become large growth sectors for us going forward and this will ramp up from next year, but we will become meaningful by about FY27.

items.statement: Target 10% top-line growth in FY25 despite 5-8% negative rate variance; aim to cross 14% EBITDA margin and reach 15% if stable
items.quote: So considering that negative rate variance, we would target to reach like 10% top line growth. We will target that in spite of negative rate variance. And as far as EBITDA is concerned, so we are now more and more confident that we should be crossing the 14% mark at the company level. And slowly, if the situation continues to be stable, then probably we'll try to reach the 15% mark.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin 15.5-16% at INR4,000 cr turnover; implies EBITDA doubling in three years
items.value: EBITDA margin 15.5-16% at INR4,000 cr revenue
items.quote: And the steady - state EBITDA, if everything goes wel l, should be in the range of 15.5% to 16% at a turnover of INR4,000 crores

items.statement: FY25 capex budget INR200-250 cr for two greenfield projects; FY26 onward mainly maintenance INR150-200 cr plus formulation oncology
items.quote: So that spill over c apex would be there for FY '25. And we are estimating, we have set the budget of around INR200 crores to INR250 crores for the coming financial year that is FY '24-'25

items.statement: Oncology formulation pipeline: 12-14 oral molecules filing over 6-18 months; target INR300-350 cr additional revenue in 24-36 months
items.quote: We are developing about 12 to 14 oral oncology molecules, which would all come into filing over the next 6 to 18 months. And many of them are kind of day one launches with patents expiring from '25 till '27, '28.

items.statement: Gross contribution expected to improve ~1% to at least 35% from current just below 34% with stable API selling prices
items.quote: So with the current selling prices of API, we expect that the gross contribution should go at least till the level of 35%. And right now, it is somewhere just below 34%. So we hope that around 1% more improvement should be there as far as gross contribution is concerned.

items.statement: API prices stabilized after December quarter; only risk is crude above USD100 pushing up solvent and KSM costs (65-70% RM crude-linked)
items.quote: Then from December to March quarter, the prices have almost stabilized now, so they are not falling further. However, recently, we saw some uptick in the crude prices. So if the crude goes beyond a certain point, then definitely that will start -- that uptick will start slipping into the prices of crude derivatives like solvents, which we use.

items.statement: Export volume declined ~10% in FY24; expect recovery on interest rate cuts, low stocks, government tenders; domestic volume grew 16-17%
items.quote: Because export market we saw a degrowth of almost around 15% for the last quarter, whereas for the domestic market, it was almost flat, means there was hardly 1% decline was there.

items.statement: Formulation margin improvement driven by shift from domestic CMO to higher-margin export business in LatAm, Africa, regulated markets; 20%+ margin sustainable
items.quote: So as a conscious decision, we are trying to replace our domestic CMO business to more of value-added export business in Latin America, Asia, Africa and now increasingly in the regulated markets. So as in every year, every quarter, our international markets contribution to sales is increasing. And majorly, that is what is leading to the higher margins.

items.statement: Geopolitical tension in Middle East could renew dollar shortages and disrupt export demand; FDA import alert on API plant unresolved, inspection hoped by Sep'24
items.quote: What we need to be watchful was -- is current geopolitical tension in the Middle East. More and more countries should not get involved in the conflict, otherwise, with total -- then the situation might be little dicey.

items.statement: Dermatology greenfield at Tarapur: final capacity 2,000 TPM, ramping through H1 FY25; Sayakha specialty chemicals greenfield to commence end Q1 FY25, scale up Q4 FY25
items.quote: So the final production capacity, for dermatology project would be around 2,000 tons per month, for the single month, but it will ramp up slowly in first half of FY '25, that is in next 2 quarters because we are getting up the production by putting in more and more reactor s on stepwise basis

items.statement: FY25 volume growth target ~15% with new capacity; negative rate variance 5-8% concentrated in H1, minimal in H2
items.quote: But for the coming years, we will definitely target around 15% sort of volume growth. Internally, we should target around 15% sort of volume growth given the addition of new capacity.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin 17-18% seen as difficult due to product cyclicality; 15-16% more achievable with diversified portfolio
items.quote: So we think that 17% / 18% EBITDA margin mark might be slightly difficult, but at least getting that 15%/ 16% mark would be this easier then what it is right now, I would say.

items.statement: Mission 25 ROA target revised from 2.5% to 2.2% for FY25
items.quote: We do think that striving for a 2.2 post tax ROA can be a reasonable goal.

items.statement: NIM target recast to 7% for FY25 from earlier 7.5% goal
items.quote: We are recasting this goal, and we believe if we close at 7% for FY25 would be a decent spike from the current levels.

items.statement: Book growth target of Rs 1,20,000 crores possible if FY25 tailwinds supportive
items.quote: And if we do so, then our book goal, which we slated in FY22 to reach close to 1,20,000 should be a possibility.

items.statement: New business mix target of 15% remains medium-term commitment
items.quote: We are in a medium term still committed to get the new businesses to contribute to 15% of the overall mix.

items.statement: Credit cost internal goal of 25 bps reduction via lower write-offs and ECL coverage easing
items.quote: What we do believe will give us some relief is f urther improvement in our write offs w hich will further come down to that 25 bps

items.statement: Branch expansion target of 150-180 branches for FY25, weighted towards H2
items.quote: We have initially given you guidance that we are looking at close to 150 to 180 branches this year.

items.statement: Disbursement growth expected 14-15% for FY25 leading to 18-20% book growth
items.quote: Probably 14%-15% disbursement growth will still lead to an 18% to 20% book growth which in our standpoint will be a good outcome for the whole year.

items.statement: Investing in tech, digital, underwriting, fraud control and SME manpower
items.quote: we will continue to keep the spends on for tech, for digital properties as well as for beefing up our manpower which are in the functions of underwriting , in the functions of fraud control and the functions of

items.statement: NII grew 16% Q-o-Q and 10% full year; cost of funds up 30% Q4 Y-o-Y and 40% full year
items.quote: On NIMs since the last quarter saw cost of fund decline, we were able to take some of the NII growth from that relief into Q-o-Q NII growth of 16% and a full year growth of 10%.

items.statement: Added 20 bps pricing in Q4 after Q3; PV segment growth dilutes overall yield
items.quote: We have in fact after Q3 added another 20-bps pricing in Q4.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 disbursements muted due to elections and agri sentiment drag
items.quote: We know that as I said, 17% is the CAGR for the last 3 years, this year we expect Q1 to be a bit muted.

items.statement: Aizawl branch fraud: Rs 136 cr provision for 2,887 accounts; 11 arrests; isolated event
items.quote: Accordingly, 2887 accounts, which required Rs. 136 crores of provisions have been made and in our estimate, this is the worst-case scenario.

items.statement: Centralized pre-disbursement checks (CPC) live for 50% branches; rest in next few months
items.quote: In the last six months, 50% of our branches have gone from a fully decentralized check to now also having a second level centralized check on docs and pre-disbursement formalities.

items.statement: Collection efficiency 89% in April vs 92% last year; attributed to election disruptions and holidays
items.quote: Coming to your second observation on collection efficiency, yes it is below last April, 89 versus 92.

items.statement: Target to add at least 6,000 MW greenfield capacity in FY25
items.quote: we will plan to add at least about 6,000 MW of greenfield capacity in FY25

items.statement: Revised 2030 renewable capacity target upward from 45 GW to 50 GW
items.quote: we have revised our renewable energy capacity target for 2030 upwards from 45 GW to now 50 GW

items.statement: Target at least 5 GW pumped hydro storage capacity by 2030
items.quote: We are targeting at Adani Green an addition of at least 5 GW of pumped hydro storage capacity by 2030

items.statement: Pumped hydro storage capital cost estimated at INR 4.5-5 crores per MW
items.quote: So we are looking at about INR 4.5 crores to INR 5 crores per MW

items.quote: Solar, we look at capital costs somewhere around 5 crores per MW

items.statement: Wind capital cost approximately INR 6.5 crores per MW
items.quote: wind is approximately 6.5 crore per MW

items.statement: 20 GW of locked-in PPAs currently
items.quote: We have 20 GW of locked in PPAs

items.statement: Industry-leading EBITDA margin of 92% in FY24
items.quote: Our consistently high operational performance has enabled us to deliver an industry-leading EBITDA margin of 92%.

items.statement: 50 GW target fully funded via debt facilities, internal accruals and promoter warrants
items.quote: Both of those things put together ensure that 100% of the equity requirements are fully funded to get to 50 GW

items.statement: Expect 3-4 year runway for merchant power due to India's power deficit
items.quote: we see a very clear three to four year runway where we'd be able to make substantially better margins, if we have additional capacities that are catered towards the merchant market

items.statement: Guidance of ~10% merchant and C&I mix in portfolio going forward
items.quote: you can consider a guidance of about 10% in terms of the mix that we would have that is open, where we would sell to merchant and C&I put together

items.statement: No supply chain, evacuation or equipment challenges expected for 6,000 MW FY25 target
items.quote: For us specifically, we will not have any of those challenges

items.statement: First 500 MW pumped hydro project commissioning in FY27
items.quote: So FY27, Apoorva is the first commissioning for plan of 500 MW that we're executing currently

items.statement: Khavda project: 2 GW solar operationalized in FY24 within 12 months
items.quote: in the same location, we have already operationalized 2 GW of solar capacity in FY24, just within 12 months of breaking ground there

items.statement: Run-rate capacity addition of 6,000-8,000 MW per year going forward
items.quote: In future years as well, we should look at executing somewhere between 6,000 to 8,000 MW every year of new capacity

items.statement: Estimates FY25 revenue growth of 35% to 40% with EBITDA margin range of 22% to 24%

items.quote: While not giving out the guidance, we are estimating a growth of between 35% to 40% in terms of revenues for FY '25 with a margin range of 22% to 24%.

items.statement: Targets 22% CAGR by end of FY25 to achieve $1 billion revenue by 2031
items.quote: We envision that we now need only 22% CAGR by the end of FY 2025 to achieve US $1 billion in revenue by 2031.

items.statement: GBS business unit to grow from 70 to 250 people by end of FY25
items.quote: The GBS business unit is already 70 people strong and expect it to grow to 250 by the end of this fiscal.

items.statement: GBS unit has 14 active customers across 20 projects
items.quote: The Gen AI business unit, GBS, under the leadership of Sridhar Mantha, President and CEO of the unit, is generating many new business opportunities. We already have 14 active customers across various industries covering 20 projects.

items.statement: FY24 EBITDA margin at 24.6%, beating 22-24% guidance range for 16th straight quarter
items.quote: Our EBITDA at ₹421 crores grew by about 11% and stands at 24.6% beating the upper band of our margin guidance range of 22% to 24%.

items.statement: Will start reporting operating margins alongside EBITDA going forward
items.quote: While we are all along been reporting and guiding on EBITDA, we would like to start reporting our operating margins as well as we go forward.

items.statement: Pipeline at record high with elongated deal cycles; India market opportunities at record high
items.quote: Our pipeline continues to be strong, though with elongated deal cycles. In growth markets like India, where we have a sizable presence, the pipeline of opportunities is at a record high.

items.statement: Created six new industry groups as independent profit centres and integrated PES and DBS into single PDES unit
items.quote: We created a new vertical organization structure comprising of six new industry groups. • We then took the rest of our business, which was functioning as two separate business units, P ES and DBS and integrated them into a single business unit , Product and Digital Engineering Services

items.statement: Margin range wider due to integration timeline of PureSoftware acquisition and time for cost synergies to materialize
items.quote: Quite a few puts and takes here on the profitability front, which is why I've given wider margin, wider margin is not to accommodate for a company which is lower than us in margins, they are reasonably close to us. There will be cost synergies as we go al ong. But all that takes 1 or 2 quarters to come through into the financials

items.statement: Raised ₹500 crores via QIP and ₹125 crores via NCDs; deploying into acquisitions
items.quote: At the year-end we held cash balances of about ₹ 1,364 crores including the ₹500 crores raise through our QIP and the ₹125 crores that we have raised through an issue of non-convertible debentures. We are now deploying part of these reserves into acquisitions.

items.statement: Built unique bioinformatics capability with molecular biology, data science, and healthcare experts
items.quote: We've built the capability in bioinformatics which no one in the industry has. This comprises experts in molecular biology, data scientists, data engineers and health care domain specialists.

items.statement: Attrition dropped to 13% from 19.8% YoY; expect to continue at these levels
items.quote: Attrition on a 12-month basis dropped to 13% from 19.80% in the previous year, and we expect these numbers to continue trending at these levels.

items.statement: Recommended final dividend of ₹3.25 per share; total FY24 dividend ₹5.75 per share
items.quote: Happy to state that keeping in line with our progressive dividend policy and capital allocation discussions, our Board of Directors of the company at the meeting held on May 6, have recommended a final dividend of ₹ 3.25 per share, subject to shareholder approval. This would take our total dividend for the year to ₹5.75.

items.statement: Expect margins to grow upwards of 25% or more in upcoming years
items.quote: Our goal is to sustain growth momentum in the medium to long run, and for the upcoming years, we expect our margins to grow upwards of 25% or more.

items.statement: Phase 2 capacity expansion to 16.5 million meters by December 2024
items.quote: In the phase 2, the company intends to increase the capacity to 16.5 million meters per annum that is an additional 3 million meters and the same should be com pleted by December of this year

items.statement: Composite hoses three lines addition by Q2 FY25
items.quote: In addition to the above , we are also completing the addition of three lines in the composite hoses production and the same should be completed by Q2 of FY25.

items.statement: Metal bellows Phase 1 capacity 120,000 pieces by December 2024
items.quote: And lastly, the expansion of a new project of metal bellows that we have planned to undertake in two phases, with a total capacity of 300,000 pieces annually at the end of phase 2 and as part of the phase 1 with a manufacturing capacity of 120,000 pieces p er year and the same is also expected to be completed by December of this year

items.statement: Project orders about 20% of overall orders in FY24
items.quote: So, on an average, our project orders are about 20% of our overall orders.

items.statement: EBITDA margins increased 75 basis points year-on-year in FY24
items.quote: So, if you see on a year -on-year basis, our EBITDA margins has increased by almost 75 basis points.

items.statement: Freight cost increase from Red Sea crisis impacted EBITDA margins by 25-30 bps
items.quote: Obviously, I won't have the exact details, but I would say at least 25 to 30 basis point minimum, the EBITDA margin would be higher at least.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margins about 25% over next 4-5 years
items.quote: And overall, over the next four to five years, our EBITDA margins should come to about 25 -odd percent in terms of margins.

items.statement: Sustained strong demand across traditional and emerging industries despite geopolitical tensions
items.quote: despite the geopolitical tensions that is ongoing in the Middle East, whic h is affecting especially the shipping routes and also the export markets, we are delighted to report sustained strong demand for our products across both the traditional and the emerging industries

items.statement: Assemblies and fittings proportion increased to 34% in FY24 from 30-31% last year
items.quote: So, last year the proportion of fittings to our overall sales was around 30% to 31% and this year is about 34% almost.

items.statement: Target value-added products 60-70% of sales in next 3-4 years from 33% currently
items.quote: To give a number, I would say about 60%. 60% to 70% on a ballpark figure.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis caused 10-15 days revenue impact in Q3 and Q4, freight costs remain elevated
items.quote: About 10 to 15 days of our sales of Q3 were impacted. And the same was actually carried forward on to Q4.

items.statement: Hyd Air Engineering acquired for INR17.20 crores fully funded by internal accruals
items.quote: We acquired Hyd Air Engineering for a total consideration of INR17.20 crores, and it was entirely funded by internal accruals.

items.statement: Zero debt on balance sheet provides financial leverage for growth
items.quote: We believe that a strong balance sheet and with zero debt in our company.

items.statement: AUM growth guided in excess of 25% for FY25
items.quote: In the coming year, we estimate our growth to be in the excess of 25%.

items.statement: Operating cost guided to rationalize to 5.7%-5.75% for FY25
items.quote: Our operating cost will further rationalize by 20 bps. We are at 5.97%. It will be around 5.7% to 5.75%.

items.statement: Credit cost guided to remain around 1.7% for FY25
items.quote: The credit cost will remain in the same range of 1.7%.

items.statement: ROA guided to reach 4.3%-4.5% for FY25
items.quote: We estimate that our ROAs will improve in the coming financial year. Definitely, it will reach to the level of around 4.3% to 4.5%.

items.statement: ROE guided to remain above 20% for FY25
items.quote: And ROE will continue to be at 20% above.

items.statement: Long-term ROA target of 4.5%
items.quote: We guide towards around 4.5% of ROA for the long run.

items.statement: GNPA target of 2% or lower for FY25
items.quote: I think it should be 200 bps or lower in the coming financial year.

items.statement: Added 336 branches in FY24, plan to add 120-125 branches in FY25
items.quote: So additional another 120-odd branches, 125 branches would be added.

items.statement: FY24 NIM at 12.7%, Q4 standalone NIM at 13.5%
items.quote: We are reporting at 12.7% of net interest margin. And if you look at for the quarter standalone, the margins have improved to around 13.5%.

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds at 10.39%, down 2 bps QoQ
items.quote: If you look at our incremental cost of fund, it is around 10.39%, which is an improvement over the last quarter by around 2 bps.

items.statement: Disbursements grew 32% YoY to INR 10,661 cr in FY24
items.quote: We disbursed INR10,661 crores worth of loan. This is an improvement of 32% year-on-year.

items.statement: 97% of disbursements to low/very low risk customers via Equifax scorecard
items.quote: So if you look at 97% of our disbursement has gone to low risk and very low risk customers only.

items.statement: Punjab exposure 1.3% of AUM (INR 155 cr), impacted portfolio INR 31 cr, wrote off INR 12 cr
items.quote: Our total exposure there is 155 crores, out of which the impact among our customers is only around 20,000 customers out of the total 1,07,000 customers. These are basically five districts around Amritsar which are impacted. So our portfolio that is impacted is around 31 crores. And out of that, we have already proactively taken a write off of 12 crores.

items.statement: Raised INR 760 cr primary capital via IPO, fully deployed
items.quote: We raised around INR 960 crores of capital through the IPO, of which INR 760 crores were primary. I would like to inform all the investors and listeners here that, the whole of this money has been deployed for business purposes.

items.statement: Closed USD 75 mn ECB (INR 622 cr) for long-term funding
items.quote: We had also closed a very, very landmark deal of external commercial borrowing of around USD 75 million, which translates to around INR622 crores. This provides us with a very effective cost of fund and also a long term availability of debt.

items.statement: Real estate new project acquisitions target INR15,000-20,000 crores for FY25
items.quote: We have about INR15,000 crores to INR20,000 crores of new projects target. We did about INR16,000 crores this year. Hopefully, we do a similar number or close to about INR20,000 crores in the coming year.

items.statement: Real estate presales target to double from INR3,985 crores in FY24
items.quote: Yes, we at least expect to double our sales performance from what we did last year.

items.statement: Pulp & Paper EBITDA margin guidance INR12-13 per kg for FY25
items.quote: And we can safely give you a guidance that we will be if not 15, we'll be close to about 12 next year. I think it is not percentage, it is INR15 per kg of paper is the margin that we are aspiring for. But the guidance right now is around INR12 to INR13.

items.statement: Significant capex planned in Pulp & Paper to address wood procurement and power cost bottlenecks
items.quote: We have a lot of capex planned to overtake all these issues that we had in the bottlenecks.

items.statement: Real estate launches planned worth ~INR12,000 crores across 9 launches in FY25
items.quote: About INR12,000 crores of launches will be there, roughly.

items.statement: Real estate demand far outstripping supply across operating markets
items.quote: I think the demand at this point of time is far more than the supply. I think there is quite a few demand. That's what we have seen personally in the markets that we are operating. Every market demand is far outstripping supply.

items.statement: Land prices becoming firmer and more expensive, making deals difficult to conclude
items.quote: So yes, the land prices have become much firmer. It's getting more and more pricey if I may say so. So that much more difficult it has become to conclude deals.

items.statement: Pulp & Paper oversupply likely to continue in FY25 as capacity additions exceed market growth
items.quote: However, oversupply in market likely to continue in FY '25 as the market growth is lower than the capacity being added by domestic as well as international mills.

items.statement: Fund raising only at project level via SPVs, not at parent or subsidiary level; no promoter funding
items.quote: We are only looking fund raising for specific projects at project level, not at a subsidiary level, not at the parent level.

items.statement: Real estate project-level EBITDA margin ~23% on revenue recognized from 3 projects
items.quote: the revenue, which is recognized for the 3 projects, Kalyan, Gurugram and Bangalore, the EBITDA margin on that is approximately 23%.

items.statement: Discontinued operations impairment done; expect max INR25 crores write-offs in FY25
