items.statement: Expect significant ordering pickup in H2 FY25 post-elections; NHAI/MORTH alone have Rs 1.2 lakh crore orders floated
items.quote: Even at the NHAI level there is more than INR 1,00,000 crores of orders that have already been floated. So, INR 1,20,000 crores of orders purely on NHAI and MORTH levels that have been floated.

items.statement: Election year historically slow for ordering; expect sharp recovery post-elections with 100-day government plan
items.quote: Election year is always a slow order ing year. And if you look at this detailing from back from a Vajpayeeji's era to now every election year is a slow year. But the year after it is usually or ordering increases significantly.

items.statement: Expect revenue growth slightly better than FY24's 12% and EBITDA margin expansion of ~100 bps annually for next couple of years
items.quote: More generally, my expectation is that we should be able to grow at a level slightly better than what we grew this year from the previous year. Margin expansion in terms of EBITDA should reflect our endeavor which I have outlined a couple of years ago, to have our EBITDA margin increase by 100 basis points every year for the next couple of years and I think that should hold.

items.statement: Expect 3-5% ARPU expansion in test-prep for current fiscal year
items.quote: going forward we are reasonably confident of a 3-5% ARPU expansion in the current fiscal year

items.statement: Intangible investments ~Rs.13 crore in FY24, amortized over 5-10 years; future investment rate to reduce 15-20% vs FY24
items.quote: They would be in the Rs.13 crore odd range for this year and we see that those kinds of investments are typically amortized anywhere between 5 to 10 years, on an average of 7 years and we will continue to make such investments over the years ahead but probably at a reducing rate of about 15 to 20 % compared to what we did this year.

items.statement: Test-prep enrollment grew ~10% in FY24; CUET student growth ~50%; Law test-takers down ~30% due to calendar shift
items.quote: FY24 we saw our volume expansion by about 10 % in terms of enrollment and the billing also has increased by 10% that would basically mean m ore or less consistent or constant average realization per

items.statement: International revenues grew ~32% in FY24; MarTech international +34%, EdTech international +28%; Indonesia and US drove 50% of MarTech international growth
items.quote: if you look at our international revenues, they have grown by about 32% in the year gone by, the MarTech revenue increase internationally has been 34% and in the EdTech segment that revenue expansion has been about 28%.

items.statement: Middle East premium admission consultancy grew 58%; Middle East volume +20%, billing +16%; 6 locations operational, plan to double in 12 months
items.quote: Our premium admission consultancy business grew by about 58% over the previous year and business in the Middle East has been growing steadily with a 20% volume expansion and a 16% billing expansion. We currently have 6 locations operational there and we are looking to double that number in the next 12 months.

items.statement: MarTech margin expansion driven by shift to higher-margin revenue mix and higher-margin international revenue (Singapore, Indonesia, US)
items.quote: MarTech showed a highly divergent trend, with revenue expanding by about 6% but margin expanding by a healthy 29% which was predominantly driven by two parameters - one being the pivoting of the revenue mix to higher margin business thereby effectively increaseing our gross margin and hence the follow-through into the business EBITDA.

items.statement: Publishing margin expanded due to paper prices cooling ~25% in last 6-9 months; expect stability and further margin improvement from selective price hikes
items.quote: As I shared about 12 months ago paper prices had hit the r oof but they have now cooled down by about 25% in the last 6 - 9 months, have been pretty stable in the last quarter and we expect that the price stability will hold and the enhanced margin should only get better in the new season because of price hike s which we will go through with in certain select title

items.statement: Platform business (Common Application Form) onboarded 40 institutions in first 4 months, sold 3,000+ forms; expect multiple-fold revenue increase
items.quote: We are extremely positive about the direction this new initiative will take in the coming years and we are expecting a multiple fold increase in the revenues through form sales through the platform.

items.statement: MarTech added 56 new clients in FY24; expect new clients to contribute 10-15% of revenue in coming year
items.quote: We continue to add new customers and we expect going forward the customers which were added last year will contribute about 10 to 15% of the revenue in the coming year and will continue to expand customer base in the current year.

items.statement: Law exam calendar shift (May to December) caused ~30% test-taker decline; recovery expected over couple of years; currently Rs.8-10 crore short of pre-COVID law revenue
items.quote: keeping that possibility aside we expect that the number of test takers will go backwards to the original numbers in a couple of years and CL being a market leader a large chunk of that increased test taker segment will proportio nately come to us

items.statement: MarTech Q4 muted due to Chinese New Year shutdown (4 weeks), Indonesia elections hiatus; best quarters typically Q2/Q3
items.quote: However, the opening for the current fiscal year has been reasonably strong usually because different multinationals in different geographies have different year endings. At the start of the new fiscal, their budgets get released at different points of time. Usually our best quarters are Q2 and Q3 with Q1 and Q4 being slightly muted.

items.statement: Evaluating inorganic M&A opportunities in EdTech and MarTech; active discussions ongoing; hopeful of decision in next 2-4 quarters; cash held in FDs meantime
items.quote: There are active opportunities both in EdTech as well as MarTech space being evaluated and we are hopeful that something would come through in the next 2 to 4 quarters.

items.statement: Added 25 new test-prep centers in FY24; expect 30-40 new centers in FY25; centers on 3-year franchise contracts with renewals/exits
items.quote: Just to add the new centers which were added was the number was 25 and we expect somewhere between 30 to 40 new centers to go live in the current

items.statement: MarTech virtual revenue 6-7% of total; expect to increase 1-2pp annually, targeting 20% in 3-5 years; 20% from tech-enabled, 80% physical events/services
items.quote: the total virtual revenue to both the virtual events platform and some bits of meta commerce of transformations into 3d environment would be in the currently the range of 6 to 7% of the total revenue, going forward we see this percentage increasing marginally every year by 1-2% points of the total revenue and we are hoping to hit that in 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: MarTech EBITDA margin target ~10.5-11% for coming year; Q4 had one-time adjustments from older project closures
items.quote: Broadly there were some one-time adjustments of older projects etc. older costs which we closed which flowed in from Q3 and into Q4 and hence there was slight mutation of profitability in Q4 but overall I think we are on track to maintain a 10½ - 11%, a bit on that business going forward at least in the coming year.

items.statement: Animal feed FY25 EBIT per ton expected to be better than FY24 average of Rs 1,531/ton
items.quote: Our average last year was about Rs. 1,531 and I can definitely F.Y. 2024 was Rs. 1,531. The only thing I can say is that F.Y. 2025 will better than that.

items.statement: Cattle feed and fish feed expected to sustain double-digit volume growth for foreseeable future
items.quote: Cattle Feed and Fish Feed the game is wide open. There is no integration likely to happen because Cattle Feed market is huge. Category conversion is at 20% level, and we believe Cattle Feed and Fish Feed can both grow in double digits for the next at least foreseeable future.

items.statement: Dairy VAP salience targeted to grow another 4-5% in FY25 from current 36%
items.quote: we hope that this year we will grow the salience by another 4%-5%.

items.statement: Astec CDMO revenue expected to maintain ~67% growth run-rate in FY25 with base now over Rs 250 Cr
items.quote: This year we have grown by almost 67% from last year and we have a very good confidence that we'll continue to maintain that run rate as we get into F .Y. 2025. Now our base for the CDMO new products have also crossed 250 Crore.

items.statement: Astec new product revenues expected to start contributing from July-August FY25
items.quote: as we move forward in F.Y. 2025 from July-August onward we will start seeing the financial performance kicked in from some of these new products which we have been working on.

items.statement: Consolidated capex run-rate of Rs 250-300 Cr to be maintained in FY25; oil palm refinery expansion decision by end of Q2
items.quote: On an average we keep on investing about Rs. 250 to 300 Crore. I think, we will maintain that run rate but the investment will come. We just have added some capacities in our dairy business. We have to invest in distribution in our chicken and dairy business. I will tell you how we invest in distribution because wherever we go , we require freezers and chillers which we invest in and a big chunk o

items.statement: Astec capex cycle to be discussed in Q3-Q4 FY25 depending on CDMO pickup
items.quote: Astec, we have commissioned one herbicide plant and capitalized it in Q 1, so we are in a situation where we have capacity to fill. But I am very sure that Astec CAPEX cycle will come under discussion in Q3 and Q4 because in case contract manufacturing or CDMO business picks up , we will require specialized capacity for specialized product for specialized customers.

items.statement: Animal feed Q4 EBIT margin Rs 1,874/ton; management expects to maintain close to Q4 levels in current quarter
items.quote: Q4 we have gone to Rs. 1,874. So, my sense is that the upward trend will continue and I am very sure whatever on the year-on-year basis I am saying, and we will be able to maintain close to Q4 numbers in this quarter also.

items.statement: Oil palm value addition reduced profit impact of 20% CPO price drop from expected 40% to actual 20%
items.quote: we had a target of Rs. 184 Crore PBT and there was a significant drop in CPO prices. There was almost a 12% - 13% drop in crude palm oil price, 20% drop. So, if we were only in crude palm oil and palm kernel oil , our profits should have fallen by 40%. But because of these profits came down only by about 20%.

items.statement: Astec enterprise business seeing no green shoots; focus on CDMO and new products to de-lever from enterprise profits
items.quote: On the enterprise side , we haven't seen any green shoots in the market. But internally I would hate to give any forecast on when the market should revive back. In turn what we are focusing on are the things which are in our hand which are the CDMO, and the new product development and our entire goal and ambition is that as we get into F.Y. 2025, we completely de -lever ourselves from enterprise p

items.statement: Fish meal prices softening; company well-placed with low inventory in India and Bangladesh
items.quote: what we are seeing now is some kind of softening has started happening and good thing is that we don't have too much of stock either in Bangladesh or India. So , my sense is that we are reasonably well placed in case the price falls.

items.statement: DDGS availability from ethanol program offsetting higher corn prices in animal feed
items.quote: if the energy prices because of corn have gone up , the protein prices because of DDGS have come down which has helped utilize the cost increase in our feed segment.

items.statement: Palm oil prices stabilizing but could rise; import duty may increase post-elections due to bumper mustard crop
items.quote: Palm oil prices have dropped somewhat but they seem to be stabilizing now and of course they could rise a little bit. We don't expect that palm oil prices will go very high but Indian prices also depend on the import duty and since we have bumper red seed crops and farmers have to be kept satisfied it is likely that after the elections import duties on imported oil could be raised.

items.statement: No equity raise planned for Astec; debt-equity ~1.3x, short-term needs to be met internally
items.quote: No, we are not looking at any raise because we strongly believe that we have industry has bottomed out and now the journey will be upwards and in this business, I am saying that debt equity is still about 1.3 or something. So, it's not a very big concern. We can tide over whatever is the short-term requirement by supporting internally.

items.statement: Branded poultry volumes grew ~15% in FY24 (Yummy's 13%, Real Good Chicken 15.6%); live bird declining
items.quote: Yummy's grew about 13% and Real Good Chicken grew about 15.6% and if we take the blended number, then the branded volumes grew by about 15% in F .Y. 2024 over F.Y. 2023 and that is the focus for this year also.

name: Home First Finance Company India Ltd

items.statement: Credit cost guidance maintained at 30-40 bps
items.quote: We continue to maintain our credit cost guidance of 30 to 40bps.

items.statement: Ex-CL spread guidance of 5.0-5.25% for medium term
items.quote: Our ex-CL Spread guidance of 5.0-5.25% stands for the medium term.

items.statement: Opex to assets guidance of around 3.0% going ahead
items.quote: We continue to maintain the guidance of around 3.0% going ahead; as we focus on expansion and get deeper into new markets.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing may increase another 10-20 bps at best
items.quote: Net-net, coming to cost of borrowing another 10-20 bps increase at best is what we're looking at.

items.statement: Co-lending to contribute around 10% of disbursements in near future
items.quote: Co-lending business is growing and expect this to contribute around 10% of disbursements in the near future.

items.statement: Targeting 20-25 branch additions per year and 60-70 touchpoints per year
items.quote: Branch expansion, we are targeting 20 to 25 branches every year. And along with that, say, about 60 to 70 touchpoints per year.

items.statement: AUM growth target of 30%
items.quote: Overall, we are targeting 30% growth.

items.statement: LAP portfolio target of 20% by March 2027 from current 13%
items.quote: Our 3-year plan is to take it to 20%. So, it will be gradual, it will not be very sharp but March'27 is 20%.

items.statement: ROA expected around 3.5% (3.4-3.6%) next year with ROE 16%+
items.quote: So that range can be 3.4% to 3.6%. But let's say you anchor around 3.5% plus/minus which essentially leaves you with a 16% plus ROE.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity target of 5x (asset-to-equity 6x) with 2-2.5 years runway
items.quote: At our planned expansion, debt-to-equity of 5x or asset-to-equity of 6x is what we have in mind.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio target of close to 30% in 3-5 years, 34-35% for next 1-2 years
items.quote: Our aim in the medium term is to get that down to around close to 30% levels. In maybe 3- to 5-year timeframe, we should be able to get it down to 30% levels. Otherwise, next 1 to 2 years, we are looking at 34%, 35% level.

items.statement: Insurance agency license obtained in Feb 2024, expect INR 5-6 Cr quarterly income from Q3
items.quote: Once we sign with at least 2 to 3 companies and cover the entire book that we onboard today, my expectation is that should add close to INR5 crores to INR6 crores of additional income into the P&L, on a quarterly basis. So, let's say Q3 onwards is when you should be able to see the full income.

items.statement: NIM expected to stabilize at 5.3-5.5% with spread at 5.0-5.25%
items.quote: Our NIM should be in a similar range where we are today like 5.3% - 5.5% is what we have thought.

items.statement: Will absorb COB increase up to 20 bps, not pass on to customers; will pass on 25-50 bps if rates rise sharply
items.quote: As we mentioned earlier, up to small increases like 10, 20 basis points, we are looking to absorb it, and we are not looking to pass it on to the customer.

items.statement: No stress seen in customer incomes; incomes growing 10-15% annually extrapolated from ticket size growth
items.quote: Ticket size growth as you can see annually, we are seeing about a 10% kind of ticket size growth. So, I would say incomes are also broadly moving up maybe 10% to 15% income growth is what we can kind of extrapolate.

items.statement: BT Out elevated due to repricing (3 PLR hikes in 2 years), but total erosion stable at 16-18%; will do cohort-based repricing
items.quote: BT Out rates are higher largely because of rates being higher because we have repriced the large part of our book and that is creating some tension with customers. That's primarily the reason.

items.statement: NHB refinance at ~20% of borrowings; drew Rs 250 Cr in Apr'24; NHB rate ~50 bps below marginal bank rate
items.quote: NHB refinance as a percentage of the overall book my sense it will be 20% on an average basis.

items.statement: Loan book growth guidance of 30%-35% for FY25
items.quote: in terms of loan book, we are talking about a 30%-35% of growth

items.statement: Deposit growth guidance of 40%-45% for FY25
items.quote: in terms of deposits we intend to have somewhere around a 40%-45% kind of a growth

items.statement: Secured book mix target of 45% by end of FY25
items.quote: by the end of next year we would want to be around 45%

items.statement: ROA guidance range of 2.3%-2.5% for medium term
items.quote: we would want to be range bound to 2.3 to 2.5

items.statement: ROE guidance of 14%-16% for next 2 years
items.quote: our aim will be to have a guidance for ROE for 14% to 16%

items.statement: Cost to income including CGFMU target of 57% for FY25
items.quote: our ambition is that for the next year, our cost to income including CGFMU will be in the region of 57%

items.statement: Credit cost outlook of 1.5%-1.8% for FY25
items.quote: I would want to be at the same stage where we are today for this financial year which has been somewhere in the range of 1.5% to 1.8%

items.statement: CGFMU expense estimate of 70-80 crores for FY25
items.quote: our expense on CGFMU will be somewhere in the range of 70 to 80 crores

items.statement: Capital raise expected in 15-18 months as CRAR approaches 20%
items.quote: We should be able to raise capital when we are inching towards that 20% number

items.statement: No slowdown or stress observed due to elections
items.quote: We haven't. We haven't to an extent not heard anything from the market or from our peers

items.statement: Vikas Loans AUM surpassed Rs. 2,600 crores, contributing over 53% of inclusive finance portfolio
items.quote: Vikas Loans, the individual loan portfolio offered to Bank's graduating JLG customers has surpassed Rs. 2,600 crores of AUM and now contributes over 53% of the inclusive finance portfolio

items.statement: NIM increased to 9.8% in FY24 from 9.5% in FY23
items.quote: NIM has increased from 9.5% in FY23 to 9.8% in FY24

items.statement: Plan to reduce Vikas Loan pricing from 28% to around 24% over next year
items.quote: our intent was really going on the pricing path in terms of reducing it from current 28% to around closer to around 24% over the next 1 year

items.statement: CGFMU claim target of 45-50 crores gross claims for FY25
items.quote: for this financial year we would look to make claims, gross claims somewhere in the region of 45 to 50 crores

items.statement: Universal bank license eligibility expected in about a year
items.quote: we will take about a year to be eligible to fulfill all the criteria for being eligible to apply for being a universal Bank

items.statement: Management expects demand improvement from Q2 FY25 and significant improvement in H2 FY25 across both segments.
items.quote: We anticipate that the overall scenario will start normalizing from second half of FY25 and we have all the enablers to regain our normal double-digit growth trajectory which we had demonstrated throughout all these years.

items.statement: Prices have bottomed out in both pigment and agro segments; prices will go up with demand improvement.
items.quote: Yes, definitely we can say that not only in the pigment segment but even in the agro segment. Prices have bottomed out completely and with the improvement in demand, we see the prices will also go up and there will be increase in volume as well as value.

items.statement: No major capex planned for next 1-2 years; all major capex completed before downturn.
items.quote: So I would say in next one or two years, there is not going to be major capex. So we are already there ready with the infrastructure in both the segments

items.statement: Debt repayment of INR140 crores planned in FY25 with further reduction in FY26.
items.quote: And regarding the debt position, yes, there is some little high debt as of now. And this financial year, we'll be repaying about INR140 crores repayment is going to be there. Again, subsequently in the next financial year, there will be further debt reduction.

items.statement: Nano Urea margins expected in 15%-17% range.
items.quote: Yes. So, the margin level would be in the range of about 15%-17%.

items.statement: Agrochemical inventory destocking nearly complete; demand improvement expected from Q2 FY25 based on customer order indications.
items.quote: In fact, it has gone to almost normal level now. And in the agrochemical segment, because it is directly linked to the agriculture, now every country in the world is talking about the food security. And as the population is increasing, arable land is decreasing, we need to have more yield agriculture crop, we need more.

items.statement: Customers showing positivity and placing small frequent orders indicating demand recovery.
items.quote: That's correct. So, customers have also started showing positivity and regarding placing the order. The only thing is people have got, you know, burned their fingers significantly because of high inventory. So, people are going cautious rather than putting big orders. They are putting small, small orders in more number of orders they are putting with the small, small quantities. But yes, that will

items.statement: Titanium dioxide plant commissioned with captive co-gen power plant to reduce energy cost; targeting domestic market to balance revenue mix.
items.quote: Moving to titanium dioxide, we have commissioned the Co-gen Power Plant, which will help us to reduce the energy cost, which is a major cost component in titanium dioxide manufacturing process.

items.statement: Nano Urea plant commissioned March 2024; capacity 5 crore bottles/year (25,000 tons); expect 60%+ utilization from Q1 FY25.
items.quote: So, as of now, the utilization level is low. But we see from the first quarter, in this quarter onwards, only the utilization level will reach to 60% plus.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on Chinese titanium dioxide imports expected in 4-6 months (provisional) which will benefit domestic producers.
items.quote: So, we see some preliminary anti-dumping duty coming on titanium dioxide on Chinese goods somewhere in next four to six months' time. So, that will help local industry significantly, as well as Meghmani Organics Limited.

items.statement: Chinese export incentives of 13%-15% enable dumping; anti-dumping initiations in multiple countries including India.
items.quote: But Chinese government is giving huge incentive on the export. So not only on titanium dioxide but I would say on majority of the products. So because of that, they get export incentive to the tune of about 13%-15%, which is significantly high.

items.statement: Working capital days (debtor, inventory, creditor) increased in FY24 but will significantly improve in FY25.
items.quote: That's correct. So, right now it has gone up, you rightly mentioned. And in this financial year, it will significantly improve again.

items.statement: Crop nutrition segment to launch 4-5 new products (fertilizer, biofertilizer, biostimulant) alongside Nano Urea.
items.quote: Further, we also plan to introduce about four to five new products in the segments of fertilizer, biofertilizer, and biostimulant category to add more products in our basket, providing a comprehensive one-stop solution for our farmers.

items.statement: FY25 will be significantly better than FY24 but not yet at pre-downturn levels.
items.quote: So, I would say the worst is over. We are very optimistic in this financial year. So, we'll be again, with the good numbers, we'll be showcasing our financial year. It won't be as good as before two years position. It will be significantly better than the last financial year.

items.statement: Agrochemical product prices at lowest levels, even below 2019; raw material prices also down; any demand improvement will raise prices and volumes.
items.quote: So I would say all the products prices have gone to the almost at the lowest level. So, even before 2019 prices even below those level prices have gone. So, this is the lowest possible price which has happened at the same time, the raw material prices have also gone down. So, this is the worst phase. So, anything, any demand improvement happening in the market will lead to increase in price as wel

items.statement: Paisabazaar growth expected at 0-10% for next quarter due to process-based slowdown
items.quote: I expect this to last at least one more quarter. And the expectation, I think, is going to be below that. So I think we would be good at maybe 0 to 10% growth for Paisa.

items.statement: Full year PAT breakeven achieved in Q3, ended year with PAT of ₹64Cr
items.quote: We had the aimed for a full year PAT break even and we are very happy to announce that we achieved that ahead of the target in Q3 itself. And have now ended the year with a PAT of ₹64Cr from a loss of ₹488Cr last year.

items.statement: Core insurance adjusted EBITDA margin improved from 6% to 14%, adjusted EBITDA now ₹324Cr
items.quote: Revenue for our online marketplaces Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, which we referred to as t he core businesses, grew 39% to ₹2,375Cr, while improving their adjusted EBITDA margin from 6% to 14%. Adjusted EBITDA for these businesses are now ₹324Cr

items.statement: Total insurance premium for quarter ₹5,123Cr, ARR reached ₹20,000Cr milestone
items.quote: Our total insurance premium for the quarter was ₹5,123Cr, and that gives us an ARR of ₹20,000Cr, which was also a long -awaited milestone.

items.statement: Renewal premium grew to ₹5,845Cr, renewal rate stable at 69%
items.quote: Our trail revenue, which was ₹577Cr up from ₹388Cr last year. So if you notice, that's almost ₹190Cr growth, and this comes at 85% margin and is a significant source of profit.

items.statement: Persistency at highest ever, porting at ~20% (half of market level), post-Covid increase from mid-teens
items.quote: Our porting of our fresh business is about 20%. So just being crystal clear on that (in that range, approximately 20% and not widely off that). And our persistency on renewals in both number of transactions and pr emium, it is the highest ever

items.statement: Branding cost growth at roughly half of premium growth rate, will grow in new financial year
items.quote: Like Sarbvir said, the brand cost increases roughly, half of the premium increase and as a percentage of revenue, it keeps coming down.

items.statement: Take rate ~16-17%, well below EoM cap of 30-35%, total cost of operations lower than other channels
items.quote: We are at a take rate of about 17-16%, maybe 16%. I don't know of any EoM cap below 30%. And in health it's actually higher, at maybe 35.

items.statement: Paisabazaar credit disbursals ARR ₹14,000Cr, credit cards issuance ₹6 Lakh Cr annualized, credit score base 43Mn
items.quote: We are now at an ARR of ₹14,000Cr on disbursals and about 6 Lacs Cr on issu ance on an annualized basis of Credit Cards. The Credit Score consumer bas e has now increased to

items.statement: Secured loans ~13-15% of disbursals, ~4% of revenue; priority to increase secured contribution
items.quote: Currently a secure d disbursal percentage would be about 13% to 15% on a quarterly basis. And one of our key priorities for this year is to try and increase the secure d growth and hence the secured contribution

items.statement: Carried forward losses of ₹2,100Cr, tax paid on treasury income only
items.quote: Yeah, we have about ₹2,100Cr of carried forward losses. So, of course, as the future years play by, we should get the benefit of those.

items.statement: No formal FY25 guidance given, management expects continued growth but refuses estimates
items.quote: We don't give estimates. Y ou are free to kind of draw your own conclusion. I hope we keep growing. I'll be amazed if we keep growing the way we are

items.statement: Volume growth target of more than 30% for FY25 and FY26
items.quote: The target is around more than 30%.

items.statement: Export revenue target of at least 20% of total revenue for FY25
items.quote: we believe the export should b e at least 20% of our total revenue for the coming year and definitely the endeavor will be to increase it further

items.statement: Export revenue target of 30-35% of total revenue by FY26
items.quote: In FY26 we are targeting between 30% and 35%.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 175 crore over two phases: Phase 1 Rs 115 crore by March 2025, Phase 2 balance by December 2025
items.quote: We announced the CAPEX of Rs. 175 crores over two phases. Phase one, including setting up for capacity to manufacture value fitting solutions and , titanium welded tubes, which is to be completed by March 2025. Phase two includes the capacity expansion for setting up a fitting solution and welded or seamless pipe or tubes by December 2025.

items.statement: Maintenance capex of Rs 15-20 crore annually
items.quote: Apart from that, there can be few more CAPEX, those will be not significant in size. So, would be maintenance sort of CAPEX which can be in the range of Rs. 15 to Rs. 20 crores.

items.statement: Current order book of Rs 240 crore with execution cycle of roughly 100 days
items.quote: That is around Rs. 240 crores, an execution of roughly 100 days, you can say.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA per kg at Rs 64-66; seamless EBITDA per kg ~Rs 85, welded ~Rs 42
items.quote: If you see on a blended basis, it is not Rs. 80, it will be in the range of you can say Rs. 64-Rs. 66 sort of number per kg.

items.statement: Endeavor to maintain or increase blended EBITDA per kg in FY25 despite mix shift toward welded
items.quote: Absolutely. It should also increase revenue.

items.statement: Pricing mechanism is fixed EBITDA per kg
items.quote: It is fixed EBITDA per kg.

items.statement: Strong demand outlook from oil & gas, semiconductor, railways, sewage, desalination and export geographies (US, Middle East, Africa)
items.quote: We are seeing those markets also are good from the revenue perspective. We are trying to cater to the Middle East and other part of the geography in the world. So, we believe the export should b e at least 20% of our total revenue for the coming year and definitely the endeavor will be to increase it further

items.statement: FY25 volume mix expected at 40-43% seamless, balance welded
items.quote: Primarily seamless will be in the range of 40%-43% and balance would be welded.

items.statement: 1 MW solar plant commissioned; expected to reduce power & fuel cost by 8-10%
items.quote: We believe the power and fuel cost that we incurred on the side of electricity we should reduce by another 8% to 10% because of that.

items.statement: Warrant money: 25% received in April 2024
items.quote: The 25% contribution had already been received in the month of April.

items.statement: Minimum 25% loan growth target maintained
items.quote: We are still holding on to that. We haven't said 30%. What we have committed is a minimum of 25% and that continues. Even this past quarter we have exceeded that.

items.statement: ROA expected around 1.8% for FY25 despite elevated credit costs
items.quote: Yes that is our expectation.

items.statement: Credit cost to remain elevated for next two quarters then normalize to 2.5-3%
items.quote: It will be around 2,5% to 3%.

items.statement: NIM expected to remain stable around 10%

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 18-20% for next 3-4 years reiterated, but near-term visibility shortened to 4-5 months due to high coffee prices

items.statement: In-house manufacturing 20% in FY24, expected to rise to 22-23% in FY25; focus on quality and control over contract manufacturing
items.quote: In the last two years it has grown from 17% to 19% to 20%. I think this year should go up to 22 %, 23%. So, that's a kind of incremental that is continuing to happen

items.statement: Logistics cost drag ~2-2.5 percentage points; may bring external consultant to accelerate improvement
items.quote: I think there's at least 2-2.5 percentage sitting just in logistics. So, to me the three leve rs of performance that should drive improvement in the coming year ; one is consumer lighting , secondly, logistics, once we start getting that right

items.statement: Steady inflow of new projects and RFPs seen currently; biotech funding environment improving; new project additions in preclinical, Phase I, and Phase II; quality of projects prioritized over quantity

items.statement: Two active GDS peptide projects: Difelikefalin DMF filing expected later in CY24; GLP-1 asset DMF filing expected in CY26; generic GLP-1 opportunity seen as huge globally, not limited to regulated markets; infrastructure and capacity planni
items.quote: We had two active projects in G DS which we are working on right now. The first one which we expect to file DMF later this year is Difelikefalin which is something that is still on track and that is something that we are excited about. There's another one which is a GLP1 which we are working on for which the DMF will be filed perhaps maybe in 2026.

items.statement: FY24 revenue mix: 80% land sales, 20% project revenue; Q4 mix: 60% land, 40% projects
items.quote: And for the full year, it is roughly around 80% of the sale came from the land and 20% from the projects.

items.statement: One Thaltej commercial project: 1.8 msf, Rs 2,100 crores revenue, start H2 FY25, finish H2 FY28
items.quote: Additionally, a new project, One Thaltej, which is a commercial project is being added to the repertoire in the current year. It is an additional 1.8 million square feet with about Rs. 2,100 crores in revenue. It is expected to start in H2 FY ’25, the second-half of this year, and finished by the second-half of FY ’28, that's just about three years.

items.statement: Malabar Retreat pre-sales: 27-30 apartments, ~Rs 67 crores revenue booked so far
items.quote: And thus we saw very good interest with bookings as of now of up to about 27 to 30 apartments totaling to around Rs. 67 crores and more in revenues and pre-sales.

items.statement: Ahmedabad residential demand rose 21.5% in Q1 calendar 2024 with 1.5% price increase
items.quote: houses demand rose by about 21.5% in the first quarter of this calendar, accompanied by about 1.5% increase in the average property rates

items.statement: Million Minds residential: two phases totalling 1.8 msf launching Q3 and Q4 FY25
items.quote: But in this year FY ‘25, we shall be launching both the phases of residential in Million Minds , one phase being launched in third quarter of this FY ’25, and the s econd phase in the fourth quarter. Together, the development of this is about 1.8 million square feet.

items.statement: Smile City township launch deferred to H1 FY26 to replan around vicinity infrastructure developments
items.quote: Hence we are now thinking that the project will start in H1 of FY ‘26. With all these ongoing and the upcoming projects, the company is set to develop over 5.5 million square feet of area which are under various stages of development.

items.statement: Net debt zero with Rs 230 crores cash surplus as of March 31, 2024; all projects self-funded from internal accruals
items.quote: Our cash flows have been very strong and even after spending for CapEx on the SE Z, as you know we have not raised any money, we are net debt zero. And given various advances for land purchases from our own sources, we still have a cash surplus of Rs. 230 crores as at March 31, 2024.

items.statement: Malabar Exotica: 60% revenue recognized in FY24, balance 40% to be booked in Q1 FY25
items.quote: 60% is already booked and about 40% is what is yet to be booked, which will be booked, mostly this entire 40% will be booked in current financial quarter of FY ‘25.

items.statement: Current inventory ~Rs 421 crores to be sold over 2-3 years
items.quote: See, our current inventory somewhere around Rs. 421 crores, which would be sold over two, three years.

items.statement: Total development pipeline: 5.5 million sq ft under various stages, highest in company history
items.quote: With all these ongoing and the upcoming projects, the company is set to develop over 5.5 million square feet of area which are under various stages of development, making this the highest development at any point in time in the company's history.

items.statement: Malabar Retreat cash flows expected over next 1-2 years; project completion and delivery in following year
items.quote: The bookings can happen over this year or it can even spill over some portion of that the next year. So the cash flows of the entire Retreat project could come in the next one or two years itself. And the last one year is the time when we finish it and deliver it.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of Rs 11 per share (110%), up from previous best of 22%
items.quote: Looking to the robust performance and the healthy cash flows, the Board of Directors has recommended a dividend of Rs. 11 per share, that is 110%, the previous best ever was 22%, and now it is 110%.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue expected to grow much faster than industry; standalone fastener revenue targeted at INR750-800 crores with current capacity
items.quote: At the consolidated level, we hope to grow definitely much faster than the industry.

items.statement: SGEM targets 10-12% EBITDA margin in steady state; improvement expected in coming year
items.quote: We will definitely see an improvement in margins in the coming year, and we continue to make progress towards our stated goal of 10% to 12% EBITDA margins in this business in a steady state.

items.statement: FY25 capex planned at ~INR60 crores for existing fastener and MCU businesses, excluding magnetics JV
items.quote: So overall, we'll be investing around to the tune of about INR60 crores next year. And that's without the -- any investment in the magnetics business. This is only for existing businesses. That's fasteners and motor control units.

items.statement: Fastener revenue split FY24: PV 27%, 2W 24%, CV 22%, Farm 13%, Retail/Aftermarket 12%, Export 2%
items.quote: Passenger vehicle for FY '24 was 27% of the total, 2-wheelers 24%, commercial vehicles 22%, farm 13%, the retail and aftermarkets 12% and 2% export. That's from revenue.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 377 bps YoY in Q4 FY24 due to calibrated price increases and efficient commodity hedging.
items.quote: We continue to witness cross-margin expansion with the improvement of 377 basis points on a year-on-year basis for the quarter 4 of the financial year contributed by calibrated price increase taken earlier and efficient hedging strategy for key commodities.

items.statement: Rural demand recovery is improving and converging with urban; management expects further pickup with good monsoon and macro factors.
items.quote: So our read is that there is improvement in rural recovery. Some of our brands showing it, some of the data from industry has also shown that there is improvement. So we are hopeful it will only get better in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Personal care segment grew double-digit; food and nutrition turned positive with mid-single-digit value growth led by Complan and Sugar Free revival.
items.quote: The personal care segment continues to register strong double-digit growth for the quarter with both Everyuth and Nycil portfolio witnessing a good demand traction. The food and nutrition segment also turned positive and reported a mid-single-digit value growth for the quarter on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Consolidated capex for FY24 was Rs. 489 million.
items.quote: Our consolidated capex for the year was Rs. 489 million.

items.statement: Inflation expected to normalize to manageable 3%-5% range; milk prices stable aiding gross margin improvement.
items.quote: So going forward we expect the inflation to be normal which is a manageable 4%, 5% or 3%, whatever that we've seen over the last 8 to 10 years rather than the extreme inflation that we saw over the last 2 years.

items.statement: Nigeria international business under pressure due to macro-economic and currency issues; recovery expected once sorted.
items.quote: Nigeria which is one of our largest markets has been under pressure in last one year because of the macro-economic and currency issues, demonetization and whole lot of those things. Once that is sorted, we believe one of the strongest equity for our brands is there.

items.statement: Low double-digit revenue growth for FY25 driven by volume from new Max plant and capacity utilization
items.quote: The guidance for next year is that we are looking at a low double-digit growth largely fueled by volume on the back of the new Max plant, which has started, and all the other plants also which are running at capacity.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement of 1-1.5% for FY25, subject to stable gas pricing
items.quote: The EBITDA target for next year or the forward statement for EBITDA is an improvement of another 1% to 1.5% on EBITDA, subject to a stable input, specifically gas pricing.

items.statement: Domestic tile demand growth of 5-6% for FY25, company to grow at double that rate
items.quote: The industry domestically is slated to grow at about 4% to 5%, maybe 6%, and to that extent, we would grow almost at double that rate.

items.statement: Export demand to grow by ₹2,000-3,000 crore in FY25 (base: ₹19,000 crore)

items.quote: capacity utilization has been approximately 86% for the FY '24, down by a percent and a half from FY'23. In Q4, we were up a little bit Q oQ and also YoY by approximately a percent on the YoY. The capacity utilization comes at 89% for the

items.quote: In FY25, we should see a growth of about 20% in the overall volume.

items.quote: And next year, we are targeting to close the AUM at about INR85mn per branch.

items.quote: The gold loan AUM including co-lending AUM stood at INR34.9 billion in March '24.

items.statement: Spreads stable at 6.4% for second consecutive quarter
items.quote: Our spreads were stable at 6.4% for a second consecutive quarter.

items.quote: cost of funds have gone up about 50 bps between Q1 and Q4. Out of that, we were able to pass on partly because some of the loans are semi-fixed in nature and some of the loans are on a floating rate.

items.statement: Affordable housing demand strong; 90% incremental demand from affordable segment
items.quote: If you see the housing demand which is in the affordable housing segment , even the incremental 90% demand is coming from affordable housing.

items.statement: Gold loan share 37% of AUM and ~50% of disbursals in Q4 FY24
items.quote: The share of gold loan AUM was 37% and the share in disbursal was approximately 50% in Q4 as well as FY24, respectively.

items.statement: Co-lending AUM rose to 11.7% of AUM in Q4 FY24 from 8.9% in Q3 FY24
items.quote: Our co-lending AUM continued to rise during Q4 FY24 increasing to 11.7% of AUM compared to 8.9% in Q3 FY24.

items.statement: Construction finance mix to stay at/below 20% of consolidated AUM
items.quote: In construction finance, we will remain guided by our cautious risk management strategy to keep its mix at/or below 20% of consolidated AUM.

items.statement: Gold loan auction triggered at 85-90% LTV mark-to-market
items.quote: And once they reach at 85% to 90%, we do the auction.

items.statement: Dividend approved at 15% per share on INR1 face value for FY24
items.quote: The Board of Directors approved dividend at the rate of 15% per share on the face value of INR1 for FY24.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 maintained at INR 7,500-10,000 crores per annum, subject to EBITDA generation and disciplined balance sheet approach
items.quote: So if you remember 2 quarters ago, we had published our capital allocation policy where we had mentioned that our capex would be in the range of INR 7,500 crore s to INR 10,000 crores depending upon the kind of EBITDA that we earn through the year

items.statement: Remaining capex of INR 15,000 crores to be spent over next 2 years on INR 31,000 crore expansion plan; maintenance capex of INR 2,500 crores annually over and above expansion capex
items.quote: This is close to INR 15,000 crores. So we have spent around 50% we have already spent and 50% we are targeting that over the next 2 years we'll spend.

items.quote: Our steel realization was down by 5% quarter-on-quarter basis. The NSR was lower in both export and domestic markets. As we exit, we see slight uptick in realization by 1% in Q1 of 2025.

items.quote: Further, we are expecting lower price of coking coal in Q1 of '25 by $30 to $40.

items.statement: Volume growth of 11% QoQ to 2.01 MT in Q4 FY24 driven by higher exports (11% vs 3% previous quarter); expect better volume run rate in FY25 vs FY24
items.quote: So we are expecting good volume in the FY '25. So exact numbers, we will not be able to tell you. But certainly, we'll do much better than the financial year '24.

items.statement: HSM on track: hit 3 MT run rate, targeting 3-3.5 MT this year and 6 MT next year; pellet plant ramped to 9,000-10,000 tpd in May; converting semis to value-added flat products
items.quote: HSM is fully on track. We have already hit the run rate for 3 million tonnes. And we will end the year probably, again, it's a forward-looking statement, not saying in particular, b ut this year, 3 to 3.5 million tonnes and next year, 6 million tonnes, that's the target

items.statement: RINL MoU for billet supply continuing; discussions ongoing for higher metallics supply; current quantities not disclosed publicly
items.quote: we are getting supply from RINL for the billets as per our MoU, which i s continuing, and we are expecting that the required quantity will get from the RINL

items.quote: So right now, the Australian mines, we have taken under care a nd maintenance due to certain issues there. So we are not operating that mines. So we have taken impairment of around INR 360 crores

items.quote: Yes. So basically, we have done from the Gare Palma around 1 million tonne and around 0.9 million tonnes from the Utkal C for the Q4, that we can explain.

items.statement: Expect gradual improvement in margins quarter after quarter in FY25 and better financial year overall
items.quote: And accordingly, we hope that in FY'25 we should see the gradual improvement in margins quarter after quarter. And we hope to have better Financial Year FY'25.

items.statement: Capex plan of Rs 100 crores for FY25 to modernize existing facilities and add value-addition capabilities
items.quote: Yes, we have the CAPEX plan for this year for Rs. 100 crores, because we always keep on modernizing our plant and we never let our plants to get outdated.

items.statement: Cotton yarn margins have improved but still not out of the woods due to unexpected cotton price decline
items.quote: There has been improvement in cotton yarn margins, but still it is not out of the woods.

items.statement: Export demand gradually improving; domestic demand expected to pick up after June 15 post-elections
items.quote: So, I think after 15th June the markets will start improving and demand will also improve, and margins will also improve.

items.statement: Green fiber unit operating at full capacity; home textile brand Nesterra has 36 collections and 900 retailers
items.quote: Our strategic investment in the green fiber unit, and that is operating at full capacity, will help us in producing sustainable products and for which the demand is continuously increasing.

items.statement: Home textile capacity utilization at 50% currently, targeting 65% this year with focus on value-added exports to developed markets
items.quote: In home textile, the capacity utilization should be about 65%.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis increasing transit time and freight costs; partially passed to buyers in value-added goods
items.quote: There are two things happening. Number one, the ships are taking more time because they have to go through different route and the ocean freights have also increased.

items.statement: Surrendered expansion land costing Rs 40 crores to avoid forfeiture; paid 20% surrender cost of Rs 8 crores
items.quote: So, it was about Rs. 40 crores, so it was better that we surrendered the land. And land is available, we can always go and take it back.

items.statement: Spinning operating at ~95% capacity utilization; expect similar range in FY25 with minor election-related labor shortage
items.quote: As far as spinning is concerned, it is already operating at about full capacity. Sometimes if the demand for one particular product is little less, there may be 2-3% less utilization in terms of capacity. So, 95% is always being used as of now.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic for FY25 with gradual recovery expected despite geopolitical uncertainties
items.quote: And we are cautiously optimistic for this year. And we definitely feel, it appears to us, that this year a gradual improvement will be there, and we will see better results going forward.

items.statement: Expect healthy growth in FY25 with rural market recovery and aim for double-digit volume growth if monsoon and macro are favorable
items.quote: For FY'24-'25, we are expecting healthy growth. And one of the things which have been slightly an issue was on the rural market. So now we see there's a gradual improvement or pickup in the rural market and the slowdown seems to be now bottoming out.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin of 16% to 17% for full year FY25 while maintaining higher A&P spend and distribution investments
items.quote: Our -- we'll target to have our EBITDA in the range of 16% to 17% for the full year.

items.statement: Normal capex expected at INR40-50 crores per year, new product launches require media spend not significant capex
items.quote: Yes, that normal capex will be to the tune of INR40 crores to INR50 crores year -- per year.

items.statement: A&P spend to sales ratio targeted at 8% to 9% range going forward, reached 9% in FY24
items.quote: we have been aiming to be between 8%, to 9%. And this year, we have reached to 9%. So yes, going forward, that range is what we would look forward for.

items.statement: Rural market slowdown bottoming out with gradual improvement and pickup seen
items.quote: So now we see there's a gradual improvement or pickup in the rural market and the slowdown seems to be now bottoming out.

items.statement: Personal Care grew 18% in Q4 and 21% for full year driven by Margo Neem soap variants, enhancing premium higher-margin portfolio mix
items.quote: Our Neem-based Margo soap with its natural benefit proposition has been delivering a robust performance. Both our base variant and the new variants, which we have launched are doing well.

items.statement: Growth assumption for FY25 is volume-led; pricing growth unpredictable and not factored into full year model
items.quote: See currently, the way things are I think it's better to take the assumption that the growth is more volume-led growth then presuming that there will be some value growth which we can't predict now for the full year.

items.statement: Direct distribution reach expanded to 1.2 million retail outlets from 1.1 million, targeting 8-10% annual expansion to continue in FY25
items.quote: We would like to continue that what we've been doing since last 2 years, 3 years. So yes, mainly 8% to 10%, that would be a good thing to continue.

items.statement: Household Insecticides segment loss increased due to higher ad spend on liquid portfolio shift and new brand ambassador; aim to turn EBIT positive by achieving 50-50 coil-liquid mix
items.quote: We believe if we can get the coil and liquid share maybe by equal 50-50 each, we will be positive in this segment as well.

items.statement: Tax rate expected to remain in 22-23% range for FY25
items.quote: Yes. So our tax rate has been in '22, '23 range for this year and it will continue for the same for the next year too.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guidance of 15-18% for pathology business
items.quote: We are expecting in FY25, the mid teen growth is degrowth that is between 15% and 18% growth is expected.

items.statement: FY25 normalized EBITDA margin guidance of 28-29%

items.statement: FY25 franchise business growth to return to high teens

items.statement: FY25 partnership business growth focus on insurance and hospital segments

items.statement: FY24 consolidated normalized EBITDA margin improved to 28%
items.quote: At a consolidated level, our normalized EBITDA at 28%, which is 1% lower than last year.

items.statement: FY24 standalone normalized EBITDA margin improved by 1% due to gross margin improvement
items.quote: Standalone normalized EBITDA margins for the year improved by 1%, primarily due to the improvement in gross margin.

items.statement: FY24 radiology EBITDA margin declined to 9% due to operational costs and revenue mix
items.quote: EBITDA margin in radiology NHL stood 9% versus 18% year-on-year, mainly due to the increased operational cost and change in revenue mix.

items.quote: We have moved to a slab-based pricing model which we implemented in May 2023. This has led to an increased energy with our franchise network with motivation to move up volumes and enter higher slabs.

items.statement: FY24 core business sample volume growth of 8% YoY, 10% QoQ
items.quote: Our year-on-year, financial year volume growth for the core business is 8% and quarter-on-quarter 10%.

items.quote: Partnership business, which excludes API and B2G for the year showed a phenomenal growth of 23%, whereas in Q4 it showed a tremendous growth of 40%.

items.statement: FY24 franchise business revenue growth of 14% YoY, 13% in Q4

items.statement: FY24 pathology revenue (excluding materials) grew 10% YoY, 16% in Q4
items.quote: pathology business excluding materials and others for the year has grown by 10% year-on-year and in Q4 it is increased by 16% year-on-year

items.statement: FY24 radiology revenue grew 18% YoY
items.quote: Radiology business, including Pulse Hitech for the year did a strong revenue growth of 18% year-on-year.

items.quote: On the billing and revenue outlook for quarter 1, matchmaking and wedding service revenue will be at a similar level of quarter 4.

items.statement: Targeting break-even in wedding services business by end of FY25
items.quote: We hope to achieve a break-even by the end of FY '25 in the wedding services business.

items.quote: As a first in this segment, we have launched Elite Matrimony Kiosk at the airport across three Indian cities, such as Chennai, Bangalore, and Delhi. We expect this initiative will provide added visibility and increased attraction for elite services.

items.statement: Matchmaking EBITDA margin 19.1% in Q4 FY24 vs 18.9% in Q3 FY24 and 21.1% a year ago
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the matchmaking business in Q4 is at 19.1 %, as compared to 18.9 % in quarter 3 and 21.1 % a year ago.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 14.2% in Q4 FY24 vs 14.3% in Q3 FY24 and 15% a year ago
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our EBITDA margins in Q4 are at 14.2%, as compared to 14.3% in quarter 3 and 15% a year ago.

items.quote: For the full year, EBITDA is at INR73.5 crores, which is 15.2 % margins, as compared to INR75 crores, which is 16.2% margins in FY '23, a decline of 2%.

items.quote: Excluding marketing expenses, our margins in matchmaking are stable at 60 % in FY '24, as compared to 61% in FY '23.

So, that way, we don't qualify to be part of the digital services. We are not compatible with a Google billing payment system. So, we are providing additional services, and additional offerings to our customers. Yes, those are the changes.

items.statement: Provision made for disputed Google service fee based on developer agreement; PAT margin would be 300 bps higher without it
items.quote: If not for the disputed Google service fee, which we have provided, our PAT margins would have been better by about 300 basis points.

items.statement: Launched Jodi for non-degree holders in Tier 2/3 cities; free for females, vernacular support

First in this segment to target the people who are non-degree holders because majority of the people are non-degree holders in Tier 2, Tier 3. Now we have Jodi which is a very simple product free for females and targeting diploma, plus 2 and below non -degree holders.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit fan growth of 15-20% CAGR vs industry single-digit growth

items.statement: Expect EBITDA improvement within two quarters as investments bear fruit

items.statement: Hyderabad plant commissioned May 6 with capacity to more than double current fan sales
