items.quote: In this quarter, I'm happy to report that we've also done façade lighting at -- in Dwarka, the Sudarshan Setu that our honorable Prime Minister had inaugurated just a few weeks ago.

items.statement: Price hike taken from April to cover EPR liability of INR 21-22 crore in FY25
items.quote: We believe it will be for the year that we are in FY '25, which will be perhaps around INR21 crores, INR22 crores, in that range, but it should not hit our P&L because we should be able to recover this cost from the market.

items.statement: Fan demand very strong in April-May as heat builds up after extended winter
items.quote: As the heat built up in the month of April and now, we are seeing in May, the demand for fans is very, very strong in the market, which is definitely good news.

items.statement: Direct-to-market states grew 46% in Q4 and 65% for full year; now 30% of sales
items.quote: As we speak, our Direct-to-Market sales have already reached about 30% of our sales done through double trade -- about 30%.

items.statement: South India now 32% of revenue, grew 33% in FY24
items.quote: In our Grow South project, I'm delighted to report that in this year, our overall sales, 32% of our overall sales are now coming from Southern India.

items.statement: Lighting price erosion close to bottoming out, may last 2 more quarters at low single-digit rate
items.quote: Going forward, I think the right term to use is, perhaps close to bottoming out, not bottomed out yet. And I don't think that the erosion should last more than 2 quarters from now.

items.statement: McKinsey engagement ending; variable pay component to be paid in Q1 FY25, then cost savings
items.quote: The last component of the variable pay will get paid out in the month of -- sorry, in this very quarter, in the very first quarter itself. So by -- so that will be accounted for in Q1 of FY '25.

items.statement: CEO search nearing completion; announcement to follow decision
items.quote: I think we're getting close to the end of the search. And soon, once the decision has been made, obviously, we'll need to make a public announcement, we will make it.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin historically 20-22%; peak not yet reached as Patalganga ramp-up continues
items.quote: we know that 20 %-22% has always been our sustainable EBITDA margin, which we have always achieved, except that FY23

items.statement: Thailand plant trial production commissioning targeted by end of June 2024
items.quote: they are planning to start the commissioning latest by June end

items.statement: SEZ land allotment letter awaited; EC application after allotment, EC approval within 6 months, then plant construction
items.quote: Once we get the allotment letter, then only we can apply for EC. Once we apply for EC and once we get the EC, which should be also as early as possible, maximum 6 months and then we will be able to start the building up of the plant

items.statement: Patalganga food grade facility full ramp-up expected to take another 2-4 years from March 2022 start
items.quote: it will take another 2 , 3, 4 years. I don't know exactly, but not so soon

items.statement: Raw material prices stable, demand similar to Q4 FY24 in April-May; Europe weak, other regions recovering
items.quote: the raw material prices are quite stable and demands are also almost more or less similar like last quarter, as at least in April-May I am seeing that

items.statement: Europe still not back on track; other international markets returning to normal but not to FY22 levels
items.quote: Europe is still not back on track. Other markets, I don't remember the demand in 22 and all that 2 years is going to remember all such things. So, now it is returning to normal

items.statement: No deliberate product mix shift; mix changes driven by market demand differences between domestic and export
items.quote: We don't make such changes by ourselves. It is depending on the market situation

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement due to stable raw material prices not rising as expected
items.quote: EBITDA margin has increased because the raw material prices didn't go up . Normally, the raw material prices go up, but the prices don't go up, and the raw material prices are much better than we expected

items.statement: Key export challenges: global slowdown (Europe), Red Sea crisis increasing lead time 1-1.5 months, long regulatory approval timelines, difficulty acquiring land for chemical industry
items.quote: Right now, there are challenges, especially one is the global slowdown. Now the world is coming back to normal, except Europe. Everything else is getting slowly , it i s getting normal. That is number one. That is the one challenge. Second is this Red Sea crisis and all that

items.statement: Cash reserves ~Rs 900 Cr in FDs (avg yield ~7%) earmarked for SEZ capex, potential acquisitions, and overseas plant; further borrowing likely needed
items.quote: The surplus has increased approximately somewhere to Rs. 900 Cr, currently there is the cash on the books in the line in the fixed deposits

items.statement: Acquisition strategy targets profitable companies with complementary product range, chemistry, markets and customers; not financially driven
items.quote: We are looking at good companies having good product range and good infrastructure suitable to us, nothing more than that. We don't look from the financial point

items.statement: Long-term contract structure unchanged: 3 months to 1 year for both sales and raw materials
items.quote: Globally, as I told you earlier with our customers, they are ranging from 3 months to 6 months to 1 year and for raw materials also for some products, some raw materials, it is 3 months, 6 months and for some raw materials it is 1 year

items.statement: New product commercialization takes 3-4 years after development for regulatory and customer approvals; monetization limited to spare capacity at Patalganga
items.quote: whatever is being developed today will come on commercialization only after 3-4 years after we get all the regulatory, regional, and customer approvals

items.statement: Spencer's Retail targets INR75-85 crore EBITDA improvement in FY25, split 50% from cost savings and 50% from top-line growth
items.quote: And the number which I mentioned was close to a three-digit mark. So, I mean, for close to INR75 to INR85 crores is the potential for our EBITDA improvement.

items.statement: Consolidated top-line growth expected at 8-10% in FY25 driven by mid-single-digit SSSG and ~10% trading area expansion
items.quote: So would it be a fair assessment, like 8 %-10% of a top-line growth can be expected at a consol level? Anuj Singh: I think I won't second guess your math. I think you've done the math

items.statement: Plan to add ~100,000 sq ft combined trading area across Spencer's and Nature's Basket in FY25 (~10% expansion)
items.quote: But roughly about 100,000 square feet combined is the kind of additional trading area which will be added next year, which is about 10%.

items.statement: Operating cost reduction of 7-8% expected from organizational restructuring done in Q4 FY24
items.quote: I will not be able to quantify I think, but it is anywhere in the region of 7% to 8% of total operating costs would come from that exercise.

items.statement: Spencer's gross margin flat at 18.1% in Q4 FY24; focus on revenue growth over margin expansion
items.quote: Our margins, which are at 18%, the thing will, we are, it's not that we are not, wanting an expansion in margins, but we are, I would say that our number one priority is to drive growth.

items.statement: Nature's Basket margins improved 120 bps in Q4 FY24 to 30%+ levels
items.quote: Nature's Basket delivered healthy 12% growth, basis of reinvigoration of certain categories like fresh, but more importantly, the launch of three new stores and a dramatic expansion in margins, which were about 120 ba sis point improved

items.statement: Q4 FY24 consolidated LFL growth of 3% YoY after netting closed stores; H2 FY24 showed growth vs H1 decline
items.quote: But if you look at it netting off the impact of the closed stores and dispensers' part of the business, it is a 3% LFL like-for-like growth on a year-on-year basis, along with a slight expansion in gross margins.

items.statement: Non-food mix at ~20%; will rebalance space toward food/fresh categories and optimize apparel allocation
items.quote: Today our non-food mix is 20% roughly. If you look at some of our stores I think in the past, I'll be honest, in a quest to increase that, we have probably given a far higher allocation to non-food.

items.statement: Fresh category focus to drive customer frequency and retention; core food portfolio (staples, FMCG, fresh) to be powered
items.quote: I Spencer’s think the category which where we will focus on and which is also strategic for us as part of the overall food offering is the fresh category

items.statement: Expanding Wholesale Bazaar B2B format selectively; e-commerce express delivery (60-min) launched in Kolkata, Varanasi, Lucknow; not pursuing quick commerce
items.quote: We will be expanding the Wholesale Bazaar. I won't say in a very proliferated manner, but in a very carefully selected manner. We will have a couple of more Wholesale Bazaars which will drive our B2B business.

items.statement: E-commerce at 12-12.5% of mix; express delivery grew orders 30% in Kolkata; store-based fulfillment model leverages density
items.quote: Our overall e-commerce orders in Calcutta have gone up by 30%, and of course you do see the surges, last couple of weeks we had an extreme, heat wave in Calcutta, and we saw that the number of orders, do spike up.

items.statement: Equity infusion up to INR300 crore approved for growth capex, capability building, and near-term debt repayment; modality/timing TBD
items.quote: The fundraise will not be just utilized for a specific purpose. It will be for managing all three.

items.statement: Seven to eight new stores in pipeline for FY25 in Eastern UP and East clusters; expansion judicious and concentric
items.quote: We have seven, eight in the pipeline already for the year which are in Eastern UP as well as in the East.

items.statement: Building capabilities in precision marketing/CRM, supply chain forecasting/inventory management, and e-commerce technology
items.quote: Three areas which I would like to kind of call out are the ones where we need to beef up our capabilities is one is in this whole area of precision marketing what I spoke about in customers.

items.statement: Leadership team refreshed in last 6 months: new CMO, Head of Operations, Marketing Head, CFO, Head of Supply Chain
items.quote: we've had just in the last si x months, I would say, we brought in a new chief me rchandising officer, we had a new head of operations, we had a marketing head

items.statement: Earmarked over INR2,000 crores as capital to be invested over the next 3 years for portfolio expansion including ~870 rooms and an office tower in Powai.
items.quote: We continue to expand our portfolio. Our current plan involves adding approximately 870 more rooms to our portfolio along with an additional office tower in Powai. To fuel this growth, we earmarked over INR2,000 crores as capital to be invested over the next 3 years.

items.statement: Capex plan of around INR15 billion for next 2 years for announced projects, largely funded through internal accruals.
items.quote: The company has capex plan of around INR15 billion for next 2 years for the announced project, which will be largely funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: Spending around INR1,500 crores for next 2 years, including INR700 crores for new commercial tower in Powai and spillover capex for commercial towers in Powai and Bengaluru.
items.quote: On capex, we'll be spending around INR1,500 crores for next 2 years. Out of that, around INR700 crores for commercial tower INR650 crores, INR700 crores at the new commercial tower, which we are adding in Powai.

items.statement: Hospitality EBITDA margin of 47.8% in Q4 FY24, up 30 bps YoY; same-store margin at 48.4% with 80 bps expansion for the quarter and 300 bps for the year.
items.quote: The quarter also delivered one of the highest EBITDA margin of 47.8%, with an expansion of 30 bps despite the new inventory, which is getting stabilized and some inventory is under renovation.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA surpassed INR6 billion mark with 42% margin for full year FY24.
items.quote: I'm pleased to announce that on a consolidated level, the company's EBITDA surpassed the INR6 billion mark with an EBITDA margin of 42%.

items.statement: ADR grew 5% YoY to INR11,862 in Q4 FY24; same-store ADR growth was 8% YoY; full year ADR growth was 17% at INR10,718.
items.quote: Q4 record ed new highs in average room rates at INR 11,862, which is up 5% over the previous year. It is up by 8% on a same-store basis

items.statement: Industry has upside of double-digit rate growth going forward; Chalet delivered 17% rate growth in FY24 and will continue to work at industry rate growths.
items.quote: We believe the industry has an upside of double-digit rate growth going forward. And to reiterate, we have delivered 17% rate growth this year.

items.statement: Robust demand pickup in Q3 FY24 continued into Q4, led by corporate travel, MICE, weddings and social events; occupancies improved 2% YoY to 76%.
items.quote: For Chalet, the robust pickup of demand seen in Q3 FY '24 continued into the next quarter in Q4, largely led by corporate travel, MICE, weddings and social events.

items.statement: Supply and demand expected to outstrip supply for at least next 2-4 years; ADR growth will moderate after some time on higher base.
items.quote: I think we've got at least for the visible future, which is the next 2 to 3, 4 years, supply and demand is expected to outstrip supply. Beyond that, it's very difficult to predict now.

items.statement: Pipeline: 125-room addition at Marriott Whitefield by end FY25 (520 total); Dukes Lonavala upgrade to ~145 keys by end CY24; Taj Delhi Airport ~390 keys opening FY26; Hyatt Regency Airoli ~280 keys opening FY27; CIGNUS 2 commercial tower co
items.quote: With strong recovery in Bangalore, we are looking forward to the 125 -room addition at the Marriott Whitefield, taking the inventory up to 520 rooms by end of FY '25. The Dukes Retreat in Lonavala is undergoing a major upgradation and repositioning. The res ort will have a final inventory of approximately 145 keys, and we look forward to welcoming guests to that hotel by end of this calendar year.

items.statement: Election impact limited to election days in respective cities; no significant government business in portfolio; travel may slow on election days in base and destination cities.
items.quote: So if I am in Delhi and I got my election happening in Delhi that day, I'd like to vote, I'd probably not travel out of Delhi. Similarly, if I have to travel to Mumbai and Mumbai elections are happening on that particular day, I may not want to travel to Mu mbai because we know the city will largely be slow on that day

items.statement: Utilities cost at all-time low of 4.1% of revenue through green power sourcing and energy-efficient equipment upgrades.
items.quote: Through our constant efforts to sourcing green power and upgrading infrastructure with energy-efficient equipment, we have achieved an all-time low utilities cost, which is 4.1% of revenue, creating new benchmark for the industry.

items.statement: Revenue target of ₹200 Bn by FY26 under Project LEAP; new mid-term goal plan to be unveiled during current financial year
items.quote: We are swiftly approaching our project LEAP target of achieving an annual turnover of ₹ 200 Bn. As previously communicated, we will unveil our new mid -term goal plan during the course of the current financial year.

items.statement: Capex of ₹8.6 Bn in FY24; ₹10-11 Bn each year for next 2-3 years to expand capacities
items.quote: In FY24, we allocated ₹ 8.6 Billion towards capex. Over the next 2-3 years, we will be investing between ₹ 10 Bn & 11 Bn, each year, to expand our capacities.

items.statement: EHV plant at Halol (~20% of capex) operational by end FY26, revenue contribution from FY27; asset turnover 5x-6x at peak
items.quote: almost 20% of the capex that I just mentioned, will go towards the EHV manufacturing plant in Halol. This will have an asset turnover of 5x to 6x at peak capacity. The plant is expected to become operational by the end of FY26, contributing to the company's top line from FY27 onwards.

items.statement: EPC open order book of ~₹48-50 Bn to be executed over next 3-4 years, largely from RDSS scheme
items.quote: We have an open order book of almost ₹48 billion in that business which we have to complete over the next 3 years to 4 years.

items.statement: Cables & Wires sustainable EBIT margin 12-13%; Q4 FY24 consolidated EBITDA margin 13.6%, FY24 13.8%
items.quote: we believe that about 12% to 13% is the margin profile that we should be able to consistently deliver on the cables and wires business.

items.statement: EPC sustainable operating margin expected in mid-to-high single digits over mid-to-long term
items.quote: Annual sustainable operating margin in this business is expected to be in high single digit over mid-to-long term.

items.statement: Robust pricing mechanism absorbs copper/aluminium price rises; no material impact on gross margins or growth expected
items.quote: we have a very robust pricing mechanism within the industry. And we have not seen any material impact of any such rise in copper prices or aluminium prices in the past. So, we believe that even this shouldn't have any form of material impact on neither on our gross margins or on growth.

items.statement: Strong demand outlook driven by infrastructure upcycle, private capex, highways, railways, power, renewables, PLI; demand sufficient for all players
items.quote: across all of these sectors, we see enough and more demand coming in over the course of next five to ten years. And as a result, we believe there is need for more capacities from domestic players.

items.statement: Cables & Wires volume growth 30-40% YoY in Q4 and FY24; cables growing faster (high 30s) than wires (low 30s); LDC cables growing faster than HDC
items.quote: The domestic Cables & Wires business registered a volume growth of between 30% to 40%, both for quarter four as well as for the entire year.

items.statement: Income Tax search: no tax demand notice or order issued; company confident of compliance and cooperating fully
items.quote: As of the present date, we want to emphasize that no tax demand notice or any other order has been issued to us by the Income Tax department.

items.statement: International business transition to distribution model in US (largest geography) to take 3-5 quarters to stabilize; Middle East 60% of Q4 international sales; target 10% of consolidated revenue by FY26
items.quote: We believe this transition will take another 3 -5 quarters to stabilize. During this time, we expect business from other geographies to continue to show robust

items.statement: FMEG turnaround expected by end of calendar year 2024; merging B2C verticals under one head, decentralizing decisions, closing execution gaps in distribution, NPD, influencer management
items.quote: We anticipate the process to be completed by the end of this calendar year, post which we expect the FMEG business to start growing at a rate better than industry averages.

items.statement: Cables & Wires capacity utilization in mid-70s% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: largely combined for cables and wires, we were operating in mid-70s during the quarter.

items.statement: EHV plant technology tie-up with large international player; product and EPC approvals expected before FY27 commercial sales
items.quote: Yes, we have tied up with a large international player. It is a tie up to get the technology for manufacturing that EHV cables.

items.statement: Expects subsidiary HALS revenue ~Rs. 800 cr in 2-3 years based on past asset turns of 2.5-2.7x
items.quote: our asset turn h as been close to 2.5 to 2.7, so based on the investment which we have already made, hopefully in the next 2 years to 3 years, the topline should be closer to Rs. 800 crores based on the investments which we have already made this is again as per our past records

items.statement: Incurred highest ever capex of Rs. 235 cr in FY24 including Rs. 215 cr in subsidiary CFCL
items.quote: We have incurred the highest CAPEX in the history of Company of approximately Rs. 235 crores during FY24 ; this includes investment in subsidiary of Rs. 215 crores.

items.statement: Pharma Intermediate capex of Rs. 30 cr to start in Q3 FY25; additional Rs. 150 cr for Performance Chemicals pending pilot outcomes
items.quote: Rs. 30 crores is the CAPEX for Pharma Intermediate which will start in Q3, an additional Rs. 150 crores CAPEX is based on the pilot runs which we are running as soon as we are successful the additional Rs. 150 crores CAPEX will be made and announcement will also be made for the same.

items.statement: Next leg of capex being firmed up based on trial run outcomes for new performance products; will announce capital commitment in due course
items.quote: we are progressively positive on our trial runs for our new products u nder performance segment and we are in process of f irming up next leg of CAPEX as we analyze more outcomes of these trial runs. We will announce the capital commitment accordingly towards the new projects in due course of

items.statement: No long-term contracts; business runs on monthly/quarterly basis for UV stabilizers targeting Indian market first
items.quote: We don't work like a long-term contract on these businesses. These are quarterly basis businesses or monthly basis businesses because primarily our first markets are Indian market where these UV stabilizers will be sold, so these are decided on monthly or on quarterly basis.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated EBITDA margin steady at 43% despite 16% revenue decline; Q4 margin 44%
items.quote: Despite decline in revenue and product diversification, Company reported steady EBITDA margin of 43% for the full year FY24, which is in line with FY23.

items.statement: Subsidiary HALS margins targeted at ~15% in FY25 due to unabsorbed overheads; medium-term target ~25% at full utilization
items.quote: on blended basis for this year we a re not targeting more than 15% for the subsidiary, for the new products in the subsidiary which is namely HALS

items.statement: Pharma Intermediate margins expected to be better than HALS 25% medium-term target
items.quote: I think that would be better, much better.

items.statement: HALS 770 sold at 2.5-3% discount to imported pricing in India with just-in-time supply advantage; global discount ~5% max
items.quote: Typically, this product discount of 2.5% to 3% because we give that advantage of not letting them stock the material. We can do just-in-time supplies which our competitors cannot.

items.statement: HALS 701 discount <5% globally as first non-Chinese producer; blended HALS realization now $7-8/kg vs earlier $9 guidance
items.quote: 7 to 8 now on blended basis , so 770 cheap, 944 is expensive, 119 is expensive , so on blended basis it is $8 you can assume.

items.statement: Volume recovery across all segments in H2 FY24; Q4 volumes surpassed pre-destocking levels; FY25 volume growth from new plants and Pharma Intermediate from Q3
items.quote: Quarter 4, we have seen a lot of volume growth coming back. Now next volume growth for FY25 will all be from the newer plants and the new Pharma Intermediate which will start in quarter 3.

items.statement: New products contribution rose to 23% in FY24 from 18.5%; HALS 770/701 showing sequential 40% volume growth; 770 at ~50% India market share targeting 70-80%
items.quote: Further new product contribution increased to 23% from 18.5%.

items.statement: HALS 701 approved with major global accounts; targeting 1,000 tpa in 3-5 months; 770 at 100-110 tpm in India; next products 622, 944, 119, 2020 launching in 3-4 weeks
items.quote: we have now started giving trial orders or commercial shipments to all our customers and I think over the next 3 months to 5 months-time frame, we should reach a decent volumes of about a 1,000 ton per annum basis, so that remains in 701.

items.statement: China has added capacities across chemical segments but not seen in Clean Science's specific product range; must keep pricing competitive to deter conventional process competition
items.quote: In our range, I have not seen any Chinese in this particular range and hence our volumes have remained intact in the China market. Of course, there is always a conventional process which the competitor can take to produce our products and hence we have to keep pricing in a manner that we are still more competitive for the buyers to buy.

items.statement: Export market ramp-up slower due to approval processes and distributor appointments; US market may take longer; targeting 200 tpm by March 2025
items.quote: export market typically takes a little longer because the approval process then appointing right distributors , stocking the material in USA , so USA could take a little longer though I would love that things should move as fast as possible, but touching 200 tons by next March should be doable.

items.statement: Tax rate: Clean Science standalone 25%, subsidiary 15% for FY25 calculations
items.quote: Clean Science is 25% while Subsidiary is 15%.

items.statement: Plan to double Blinkit store count in next 12 months, mostly in top 7-8 cities
items.quote: Broadly what we are saying is that the store count will double from here over the next 12 months and most of those stores will come in the top 7-8 cities.

items.statement: Food delivery GOV growth guided at 20%+
items.quote: We expect that as the business GOV continues to grow 20%+ (which we have guided on), that will likely be a combination of some AOV increase and order volume increase and majority of the order volume increase would come from transacting customers growing.

items.statement: Blinkit to remain at least EBITDA neutral during aggressive expansion
items.quote: Our attempt is to keep reinvesting back into the business to grow as fast as possible while maintaining neutrality on the EBITDA side - that's our strategy.

items.statement: Store expansion guidance includes element of hope, not all 500 stores tied up
items.quote: Having said that, Vivek, in all our guidance, there is some element of hope. So it's not like we have everything tied up for these 500 stores. But we are fairly hopeful that this is a realistic target to take for the next year.

items.statement: Each top metro can eventually support 500 stores, runway beyond 12 months
items.quote: And from a more long-term perspective, each of these 4/5 top metros can easily have, for example, 500 stores each. So that runway on store expansion will continue fairly meaningfully beyond the next 12 months.

items.statement: Hyperpure EBITDA margin improved from -9% to -2% YoY, improvement to continue but focus on growth
items.quote: Similarly, on the margin front, if you look at the last five to seven quarters, directionally, the EBITDA margins have improved from negative 9% in Q4 last year to negative 2% now, and we expect that change to continue.

items.statement: Blinkit take rate increased 1 percentage point in Q4, upward trend expected to continue
items.quote: The take rate has increased by one percentage point in this quarter. And it's a composite number, including product margin, ad income, and delivery charges. And at this point, we expect each of these to contribute towards the growth in take rate.

items.statement: Blinkit charges INR 20 per delivery, will not discount to compete, focus on service quality
items.quote: Our focus is to build a valuable service that customers actually are willing to pay more for rather than trying to provide an inferior service and leaning on discounting to grow.

items.statement: Delhi NCR 7% sequential growth not concerning, seasonality and store mix impact, no demand saturation
items.quote: So Ashwin, there is seasonality also involved here. The overall business grew at 14%, and most of our new stores in this quarter were actually non-Delhi NCR. So, to that extent, 7% growth is not bad according to us. There's no saturation here in terms of demand or anything.

items.statement: Zomato Everyday expanding to Mumbai and Bengaluru over next few months, slow gradual expansion
items.quote: Right now, it's largely in Gurgaon, but over the next few months, we'll see maybe Mumbai and Bengaluru being added as cities where we'll launch Everyday, and then we'll take it from there in terms of other cities that we want to expand in.

items.statement: Top worries: maintaining innovation pace and team mindset to keep innovating daily
items.quote: Vivek, we have to innovate on behalf of our customers. And we have to be paranoid about not falling behind on that innovation ladder. Because we believe that our business is all about constantly making things better, constantly innovating, getting better products to the market.

items.statement: ESOP pool expanded by 2%, expected to last 5+ years for leadership and employee incentives
items.quote: But we just wanted to expand that a little bit by 2% right now and we believe then with that, we should be good for the next 5 years at least or more in terms of adequately incentivizing our leadership and generally employees at Zomato and Blinkit.

items.statement: ESOP cost will increase from INR 161 crores quarterly run rate going forward
items.quote: Yes, it will increase from INR 161 crores for sure going forward.

items.statement: Blinkit MTCs expected to cross Zomato MTCs, no specific timeline given
items.quote: Absolutely. I think that seems like it will happen.

items.statement: Targets 25% revenue growth for FY25 with H2 weighted growth due to CDMO ramp-up
items.quote: I firmly believe we will sustain our growth trajectory target, targeting for a revenue growth of 25% for the year FY '25.

items.statement: Expects H1:H2 revenue split of 40:60 in FY25 vs historical 45:55 due to CDMO commercialization in H2
items.quote: Now, given we are expecting CDMO contract commercializing in H2 FY '25, the split will readjust to 40:60 ratio.

items.statement: FY25 capex guided at INR250 crores including INR70 crores for Ankleshwar Unit 2, INR100 crores for electrolyte additives, INR50 crores for solar plant
items.quote: For the year FY '25, we are expecting capex to be around INR250 crores. Split of the current capex will be, around INR70 crores is the pending capex of Ankleshwar Unit 2; around INR100 crores capex related to electrolyte additive and related infrastructure; and INR50 crores capex towards the captive solar power plant.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected similar to FY25 for maintenance, no additional project capex decided yet
items.quote: And similarly the -- similar capex is expected for FY '26 also for maintenance. For any additional project capex, we have not yet decided or announced any capex as of now.

items.statement: Existing CDMO project expected to ramp up from H2 FY25 with confirmed order in hand
items.quote: I would like to highlight that our existing CDMO project is expected to ramp up from second half of FY '25 onwards with a confirmed order in hand.

items.statement: Firm order in hand for electrolyte additives with supplies starting Q2 FY25
items.quote: We have a firm order in our hand, and supplies are expected to slowly start it from Q2FY '25 onwards.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin at 19.2%, up 326 bps sequentially; target to return to historical 21% base margin
items.quote: As guided in previous conference call, EBITDA margin continued strong sequential growth trend, coming in at 19.2% for the quarter, which is down by 269 basis points on Y-o-Y basis and expansion of 326 basis points on a sequential basis.

items.statement: First target is to go back to previous base margin of 21%, then see steady-state growth
items.quote: So, Jason, as we have explained earlier also, our first target is to go back to our previous base margin of 21%.

items.statement: Raw material prices stabilized, final product prices stable with upward bias expected in H2 FY25
items.quote: Raw material prices have stabilized, indicating stability in final product prices with an upward bias expected in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Export demand gradually recovering with robust uptick expected in H2 FY25
items.quote: Export demand is gradually recovering with expectations for a robust uptick in the second half of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Electrolyte additives business to grow 100% in FY26 on FY25 base with capacity expansion
items.quote: The ramp-up will be slow in FY '25, but we expect to grow this business by 100% in FY '26 on FY '25 base with capacity expansion of electrolyte additives business.

items.statement: Apixaban to grow strongly from H2 FY25, peak in FY26-27 at generic launch; part of 26+ DMFs
items.quote: Apixaban is a strong product for us, and it will be definitely growing starting from H2 FY '25, and it will be going to peak on FY '26-'27, at the time of launching for the generics.

items.statement: Baba Fine Chem integration delayed due to customer vendor qualification process; expected to complete in H1 FY25
