items.statement: Restructuring discussions ongoing with no decision on delisting or REIT; no timeline provided; small REIT regulations under review but prima facie for unlisted companies.
items.quote: There is no decision at all on which option we are going to take. We've never put forward any information that says that we've agreed on delisting or on something other than a delisting.

items.statement: Company will stay in old tax regime due to MAT credit (~Rs. 25 crores remaining, to run down in ~2 years); moving to new regime offers nominal benefit vs restructuring benefits under old regime.
items.quote: The company has decided to stay with the old tax regime for the present. This is primarily due to the accumulated MAT credit available for set-offs in the old tax regime.

items.statement: Debt has 3 years remaining of interest-only moratorium (linked to T-bills), then 25% repayment over years 6-10, then 75% bullet at year 10.
items.quote: We have a 5-year moratorium on our debt where we pay interest only. Out of that, two years is over so far, so we have three more years of interest only. Then we have a situation where we pay 25% of the debt between years 6 and 10.

items.statement: Nirlon House restructuring complex due to 9-10 owners; no advanced stage discussions; Nirlon's share mostly licensed out; will update when significant progress.
items.quote: We have not really said at any point in time that any discussions are at an advanced stage. So what I said earlier on the call, is because of the profile of the asset, which is owned by multiple owners, these discussions and what we would like to do is definitely going to take some time.

items.statement: Nirlon Management Services contract renewed on similar terms; no development fees as no significant development envisaged.
items.quote: the new terms are very s imilar to the existing contract, of course, because there is no significant development envisaged in NL at this point in time. There are no development fees as part of the new contract

items.statement: Fair value of property per INDAS is Rs. 4,500 crores as of March 31, 2024; management does not publish market valuation.
items.quote: The valuation of the company as on 31st March is approximately Rs. 4,500 crores. Kunal Sagar: It is not a market value. This is the fair value in our annual report, as we are required to present it

items.statement: Maintain 15-20% EPS growth and 18% ROE targets
items.quote: At this time, we will stay with 15% to 20% EPS growth, and 18% ROE.

items.statement: Auto segment Rs 27,000 crore capex over next 5 years, self-funded
items.quote: For auto, it will take a bulk of that which is Rs. 27,000 crores. EV is 12,000 but w e are not giving up on ICE. ICE is still very important and ICE is going to continue to be a mainstay for the next few years and therefore ICE will continue to get Rs. 14,000 crores of CAPEX in this time period

items.statement: Farm segment Rs 5,000 crore investment over next 3 years
items.quote: For farm, we've got Rs. 5,000 crores that we've outlined right now, again, driving some of the growth in the farm business.

items.statement: Services segment Rs 5,000 crore investment over next 3 years
items.quote: And services again we've outlined 5000 crores right now. As Mahindra finance grows, it will need capital to fund its growth but beyond that our growth gems are doing well and we will put more capital there.

items.statement: Auto capacity expansion from 49,000 to 64,000/month by end FY25, then to 72,000
items.quote: We exited March at 49,000 capacity. By end of F25, we should be at 64. The breakup of 64 increase, which is the 15,000 number, is 5,000 between Thar 5 -door an d XUV 3XO and 10,000 which is the first lot of the born electric capacity

items.statement: SUV booking backlog at 220,000 including 50,000 XUV 3XO first-hour bookings
items.quote: The booking number at this point of time stands at 220,000, this is now upgraded or updated to only add the first hour of XUV 3XO bookings which is 50,000.

items.statement: Target mid to high teen growth in FY25 for auto
items.quote: We are very confident on mid to high teen growth rate in F25. We stay with that.

items.statement: Farm sector expected to grow at plus 5% in FY25
items.quote: On a balance we think the year will grow at plus 5%.

items.statement: Core tractor margin at 17.7% for FY24, 17.6% in Q4 despite volume reduction
items.quote: The core tractor margin has gone up to 17.7 for the year. But interestingly when you see the quarter trend, in the quarter the core tractor margin is 17.6.

items.statement: Auto margin balancing growth and margin, new launches start with lower margins
items.quote: For every new launch, there will be lower margins. So, the 3X0 also at the start will have lower margins and what it will go up, the Thar 5 door will be coming in will have the same thing.

items.statement: EV percentage margins lower than ICE due to lower GST
items.quote: The percentage for electric will be lower because GST is far lower. So, while the same if you let's say you have the same margin on an ICE vehicle and an electric vehicle, the percentage margin will be lower on electric because the GST is lower.

items.statement: CAFE III norms may require 15-25% EV penetration by 2027-28
items.quote: Our guess is 15% to 25%.

items.statement: BII and Temasek committed Rs 2,700 crore for EV business, additional Rs 725 crore from BII under review
items.quote: BII has already put in 1200 crores, Temasek has put in 300 and they will put in their additional 900 to hit 1200. But beyond that, we had an additional Rs. 725 crore transfer from BII.

items.statement: Mahindra Finance AUM reached Rs 1 lakh crore, grew 24%, GS3 at 3.4%
items.quote: It has reached one lakh crore of assets under management. Assets under management grew at 24%. In a year that has seen interest rates go up, in a year where we cut back on certain segments and did not lend to them because we wanted to improve asset quality and therefore even more importantly asset quality is up significantly and you see the GS3 numbers having come down to 3.4% now.

items.statement: Tech Mahindra turnaround expected over 2-3 years after 52% profit decline
items.quote: It will take a 2-to-3 year time period for the full turnaround, but there's a clear part that has been outlined. The impact for this year was negative where profit was down 52% from the prior year, but that's something that we see recovering very well over the next two to three years.

items.statement: Tractor industry growth expectation for FY25 is 5% with potential upside
items.quote: So, right now I think 5% will be a good starting point. But hopefully there will be more upside triggers to that than what we are taking on board.

items.statement: EV capex for FY25-27 estimated at Rs 12,000 crores in addition to Rs 4,000 crores already spent
items.quote: And now, having gone through that in detail, the estimate for the next 3 years is 12,000 in addition to the 4000 that we had.

items.statement: XUV 3XO capacity is 9,000 per month, scalable to 10,500 with minimal investment
items.quote: We did say that the capacity we have is 9000 a month, which is higher than the XUV300 capacity. That was part of that 49,000 to 55,000 that you saw on that slide. So, we said we have 9000 and with the very short lead time and a very minimal investment, it can go up to 10,500.

items.statement: XUV 3XO received 50,000 bookings with gasoline 65-70%, diesel ~30%, automatic ~20%
items.quote: I think early numbers are gasoline is 65%-70% and diesel is about 30%. I don't know the automatic you have. I don't ha ve that number yet. So, this is the only one I have right now, automatic about 20

items.statement: Tractor demand optimism for H2 FY25 driven by positive farmer terms of trade and monsoon
items.quote: There is a lot of optimism about how second half can bounce back very strongly. So, it's too early to call, but April was better than what we thought and hopefully we will see a better than 5% growth as we go along.

items.statement: XUV 3XO attracting new customers: 25% first-time buyers, 25% hatchback upgraders, 15% existing Mahindra owners
items.quote: So, the one data that we have not out of the 50,000 but the first lot of inquiries and test drives that were going on is 25% no vehicle ownership out of the first lot of people 25% hatch. So, it's a very different and only 15% Mahindra ownership out of the first lot of customers coming in.

items.statement: TREM 5 implementation in 2026 very unlikely; if implemented would cause significant FY25 volume upswing
items.quote: TREM 5, it is 26 . That's the current level of postponement. I mean, our sense is it's very unlikely to happen in 2026, very unlikely. So, of course if it were to happen in 26 , there would be a huge upswing in 2025 volumes but I would not count on the 2026 im plementation date certainly not the way it's envisaged with all models going into TREM 5 at the same time and all horsepower

items.statement: BEV portfolio targeting psychographic segment wanting latest tech and wow factor, not just existing Mahindra customers
items.quote: I would rather put it as attitude or a psychographic definition which is around people who want to stand out, do things differently, experience new things and definitely are hungry for experiencing the latest tech and this product is going to come with tech which is unseen in vehicles of way higher price points.

items.statement: Last mile mobility raised Rs 1,000 crores; investing in Zaheerabad plant for electric 3-wheeler capacity
items.quote: We've raised money as you know we have 600 from one investor and 400 now from the other, so Rs. 1000 crores. We have aggressive growth plans, so there is work happening on new gen platform and new completely new products for the future. We are also investing in capacity at Zaheerabad plant.

items.statement: Electric 3-wheeler penetration expected to rise from 11% to 40-50% in foreseeable future
items.quote: Over the next few years without defining what that is but in the foreseeable future we think that category penetration should go to 40% to 50% which would mean a very significant increase now.

items.statement: Core tractor margins supported by benign commodity prices in Q4 and cost management during downcycle
items.quote: I think quarter 4 comm odity prices on the tractor side have been benign. That has helped. Rubber went up now which will see some effect of that in quarter one, but overall commodity prices for tractors were pretty benign as well in quarter 4, which helped the margin

items.statement: Growth Gems portfolio targeting collective market cap of $17 billion by FY30 from $3.4 billion in FY23
items.quote: We want that 3.4 to go to 17 billion by the time we get to fiscal 30. So, we are looking at a significant growth in the growth gems overall and we are on path for that.

items.statement: M&A strategy to continue in core businesses and growth gems; may explore one new area beyond current footprint if it makes sense
items.quote: We will look at potentially one new area of growth. We have been looking at that frankly for the last two years but we haven't been able to get something that we say this really makes sense. So, if we don't get something we can say it really makes sense, we won't do anything. If we do, then we will look at one potential new area where we can leverage the Mahindra brand, where we feel we can delive

items.statement: Holidays business has high demand and occupancy; allocated Rs 5,000 crores investment from services capex
items.quote: The 5,000-crore investment we saw in services, that is a good amount that's allocated for Holidays because occupancy rates are high. The demand from customers is very high. We can deliver very well in this space. So, that's one that we see with a clear 5x growth path.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 is INR 1,000 crores
items.quote: And our Capex guidance for the coming year, which is FY25, is in the region of INR 1,000 crores.

items.statement: FY24 actual Capex spend was INR 700 crores against guidance of INR 1,100 crores
items.quote: The actual Capex cash flow for FY24 was significantly lower than the guidance as we curtailed Capex. Against a guidance of INR 1,100 crores, the spend was only around INR 700 crores.

items.statement: Expect demand in India to pick up post elections; April 2024 saw double-digit growth in CV and PV volumes
items.quote: We expect the demand in India to pick up post elections. We have already registered a double-digit growth in our commercial vehicle and passenger car volumes for the month of April 2024.

items.statement: Expect Europe demand momentum to be better in FY25 vs last year; April 2024 volumes grew double-digit
items.quote: Coming to Europe, we expect the demand momentum to be better in FY25 compared to last year. In Europe also, markets registered a double-digit growth in volumes in the month of April 2024.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin for Q4 FY24 was 16.4%; excluding EPR liability would be 17.8%
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA for the quarter at INR 10.3 billion, was a margin of 16.4% compared to 16% in the same period last year. This included the EPR liability on the India Operations which Neeraj talked about. Excluding that, the consolidated EBITDA would have been at 17.8%.

items.statement: India Operations EBITDA margin for Q4 FY24 was 15.6%; excluding EPR liability would be 17.2%
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 6.8 billion, a margin of 15.6% compared to 15.9% in the same period last year. Again, if we exclude the EPR liability of INR 685 million, the margin for India Operations would have been at 17.2%.

items.statement: Europe Operations Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin was 19.1%, best-ever Q4 performance
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at EUR 35 million, with a robust EBITDA margin performance of 19.1% compared to 18.1% for the same period last year. This has been our best-ever Q4 performance for the European Operations.

items.statement: Raw material costs expected to rise mid-single digits in Q1 FY25; 3% price hike taken in May, may need another 2-2.5% increase
items.quote: In terms of raw material outlook, we expect the raw material cost to go up by mid-single digits in the current quarter. We will seek to negate that through price increases.

items.statement: May price increase of ~3% negates EPR and partially covers raw material; another small increase may be needed for Q1
items.quote: In May, we have taken about 3%. That negates the entire EPR and maybe to a certain extent, raw material. We may need another small increase to completely cover the entire raw material and the EPR cost increase for Q1.

items.statement: Europe UHP/UUHP proportion improved to 47% in Q4 FY24 from steady-state average of 43%
items.quote: The large part of this in the last quarter was a better mix. As Neeraj talked about, the UHP proportion was significantly higher at 47% against our more steady-state average of 43%.

items.statement: EPR liability of INR 68 crores charged in FY24; certificates in shortfall but availability improving
items.quote: Please note that this is despite additional charge of INR 68 crores on account of EPR liability.

items.statement: Dividend policy payout range 20-35%; Board declared INR 6 dividend, an all-time high
items.quote: We have a very clear, clearly listed dividend policy, which has been cleared by the Board, which is to say that the payout has to be between 20% to 35%. You also have to look at future spends as we go along. And therefore, the Board yesterday only has declared a INR 6 dividend, which is an all-time high.

items.statement: Expect Europe Operations to deliver 16-17% EBITDA margin consistently in FY25
items.quote: A 16% to 17% EBITDA margin for our European Operations with their current mix profile is something we are looking to deliver on a consistent basis.

items.statement: PCR capacity utilisation in 80s; small capacity expansion may start in H2 FY25 for FY27 needs
items.quote: If the current expectations on demand hold up, and we will be carefully watching that, maybe in the second half we will start a small capacity expansion on passenger car, nothing has been committed yet.

items.statement: Expect high single-digit CV growth and double-digit PCR growth in India for FY25
items.quote: My expectations would be a high single-digit for CV and a double-digit for PCR.

items.statement: Europe plans 1-2% price increase in Q2 FY25 due to cost push
items.quote: And in addition to this we are also planning, Amyn, to take a price increase of around 1% to 2% in quarter two, given the cost push that we are having so we will be taking -- we planned it, let's see how it goes.

items.statement: Three-to-five-year CAGR for like-to-like consumption growth estimated at 11-12%
items.quote: I would estimate anywhere between 11 % to 12% kind of growth.

items.statement: Targeting Rs. 400 crore residential sales in FY25 from ready inventory in Bangalore
items.quote: This would be our guidance for FY 25 that we are targeting to get about aim to sell about Rs. 400 crores.

items.statement: Trading occupancy expected to reach 95-96% by end of FY25
items.quote: we should be in 95% - 96% range for sure.

items.statement: Capex of Rs. 1,670 crore deployed in FY24 across assets under development and one land acquisition
items.quote: We have reinvested a considerable amount of this cash flow through capital expenditure acro ss assets under development and one land acquisition during the year in total aggregating about Rs. 1,670

items.statement: FY24 gross leasing over 500,000 sq ft with 360,000 sq ft new leasing and 170,000 sq ft renewals
items.quote: FY24 gross leasing has been over half a million square feet out of which approximately 3.6 lakh square feet is new leasing and 1.7 lakh square feet is renewal.

items.statement: New mall EBITDA margins to converge with existing mall margins as they stabilize in FY25
items.quote: going forward in FY25, EBITDA margins from new malls should start moving towards the margins we see for our existing operational malls as these malls stabilize

items.statement: Residential prices at Rs. 24,000+ per sq ft vs Rs. 15,000+ in 2019; Kolkata micro-market rates at Rs. 18,000-20,000 per sq ft
items.quote: We have taken some price hikes and the market has also accepted that well. And we are selling at about Rs. 24,000 per square foot plus plus, compared to Rs. 15,000 per square foot plus plus in 2019.

items.statement: Strong residential demand in Kolkata micro-market with rates exceeding Rs. 18,000-20,000 per sq ft
items.quote: micro market there seems to be very, very strong and stable. Our primary research is showing rates in that micro market to be in excess of about Rs. 18,000 – Rs.20,000

items.statement: F&B and entertainment allocation increased to 30% of GLA in new malls from 15% historically
items.quote: We have significantly increased the percentage of gross leasable area occupied by F&B in the new malls we maybe in about 15 %- 16% range for F&B alone. And then you add that, entertainment centers, multiplex and entertainment options, you are inching closer to about 30%.

items.statement: Retail sweet spot moved to 1.4-1.5 million sq ft due to demand from global brands
items.quote: No, absolutely the sweet spot has moved up simply because of the demand from retail brands. So many new global brands entering into the country its becoming, the sweet spot now is closer to about 1.4 -1.5 million square feet.

items.statement: Not actively pursuing new residential projects; selective on land in mature markets with consistent absorption
items.quote: So currently, we don't have any active plans on expanding on Residential. We are not in any race to become a larger Residential developer.

items.statement: Two more land transactions under pursuit to close in calendar year 2024 adding 2-2.5 million sq ft over 4-5 years
items.quote: There are probably two more real transactions that we are currently pursuing, and we should be able to conclude them in this calendar year. So that would add maybe another 2 - 2.5 million to our portfolio in the next four years or four to five years.

items.statement: Office assets: Asia Towers Bangalore near completion awaiting OC; Pune and Chennai Phase 1 (~1M sq ft) ready by end of CY2024; Mumbai offices by 2027; Bangalore offices by CY2026
items.quote: Asia Towers, Bangalore is nearly complete, we are waiting for the OC, and we should be able to commence operations immediately thereafter. Phoenix Millennium Towers at Pune, Wakad - these will be ready by the end of this calendar year and Chennai as well.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 BOPP margins expected steady at March 2024 level
items.quote: Q1' FY25 outlook for BOPP margins remain steady in line with the March 2024 month level.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals subsidiary to achieve double-digit EBITDA and over 20% ROCE in FY25
items.quote: What we feel now is that speciality chemical subsidiary is all set to make double digit EBITDA next year i.e. in FY'25 with more than 20% ROCE.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 300-350 crore planned for next year, mainly on BOPP production line
items.quote: We are looking for close to Rs. 300 to 350 crore CAPEX in next one year which will be largely on BOPP production line.

items.statement: BOPP film margin improved to Rs 12 per kg in Q4 FY24 from Rs 9 per kg in Q3 FY24
items.quote: BOPP film margin has been running at Rs. 12 per kg during March 2024 quarter versus Rs. 9 per kg in December 2023 quarter.

items.statement: Specialty sales increased to 66% of total volume in Q4 FY24 from 61% in Q3 FY24
items.quote: The specialty sales have increased to 66% of total volume in Quarter 4 compared to 64% for the full year FY24 and 61% in December 2023 quarter.

items.statement: Specialty mix target of 68-70% for FY25
items.quote: this year, we are hoping that we will be somewhere close to 68 to 70%.

items.statement: BOPP and CPP lines to increase production capacity by close to 50% over 12-15 months
items.quote: Both the lines will be the world's largest production capacity lines and will increase the company's production capacity by close to 50% in a phased manner over next 12 to 15 months.

items.statement: High-speed BOPP and CPP lines expected to rationalize production cost by 3-5%
items.quote: With these high-speed lines, it should rationalize cost of production between 3% to 5% depending on the product.

items.statement: Renewable power cost rationalization to add Rs 25 crore annually from April 2024
items.quote: Cost rationalization on renewable power should add to the bottom line starting from April 2024. We expect annual impact to be close to Rs. 25 crores.

items.statement: North Korea plant relocation to India to rationalize cost by ~$1 million, operations to start Q2 FY25
items.quote: Post relocation to India, this production line should rationalize the cost by close to U.S. $ 1 million with improved capacity utilization of the line. We expect this line to start commencement of operation in India from Q2'FY5.

items.statement: Rigid packaging expected to reach 80% capacity utilization by H2 FY25
items.quote: we expect from the second half of FY25 we should be close to 80% capacity utilization.

items.statement: BOPET film margins remain negative; company to rationalize volume and focus on specialty and high shrink films
items.quote: The margin for the BOPET film, which is close to 8% of our top line, continues to remain negative. For BOPET films what we are going to focus on now is to be selective in terms of the volume. So, we will rationalize the volume to reduce the loss-making sales and focus more and more on specialty films and high shrink films sales.

items.statement: Net debt reduction expected to start from FY26; FY25 net debt may increase by Rs 20-50 crore from current Rs 561 crore
items.quote: Currently we are at Rs. 550 crores of net debt. We do not expect much change in the net debt level except that there maybe it may increase by Rs. 20, 30, or 50 crores. That will be clear at the end of March 2025, from there on, as we indicated earlier on the call, you may expect some reduction coming in.

items.statement: FY25 EXIM growth 15%, Domestic 25%, overall 18-20%
items.quote: I would like to give guidance for FY '25 EXIM, we are hoping 15% growth. Domestic, we are hoping 25% growth. That makes overall 18% to 20% growth in FY '25.

items.statement: FY25 capex budget Rs 610 crore, subject to mid-year review
items.quote: As far as Capex budget is concerned, now we have finalized the Capex budget of Rs. 610 crores, primarily centered at wagons, containers and rolling stock, etc., development of terminals, land procurement for terminals and IT.

items.statement: EBITDA margin maintained at 25% for FY25
items.quote: And our margins, EBITDA, which is in the range of 25%, we are very confident that we will be able to maintain the 25% EBITDA in this financial year also.

items.statement: 100% pass-through of rail haulage hike in EXIM, strategic in domestic
items.quote: In the EXIM segment, we have passed through the entire amount. In domestic segment, we have passed strategically. We have not passed everywhere, depending on the stream, depending on the capability of the customers to absorb that part, that hike.

items.statement: Drivers: bulk cement in tank containers, double-stack to Varnama near Nhava Sheva, new terminals, DPD movement
items.quote: The drivers for growth in this financial year will be bulk cement in tank containers, which is a new product that we are going to launch, then we will get -- we will be running double-stack trains to Varnama near Nhava Sheva very soon. And we are expecting sizable additional business at our new terminals.

items.statement: First/last mile 25% of volume, target 50% FY25, 80-85% FY26
items.quote: First mile, last mile, 25% of our entire volume, we are now providing first mile, last mile service to our customers. which has been very well appreciated by them. And our target this year is 50%. And by next year, that is FY '26, we are confident of reaching this number to 80% to 85% of our total volume, we will be providing first mile, last mile.

items.statement: LLF provision FY25 Rs 400-420 crore; Gati Shakti could reduce TKD cost 60-65%
items.quote: So, for the current FY, if you missed the discussion, we had a long discussion on LLF going forward. So, the one answer to your question is this year, our provisions will be hovering around Rs. 400 crores to Rs. 420 crores.

items.statement: Record double-stack trains 5,440 in FY24 (+33%), 14 new rakes, 7,653 containers, 90 LNG trucks, 200 more LNG trucks authorized
items.quote: Then we have run record number of double-stacked trains in the FY. That is 5,440, which is a growth of 33%. In the FY '23, we could run only 4,097 double-stack trains.

items.statement: JNPT DFC connection expected by March 2025 per DFC officers
items.quote: Yes, as per the Dedicated Freight Corridor officers, JNPT will be commissioned on DFC by March 2025. That is a projection they have given.

items.statement: Reiterated FY25 EBITDA per ton guidance of INR 18,000-20,000 and 20% volume growth
items.quote: Absolutely. We are quite confident of achieving that and we are reiterating our guidance.

items.statement: Reiterated full year FY25 guidance of 20% volume growth with EBITDA margin of INR 18,000 to INR 20,000 per ton
items.quote: But concerning all this thing I think if you look at a full year basis we are reiterating our guidance of 20% volume growth with an EBITDA margin of INR18,00 0 to INR20,000.

items.statement: Announced total expansion capex of INR 5,400 crores including Indonesia JV, Chromeni acquisition, Jajpur downstream, and infrastructure
items.quote: We have announced a total expansion capex of around INR5,400 crores. With these acquisitions and investments, we have orchestrated a plan to become one of the largest stainless steel producers in the world.

items.statement: FY25 total capex outlook of INR 4,700-4,800 crores including spillover from FY24, plus INR 500 crores maintenance capex
items.quote: With this, the total capex outlook of FY '25 is expected to be around INR4,700 crores to INR4,800 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex estimated at INR 1,200-1,300 crores for Odisha HR/CR capacity, Indonesia SMS, Jajpur infrastructure, and ESG renewables
items.quote: So overall, we are expecting that what capex we have outline right now close to around INR1,200 crores to say INR1,300 crores of the capex next year in FY '26.

items.statement: Export order book impacted by Red Sea crisis; stopped booking new export orders due to high freight costs
items.quote: So we actually stopped booking those kind of orders in our books which are reflected in Q4.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA per ton impacted by INR 250-300 crores due to nickel price fall, Red Sea freight costs, and lower exports
items.quote: So all put together they all have close to INR250 crores impact on these mul tiple events which has happened INR250 crores to INR300 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 expected to be better than Q4 FY24 as Red Sea impact stabilizes and nickel prices recover
items.quote: No Q1 is expected to be better than Q4.

items.statement: Strong domestic demand across all major segments including railway, auto, pipe & tube, lift elevator, and special grades
items.quote: In the domestic market, we experienced strong demand across all major segments. The railway sector in particular, saw unprecedented growth, achieving its highest ever sales in the wagon segment, while demand for passenger coaches and Metro remains robust.

items.statement: Export markets remain muted with geopolitical issues including Red Sea crisis impacting export performance
items.quote: On the export front, our key markets continued to see muted demand along with geopolitical issues such as the one on going in the Red Sea. These challenges have had an impact on our export performance and prevented us on optimizing our sales mix.

items.statement: FY24 product mix: 200 series 35%, 300 series 45%, 400 series 20%; 400 series stable vs FY23 24%
items.quote: In FY'24, basically series wise, 200 serie s at almost 35%; 300 series was close to around 45%; and 400 was around 20%.

items.statement: Chinese imports surged 20% YoY in FY24 and increased 20% QoQ in Q4; dumping continues to threaten MSME sector
items.quote: On the import side, imports from China continue to surge with around 20% increase on a year -on-year basis. With a consistent increase in Chinese dumping, the stainless steel market in India continues to be flooded by substandard exports.

items.statement: No immediate government relief expected on Chinese dumping; dialogue ongoing but short-term outlook negative
items.quote: So the dialogue is always on, and we always expect that something positive should come out, but immediately, in the short term, I don't see anything, maybe in the medium term, some relief could come, but nothing to really mention at the moment.

items.statement: Indonesia NPI project expected to commission in early Q2 FY25, with commercial sales starting then and 90% utilization by FY26
items.quote: But I can inform that we see that early Q2 '25, we are expecting it to get commissioned.

items.statement: Chromeni Steels acquisition (54% stake, INR 1,340 crores) to be operational within 6 months; targeting 100% ownership
items.quote: So this pl ant is not operational. This plant was closed somewhere in the middle of 2020 and since then it is closed, but we hope that within 6 months' time we should make it operational.

items.statement: Rabirun tube plant started trial production; expected to reach 1,000-1,500 tons per quarter in next couple of quarters
items.quote: And on Rabirun, we have just started now producing our tubes. We have just started it, so it will also gradually pick up. And we expect it to go to the level of 1,000 to 1,500 in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: If billing grows 15-16% YoY, margins can be maintained; 20% growth helps improve margins; 9-10% growth may dip margins short term
items.quote: If we are able to grow our revenue, grow our billing by 15-16% year on year, we should be able to maintain margin. If we are able to grow at 20%, that will help us improve our margins. And if we grow at 9-10%, then our margins might take a dip in the short term.

items.statement: IT hiring showing early signs of recovery with more jobs posted and CVs viewed; utilization rates nearing pre-COVID levels
items.quote: On our website, more IT jobs are being posted every day than was the case three months ago. On our website, more CVs are being viewed by IT companies than was the case maybe 3-4 months ago.

items.statement: Non-IT hiring growth has slowed from a year ago due to higher talent supply from IT sector not hiring
items.quote: Non-IT growth has also slowed down from maybe a year, year and a half back. Some sectors continue to sort of do well. Growth in other sectors seem to have moderated a little bit.

items.statement: Recruitment margins fell due to flattish billing growth and 10% manpower cost increase plus higher marketing and overhead
items.quote: Margins have fallen because billing growth was almost flattish last year and costs went up. Manpower costs must have gone up by 10%. Marketing costs must have gone up. Overhead must have gone up.

items.statement: Sales headcount will grow in FY25; more hiring in data science and machine learning over next couple of quarters
items.quote: We are expanding our sales team, so we're hiring more sales people. Now, some of them have been hired, but some are yet to be hired. So, Naukri headcount will grow next year over last year.

items.statement: 99acres could generate cash if it grows 25-30% again this year; needs 2-3 more solid quarters to confirm
items.quote: If we are able to grow the 99acres business by 25-30% again this year, then we should be able to make some, generate some cash this year. But fingers crossed, I mean, see, we've had a good 4-5-6-7 quarters in 99acres.

items.statement: 99acres is price taker in new homes segment (competing with Facebook/Google); plans to slowly raise prices in resale/rental as value delivered increases
items.quote: In the new home part of the business, our real competition is actually portals like Facebook and Google, and the price is really set by them. And we are price takers in that market. And in the resale and rental market, we are a leader. But of course, we have competition from players like Magic Bricks and housing. And there we believe there is an opportunity to take prices up further, because we be

items.statement: US election, generative AI impact, and skill-specific demand create uncertainty for IT hiring recovery
items.quote: there is this whole overhang of the US election and of generative AI and what it could do and so many other things that it's very hard for us to call what the next few months are going to look like

items.statement: Board increased dividend to Rs. 22/share (16% YoY); cash balance of Rs. 4,191 crore deemed right-sized after accounting for deferred revenue and 12-month expenses
items.quote: The Board has proposed a final dividend of Rs. 12 per share along with the interim dividend of Rs. 10 per share. The total dividend for FY24 is Rs. 22 per share, a 16% year-on-year increase.

items.statement: No plans to sell stakes in Zomato or PolicyBazaar; believe significant growth and valuation upside remains
items.quote: Look, I mean, the board is always open to a discussion around this, but what we believe is that there's plenty of growth left and valuation left in both these companies. And for the moment, we would like to hold and not sell.

items.statement: Operating margin guidance maintained at 2.4% to 2.6% steady-state range
items.quote: We would want to mention that between -- I mean we maintain that between 2.4% to 2.6%. And we are at that rate. We are very clear about it.

items.statement: Gross margin in India SISA business expected to remain steady and flat
items.quote: We don't see any particular change in the gross margin on any of these business units. It will remain steady and flat.

items.statement: India enterprise demand strong but Q4/Q1 softer due to election deferrals; consumer and mobility to benefit from AI-enabled devices
items.quote: the enterprise segment, the demand continues to be very strong, and we are quite bullish in the next year as well. As I mentioned, bo th Q4, our Q4 and our Q1 has been softer because of the elections and postponement of capital decisions, both in corporates and

items.statement: Africa weakness expected to continue 1-2 quarters then improve; Nigeria stressed, Egypt and Kenya improving, South Africa new growth driver
items.quote: we expect this to continue for a bit more. We do expect in 1 or 2 quarters, things to improve as well. But w e will continue to make sure that we are focused on profitable business and not take undue risks in these markets

items.statement: Turkey enterprise softer, mobility opportunity continues but managed cautiously due to 50%+ interest rates
items.quote: Turkey, it's generally softer. So the market is softer, especially starting in enterprise. Enterprise, you can see a decline in the market size. The mobility part continues to offer good opportunity. And we are just trying to manage not to push the envelope there from a market share perspective so that -- because the borrowing where as Krishnan mentioned earlier, is 50% interest rates.

items.statement: India TSG growth impacted by election-related capex postponements in government and corporate deals
items.quote: Our TSG business could have done well had this election hangover is not there because the capex are all postponed, which also had a negative impact in terms of our TSG growth in India.

items.statement: Paynet divestment SPA signed for USD 87 million plus adjusted net cash; regulatory approvals pending; proceeds to fix Arena debt structure
items.value: USD 87 million plus adjusted net cash
items.quote: The SPA was signed for USD 87 million plus adjusted net cash. There are regulatory approvals needed. However, once the deal is consummated, the proceeds would be used to correct the debt structure at Arena and focus on core business of IT distribution.

items.statement: Turkey interest cost at 4.7% of revenue (up from 3.2%) with central bank rate ~50%, inflation 68.5%, currency depreciation 59%
items.quote: Interest cost, as a percentage of our revenue, was 3.2%, which itself was very high, considering the nature of our business. This has further moved up to 4.7 percentage of revenue in the current year, full year.

items.statement: Africa currency volatility: Nigeria depreciated 27% in Q4, Egypt 34.8%, Kenya appreciated 17.7%; limited hedging mechanisms available
items.quote: In Nigeria, it got depreciated by 27% in 1 quarter. In Egypt, it got depreciated by 34.8% in 1 quarter. Please understand, in some of these markets, there are no proper hedging mechanism available.

items.statement: Working capital days guidance maintained at 35-40 days; Q4 achieved 34 days through operational efficiency focus
items.quote: And similarly, working capital also, we have guided 35 to 40. We are within that range.

items.statement: Cloud business grew 29% in Q4, 33% for year; subscription revenue exceeds $1 billion across hyperscaler, PaaS and SaaS
items.quote: Overall in our business, the subscription piece has become more than $1 billion. Between the hyperscaler piece as well as the TSG platform-as-a-service and the software-as-a-service piece.

items.statement: Debt-equity comfort zone 0.6-0.7x; sufficient capital for future growth spikes while maintaining return ratios
items.quote: So we will ensure that our debt equity, our internal comfort is between 0.6 and 0.7, and that's something which we are quite comfortable. And with the current debt equity ratio, we think we have sufficient capital for any spike in the future growth.

items.statement: ROE 18% and ROCE above 21% for Q4; full year ROE 17% and ROCE 22.5%
items.quote: For the quarter, return on equity is about 18%, and return on capital employed, above 21%. For the full year, it is 17% and 22.5%.

items.statement: India revenue contribution 47%, Middle East & Africa 40% (KSA 30%, Africa 20%, Rest of ME 50%), Turkey 12%
items.quote: Overall, India contributes about 47% of our revenue. Middle East and Africa, 40%. The balance, 12%, it comes out of Turkey. That's the split. Between Middle East and Africa, if you split that further into KSA, which is an important market, as I mentioned, that contributes about 30%; Africa about 20%. All these rough results plus or minus 1% or 2%. Rest of Middle East, which includes U.A.E. within

items.statement: Arena Turkey revenue INR 10,200 crores for FY24 (~10-11% of total); profitable despite high interest rates
items.quote: Arena is about 10, 11 percentage of our total business. For last year, our revenue in Arena in Indian rupees is about INR10,200 crores. And for the quarter, it's about INR2,400 crores. So it's roughly about 10%, 11%.

items.statement: Factoring cost INR 79 crores in Q4 FY24 vs INR 48 crores in Q4 FY23; total finance cost INR 219 crores vs INR 163 crores
items.quote: So the factoring cost overall for the quarter is INR79 crores vis-a-vis INR48 crores in Q4 of previous year.

items.statement: FY24 order booking was ₹18.78 billion, up 17% y-o-y, with a record closing order book of ₹15.53 billion, up 17% y-o-y.
items.quote: Order booking for financial year FY 24 was ₹18.78 billion, an increase of 17% year-over-year (y-o-y) while revenues for the same year came in at ₹16.54 billion, which was 33% higher y-o-y.

items.statement: Product order booking increased 10% y-o-y to an all-time high of ₹12.61 billion in FY24.
items.quote: On the product side, order booking has increased by 10% y-o-y to reach an all-time high of ₹12.61 billion, and the key growth drivers continue to be the areas of renewable energy, power generation, industrial cogeneration as well as API and other both power and drive turbines.

items.statement: Aftermarket order booking for FY24 stood at ₹6.17 billion, growing 34% y-o-y.
items.quote: The order booking for the year stood at ₹6.17 billion, gro wing by 34% when compared with the corresponding period of the previous year

items.statement: Management expects workforce expansion of 20-25% in FY25 and aims to sustain growth predictably.
items.quote: Yes, we are going to be expanding our workforce up with anywhere between 20 -25% in the coming year, which is FY 25.

items.statement: Capex for the coming year or couple of years is estimated at ₹90-100 crore, including ~₹40-50 crore for the US subsidiary and R&D strengthening.
items.quote: But overall, if we are lo oking at the Capex somewhere in the region of about ₹90 crore to ₹100 crore in the coming year or coming, let's say, couple of years, these are things that I think the Company can easily afford.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to stay at least at current levels (~20%); aftermarket margins historically stable within 1-2% range.
items.quote: Margins do not seem to be a problem at this current point in time to at least stay at the same margins that we have.

items.statement: Domestic market enquiries robust but order finalisation delayed in Q3/Q4 FY24 due to elections; pickup expected by June-July.
items.quote: These are typically whenever there is election cyc le, then we look at that. But a majority of this discussion is going on, finali sation is getting delayed. We are hopeful that probably by end June, July , the finali sation pattern will pick up.

items.statement: Domestic 0-100 MW market grew to ~2,100-2,200 MW in FY24 vs expected 2,500 MW (~25% growth); strong enquiry pipeline from steel, cement, waste heat recovery.
items.quote: The domestic market , all indications are that it could grow very robustly. The lack of order booking in Q3 and Q4 in domestic market and actually for the last 4-5 months of the financial year led to what was expected to be a very good growth in the market to approximately 2,500 -odd MWs. But it probably came in somewhere in the region of about 2,100 - 2,200 MWs.

items.statement: Aftermarket contributed 33% of total turnover in FY24; export and aftermarket share increasing.
items.quote: The turnover at the same time was ₹5.38 billion, which was higher by 31% and aftermarket contributed 33% of the total turnover in FY 24.

items.statement: Enquiry book declined 5-7% y-o-y due to geopolitical constraints; domestic finalisation conservative.
items.quote: The enquiry book has declined by about 5 -7%, but it is higher than the global market even for a year. So, we find that it's not a constraint even if the enquiry book has come down.

items.statement: US service subsidiary established, hiring done, machinery ordered, shed leased; business commenced as per plan.
items.quote: The subsidiary, as you have seen from our quarterly reporting has already been established. People have already been hired. The executive who will be handling the region is already in place in the United States. Machinery has been ordered, shed has been leased and we are already on track as far as our business plan goes to achieve our order booking and revenue for this year.

items.statement: Commodity price pressures (e.g., copper) exist but are manageable; no major margin impact expected.
items.quote: Also, the commodity price -based issue that we had in the past are somewhat in a sense behind us though we d o see some commodity pressures in areas like copper, etc. But having said that, those are all manageable.

items.statement: Production capacity is 250+ units, flexible, can be increased by up to a third at short notice; current utilisation ~75%.
items.quote: Our total production capacity is 250 + and it is flexible, and it can be increased at a short notice to the desired level.

items.statement: Export growth to be sustained predictably via multi-year efforts in new geographies, product and service expansion.
items.quote: Yes, most definitely. Our efforts are towards that effect, and we want to sustain growth in a very pred ictable way. So, our efforts are geared towards building competency so that we can sustain it.

items.statement: API turbines not yet double-digit revenue share but a core segment with strong international momentum and installed base.
items.quote: No, this is a core segment for the Company . We have extremely good products for this market. As we get closer to customers, as we get registered with them, we've become more relevant. We already have a good installed base in this sector.

items.statement: Plan to open minimum 25 new restaurants in next 3 years
items.quote: In the next 3 years we would be opening minimum of 25 new restaurants.

items.statement: Capex for new expansion is INR25 crores for current year covering 8-9 restaurants
items.quote: INR25 crores for the new expansion.

items.statement: Renovation capex around INR2 crores per store for stores over 17-18 years old
items.quote: The first point is the capex is around INR2 crores per store.

items.statement: Renovated stores see 25% overall revenue jump including liquor, food and delivery
items.quote: we've also understood that we do have a 25% overall revenue jump which includes our liquor, food, as well as delivery for the units.

items.statement: Headroom to increase prices by 10-12% despite absorbing 40% chicken inflation
items.quote: But there is a headroom of going to at least 10%-12% in terms of pricing.

items.statement: Delivery now 28% of total revenue, up from 7-8% pre-pandemic
items.quote: 28%, to be specific, was delivery and the balance is dining.

items.statement: Liquor share 11-12% currently; target 15-18% with line-of-sight bars and Episode expansion
items.quote: going forward, there's a scope to go into a level of 15 to 18%.

items.statement: Episode One liquor ratio 60% liquor, 40% food vs under 20% in Asian restaurants
items.quote: we see o ur liquor ratios in that space is 60-40, which is 60% being liquor, 40% being food

items.statement: 8 new restaurants on track to open by 9th May in current year
items.quote: In the years t o come next this current year we are on track to open 8 new restaurants on 9th May coming

items.statement: New stores take 6-8 months to breakeven causing short-term margin pressure
items.quote: Between six to eight months.

items.statement: Middle East expansion via franchisee-owned company-operated model; 2 more Dubai stores and Saudi entry planned
items.quote: Within the Gulf, we are look ing at minimum two stores in Dubai. And we're looking at Saudi

items.statement: Catering vertical Speciality Experiences growing; banqueting hall in Calcutta finishing, Bandra partnership underway
items.quote: we've already built one banqueting hall in Cal cutta which is fairly large. It's getting into finishing stages. So, the second one is coming in Bombay where we already have an asset and we are renovating

items.statement: Targeting INR 500 crores gross revenue and INR 45-50 crores EBITDA for FY25
items.quote: That's exactly what we are targeting here.

items.statement: AUM target of INR 400-475 crores for FY25, up from INR 179 crores currently
items.quote: I think the AUM growth, given the partnerships that we have created and built, I think the INR 400 crores, INR 450 crores, INR 475 crores number, I think is not a pipe dream. We will probably end up achieving this.

items.statement: Plan to raise INR 200 crores additional debt in FY25 for lending book growth
items.quote: So another INR 200 crores rupees we are planning to raise in the current year.

items.statement: Acquired SuperScan AI toolkit from Orbo.ai for INR 8 crores upfront plus up to INR 8 crores deferred
items.quote: An initial amount of INR 8 crores will be paid as cash and a maximum amount of another INR 8 crores will be paid as deferred consideration depending on the performance of the company and basis some pre-agreed milestones.

items.statement: Signed soundbox contract for 500,000 devices with leading PSU bank, execution from Q1 FY25
items.quote: We have backed a contract for providing a soundbox platform supporting nearly 500,000 soundboxes for a leading PSU bank. We expect to execute this contract Q1 FY 25 onwards.

items.statement: Seven existing SuperScan contracts with large BFSI clients, four already generating revenue
items.quote: We've already got about seven contracts that have been signed. And this is all with majority large, large clients.

items.statement: Achieved adjusted EBITDA breakeven (ex-ESOP) in Q4 FY24, first profitable quarter
items.quote: I am pleased to report that we have concluded FY '24 on a strong note with two key developments. Number one, we broke even at the adjusted EBITDA level, which is ex-ESOP in Q4- FY 24, an important milestone in our journey.

items.statement: iServeU subsidiary turned EBITDA positive in Q4 FY24 with INR 1.2 crores recoveries
items.quote: I am happy to report that iServeU has seen some recoveries amounting to INR1.2 crores to this effect for Q4 FY 24. Going forward, we expect to see this trend to continue.

items.statement: Net take rate target of 7-10 bps on GTV business, shifting focus from gross to net revenue
items.quote: I would actually start tracking the business on net revenues. And I would start saying, what are the net revenues that we are delivering and are we on track to deliver the 7 bps to 10 bps on the net revenue basis

items.statement: FLDG regulatory clarity creates significant opportunity for tech-first NBFC lending and distribution
items.quote: We welcome the recent clarification from the regulator on FLDG guidelines which apart from providing the clarity for the industry also creates a significant opportunity for a tech-first NBFC like us.

items.statement: Fintech channel now contributes 45% of AUM mix, up from 20% at launch in October 2023
items.quote: I am happy to report that the fintech channel now contributes nearly 45% of our AUM mix up from 20% since its launch in October 2023.

items.statement: Non-GTV SaaS revenues expected to become as large or larger than GTV business in contribution
items.quote: My expectation is that the non-GTV business should be almost as big, if not bigger than the GTV business. Because the GTV business and I'm talking not purely from a revenue standpoint I'm talking from contribution standpoint because that's what really matters.

items.statement: UPI acquiring disruption in Nov-Feb due to bank licensing interpretation, resolved by mid-Feb
items.quote: Come November, December is when we had a little bit of a challenge where some of the banks took an interpretation where we needed to have certain licensing for them to be able to behave like a nodal account for our settlements.

items.statement: Raised INR 60 crores in FY24 from three lenders; existing lenders expected to provide INR 100 crores of FY25 target
items.quote: Out of that, these three lenders have lent us INR 60 crores. So we definitely feel that because of the good track record and relationship with the three lenders, out of the INR 200 crores incremental, we are expecting about INR 100 crores from these three lenders only.

items.statement: SuperScan acquisition includes 8 AI engineers and on-prem deployment model for BFSI data sensitivity
items.quote: We're also getting eight engineers who are completely AI trained. To me, that was a very, very big part of the whole proposition.

items.statement: Expects consolidated revenue of INR 875-935 crores in FY25 with 15-20% growth
items.quote: In my opinion, we should be close to INR 875 crores to INR 935 crores.

items.statement: Targets consolidated revenue above INR 1,100 crores in FY26 with EBITDA margin around 10%
items.quote: I think that within FY25-26, we should be, closely in a bracket of more than INR 1,100 crores also.

items.statement: Expects at least 20% growth in top line and bottom line in FY25 over FY24
items.quote: I expect at least 20% growth in terms of the top line as well as in the bottom line.

items.statement: Planned capex of INR 215 crores funded through internal accruals and promoter preferential issue
items.quote: Our planned capex of INR 215 crores, primarily funded through internal accruals and a preferential issue to the promoter, will facilitate the expansion of our existing capabilities.

items.statement: Completed INR 50 crores capex in FY24 including INR 16.12 crores for 3.8 MW solar plant and INR 33.46 crores for chemical and fertilizer verticals
items.quote: During the financial year, we successfully completed the consolidated capex of INR 50 crores, out of which INR 16.12 crores was allotted for the further establishment of 3.8-megawatt DC solar power plant and INR 33.46 crores were directed towards investment in our Chemical and Fertilizer verticals.

items.statement: Unit 6 fertilizer expansion of 150,000 tons capacity and Unit 4 water-soluble plant of 12,000 tons capacity underway
items.quote: In Unit 6 we are building up a facility of 1,50,000 tons. Aditya Sen: And Unit 4? Punit Makharia: Unit 4 is, that's a specialty product. That is why we call it as a WS water-soluble fertilizer. The installed capacity would be around 12,000 tons

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin around 10% in FY26 if things go well
items.quote: I can tell you what I expect is that at least we should be in a range of maybe 10% or so around.

items.statement: Sees industry stabilization and improvement in volumes and revenue from Q4 FY24 onwards
items.quote: I personally see that the whole industry and the market now has started going towards the stabilization phase.

items.statement: Expects decent fertilizer offtake in FY25 supported by improved subsidy and monsoon outlook
items.quote: Sir, I am expecting a decent offtake, not a very strong offtake, honestly speaking.

items.statement: Dyes Intermediate volume grew 82% and revenue 64% in FY24; Acid revenue declined 26% due to internal consumption in Unit 5
items.quote: Dyes Intermediate saw a significant volume growth of 82% and Acid grew by 19%, while Fertilizer and Animal feed experienced marginal declines. Revenue from Dyes Intermediate grew by 64%, whereas Acid revenue declined by 26%.

items.statement: Chemical segment volume grew 26% in FY24; Fertilizer volume declined 1%
items.quote: For the entire financial year, the volume of Chemicals was 57,270 metric ton, a significant 26% year-on-year growth. Fertilizers however show a slight decline of 1% totalling to 2,09,500 metric ton.

items.statement: Rock phosphate prices stable at $140-148 per ton, not at $305 or $200 as suggested
items.quote: It has been always, in the range of $140 to $148. And right now, also, it is almost in the range of $142.

items.statement: Government of India mandated reasonable profit margins of 10-12% PAT for fertilizer business
items.quote: Government of India has already given you a decent reasonable profit margins for fertilizer business. That is, I think, 12% to 10%, something like that, on a PAT level.

items.statement: Solar capex of INR 37-38 crores (ex-GST) with expected payback in 3.5 years; no debt taken for solar expansion
items.quote: Sir, without GST investment is almost INR 37-38 crores. And as far as my understanding is concerned, the repayment would be in three and a half years or so, leaving apart the depreciation benefits and the taxation benefits. We have not taken any kind of a debt or loan on the solar expansion.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 65%, targeting 75% in FY25; 50-60% of new capex is for backward integration
items.quote: Sir, it's almost in the range of 65% of our existing capacity. And whatever the capacities we are building up in future, out of that, almost the 50-60% expansion is towards the backward integration.

items.statement: Expect volume growth of more than 15% in FY25 if power demand grows 7-8%
items.quote: if the demand in the country increases by 8%, we should be able to grow more than 15%.

items.statement: Expect REC segment volume growth of 25-30% in FY25
items.quote: REC segment, we are expecting almost about 25% to 30% growth.

items.statement: Expect long-duration contract volume of 15 BU in FY25
items.quote: Almost about 15 BU is our expectation.

items.statement: Expect gas exchange volume growth of at least 30-40%
items.quote: we feel gas exchange volumes definitely should increase at a rate of at least 30%, 40% because gas exchange is in a nascent stage now.

items.statement: Power demand grew 12% in first 45 days of FY25, expected to grow 8% for full year
items.quote: In the first 45 days of this year, that demand has grown by almost 12%. And during this year it is expected to grow by almost about 8%.

items.statement: Short-term market share of total generation increased to 15% in FY24 from 13% in FY23
items.quote: the short-term market has grown to almost about 15% of the country's generation, up from 13% in FY '23.

items.statement: Exchange share of total generation increased to 8% in FY24 from 7% in FY23
items.quote: exchanges have grown to 8% of overall generation from 7% in FY '23.

items.statement: Long-duration contracts reached 10 BU in FY24 vs 1.6 BU in FY23
items.quote: long-duration contracts in FY '24 on the exchange platform recorded 10 billion units which is much higher than 1.6 billion which we did in FY '23.

items.statement: REC volume doubled in Q4 FY24 YoY to 32.5 lakh certificates; full year volume up 27% to 75 lakh
items.quote: At nearly 32.5 lakh certificates , REC volume in quarter 4 of FY '24 was twice that of same quarter last year and at 75 lakh certificates in the whole year , the volume was higher by almost 27% with respect to FY '23.

items.statement: DAM clearing price fell 18% YoY in Q4 FY24 to INR4.80/unit; FY24 price fell 12% to INR5.24/unit
items.quote: The average market clearing price in the DAM segment during quarter 4 FY '24 period was INR4.80 per unit compared to INR5.83 in quarter 4 of FY '23, a decline of almost about 18%.

items.statement: Operating at high margin of 86-87%; margins should improve with volume growth due to fixed cost base
items.quote: As it is, we are operating at a pretty high margin of almost about 86%, 87%.

items.statement: Market coupling simulation still in progress; no near-term implementation expected
items.quote: I think that process has not yet begun. Development of software takes a lot of time. It has to be developed, it has to be tested and then the simulation has to start.

items.statement: Carbon credit market launch delayed 5-6 months pending policy clarity on voluntary vs mandatory market
items.quote: I think we will need another 5, 6 months' time for that clarity to come.

items.statement: 20 GW thermal capacity addition expected in FY25; 50 GW more in next 4-5 years
items.quote: around 20 gigawatt of thermal capacity addition is expected during the year, which will increase thermal generation by almost about 10%.

items.statement: Government targets spot market share of 25% of generation by 2030; exchange share could reach 16-17%
items.quote: Government of India, in fact, has been working on this. And in the draft National Electricity Plan, they have projected a number of 25% for the spot market, of the total generation by 2030.

items.statement: Management expects to participate in more than 150 bids costing over INR 75,000 crores in FY25 with a success rate yielding INR 20,000 crores order inflow, targeting order book of INR 92,000-1,00,000 crores and revenue of INR 23,000 crores.
items.quote: For FY24-25 we will definitely be participating in more than 150 bids costing more than INR 75,000crores. Success rate is INR 20,000 crores. So, you can calculate the kind of inflow which we are expecting. All the time, we want to have the order book to be three, four times. If our turnover this year was INR 21,700 and next year we plan for INR23,000 crores, So the order book all the time should b

items.statement: First bidding projects Indore Metro (10.66%) and Maldives (11%) achieved margins above 10%, higher than the 8.5% fixed nomination margin.
items.quote: In the FY'23-'24, it has given the margin of 10.66%. And the first overseas project of Maldives, it has resulted into a margin of 11%. And the total turnover in these two projects is roug hly INR1,000 crores with a margin of 10% plus

items.statement: Management targets bottom line growth of roughly 15% to continue over the next five years while top line grows 5-7%.
items.quote: We have all the time saying that -- we have been saying that we are more focused towards the bottom line. We want to get the better margins. And we want to grow with this tradition that the top line may increase by 5%. The bottom line growth, which is roug hly 15%, should continue over the next five years

items.statement: RVNL can infuse up to 30% of net worth (~INR 2,200 crores) in SPVs/JVs without ministry approval; net worth ~INR 7,867 crores.
items.quote: So, what I understand is around 30% of the net worth we can infuse, which is around, in this time net worth is 7,000 today? Net worth is around 7,000. So, 30 % of the net worth we can infuse. And beyond that, if you want to invest, then you will have to go to the Ministry of Railways and Ministry of Finance. So, what I am saying is that, with our objective, whatever opportunities come, either we w

items.statement: Management sees strong opportunity in capacity augmentation projects as Indian Railways targets 3,000 million tons loading by 2030 from current 1,500 million tons.
items.quote: Presently, the traffic loading is around 1,500 million tons. They are planning 2,000 by 2030, 3,000 million tons. For that, the capacity augmentation projects, there are a large number of projects which will come up. We are keen for that.

items.statement: RVNL executing metros in seven cities; signaling vertical secured orders worth over INR 700 crores including INR 250 crore ABS project in Southern Railway.
items.quote: Let me, let me talk about the signaling system. So, this is a new vertical. So, we have got order worth more than INR700 crores. items.statement: Exotech Q4 FY2024 EBITDA margin at 18.1%
items.quote: Exotech recorded EBITDA margin of 18.1%, underscoring our commitment to operational excellence and profitability.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to Rs.163.5 million by end FY2024 after temporary increase for Walter Pack acquisition
items.quote: our net debt level stand at Rs. 163.5 million, reflecting our strong cash flow performance.

items.statement: Site 3++ capex Rs 200 crore, expected to come online and stabilize in Q4 FY25
items.quote: To start with, site 3++ is Rs. 200 crores of investment and it is expected to come online and stabilize in Q4 of this financial year 2024-25.

items.statement: Site 5 capex Rs 500 crore, first phase online December 2025, stabilization Q4 FY26, potential unlocking FY27
items.quote: And talking about site 5, we are estimating all getting online in the phase wise manner where the first phase will get online in December of 2025 which will stabilize in the last quarter of 2025-26 and potential will start unlocking in 26-27 for that site. This is expansion of Rs. 500 crores of capital investment.

items.statement: Revenue loss of Rs 150-200 crore over 4 months due to fire accident, pushed to future quarters
items.quote: We lost almost close to Rs. 150 crores to Rs. 200 crores of revenue, which we are assuming in two quarters, I mean 4 months.

items.statement: Pricing pressure from China continues, no price correction expected in Q1-Q2 FY25, hope for improvement from Q2
items.quote: Currently for Q1 and Q2, no, we are not expecting any price to be correcting, but we are seeing a good demand at least to start with, which is a very positive note and with the demand we hope that from Q2 onwards, the pricing will go towards the North.

items.statement: Agro expected at 30-35% of topline in FY25, LSM 59%, CRAMS 14%, contract/exclusive 26% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: We are anticipating 30% to 35% of our total topline to be agro for this financial year.

items.statement: Site 4 commercialized for oil field services, first phase revenue from Q1 FY25, significant contribution expected in coming quarters
items.quote: Production and supply of products from this site 4 to this particular customer will increase in phases with the first phase beginning in this first quarter of fiscal 2025. By the coming quarters, we anticipate very significant revenue contribution from this site 4 in the oil field services domain.

items.statement: Electrolyte additives partial commercialization by end of calendar year 2024, full commercialization in site 3++ by end of FY25 or quarter thereafter
items.quote: So, the commercialization will be partially done by the end of this calendar year and the full commercialization will happen in the site 3++, which will be by the end of this fiscal year or the quarter thereafter.

items.statement: 15 MW solar plant commissioning in 3 phases: Phase 1 end May 2024, Phase 2 July 2024, Phase 3 September 2024
items.quote: Commissioning of the new 15 MW solar power plant will be adding to saving of electricity expenses, which will be done in 3 phases. Phase 1 will come online in the end of May 2024, second phase will start online by July 2024 and the last phase will start in September 2024.

items.statement: Site 2 expected to resume 75% operations soon, full revocation order awaited
items.quote: We're expecting to receive revocation of the closure order of site 2 to resume operations to the extent of 75% of our capacity in the next coming days.

items.statement: CRAMS portfolio grew year-on-year despite accident, significant expansion expected in FY25 with new projects and customers
items.quote: Even with the recent setbacks, our CRAMS portfolio has in fact grown year-on-year and we anticipate the upcoming fiscal year will see a significant expansion of this CRAMS portfolio with new projects and new customers being added across the industry spectrum.

items.statement: Otsuka partnership to contribute substantial revenue for first time in FY25
items.quote: This upcoming fiscal year will see substantial revenue contributions coming up for the first time from our partnership with Otsuka, thus transforming the work done over the last several years and building this partnership into a substantial commercial business.

items.statement: Management expects 30-35% year-on-year revenue growth for the company
items.quote: And for our company, it will be around 30% to 35% year-on-year.

items.statement: Management targets at least 25-30% growth and expects to reach INR1,000 crores revenue in FY25
items.quote: Obviously, we are thinking of at least 25% to 30% growth. Since we have achieved around [3820 31:26], if we add up 30%, it will surely reach INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: New 10,000 sq ft flagship showroom under construction at NSC Bose Road, Chennai, targeting opening by May 2025
items.quote: We have acquired a 3,045 square feet, around 3,304 square meters of land plot on NSC Bose Road and then commence prominent construction stage for the showroom, anticipating to open by May 2025.

items.statement: B2B gross margin 3.5-4%, retail margin 8-9%; overall margin to improve as retail mix increases from 10% to 25% in 2 years
items.quote: If the proportion of retail is going to increase of 20% then the retail is increased, then 8% margin it would be around what they say going to be 1.6% increase. So the retail margin overall margin from B2B, B2C is increased by half a percent, 0.7, 0.8 like that.

items.statement: Diamond sales currently 2% of total; focus on expanding diamond, kundan, jadau, polki segments in new showroom
items.quote: The proportion currently since we are not into B2B distribution of diamonds still now and the current proportion of diamond sales is nearly 2% of the total sales.

items.statement: Volume demand increasing substantially; gold price spikes drive investment demand and higher volumes
items.quote: Volume side also, the demand has been increasing and it will increase substantially.

items.statement: Management sees no major risks due to 50 years experience; all risk segments filtered by experienced management
items.quote: Since we are in the field from the past 50 years our management has a very vast experience. So, all the risk segments has been already filtered by the management with their experience.

items.statement: Inventory turns 4x per year; no hedging policy as gold prices consistently reach new highs
items.quote: Sir, in a year, it rotates around four times.

items.statement: Plan to insource 20% of manufacturing within 2 years; CAD design and automated manufacturing to be implemented
items.quote: Then you can take up, in the coming two years, at least 20% of the production should be of in-house.

items.statement: Geographical expansion planned: 3-4 new showrooms in 2 years after flagship opening
items.quote: And regarding geographical expansion, after opening of this new showroom, we surely have a program of expanding geographically for at least three to four showrooms in coming two to three years, two years, sorry.

items.statement: B2C revenue share target 25% in 2 years from current 10%; EPS impacted by increased share count post-listing
items.quote: Sir, since we have an analysis and we think that in coming years, when the storeroom gate opens, at least the B2C proportion should be at least 25% in the whole wholesale value, whole top line.

items.statement: Online platform finalized, implementation shortly alongside new showroom opening
items.quote: We have finalized the online presentation. Now we are working on it. It will be implemented very shortly along with the new showroom opening.

items.statement: Planning to report quarterly results going forward
items.quote: Yes, we are planning to have and we are working on the plan to give more results on quarterly basis.

items.statement: Volume growth target ~25% YoY; price appreciation additional to value growth
items.quote: So on the volume basis we targeting around 25%, right? Rajesh Mehta: Yes, sir. Raj Sanghvi: And whatever is increased in the price that would be additional

items.statement: B2B margin of 3.5-4% considered sustainable due to product creation capabilities
items.quote: Yes, sir. It is sustainable, because we have been working on the creation of the products and all. So we will see to it that we get that set of margins achieved.

items.statement: Volume aspiration to cross 1 million TEUs in four years from listing, targeting FY27-28
items.quote: When we spoke about that, it was a time in which we were listed and we said our volume aspiration is to cross a million TUs in four years.

items.statement: Expect to return to previous quarter EBITDA margin levels through volume growth and cost savings
items.quote: we believe that we will be coming back to the EBITDA margin levels of the previous last two quarters which w e have seen

items.statement: FY24 capex included INR23 crores for Mundra land; Mundra CFS development, Jhajjar ICD in FY26, and existing facility upgrades are key capex priorities
items.quote: This year's capex budget, apart from, so this in FY '24, we invested in Mundra land close to INR23 crores.

items.statement: Speedy JNPT license valid till December 2025; renewal discussions start Q1 of last year with option to extend 10 years
items.quote: Speedy JNPT, we have the license till 2025 December. We have had a good track record of performance. And as of now, the indication is as per the tender document, you get the renewal in the first quarter of the last year of operation.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 32.4% in Q4 FY24 from 31.6% in Q3 FY24; EBITDA per TEU at INR1,760
items.quote: The gross margin percentage has improved to 32.4% from 31.6% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Every 10% volume increase expected to improve gross margin by 2% due to 30% fixed operating expenses
items.quote: We believe that every 10% increase in our volume would give us incremental EBITDA. Our gross margin percentage would go up by 2% because lot of our, close to 30% of our operation expenses are fixed and they won't go up in case our volume goes up.

items.statement: April volumes showed growth over previous year; exports recovering as seasonal commodity bans lifted; volume uptake already underway
items.quote: April, we have shared the volumes with the stock exchanges and we have had growth over the previous year April numbers which indicates that volumes are starting to bounce back and we expect that trend to continue.

items.statement: Import-export mix stable at 76-77% imports, balance exports
items.quote: No, it has remained similar compared to the previous quarters. I think it is 76 %-77% imports, balance, exports. That has been the average.

items.statement: One-off impacts in Q4 FY24: INR1 crore bad debt provision and INR70 lakhs year-end employee gratuity/leave encashment valuation
items.quote: This is, few of them are like bad debts provision which we have done in the current quarter around close to INR1 crores and one-off adjustments on account of year-end employee gratuity and leave encashment valuation, that is also around INR70 lakhs.

items.statement: ICD Jhajjar land consolidation progressing; targeted launch in 2026
items.quote: ICD Jhajjar, with regard to the land acquisition and related steps, we are progressing as per the plan that we have. And 2026 is the targeted launch of ICD Jhajjar.

items.statement: Gati Shakti Terminal opportunities identified in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Haryana; not yet out for tender
items.quote: In terms of Gati Shakti Terminals, there are a few identified locations that we have. One in Gujarat, one in Maharashtra, and one in Haryana that we have in our list based upon the potential identification that we have done. These are still not coming for tender.

items.statement: Gati Shakti Terminals expected to be exclusive facilities, not common user
items.quote: Our understanding on that is it is an exclusive terminal at this point in time. And that is how some of the existing terminals or the terminals which have been tendered are gone. So we expect the same to continue.

items.statement: Mundra has regulated number of CFSs; company holds two facilities with reasonable market share in growing market
items.quote: Mundra has got a regulated number of CFSs at this point in time. So it is not as widespread number of CFSs compared to JNPT. So that is one point. Second is we have got two facilities in Mundra. And therefore, in our estimate, we have a reasonable market share in a market which is growing.

items.statement: Market share estimated at 10-11% of addressable market in ports where present
items.quote: So, we estimate our market share to be in excess of 10%, maybe 10% to 11% is our estimation of our market share of the addressable market.

items.statement: Historical volume growth 1-2 percentage points above industry; FY24 volume grew 8% vs industry 6.5-7%
items.quote: Even last year when our volumes have grown by about 8%, the industry volume growth was about 7%. So, when I talk about the industry, this is the addressable market which comes into the CFS that we keep track of and this is the addressable market in the ports in which we are present.
