items.statement: Akshaya Tritiya demand deferred but not denied; expecting strong recovery in Q1 and Q2
items.quote: The Akshay Trithya which has deferred has not really deferred that -- not really has denied the demand part of it and the demand is there and the quarter one, I think we will be showing you a better picture than the last year quarter one.

items.statement: Normalized profit estimated at INR23-24 crores excluding COGS impact from gold price spike
items.quote: So, the normalized profit would be around INR23-24 crores, you know, in general because, the sales has gone up, the unit quantity of gold sold has gone up.

items.statement: Planning new factory with 5x current capacity; land procurement underway
items.quote: The factory will be coming up, which will be at least having 5x of the capacity which is currently installed.

items.statement: Hedge gold quantity with gold quantity, not rupees; rupee hedging would require INR45 crores margin money
items.quote: On the part of gold hedging, again, I am repeating that it will be we hedge a unit of gold and not a unit of gold with rupee. And if you were to do so, then we would have to pay, let's say, you know, if you had purchased, let's say my balance sheet right now has a gold of let's say 250 kg, 300 kg. So, if I had to hedge that thing, then I had to pay a margin money, which would actually, if you just

items.statement: Service business volume growth projected at 15-20%; retail on track for 600 kg target
items.quote: The service business will again progress by around 15 % to 20% by volumes and the retail part of it is going smooth so in that case whatever the projections we have made for around 600 kg of top line, we are on track of it.

items.statement: GP dip due to weighted average accounting; higher gold procurement costs affected COGS
items.quote: The GP has got hit because we were following the weighted average accounting method in which the procurement of gold, which has been done at a higher rate, has affected the total average cost of goods and thus there is a dip in GP.

items.statement: Expecting strong recovery in Q1 and Q2 FY25; committed to fulfilling business targets
items.quote: Nonetheless, in quarter one and quarter two of this year, we are expecting a strong recovery. And I think we remember quite well our commitments and we are strongly focused on the business operations and on the business to fulfill that.

items.statement: JV commercial operations expected to commence in early 2027
items.quote: As stated in the investor presentation, we expect the JV company to commence commercial operations in early 2027.

items.statement: JV project estimated cost USD165 million with Ester equity commitment USD33 million (INR275 crore)
items.quote: The project is estimated to be set up at a cost of USD165 million. The funding for which will be in the form of debt and equity in the ratio of 60-40 with Ester's equity commitment in the JV being USD33 million, or INR275 crore.

items.statement: Will approach capital markets to raise equity funds for JV investment
items.quote: We will be approaching the capital markets to raise funds through the equity route for this investment.

items.statement: JV expected to generate IRR of about 25% and equity IRR of 35% with 5-year payback
items.quote: We expect the project to generate an IRR of about 25% and equity IRR of 35%, translating into a payback period of about 5 years.

items.statement: JV initial annual production 70,000 tons rDMT and 23,000 tons rMEG
items.quote: To start with, JV company will annually produce 70,000 tons of rDMT and 23,000 tons of rMEG, which will be scaled up over time.

items.statement: Domestic polyester film demand growing at more than 15% per annum
items.quote: In fact, it is actually more than 15%, although we mentioned 13% in our speech. But it is, in fact, more than 15%.

items.statement: Demand-supply overhang in BOPET estimated at 15-20%, improvement expected in next couple of quarters
items.quote: The demand-supply gap has reduced substantially and I would now imagine that the overhang is about 15% to 20%. That's about it. And I think we will start seeing improvement in spread over the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Specialty Polymer revenue target to almost double from INR100 crore to INR180-200 crore in FY25
items.quote: About INR100 crore turnover. And this year, the target is to almost double that number. and I think over the next 3 to 4 years, we can look at a turnover of about INR350 crore to INR400 crore.

items.statement: Specialty Polymer 3-4 year revenue target INR350-400 crore
items.quote: And this year, the target is to almost double that number. and I think over the next 3 to 4 years, we can look at a turnover of about INR350 crore to INR400 crore.

items.statement: Value-added film incremental margin INR6/kg domestic, INR40-50/kg export over commodity INR15/kg
items.quote: The metallized the print film in the domestic market because the component of value-added product that is getting sold in India is not much, the incremental value addition is about INR6 against INR15 we will be getting INR21 on an overall basis.

items.statement: No domestic BOPET capacity additions for next 2-3 years
items.quote: Yes. So domestic, there is no more capacity coming up for the next 2 years to 3 years.

items.statement: EBITDA margins to substantially improve in FY25, near balance by FY26 halfway
items.quote: I think as far as the EBITDA margins are concerned, you will see a substantial improvement in FY '25. And I think we should be reaching a state of near balance in FY '26, halfway to FY '26.

items.statement: Capacity utilization to reach 75-80% at Telangana and Khatima plants over next couple of quarters
items.quote: Which will now improve to 75% to 80% over the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Maintenance capex run rate INR15-20 crore for FY25 and FY26
items.quote: Run rate for maintenance would be in the range of INR15 crore to INR20 crore, yes.

items.statement: Value-added film share target 30-35% from current 28% at Ester Industries
items.quote: We are targeting about 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Plastic Waste Management Rules mandate 10% recycled content from April 2025, other substrates cannot offer recycled content
items.quote: The plastic waste management rules mandate 10% recycled content in flexible packaging laminates. This regulation will further boost the demand for polyester film with conversion taking place from other substrates to polyester because other substrates cannot offer recycling content.

items.statement: Second half of FY25 will be substantially better than first half due to backward integration and expansion coming online
items.quote: I think that the second half of the year would be meaningfully better than the first half because both factors would be different.

items.statement: Agrochemical demand revival expected around mid to end of Q2 FY25
items.quote: So, revival will take place after maybe around mid of the 2nd quarter.

items.statement: FY25 cash capex outflow expected at Rs. 1,000-1,200 crore
items.quote: Cash outflow for last year was somewhere around Rs. 800 to 900 crore and this year it will be around Rs. 1,000 to 1,200 crore cash outflow

items.statement: Rs. 14,000 crore MoU investments to be commissioned by end of 2027 or early 2028
items.quote: We have also categorically said that by and large, everything needs to be in line, online by mid, I think, 2027.

items.statement: Multi-year contracts and successful pilots expected to buoy future performance
items.quote: Future performance is anticipated to be buoyed by multi -year contracts, successful pilots, and new product introductions, along with new formulation introductions.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 phenol spreads were among the lowest since commissioning, with benzene price equal to phenol price
items.quote: Just to give you an example, benzene is the raw material for phenol and the price of benzene is the same as the price of phenol.

items.statement: AI segment EBIT margin was 16.4% in FY24 despite challenging environment
items.quote: In FY24, revenue came in at Rs. 2,724 crore. EBIT came in at Rs. 446 crore translating into a margin of 16.4% despite the current environment and challenging circumstances.

items.statement: Company adopted product pricing to rapidly transmit input price increases, preserving profitability
items.quote: DNL has also adopted product pricing to more rapidly transmit inc rease in input prices resulting in improved margin performance despite fluctuation in profit s

items.statement: Volume-led recovery in AI segment across dyes, pigments, fuel additives, glass, home and personal care
items.quote: In the Advanced Intermediates segment, I think there is a good volume -led recovery, which seems to be relatively sustainable and consistent when it comes to applications in dyes and pigments, in f uel additives, in glass, in home and personal care.

items.statement: Fluorination plant commissioned in Dahej, enabling backward integration for agrochemicals and contract manufacturing opportunities
items.quote: Deepak has commissioned production of its fluorination asset in Dahej. These developments strengthen Deepak's backward integration for crucial agrochemicals, enhancing the company's supply chain resilience, as well as being able to participate in various contract manufacturing opportunities

items.statement: Chinese dumping and destocking of intermediates impacting global pricing, but no new capacity announced in Deepak's core segments
items.quote: There has been a stockpiling of many of these feedstock s, many of these intermediates that are kind of getting unleashed over the last four quarters onto the global landscape.

items.statement: Long-term supply agreement secured with Petronet LNG to ensure steady supply and mitigate project risks
items.quote: During FY24, we secured a long-term supply agreement with Petronet LNG to ensure a steady supply and mitigate project risks.

items.statement: Board approved increasing stake in Deepak Oman Industries to 51%, making it a subsidiary
items.quote: DNL's board has approved increasing of stake in Deepak Oman Industries FZC LLC (DOIL) to 51%, effectively making DOIL the subsidiary of DNL.

The Photo-chlorination one is being commissioned, and we expect regular operations imminently. Our solvent project is progressing as scheduled and will be commissioned on time. The Acid Unit has also made significant progress, with manufacturing expected to begin in the next quarter or so.

items.statement: Mid-double-digit volume growth guided for FY25; 11-13% volume growth guided for FY26 on existing business
items.quote: our double digit growth guidance is for volumes, our sales will grow higher than that, EBITDA will grow even higher than the net revenue.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected 300-400 bps above volume guidance for FY25 and FY26
items.quote: revenue guidance, while difficult to give would be somewhere around 300 to 400 bps over and above the volume guidance

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of around 14% for FY25, targeting 15%+ over next 2-3 years
items.quote: EBITDA margins from a guidance perspective, . while FY25 guidance is somewhere around 14%. Over the next two to three years, we do expect this to increase to 15 and beyond.

items.statement: Regular maintenance capex less than Rs. 25 crore per year for next two years; grain distillery capex ~Rs. 50 crore but no affirmative plan
items.quote: the regular maintenance CAPEX for next two years we envisage will be less than Rs. 25 crore per year.

items.quote: the matter is sub-judice, it is already we have a favorable judgment at High Court level, but matter is under appeal. So, whatever time it takes, but in all forums, currently we have had judgments in our favor recognizing our ownership of the mark.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to Rs. 74 crore in FY24; targeting net debt free in FY25; Kotak loan rate reduced from 13% to 9.95% from mid-Q1 FY25
items.quote: bringing our net debt down to Rs. 74 crore. This sharp reduction in debt has further reduced our finance cost s significantly, from Rs. 40 crore in FY23 to Rs. 27 crore in FY24. As guided earlier as well , we are targeting to become net debt free over the course of FY25.

items.statement: Expect continued strength in order book for most of 2025 based on key customer projections
items.quote: As far as the reclaim rubber side is concerned, we expect continued strength in the order book for most of 2025 based on projections received from key customers.

items.statement: Invested Rs 499 million in FY24 across biofuel heating, technology upgrade, site upgrades, firefighting, and land purchase
items.quote: During the year, the Company has invested in CAPEX of Rs. 499 million in various projects including biofuel heating system for energy cost saving, technology upgradation in manufacturing process, site upgradation across all locations, firefighting system upgradation and for purchase of land at Solapur and for the subsidiary.

items.statement: Crumb rubber plant planned in two phases, total project cost Rs 35-40 crore plus land, approx 30,000 tons per phase
items.quote: I think the total project cost envisaged is closer to about 35 to 40 crores over and above the land acquisition that's being made. As far as the capacity is concerned, as I said, it's happening in two phases. So, I don't have the exact numbers, but I think you will pick it up in the MDA once it is done , but approximately it will be 30-40,000 tons in each phase.

items.statement: Historical EBITDA margins steadily increasing; expect positive trend to continue as utilization improves
items.quote: if you look at the historic numbers over the last three or four years, EBITDA margins have been steadily increasing . So, the attempt at and efforts are all at improving the margins on a standalone basis.

items.statement: Energy cost reduced 4% via wind/solar; further savings expected from bio-briquette systems
items.quote: on account of substitution to green energy sources by way of wind power and solar power, the energy cost at GRP has reduced by 4% with further savings expected in the full year on account of investments that the Company has made in Bio Briquette systems to reduce its fuel consumption.

items.statement: Wage cost rose only 2% vs 9% minimum wage hike due to automation and efficiency
items.quote: On account of increased wage inflation, minimum wages across most states that we operate in have risen by 9%. Again, on account of steps towards automation and improved manpower efficiency, the overall wage cost increase for GRP has been only a 2% increase versus the 9% minimum wage increases.

items.statement: India rubber demand up 4% in CY23 but reclaim rubber demand fell 4%; GRP grew domestic market share by 3 percentage points
items.quote: In India, on the other hand, the demand for rubbers has increased by 4% in calendar year 2023, but the reclaim rubber demand fell by about 4%. In backdrop of this, GRP has been able to grow its market share in India by 3 percentage points in the calendar year 2023 over 2022.

items.statement: Export volumes decreased 11% aligned with subdued global conditions; export share maintained
items.quote: Our export volumes have decreased by about 11% , and that is aligned with the subdued global market conditions, which reflected in a 3.5% decline in overall rubber consumption, although the reclaim rubber exports from India were by and large unchanged. Our share of exports from the country is maintained

items.statement: Engineering plastic volumes grew 13% despite Q1 disruption from fire; new ocean-plastic product range launched
items.quote: Despite such volatility in the nylon prices during the year, GRP was able to grow its volumes in this sector by 13%. Now this increase is quite significant given that the Company's operations had not stabilized until the end of Q1 post the fire incident in February 2023 at its engineering plastic plant.

items.statement: Repurposed polyolefin subsidiary started manufacturing in Q4 FY24 with key customer approvals in paint and lubricant packaging
items.quote: As GRP set up the repurposed polyolefin business under a wholly owned subsidiary, this Company formally started its manufacturing operations in Q4 of FY '2024 along with obtaining key customer approvals in the paint and lubricant packaging sector.

items.statement: New reclaim rubber technology commissioned; approvals expected in current year to drive growth
items.quote: GRP has successfully commissioned a new technology for manufacturing reclaim rubber. items.quote: While ocean freights tended lower for the first half of the year, increased tensions, and escalation of the regional conflict in the Middle East led to an increase in freight costs as a result, lowering margins in the fourth quarter of the financial year.

items.statement: EPR policy weightages and conversion factors subject to change; credit prices dynamic and not disclosed
items.quote: There is also a conversion factor which is under the purview of the steering committee of the government and therefore there is a possibility that it will change. items.statement: Rights issue approved by exchanges; will decide timing based on cash flow needs and EPR clarity
items.quote: we have very recently received the approval from both the exchanges on the draft letter of offer. items.quote: We will do 400 crores. 400 crores we will do. That will be 100% growth over Q1 of last year.

items.quote: For FY '25 is concerned, we are projecting from, so there are three parts to it which we have, sorry, I will say that, first is the two-wheeler, we will be targeting somewhere around 1,100 CR of fresh disbursement. items.statement: Blended yield target of ~20% for FY25 from Q1
items.quote: Blended would be somewhere that will come close to 20 odd per cent including my processing fee and everything. 20% is something which I am expecting as a blended yield for the whole year. And this will be from Q1 itself.

items.statement: OPEX growth guidance of 6-8% for FY25 and similar for FY26

items.quote: for used cars, LCV, since these are new products wherein we are not expecting much of that kind of bad repayments into that and since we have industry experts to o, we are expecting to bring an overall ECL of somewhere around 0.6% to 0.75% on these two products. items.statement: Plan to implement risk-based pricing during FY25 using scorecards

That we have not implemented yet, but we sometime during the year we will also go into a risk-based pricing where we will be able to price the better profile customers at say a lower price or give benefit of the price to the better-quality customer, and of course charge higher from the high custom

items.statement: MCSL own disbursements running at 25% of full-year FY24 volume in April-May; target to match full-year FY24 own disbursement by September
items.quote: Today we are, as we speak, we are already at 25% of what we did in the whole of last year. So, the plan for this year or first half of the year is to cover up whatever we have done in the whole of last year to cover up in by September.

items.statement: Security receipt balance from ARC sale down to Rs 6.63 crore from Rs 102.22 crore at Q2 end with no impairment
items.quote: Those security receipt now standing at a balance of only 663 CR, which provide that is even if the case have been sold through NPAs and all, but yes, it comes to the organization is equally focused that yes, this security receipt balance has to go down, and it's going down extremely well, and there is no impairment has been provided in the books as per the rating agencies are concerned as of 31st

items.statement: Fixed deposit book growing: raised Rs 6 crore fresh and renewed Rs 7 crore in Q4; hired dedicated FD team
items.quote: In Q4, we have seen the results as well. Our deposit books has started getting growing now. We have been able to raise 6 crore as additional funding, and we have been able to renew 7 crore fixed deposits during the last quarter itself. So, now we have seen the deposit book. We have also hired a fresh team for fixed deposits in the Q4 itself.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 order bookings were INR 13.3 billion, up 53% YoY; FY24 order bookings were INR 57.9 billion, up 112% YoY; order backlog improved to INR 62.7 billion, up 70% YoY
items.quote: For FY23-24, our order booking was INR 57.9 billion compared to INR 27.4 billion, up 112% YoY. This strong order pipeline helped us to improve our order backlog to 62.7 BINR as against 37 BINR of last year an impressive increase of 70%.

items.statement: Management expects order intake momentum to sustain in FY25, closely monitoring transmission projects under finalization
items.quote: we expect the momentum to be there . We are looking and closely monitoring the situation because we see a number of transmission projects which are under finalization now where the reverse options and things are happening. So, we are looking at the sustained ‘24-25 as well.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin was 12.8%, up 8.3 percentage points YoY; FY24 EBITDA margin was 10.8%, up 5.9 percentage points YoY; gross margin for FY24 was 34.5%, up 5.5 percentage points YoY
items.quote: On an overall basis the EBITDA for the financial year was 10.8%, which represents about 5.9 points increase versus the corresponding last financial year.

items.statement: FY24 revenue mix: 70% products/services/other, 30% projects; order book project mix lower than 30%; strategy is product-heavy
items.quote: So, project is we have about 30% of the total 31 billion revenue that we achieved in the last financial year and 70% is from the products, services and other business.

items.statement: No specific capex plans disclosed; capacity expansion through lean debottlenecking and process improvements; any capex will be officially declared
items.quote: So, if that will be there then we will be anyhow de claring that officially to all our shareholders at the same time. We would not like to comment anything on an investor call on this subject

items.statement: Export orders historically have better margins than domestic; India pricing and margins improving; lean, sourcing savings, risk mitigation levers in place to improve margins further
items.quote: Yes, generally the export orders margin are better than the margins that we get in the India business historically. But India market, the pricing is also improving and the margins are also becoming better.

items.quote: We are looking at about—close to in next 2 to 3 yea rs we are looking at about—15 to 20 STATCOMs to be put in India. items.statement: Company became debt-free; cash and equivalents INR 2,765 million as of March 31, 2024; cash generated INR 4,495 million in FY24; board recommended dividend of Rs 2/share after 5-year gap
items.quote: The cash and cash equivalent balance was at 2,765 MINR as on March 31, 2024 vs 1,573 MINR as on Dec 31, 2023 and Net debt of 1,730 MINR as on March 31, 2023. The cash generated was 1,192 MINR in Q4 and 4,495 MINR during the FY 23-24.

items.statement: Related party export orders (65-75% of export bookings) under negotiation; outcome expected in H1 FY25; not limited to HVDC, includes AIS, GIS, substation products
items.quote: In terms of the subsequent approval that we had taken as a related party, those contracts are still under discussion and negotiation and the related parties or the other group companies are participating in further tenders with the third parties. If they win and we are able to negotiate with the related parties, we expect to have a momentum in the first half of this financial year.

items.statement: Management targets FY25 consolidated revenue of INR1,600-1,800 crores and EBITDA of INR160-200 crores including other income.
items.quote: As far as top line is concerned; we have done about INR400 crores in last quarter. So, if we assume that run rate, then we can definitely cross INR1,600 crores, plus whatever this benzene downstream can give us. So nearly INR1,600 crores to INR1,800 crores can be a range where we will target to close our business.

items.statement: Management expects FY25 revenue of INR1,700-1,800 crores and EBITDA margin of 10-12%.
items.quote: So for this year, as per the last quarter of FY '24, we did almost INR400 crores of top line. So we should do minimum of around INR1,700 crores because the new business will also add on. So around INR1,700 crores to INR1,800 crores of top line, we should be able to do. And I think EBITDA level, we can be around 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Benzene derivatives greenfield project investment is around INR390 crores (excluding land) with expected turnover of INR400 crores at 85-90% utilization and 5-year payback.
items.value: 390 crores capex; 400 crores turnover at 85-90% utilization
items.quote: So the total investment other than the land and everything, it's less than INR400 crores, so it's around INR390 crores that has been the investment. And the expected turnover at 85%, 90% utilization is around INR400 crores.

items.statement: No new capex planned for next 2 years beyond maintenance; focus on debt reduction.
items.quote: Yes. That is what we are planning at present.

items.statement: Benzene downstream products (MCB, PNCB, ONCB) commercial production started Dec 2023 and Mar 2024; full utilization of 60-70% expected in 1.5-2 months.
items.quote: So, I think for another 1 to 2 months, we'll not be selling much in the market. So, I think after 1.5, 2 months, we will be coming to the market full-fledged with utilization of at least 60%, 70%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin was 7.7% in Q4 FY24; FY24 EBITDA INR119 crores (down 18% YoY).
items.quote: EBIDTA stood at INR31 crores for Q4 FY '24 with a margin of 7.7%; net profit for the quarter stood at INR2 crores for Q4 FY '24.

items.statement: Chlor Alkali margins historically 16-20%; peak revenue potential INR350-370 crores at full utilization.
items.quote: Chlor Alkali margins vary from say, 16% to 20%. And before 2 years, there was very good time over at that time, even more than 25% margin was also there, but that was normal. We steady case, we can expect about 18% to 20%, 16% to 20% margin.

items.statement: Dye Intermediates and Dyestuffs realization increased slightly 2-3 months ago but has been flat since.
items.quote: Realization increased a little bit 3 months before, 2 to 3 months before. Since then, it has been flat.

items.statement: Demand stability observed over last 2-3 months; destocking ended with gradual recovery at low speed; US/Europe remain slow; China slowdown causing excess volumes.
items.quote: Since last couple of months, we have been experiencing stability in the demand for our industry products. It seems destocking position has come to an end and gradual recovery, but at low speed, is there.

items.statement: Dye Intermediates and Dyestuffs volumes near peak utilization (~80%); no major volume growth expected; focus on diversification.
items.quote: So Dye Intermediates and Dyestuffs, they are a batch type manufacturing process. So there, reaching 90% plus is not possible. Usually, the work -- the peak utilization is about 80%. We are already close to that.

items.statement: Sen-er Boya (Turkey) recorded INR16 crores hyperinflation accounting loss (AS29) in Q4 FY24; volumes gradually recovering post-earthquake but timeline uncertain.
items.quote: During the Q4 FY '24, on implementation of AS29, there is a INR16 crores loss and the sale is already part of declared results.

items.statement: Net debt INR830 crores at March 2024 (peak); targeting INR100-120 crores annual repayment to become debt-free in ~5 years.
items.quote: See, at March balance sheet, our net debt was about INR830 crores. This is something a peak debt of what we are estimating. And every year, about INR100 crores reduction should be there.

items.statement: Permanently stopping production at Vatva Units 1, 3, 4 (built 1989-93); <3% tonnage capacity reduction; fixed overhead reduction to improve efficiency.
items.quote: Furthermore, company will dismantle and sell manufacturing facilities, and it will lead to a reduction of less than 3% in the total tonnage production capacity of the company.

items.statement: Chlor Alkali utilization at 82-83%; targeting 85-87% blended utilization in FY25 with 8-9 months at ~90%.
items.quote: Yes, it is already at 82%, 83%. I think there is still room to go up to 92%, 93% utilization. And things are in place for that. So I think about 8 months of the year, we should do around 90% and the remaining about 80%.

items.statement: Punjab government incentives ~INR20 crores/year expected within 2-3 months post-election approval.

items.statement: Inventory days elevated due to integration and 100+ dyestuff SKUs requiring stock for quick delivery; no significant improvement expected.

At the same time, our final product Dyestuff, over there, there are lots of products, more than 100 products. So, to match the required and quick delivery to customers, we are required to give larger stock. So, this is the level that will remain more or less same.

items.statement: FY24 consolidated EBITDA margin at 26%-27%, better than long-term industry and company average; FY22-23 was an outlier year.
items.quote: At the 26%-27% EBITDA margin also I would say that this is better than the long-term average EBITDA of the paper industry and our own long-term average.

items.statement: Expects FY25 to be tougher due to competition and dumping from ASEAN countries.
items.quote: The year gone by is over but the coming year is likely to be tougher I would say that the competition and also the dumping of paper from the ASEAN countries will pose a challenge in time to come.

items.statement: Sirpur Paper EBITDA ~30% for FY24 including state incentive on accrual basis; excluding incentive, EBITDA ~22%-23%.
items.quote: So, if I exclude that incentive part then the EBITDA would be close to 22%-23% this is on this part.

items.quote: In fact the corrugation industry has a very bad time the year '23-24 in the normal course, their EBITDA should be around 12% to 14%, but it was a bad year and it was around 10%.

items.quote: The wood cost which is a basic raw material for integrated pulp manufacturer remain very high in fact, it has gone up sharply by close to 30%-35%.

items.statement: April NSR increase only in packaging board segment, not enough to cover wood inflation; further price increases depend on demand-supply.
items.quote: No, see the NSR increase in April this year increase is just in a packaging board one particular segment. There is nothing as a major increase.

items.quote: Right now, our capacity utilization is close to 55%-60% month different month different period, but on an annual basis, our utilization is close to 55%-60%.

items.quote: I would say that we are more worried on the import coming from the Indonesia because the Indonesia is a part of ASEAN bloc.

items.statement: Packaging board machine (FY22) at 100% installed capacity; debottlenecking to add 10%-15% more output; further expansion when domestic demand-supply favorable.
items.quote: We are doing debottlenecking of the same machine and hopefully we should be able to increase production by close to 10% to 15% from the same machine this is 1.

items.quote: So, whatever the free cash flow will be there in the company that will become a war chest for all our project or acquisition or expansion, no question of converting the company into zero debt company.

items.statement: Corrugated box conversion cost typically Rs 7-10/kg, up to Rs 20/kg for specialized boxes; pricing linked to kraft paper prices.

items.quote: So, it should be around the range of INR6 crores, INR7 crores maybe overall across the year.

items.statement: Government pipeline is very healthy and expected to bear fruit in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: EBITDA margin percentage expected to remain around 20% in transition phase; absolute EBITDA will grow year-on-year.

items.statement: Margin percentage will vary quarterly based on revenue composition across segments like government managed services, cloud, data services, and low-code platforms.
items.quote: But from a margin standpoint, that will also depend on the composition of revenue, because each of the segments that we are trying to -- which -- is gaining traction. And it also depends on the opportunities we are trying to materialize.

items.quote: Our existing business grew to INR92.98 crores from INR79.08 crores. Our additional tech-enabled services business grew to INR21.5 crores from INR11.5 crores, that's almost 87% growth.

items.quote: Now the definition of our core offerings has expanded. So now we're not just doing licenses of our one communication platform alone, we have our communication end-to-end communication governance platform. We have our data platform and a low code platform to deliver managed services.

items.quote: We have a risk assessment team internally, which has been formed now, is once bitten, twice shy, there are many deals which we are even turning it down until unless things are there.

items.quote: Last year when we had this conversation, we have almost 600 people. This year, we have 540, that 60 people left. And we've invested all of this money into bringing in more sales personnel and investing in AI/ML.

items.quote: In terms of logo additions, we were we were able to add, I think, about three on the banking side. We added one in Sn Lanka, one in the Middle East from Dubai. And then on the government side, I think we added almost 10 logos last year.

items.statement: Expect total alcohol volumes to rise substantially to approximately 21-21.5 crore litres in FY25
items.quote: For the present fiscal year, we expect our total alcohol volumes to rise quite substantially to approximately 21 - 21.5 crore litres.

items.statement: Executing capex to enhance gears capacity from ₹250 crore to over ₹500 crore, excluding defence
items.quote: The business is currently executing a capex program, which enhances the capacity of our gears business from ₹ 250 crore to over ₹ 500 crore.

items.statement: Power Transmission closing order book at ₹287 crore including ₹90 crore long-duration orders
items.quote: The outstanding order book, as I mentioned, on the 31 st of March stood at ₹ 287 crore, including some loan duration orders of just under ₹ 90 crore.

items.quote: The outstanding order book on the 31st of March stood at ₹ 1,233 crore, which included ₹ 880 crore towards O&M contracts for a longer period of time.

items.statement: Power Transmission PBIT margin improved 275 bps to 36.7% in FY24
items.quote: The PBIT of the business grew faster than revenues at just over 40% - 40.1% to ₹ 107.1 crore with PBIT margins of 36.7%, up by almost 275 bps, compared on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Water business PBIT margin improved 600 bps to 12.8% in FY24
items.quote: The PBIT margins stood at a healthy double -digit at 12.8% for the year, up by almost 600 bps Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Maize procurement prices down 10-15% from previous year due to 20% higher crop
items.quote: The prices that we are seeing now for the first crop, what we're procuring for Bihar is substantially 10-12-15% lower than the prices that we were procuring earlier.

items.statement: Co238 variety reduced from 77% to below 50% of cane area, targeting optimal levels in two years
items.quote: Last year, it was 77%. In the coming year, it will be just below 50%. And we expect that in two years' time, we'll be at absolutely optimal levels.

items.statement: Rani Nangal distillery commissioned at full capacity, running on grain for next few months
items.quote: The Rani Nangal distillery is now functioning at full capacity. It is commissioned at the very onset of this quarter and is running extremely well. We have started these operations on grain and intend to continue with this for the next few months.

items.statement: No fresh capex considered at this point; all previous capex under execution
items.quote: I should mention that there is no fresh capex that has been considered at this particular point. It is all the previous capex that I've spoken about in previous conference calls, which is under execution by the Company.

items.statement: Expect surge in Water business opportunities post-election results with new funding from Central and State Governments
items.quote: We anticipate that post -election results, there will be a surge in business opportunities and new funding is expected to flow both Central and State Governments.

items.statement: Current sugar realisations at ~₹3,950/quintal refined and ₹3,900 sulphitation; expect prices to hold or improve
items.quote: Current sugar reali sations today stand at approximately ₹ 3,950 per quintal, for refined sugar at ₹ 3,900 for sulphitation sugar.

items.statement: Sugar inventories building domestically; ISMA requested 2 MMT export which is under government consideration
items.quote: As a result, as I'm sure you all know, ISMA has written to the Government requesting a n export of 2 million metric tonnes, which we hope is under consideration.

items.statement: Aim to double revenue to $200M and triple PAT to INR160-180 crores by FY26
items.quote: So we are aiming for anywhere between INR160 crores to INR180 crores of PAT by FY'26.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin of 15-15.5% in FY25, up from 13.7% in FY24
items.quote: So we will look at getting to about 15% or anywhere in the range of 15% to 15.5% on EBITDA this year.

items.quote: So if the industry growth rate is 14%-15%, we expect to grow better than that. And in certain verticals, yes, the growth will be back-ended specifically when it comes to PES, for example.

items.statement: Confirmed order book increased 27% to INR749 crores, executable in FY25
items.quote: Our confirmed order book across all entities stands at INR749 crores as against INR589 crores at the beginning of the year, an increase of 27%.

items.statement: Executable defence production orders of INR272 crores over 12-18 months
items.quote: It would be generally in the range of 12 months to 18 months.

items.statement: Plan to open marketing office in Dubai in FY25 for energy vertical
items.quote: The company, considering the potential of this vertical has positioned the business unit head in Dubai to enhance current relationships and build new relationships in the Middle East and seeks to open a marketing office in Dubai in FY '25.

items.statement: Defence production EBITDA margin ~30% on INR112 crores revenue in FY24
items.quote: So essentially, for FY '24 the production revenues was INR112 crores on which we made an EBITDA of INR33.18 crores which is about 30%.

items.statement: Digital investments to be EBITDA neutral to positive in FY25 vs negative in FY24
items.quote: As stated earlier with the digital investments was negative to EBITDA in FY' 24, the same as expected to be neutral to positive in FY'25.

items.statement: Heavy engineering growth expected to return in H2 FY25 after US capex slowdown
items.quote: That growth will be muted in this vertical in the first two quarters of FY '25, we expect growth to return to this vertical in the second half of the financial year FY '25.

items.statement: PES production growth expected to return in later part of FY25 as semiconductor inventory clears
items.quote: We expect that growth will return to this vertical during the later part of FY'25 with fleshing out of built-up inventories.

items.statement: Revenue from new customers increased 5x to INR69 crores (7% of revenue) in FY24
items.quote: The outcome of this can be seen from revenue from new customers increasing by 5x from INR14 crores in FY'23 to INR69 crores in FY'24 and contributing to 7% of revenue in FY' 24 versus 2% in FY'23.

items.statement: Anti-drone addressable opportunity INR3,000 crores over 5 years in India, plus exports
items.quote: The addressable opportunity in this area within India is about INR 3,000 crores for the next five years, not to speak of potential for exports.

items.statement: Finance cost to reduce by ~50% in FY25 after debt repayment
items.quote: Upon the retirement of debt in FY '25 we expect that these INR56 crores of finance cost and what is there on the P&L will reduce by at least 50%.

items.statement: Attrition fell from 20% to 16% in FY24; headcount 3,000+ with 500+ net billable adds
items.quote: Our attrition has fallen from 20% in FY' 23 to 16% in FY' 24. There is substantial headroom for growth in each of these verticals we serve.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guided at 12% to 15% with bulk of growth in H2
items.quote: I did talk about the FY '25 outlook, but for completeness, we expect to grow 12% to 15%. Bulk of the growth w ill come in
