items.statement: Targeting 2x revenue over next 3 years and 3x over 5 years from current levels
items.quote: And we are hopeful that we will be able to double our revenues over the next three years, and we'll be targeting that. And in saying this, I would also like to say that -- we are also targeting a 3x over five years.

items.statement: Electric Crane launch expected by July 2024 after RTO registration regulations finalized post-elections; Aerial Work Platform deliveries starting June 2024
items.quote: So hopefully, we will be able to start to sell our Electric Cranes by July onwards, which has been ready with us for quite some time now. The Aerial Work Platforms, more or less everything is in place and the product has productionized. So we expect to start deliver ing this product

items.statement: White labelling for American and Turkish companies already initiated; exploring acquisition targets (INR100-200 crores) for export market access
items.quote: Our intention is to spend maybe up to INR100 crores, INR200 crores. We have identified some targets and take over that company.

items.statement: Joint venture announcement with foreign brand delayed by 2-3 quarters due to NDA and strategic considerations
items.quote: It is in very advanced stages. More or less everything is true. It is just that we have an NDA so really can't disclose. There is some further, I would say, a technical -- it's not really a technical problem, but it's something in the interest of the joint vent ure that we'll be delaying this formation of the joint venture of announcement by maybe another two quarters, three quarters which I reall

items.statement: Management anticipates 12% to 15% organic revenue growth for FY25.
items.quote: So, it is difficult to give a number on this but we will grow organically in this around 12% to 15% is what we anticipate in the coming year.

items.statement: Company expects to spend INR250 crores to INR300 crores over the next 3 years for capacity expansion, four-wheeler projects, and hub motor units.
items.quote: We expect to spend INR250 crores to INR300 crores over the next 3 years to drive our future growth.

items.statement: Received orders from three Indian passenger car OEMs and RFQs from three more; one small lamp order worth ~INR10 crores annually to start SOP in 3-4 months.
items.quote: So, this is a small order at this moment around INR10 crores annually approximately for a full calendar year, but it is more of a beginning to start with the customer.

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 13.6% in Q4 FY24; management aims to improve margins in FY25 from the current 13% plus level.
items.quote: So, we are already on 13% plus and we definitely would try to do our best about the improvement of the margin.

items.statement: No price hikes; pricing fixed at development stage with raw material changes passed through via customer compensation.
items.quote: No pricing gets settled at the time of development and once the product is designed there is no change. It is then only the raw material change which is passed through and we get compensated by the customer product most of the customers not all, but most of the customers.

items.statement: Two-wheeler industry expected to grow double-digit for the next couple of years, supported by rural demand and consumer sentiment.
items.quote: So, double-digit growth is something that we definitely expect going forward, not just for the current quarter or two, but for the next couple of years.

items.statement: LED lighting share of automotive lighting revenue rose to 52% in FY24 from 49% in FY23; expected to reach 75% in next 2-3 years.
items.quote: Next 2 years, 3 years, it is going to touch 75%.

items.statement: Ambient lighting opportunity estimated at INR500-1000 crores in 3-5 years; internally developed technology with German agency support; working on 3 RFQs targeting finalization in FY25.
items.quote: So, currently we are working on three RFQs on this because we already could manage to get RFQ from the customer and we hope to finalize at least one of them in this financial year and having done that it will lead to more such businesses. So, we see a high potential in this business and the scope can go up to in, let's say, 3 years to 5 years up to INR500 crores to INR1000 crores that is the kind

items.statement: Maintenance capex ~INR40-45 crores/year; FY24 capex was INR85.86 crores; incremental capex for Hosur expansion and four-wheeler projects.
items.quote: No, so just our maintenance capex is more like INR40-INR45 crores. So we're just saying that over and above maintenance, there is some requirement, as we mentioned, there is requirement at those who plant, there could be requirement for 4-wheeler thing at some point in future.

items.statement: European passenger car headlamp order: new development, design approved, prototype under approval, supply start expected by end of FY25.
items.quote: One of the orders that we received for headlamps for European is a totally new development. So we are designing it in here. Right. And the development is on. Design has already been approved by the customer. Prototype is under approval. And this development time will take another six months for the tool to be developed. And then we will start the supply, let's say, in around the end of this financ

items.statement: Developing laser headlamp, night vision, and ambient lighting technologies for two-wheelers and four-wheelers; laser tech aims to be industry first.
items.quote: We are working on three main technologies. One is a laser technology which is a technology of the future and that will go both in two wheelers and four wheelers and we propose to be the first in the industry to launch that.

items.statement: Hero MotoCorp pipeline includes 6-7 new projects (mass market and Harley); 3 in tooling, 3 in design; expects Hero to become top 5 customer.
items.quote: No, we are very much convinced about this and we will be working together with Hero, not only 7 projects, further projects are also in the pipeline. And we hope this overall customer range, Hero will be also on the top.

items.statement: Yamaha Aerox 160 and export model launched last year driving revenue growth; more models in pipeline expected to sustain run rate.
items.quote: Yes, there are two models which has been launched during last year. This one is of Aerox 160 and other model is for export. So those models have given us positive growth and sales figure overall.

items.statement: No greenfield capex for passenger vehicles in next 2 years; will evaluate after securing a large order anticipated next financial year.
items.quote: So at this moment, for this financial year, we do not see any greenfield investment for passenger vehicles. And honestly, I don't see next year also. Because going forward, we will be targeting one big order, which we anticipate in next financial year, which will lead us to set up a plant.

items.statement: Management plans for a gradual uptick in FY25, expecting buoyancy in the later part of the year driven by monsoon and industrial output, but budgets cautiously.
items.quote: FY'25, you know, I can see things may improve, but it is good if we plan that the uptick is gradual. I think later part of the year should be buoyant because I can see the growth in economy.

items.statement: Demand showed a slight uptick towards the end of Q4 FY24; management expects gradual recovery in FY25 with stronger growth in the second half linked to monsoon and economic indicators.
items.quote: During Q4, the operating environment remained largely consistent with the preceding quarters, with a slight uptick in growth witnessed towards the end of the quarter.

items.statement: Women's innerwear and accessories/socks showed better growth than men's innerwear in Q4; athleisure grew in Q4 but declined for full FY24 due to weak first half.
items.quote: We see positive trends in women's in other as well. So, the growth has been good in this quarter, although it is lesser than what you typically used to the teens category, but yes compared to the men's inner wear, the women inner wear has shown a better growth

items.statement: Channel inventory reduced by 6 days for full year and 3 days in Q4; absolute channel inventory estimated at ~20 million pieces, still elevated vs ideal levels, especially in athleisure.
items.quote: The inventory in the channel outside of page, which we have access to, which is the channel part and I am not counting the retailer inventory, should be give or take about 20 million pieces.

items.statement: Investing in distribution management system modernization, network expansion (106,000+ MBOs, 1,382 EBOs, 1,670+ LFS), and D2C/e-commerce capabilities.
items.quote: We have embarked on this journey to modernize our distribution management system, aligning with our commitment to continuous improvement. Our distribution network expansions remain in line with our plan.

items.statement: No product price increases taken; margins protected via favorable fabric costs and operational expense optimization.
items.quote: favorable fabric costs and operational expenses optimization contributed to strengthening the operating margins without touching product prices.

items.statement: Received favorable CESTAT ruling overturning customs duty undervaluation allegation; entire demand dropped, INR 3 crore voluntarily paid refunded.
items.quote: So, in this order, it has been in our favour and the suspect has ruled that there has not been any undervaluation. So, it has been a favorable order and what we have done has been legally upheld.

items.statement: E-commerce grew ~30% YoY in FY24, contributing 8%+ of annual revenue and 10%+ in Q4; growth consistent across categories and price points.
items.quote: For the entire year, it was slightly less as far as contribution was concerned. It was around 8% plus for the e-commerce business and it is growing phenomenally.

items.statement: Ad spend at 3.9% of revenue (INR 180 cr) in FY24; guided range 4-4.5% for FY25 with disproportionate allocation to women's and kids' categories.
items.quote: Typically, as we explained earlier, that we typically spend around 4% to 4.5% of revenues ad spend. So, that momentum will continue.

items.statement: EBO network consolidation/relocation to larger stores continues in H1 FY25; net additions positive but offset by closures for better locations.
items.quote: The reason you have seen some level of consolidation in the last financial year, which I see also happening maybe for parts of this year, maybe the first half of this year.

items.statement: Inventory days improved to 93 days (from 124 in Q4 FY23); finished goods ~70 days; working capital days increased to 75 from 59.
items.quote: Inventory days was 93 as against 124 days in Q4 FY'23. The improvement in inventory days is in line with our continuing efforts for healthier inventory.

items.statement: Expect similar or slightly better EBITDA margin improvement of ~2% in FY25
items.quote: I am expecting similar type or slightly better than this in the next financial year. So, we are maintaining our guidance which we have given earlier.

items.statement: Expect 5-6% ARPOB growth in FY25 driven by specialty and payor mix
items.quote: I am expecting more like 5% to 6% ARPOB growth, mainly driven by the specialty and the payor mix improvement.

items.statement: Price increase of 2-2.5% factored in Q1 FY25
items.quote: So, we generally increase our price by 2% to 2.5% depending upon other competition prices and the market research. So, that will continue.

items.statement: Additional capex of Rs 1,200-1,300 crores for Brownfield expansion of ~2,200 beds
items.quote: So, additional CAPEX will be somewhere around Rs. 1,200 crores to Rs. 1,300 crores, which include equipment also, everything put together.

items.statement: Target 25% EBITDA margin in 2-3 years
items.quote: And we expect that we will be around 25% margin in the next 2 to 3 years' time.

items.statement: Expect 7-8% volume growth from occupancy and Brownfield expansion
items.quote: Yes, we expect around 7% to 8% from the volume side, and it will be mainly driven by better occupancy growth as well as this Brownfield expansion kicking in.

items.statement: Agilus Diagnostics to grow in line with industry at 8-10% over next 2-3 years
items.quote: So, we will be in line with the industry growth. So, the industry is expected to grow at about 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Agilus took 5-7% price increase in B2C business in Feb 2024
items.quote: We have taken a price increase of about 5% to 7% for the B2C business. So, that also will be kicking in for this financial year.

items.statement: Adding 100 beds in Faridabad and Shalimar Bagh, 100 beds in Manesar by Q2, 100 beds in Kolkata by Q1, BG Road beds by Q2 end
items.quote: is the Faridabad unit, which we are adding the beds, the expansion is almost completed, 50 beds we will be adding. Shalimar Bagh also, there 50 beds we will be adding, and this takes us to 100 beds for the current financial year. For Manesar facility, we are expecting to open by second quarter of this financial year, and we will be opening initially 100 beds, and we will see how the ramp-up goes o

items.statement: Put option liability for Agilus PE investors to be resolved by Sep-Oct 2024; funding via debt/equity mix
items.quote: Yes. So, by August, we will be knowing which direction we are going, means the next call for the first quarter. We will be having clear idea, which way we are going and maybe another one month. You are right, absolutely September, October may be the time by when this will be finalized.

items.statement: Legal costs of Rs 30-50 crores annually for legacy cases; expected to decline as cases resolve
items.quote: Right now, we are incurring almost Rs. 30 crores to Rs. 50 crores in the legal cost, which is relating to these legacy type of issues. As we are able to resolve all these issues, this cost will definitely go down.

items.statement: Key specialties (oncology, cardiac, neuro, renal) grew 13% to 62% of hospital revenue
items.quote: These specialties collectively experienced a 13% year-on-year growth in Financial Year '24 accounting for 62% of the total hospital business revenue, up from 61% in the corresponding previous period.

items.statement: Target 6,000 beds over next few years; on track
items.quote: Our plans to ramp up the Brownfield beds capacity remains on track and would enable us to potentially close to 6,000 beds over the next few years.

items.statement: CGHS rate revision expected soon after 10 years; could benefit 20% government revenue
items.quote: Last year, some of the diagnostic rates were revised upwards. However, the rest of the packages, which forms the bulk of the CGHS work was not revised at that time. But what we believe we have been made to understand by the Health Secretary is that the work is in progress, and that is likely to be revised sometime in near future.

items.statement: Dividend of Rs 1 per share (10% face value) recommended for second consecutive year
items.quote: I am delighted to announce that our Board has recommended a dividend of Rs. 1 per share, which is equivalent to 10% of the face value for the second consecutive year, subject to shareholders' approval.

items.statement: Annual network addition guidance for FY25: 180 Domino's India, 50 Domino's Turkey, 20 Domino's Bangladesh, 70 COFFY, 50 Popeyes, 25 Hong's Kitchen stores
items.quote: The annual network addition guidance for FY 2025 will be: 180 stores for Domino's India, 50 for Domino's in Turkey, 20 for Domino's in Bangladesh. In COFFY, we intend to open 70 stores. In Popeyes, our guidance stands at 50 restaurants and 25 for Hong's Kitchen.

items.statement: Capex per store can reduce by almost 15% through landlord partnerships and new capex reduction front
items.quote: We've also opened up a new front on capex. We're also looking at capex reduction, partnering with landlords on investments for capex, Capex can come down by almost 15% per store.

items.statement: Targeting 21% Op EBITDA margin at 2.5-3% consistent LFL growth for Domino's India
items.quote: At about 2.5% to 3% LFL on consistent basis, our margins should be closer to 21% Op. EBITDA.

items.statement: Positive LFL growth in Q4 FY24 and current quarter (April) for Domino's India; delivery LFL at 7.8% in Q4
items.quote: Despite high inflation in the past and a challenging demand environment, we not only resisted the allure of taking any price hike increase in the last seven quarters but work firmly on three work streams.

items.statement: No price increases in last 7 quarters; waived delivery fees to drive growth; introduced packaging charges in March to partially offset ticket price decline
items.quote: As against any price increase, we moved a step further to sharpen the value on offer to customers with a waiver of delivery fees after successfully piloting, testing, controlling, fine-tuning for nearly five months before we took the decision.

items.statement: Domino's India network at nearly 2,000 stores across 421 cities; added 28 new cities in FY24
items.quote: We are nearing 2,000 stores in Domino's. As you can see, we have accelerated the pace of new city expansion. We have added 28 new cities in the last year and now have presence in 421 cities.

items.statement: Delivery mix at 67.9% in Q4; delivery channel revenue up 12%; dine-in decline arrested in lunch hours with INR 99 four-course meal
items.quote: Delivery continues to chart new quarterly record with delivery mix at 67.9%. Delivery channel revenue was up by 12.0%.

items.statement: Dine-in LFL declined ~10% in Q4 due to delivery fee waiver fueling delivery channel; taking steps to arrest decline
items.quote: No, it is not 15%, but 10% That's also large, right? I mean, I think that's the point that you are making. So I think it is natural if you provide such heavy ammunition to one channel, which has inherent structural tailwinds where dine-in takeaway is moving to delivery.

items.statement: Medium-term target revised to 4,000 Domino's India stores over ~5 years using data-driven store placement
items.quote: Why we are revising it upwards is the following. Firstly, the teams are using data and technology. Like you see there is ~11 million monthly active users, right? And over a year, this is another like 40 million to 50 million monthly active users that log on.

items.statement: High capex phase to continue for next couple of years in India; no free cash flow generation expected for at least next year
items.quote: At least for the next year, you won't see net of capex, you won't see any cash flow generation coming through, yes.

items.statement: India leverage at ~0.4x debt/EBITDA; comfortable with 0.3-0.5x range; Turkey cash flows to service DP Eurasia acquisition debt
items.quote: Currently, a India business has ~0.4 leverage. I think it's a comfortable leverage in a growth market like India. We're not uncomfortable about it.

items.statement: COFFY reached 100+ stores in Turkey, 8th largest cafe brand; medium-term potential seen at 350 stores
items.quote: COFFY also became the first amongst our new brand portfolio to have recently crossed 100th store milestone. The AWO of 2,000+ also inspires our other emerging businesses to shorten the learning curve further. We view the medium-term potential as 350 stores.

items.statement: Popeyes expansion accelerated to 50 stores in FY25; product fit established, gross margins improving, own app/delivery launched
items.quote: In Popeyes, our guidance stands at 50 restaurants and 25 for Hong's Kitchen.

items.statement: Gross margin at 76.6% for India segment (+135 bps YoY) led by Project Vijay and commodity deflation; Op EBITDA margin at 19.1% (-100 bps YoY) due to delivery fee waiver and growth investments
items.quote: While the gross margin came in at 76.6%, an improvement of 135 basis points year-on-year, led by Project Vijay and commodity deflation, the operating EBITDA margin came in at 19.1%, down 100 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: New customer acquisition pace increased materially; average frequency ~3 transactions/year; early signs of repeat rate improvement
items.quote: Now the most important thing over there is our pace of new customers have increased materially. Now some of them will buy once, but many of them will buy three times a year. The average frequency is 3. That's what we've seen historically.

items.statement: Targeting order inflow of INR 12,000 to 15,000 crores for FY25
items.quote: So, we are targeting around INR 12000 to INR 15000 crores of inflow. Because there will be a good aggressive orders coming from state as well as center post elections.

items.statement: Expecting 15% revenue growth on EPC business for FY25
items.quote: So, we expect to grow by around 15% for FY24-25 on the EPC.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of around 9.5% for FY25 and 11%-11.5% for FY26
items.quote: So, FY25 we should be back around 9.5% of EBITDA margins, slightly better than that and then in FY25-26, definitely should be in the range of 11%- 11.5%.

items.statement: PAT margin guidance of 5% to 6% for FY25
items.quote: As far as PAT is concerned, it's all a mix of how the profits will pan out. Depending on the EBITDA margins, we should be in the range of 5% to 6% for PAT.

items.statement: CAPEX guidance of approximately INR 100 to 110 crores for FY25
items.quote: CAPEX guidance would be approximately 100 to 110 crores.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 11,697 crores as of 31st March 2024
items.quote: As on 31st March 2024 our balance order book stands at 11,697 crores.

items.statement: FY24 order inflow was INR 1,953 crores
items.quote: The total order for FY24 intake was INR 1,953 crores.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin was 8.8% for FY24
items.quote: EBITDA for the period stood at INR 691 crores with an EBITDA margin of 8.8%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin was 24.6% for FY24
items.quote: EBITDA for the period stood at INR 2,458 crores with a EBITDA margin of 24.6%.

items.statement: Bitumen cost is 20% to 30% of total road construction cost depending on composition
items.quote: 20% to 30% is depending upon the composition.

items.statement: Expecting flurry of bidding post June 2024 and ramp up of order book in Q2 FY25
items.quote: So, we believe that , post June there should be a flurry of biddings happening and we can ramp up our order book during this next Q2 and further on.

items.statement: SPA signing for HAM projects targeted before June 2024; BOT assets monetization may extend to December 2024
items.quote: SPA should be signed before June, by June.

items.statement: Approved fundraise via CPs and NCDs to realign working capital maturity, not to increase overall debt
items.quote: So, basically, we have taken an approval from an arbitrage purpose and from realigning the working capital as short term and long term requirement. So, that will be basic run like replacing certain WCL with CPs.

items.statement: Now bidding across roads, railways, power T&D, solar, buildings and overseas; 50% focus on roads
items.quote: So, segment wise road is our primary segment, road and bridges , then power distribution and transmission is a segment, solar is one of the segments where we are now qualified to bid and buildings is there, railways is we are looking at railways very aggressively.

items.statement: Pending equity commitment for HAM projects is approximately INR 153 crores for FY25
items.quote: As far as balance equity commitment for our HAM projects is approximately INR 153 crores.

items.statement: Water treatment project execution started, civil works ongoing, electromechanical from Q3 FY25; expect INR 400 crores revenue in FY25
items.quote: Should be able to book around Rs.400 crores.

items.statement: Expect existing inventory to be reduced by 40% to 45% in the next two years, not considering fresh investments.
items.quote: We expect the existing inventory to be reduced by around 40% to 45% in the next two years, this is not considering fresh investments in content.

items.statement: Aim to bring down overall debt by about 100 crore over the next two years.
items.quote: we are also aiming to bring down the overall debt by about 100 crore over the next two

items.statement: Estimating investment in new initiatives for FY25 to be approximately in the range of 50 crores.
items.quote: We are estimating that investme nt to be approximately in the range of about 50 crores

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA for existing operations in Q4 FY24 was approximately INR 3 crores and for full year FY24 was INR 81 crores.
items.quote: if you were to adjust for this investment, the adjusted EBITDA for the existing operations in Q4 and year ended FY24 would have been approximately INR 3 crores and INR 81 crores respectively.

items.statement: FMCG advertising revenues showing signs of revival, better than last quarter, moving positively; hopeful for improvement post-elections and festive season.
items.quote: Advertising r evenues in a while, at an overall level we can see that FMCG advertising revenues are showing some signs of revival not yet fully up there, but definitely better than the last quarter, it is moving positively, the indications are positive, hopefully after the election, certainty in the market things would be better

items.statement: Digital media revenues for Q4 FY24 stood at around INR 64 crores up 28% YoY; Traditional media revenues for Q4 FY24 stood at Rs.135 crore up 21% YoY.
items.quote: Digital Media revenues for the 4th Quarter stood at around INR 64 crores up by 28% year-on-year while for the financial year ended it was around Rs.249 crores witnessing a growth of around 11% Y-o-Y. Traditional media revenues for the 4th Quarter stood at Rs.135 crore which grew by around 21% Y-o-Y

items.statement: Incremental inventory write-off of approximately 10 crores in Q4 FY24 due to change in amortization estimation; expected to keep margins under pressure in near term.
items.quote: Approximately around 10 odd crore incremental write off would be there.

items.statement: Management expects 20-25% sales growth to be achievable over the next 4-5 years driven by real estate sector strength
items.quote: On that basis only, we have worked out that 20%-25% growth is definitely achievable.

items.statement: Internal projection to reach INR100 crores fluted panel revenue in 3 years, not formal guidance
items.quote: In another 3 years we are quite comfortable that we can increase the volumes of this fluted panel market u p to INR100 crores

items.statement: Current order book of INR140 crores for project business (UPVC windows and modular furniture), expected to increase by end of FY25
items.quote: Currently, we are having the order book of INR140 crores. So by the end of FY '25, it will be more.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin range of 14-18% for the business, targeting 2-3% improvement this year
items.quote: So we can say around 14-18% is the current range for the margin in our line of business.

items.statement: Gross margin of 45% is sustainable at gross level due to focus on high-margin products like fluted panels
items.quote: Yes, at the gross level, 45% is definitely sustainable. At the gross level.

items.statement: No major capex planned for next 2-3 years; regular maintenance capex of INR8-10 crores annually across 5 plants
items.quote: Regular capex you can say around INR8-INR10 crores, but it is regular capex because we are running around 5 plants.

items.statement: Extrusion capacity expanding from 24,000 to ~27,000 metric tons per annum with Bangalore plant addition
items.quote: Altogether we will be having around 27,000 metric ton capacity for the extrusion.

items.statement: Strong demand outlook driven by real estate growth, renovation activity, and shift from wood to PVC substitutes
items.quote: So all those things are giving us the sense that in coming years, maybe another 4-5 years, we can have a vision that industry shou ld grow at a better speed

items.statement: Fluted panel revenue reached INR30 crores in FY24 with 3-4% higher margins vs traditional profiles; produced at Jaipur, Coimbatore, and now Bangalore
items.quote: Fluted panel this year is INR30 crores.

items.statement: DSTONA (SPC) segment expected to gain momentum as market awareness increases; capacity already established for 1mm to 5mm sheets
items.quote: I think in the coming years, DSTONA will be in high demand. Because now, a lot of people are asking about it and a lot of demand we are getting.

items.statement: PVC prices expected to remain in 75-85 range; temporary recent increases due to logistics issues from China; company passes on sustained price hikes
items.quote: See last year the PVC prices were in the range of 75 to 85. This year also we also see in the same range.

items.statement: No pricing pressure expected from new competitors like Supreme Industries; large players increase market awareness and grow overall UPVC demand
items.quote: In fact, it will be a market shift also towards the UPVC windows from the other products, board and aluminium. So, it will increase the volumes and demands.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle target of ~100 days for stock and debtors combined, down from 158 days in FY24
items.quote: So we are looking for a figure of 100, approximately 100 days debtors and stock levels.

items.statement: Export revenue currently 1.5-2% of topline from modular furniture to European brand; aiming for better figures this year
items.quote: It's around 1.5% to 2% only for the overall top line. But definitely this year we are looking for some better figures.

items.statement: Geographic focus on penetrating Western region (Maharashtra, Mumbai, Pune) with new showroom, dealers, sales team and digital promotion
items.quote: We are putting our more efforts for the Western region, particularly Maharashtra, Mumbai, and Pune. We have opened our showroom in Mumbai.

items.statement: Arizo Studio Delhi NCR showroom on track to be fully operational in first half of FY25
items.quote: As scheduled earlier also, in the first half '25, they will -- it will be fully operational.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guidance of 10% over FY24
items.quote: See, for FY '25, we express our guidance of 10% over FY '24, given the prevalent position.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin guidance of 12% to 12.5%
items.quote: So the EBITDA margin for the FY '25, we are expecting around 12% to 12.5%, which is slightly lesser than what earlier.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth not less than 10% over FY25
items.quote: But the growth will not be less than 10% in FY '26.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book of Rs 15,490 crore as of March 2024, over Rs 20,400 crore including two new EPC contracts
items.quote: As of 31st March 2024, the company’s unexecuted order book stands at Rs. 15,490 crores which does not include the contract value of 2 EPC contracts recently secured for an aggregate value of Rs. 4,994 Crores. Upon inclusion of these 2 EPC projects, our unexecuted order book wo uld be over Rs. 20,400 Crores which is 2.7 times of FY 24 Revenue

items.statement: FY25 order inflow guidance of Rs 13,000-15,000 crore including Rs 5,000 crore already secured
items.quote: FY '25, we have already received projects worth of INR5,000 crores we secured -- L1. And apart from that, we are expecting another INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores. So the cumulative, it would be around INR13,000 crores to INR15,000 crores during FY '25, order inflow.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance of Rs 100-120 crore for new HAM projects and MSRDC
items.quote: Last year, we have taken around INR46 crores. And this year, we are expecting INR100 crores to INR120 crores capex.

items.statement: MSRDC project EBITDA margin expected between 12.5% and 13%
items.quote: There was a substantial competition by all big players. And there, we are expecting an EBITDA margin of, as we said, between 12.5% and 13%.

items.statement: JJM revenue guidance of Rs 2,500 crore for FY25
items.quote: For FY '25, our guidance for the JJM is INR2,500 crores.

items.statement: Bidding priority: EPC first, then HAM, then BOT toll cautiously

items.statement: Essentials BU targets 3-5x asset turn and 8-12% EBITDA margin

items.statement: Essentials BU new product share increased 2% QoQ on larger volume; Specialties BU improved mix driving robust top and bottom line growth
items.quote: In the Essentials BU, the share of new products on a larger volume has increased 2% quarter-on-quarter. And in the Specialties BU, the improved product mix has resulted in continued robust growth in top and bottom line.

items.statement: Standalone Q4 FY24 gross margin 36% vs 32% in Q3 FY24; EBITDA INR106 crores (+50% QoQ, +44% YoY); adjusted EBITDA growth 36% QoQ, 31% YoY
items.quote: Operational excellence and the improved product mix have resulted in a higher gross margin for the quarter at 36% versus 32% in quarter 3 of FY '24. The quarterly EBITDA at INR106 crores is 50% higher quarter-on-quarter and 44% higher year-on-year for the quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated Q4 FY24 gross margin 37% vs 31% in Q3 FY24; EBITDA INR98 crores (+70% QoQ, +52% YoY); adjusted EBITDA INR88 crores (+53% QoQ, +36% YoY)
items.quote: Gross margin at a consolidated level is 37% for the quarter versus 31% for quarter 3 of FY '24 and 34% for quarter 4 of FY '23. The EBITDA at INR98 crores is 70% higher quarter-on-quarter and 52% higher year-on-year.

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of 30% of face value per share, total payout INR16.5 crores
items.quote: Given the strong cash flow from operations and the robust profitability, the Board has recommended a dividend of 30% of face value per share, with a total payout of INR16.5 crores.

items.statement: Merger of wholly-owned subsidiary Yellowstone Fine Chemicals Private Limited approved for capital efficiency and cost rationalization
items.quote: Lastly, the Board has approved the merger of the wholly-owned subsidiary at Lote, Yellowstone Fine Chemicals Private Limited, into Laxmi Organic Industries. Not only will this merger be more efficient from a capital funding and asset utilizati on perspective, but also rationalize the corporate structure, resulting in savings of administrative and compliance costs

items.statement: Healthy cash flow from operations at close to INR600 crores for FY25 will fund growth projects

items.statement: FY24 capitalization ~INR270-275 crores, of which INR190 crores at YFCPL (fluoro intermediates subsidiary)

items.quote: Not only had we bought almost about 95% to 97% of ethanol as imports, but we've also consciously realized that unless there's a major price arbitrage, it may make sense for us to continue to import.

items.quote: FY'25, we do expect it to definitely be a better year than FY'24 was. Like we said, FY'24 was a difficult year with a lot of challenges that were thrown at us. But we believe that the things have stabilized, especially in the PVC business, both on Paste and Suspension.

items.statement: Paste PVC expansion commissioned in Q4 FY24, expected to ramp to 100% operating rate by end of Q1 FY25
items.quote: We commissioned the 41,000 ton Paste PVC expansion project during Q4 of the last year. items.statement: CMC Phase 2 expansion expected to be completed by end of Q1 FY25
items.quote: Further, the construction of Phase 2 of the CMC expansion project is underway, and we expect to complete this by the end of the first quarter of the current year.

items.statement: Fourth LoI signed with agrochemical innovator for advanced intermediate, commercial supplies expected from calendar 2025, 5-year revenue potential ~INR500 crores

items.quote: we expect Q1 to be Rs 500 to 600 crores. This includes investment in marketing inFebruary and March of last quarter we effectively paused most user growth marketing. We haverestarted that so if you include that impact as well, we expect Rs 500 to 600 crores

items.quote: And FY'25-FY'26, our plan is to make sure that the brand grows in double -digit in terms of value growth as the company growth is about 20% in general.

items.quote: Yes, historically we have always been around 12%. So, sometimes plus, sometimes minus and we will be reaching, we are confident of reaching there as we utilize our capacities continuously which we have started utilizing from this quarter.

items.quote: Mr. Basu what we were discussing, and we told you these are order s that we are negotiating, and we are very likely to get, we are in advanced stage. But that cycle starts from FY27 or FY28 and for the next six years

items.quote: we look at two metrics. Number one our IRRs which is 25% plus and we look at through overall project life cycle cash margin of 20% to 25%

items.quote: we have budgeted for INR300 to INR400 crores for that particular acquisition in this particular fiscal year

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 22% to 25% for FY25

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 16% to 17% for FY25 on conservative basis

items.quote: Yash, we are planning for a capex of around INR 210 million to INR 225 million for FY ’25. Sorry, INR 210 and INR 225 crores for FY’25.

items.quote: But currently, we are just trying to service our existing, domestic trade. And as far as, business from FILA, for the entire, for the stationary line, we have, entire, like we have our open books like, order books available to service FILA demand

items.statement: Gross margin improvement from ASP increases, better procurement, and product mix shift to lower material consumption items
items.quote: So the increase in consumption margins have been on account of three factors. One, our ability and to increa se the selling prices have resulted in our ASPs increasing a bit, which has been because of increase in selling prices as well as change of product mix

items.statement: Domestic demand strong across all categories; exports deprioritized due to supply constraints
items.quote: As a company our priority has always been to domestic markets. And for us, it's a good problem that we have always been at a short supply to our existing Indian trade.

items.quote: So, for us, the entire year is going to be ramping up ourselves to create a very out-of-the-league product line first and then offering the same to our consumer in a small back-to-school which we'll see prior to Diwali and in between Christmas.

items.statement: Wooden pencil capacity expansion expected to commercialize by Q4 FY25; utilization currently over 90%
items.quote: And we believe that by Q4 ‘25, that capacity addition should come in commercial production.

items.statement: No direct sales to schools; channel partners handle institutional orders; DOMS Art League and KidZania studio for brand engagement

items.statement: FY25 top-line growth of 25% to 30% within existing facility

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin range of 33% to 35% depending on product revenue mix

items.statement: Finance cost expected to drop to approximately INR3 crores per quarter from FY25

items.statement: PAT margin expected to improve from H2 FY25 onward due to lower finance cost and improving efficiencies
items.quote: We expect PAT margin to improve from H2 of FY‘2025 onward on account of lower finance cost and improving our efficiencies.

items.statement: Order book increased to INR3,000+ crores as of March 2024 from INR2,000 crores in March 2023

items.statement: EBITDA margin band of 33% to 36-37% and gross margin band of 82% to 86% expected to sustain despite mix changes
items.quote: So, this is the only range that our EBITDA margin is going to be at and our gross margin despite the change in revenue mix etc will always be between 82% to 86%.

items.statement: Energy segment to grow 25-30%, Aerospace & Defense at least 35-40%, Oil & Gas potentially 2x-3x due to small base
items.quote: Energy business will continue to grow at 25% to 30%. Aerospace, also has a larger growth, but you can assume that it will grow at least about 35% to 40%. Oil and gas, because the base is smaller, it could potentially go 2x or 3x also.

items.statement: Working capital cash-to-cash cycle targeted at 140-150 days; currently elevated due to qualification inventory
items.quote: Ideally, we expect our business's working capital on a blended level to be anywhere between 140 days to 150 days of cash to cash.

items.statement: New Hyderabad facility 10x existing capacity; incremental revenue from FY26; Phase 1 progressing well
items.quote: The state-of-the-art facility will include dedicated factories within the larger factory, tailored especially for our customers. Phase 1 is progressing well, aligning with our strategic vision for long -term growth.

items.statement: IPO proceeds deployed from Q1 FY25; CCDs converted (INR160 crores) and term loans redeemed (INR72 crores) in FY24; current debt ~INR37 crores

As a result of our total finance cost for the year including, includes INR29 crores of non -recurring cost towards interest and on CCDs and the one -time impact of IND AS on term loan closures that we have closed, we have short closed the loans.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 80-85%; FY25 growth on track despite constraints
items.quote: 80% to 85%. Mahesh Bendre: Okay. So still we are expecting 25% growth in FY'25. Rakesh Chopdar: Yes. This was the plan. This was the plan from day one. This was the plan from FY'24. We had a thing that we will grow 25 -30%, but, you know, luckily we grew 35 %. The same thing with FY '25, we are on

items.statement: Unit III facility near Kakinada progressing well with production expected to commence phase-wise during FY2024-25
items.quote: Unit III facility near Kakinada is progress ing well with production activity expected to commence phase wise during financial year 2024-25

items.statement: Expecting double-digit growth going forward, ex-COVID products saw double-digit growth this year

Like even this year, ex-COVID products, we did see a double-digit growth. And coming forward, that's what we are expecting to see a double-digit growth.

items.statement: Pricing pressure continues in generic business across regulated and non-regulated markets, difficult to predict when it will stabilize, similar to 2009-10 cycle
items.quote: Yes. So there is pricing constr aints across the world, we are seeing both in the regulated and nonregulated markets. It's very hard to say when this will stabilize. Sometimes it takes one year, sometimes it takes 2 years. This has happened in the past in the year 2009-10, so it's repeating again, but prices will stabilize over time

items.statement: Gross margins protected by backward integration and cost efficiency efforts, fair assumption that no big dip in gross margin
items.quote: I mean, I would say that is a fair assumption for now.

items.statement: Generic volumes consistently increasing, no market share loss, confident volumes will support growth next year despite price erosion

items.statement: Seven post-patent expiry generic molecules identified for FY25 onwards, 1-2 molecules coming off patent in FY25, continuing for next 3-4 years

items.quote: We have set up a complete innovative lab right now, where we are using flow chemistry, we are using mechanochemistry, okay? We are using different equipments -- microwave technology. items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to stabilize at pre-COVID levels but with quarterly fluctuations due to commodity volatility

items.quote: We're extremely bullish on our aftermarket potential after three years. We have maintained our market share very strongly in this environment and we think we should be able to do it.

items.quote: We are designing the complete solution for them. We are designing and we are using technology for that, from remote, from our office, from GPS activated devices. We are designing the plan for the layout of the roof and designing a solar solution for them.

items.quote: Chloride metals today supplies about 60% to 65% of Exide sales requirement, which is only to go up because they also plan to invest in their capacity.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY25 is 3% to 5%, starting near breakeven and improving through the year

items.statement: Tech:BFSI revenue mix shifted from 76:24 to 64:36 in FY24; BFSI grew 83% YoY in Q4, tech grew 5% YoY
items.quote: Our tech BFSI ratio moved from 76 :24 to 64:36.

items.statement: Recovery from -33% YoY in Q1 FY24 to +24% YoY in Q4 FY24 driven by Tier 2 GSIs, GCCs, BFSI, and India enterprise demand
items.quote: We pivoted focus from Tier 1 to Tier 2 GSIs as well as increased penetration in GCCs. We got into advanced technology training skills, and in BFSI, we increased penetration in large private banks and broad-based our offering.

items.statement: Capex for Q4 FY24 was INR91 million
items.quote: capex for the quarter was at INR91 million.

items.statement: Tier 1 GSI hiring freeze persisted for 6 consecutive quarters, unprecedented in company history including COVID period
items.quote: the technology sector has had an unprecedented reduction in workforce never in 6 consecutive quarter or ev en during COVID it was only 2 quarters

items.statement: Net cash at end of Q4 FY24 was INR7,185 million, up marginally despite dividend payout
items.quote: Net cash at the end of the quarter was INR7,185 million, and this is a small increase over INR7,179 million last quarter and INR7,157 million last year.

items.statement: Headcount reduced by 206 during FY24 as part of cost and product rationalization
items.quote: Headcount over the year has reduced by 206 and that's a part of our cost rationalization as well as product risk rationalization that we have been implementing.

items.quote: The Board of Directors met today and recommended a dividend of INR0.75 per share, final dividend of INR0.75 per share versus or this was in addition to the interim dividend of INR0.50 per share, which was paid in October 31 -- on October 31, 2023.

items.statement: Generative AI components added across all program portfolio; new specialized GenAI programs launched for customers

items.statement: Value destruction in tech sector creates risk of wrong inorganic acquisition choices; company being selective
items.quote: There is a lot of destruction, I should say, value destruction, which has taken place in the tech sector, and therefore, one has to be careful that we don't make wrong choices.

items.statement: New CEO appointed, effective July 1st

items.statement: EBITDA will decline in Q1 and Q2 FY25 due to Jindal Supreme de-hire, then improve sharply from Q3 FY25

items.statement: If Jindal Pioneer acquisition completes in H1 FY25, earnings will rise in those quarters instead of declining

items.statement: Order book as of 31 March 2024 stands at US$ 251 million

items.statement: Rig segment generates >90% of EBITDA; Mud Logging and Directional Drilling are minor contributors
items.quote: Majority of EBITDA is generated from the rig segment. More than 90% is coming from the rig segment.

items.statement: Regulatory approval for Jindal Pioneer acquisition pending; timeline uncertain despite all other approvals in place
items.quote: We have submitted an application in the third week of April, 24. We are following up on that application. items.statement: Q4 FY24 normalized EBITDA ~Rs 55 crore after Rs 6 crore one-time write-off from ONGC settlement
items.quote: For Quarter 4, there was only one transaction, which was one -time, that was to the extent of Rs. 6 crores, US$ 1.7 million was receivable, out of which settlement was done for US$ 0.98 million , so around US$ 0.7 million was written-off, and that was the expense that was written-off. items.statement: International expansion targeting US/North America market after MENA diligence showed insufficient depth; US offers large TAM and better ROI

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 59.1% in Q4 FY24 from 51.3% in Q3 FY24 and 48.3% in Q4 FY23 due to higher program fee contribution
items.quote: Gross margin is 59.1% compared to 51.3% in Q3 and 48.3% in Q4 FY23 which is on account of increase in program fee contribution in revenue mix.

items.statement: Effective tax rate guided at 26%-27% from FY25 onwards
items.quote: So effective tax rate from this year onwards, if you see, will be around 26%-27%.

items.statement: Receivable days guided at 55-60 days with efforts to improve over next couple of years
items.quote: It will continue to be at 55 days-60 days, but we are working on it. Best to leverage that in the upcoming couple of years.

items.statement: ESOP cost for FY25 guided at ~INR8 crores without new issuances
items.quote: With the existing set of costs, without any new issuance of ESOPs, this year it will be around INR8 crores.

items.statement: Cashback and incentives line includes ~25-30% cost of funds; expect blended CoF to decrease as usage becomes more ubiquitous and terms improve with scale
items.quote: It would be about 25%-30% would be cost of funds.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 34-35 crores after adjusting for FY24 execution and new orders in April-May.
items.quote: And the remaining work order in hand after reducing the financial year '24 result is almost to the tune of INR 30 crores from last year and since April and May we have got almost to the tune of INR 5.44 crores order. So cumulatively we have kind of INR 34 crores to INR 35 crores order book in hand right now.

items.statement: Most current order book projects expected to be completed within one year.
items.quote: And most of these projects will be completed or expected to be completed within one year.

items.statement: Management projects consistent revenue growth north of 50% for the next few years.
items.quote: Absolutely. That's what we have been projecting. We want to be consistently achieving what we have been achieving in the last year or so, three quarters. And we are very positive and optimistic that we could continue looking at what order book values we have right now.

items.statement: Management expects to consistently deliver margins similar to FY24 levels (approx 38-40% EBITDA margin).
items.quote: So that's a mix of our revenue streams. Each of them will have a different profitability, as you would be aware, Akhil. But on an average, what we have achieved in this year is going to be consistently delivered is what we are anticipating.

items.statement: Revenue mix is approximately 55-60% consulting, 25% technology/EPC implementation, and 20% R&D.
items.quote: See, our mix of revenues are actually from both EPCs as well as, EPCs as well as consulting and research, which is to the tune of consulting about, let's say, 55% to 60%. And about 25% is usually from our technology, that is our implementation in EPC, whereas our R&D is also growing, which is about 20%.

items.statement: Monthly revenue run rate is currently INR 2-2.5 crores.
items.quote: Approximately INR 1.97 crores. That is INR 2 crores. Approximately INR 2 crores to INR 2.5 crores.

items.statement: Carbon credit ownership is limited because most technologies are delivered via EPC contracts where the client owns the asset; future proprietary green technologies aim to include carbon revenue sharing.
items.quote: The problem with us is because we are mostly providing the technologies as an EPC contract for which someone else pays us. So there the carbon credit market doesn't work in our favour so that is a challenge. But now the technologies which we have we are patenting and which we are researching on is going to have a carbon component. That will be benefited to your customer also. So you are planning t

items.statement: No immediate plan for stake dilution or fund raise in the next 12 months; expansions are being evaluated.
items.quote: Sir, nothing planned right now. We have too many things. It is too early for me to state anything. But there are too many things going on in our mind with their expansions and we will definitely be coming back to you the way we plan.

items.statement: Employee strength is 70+, targeting 90-95 soon amid active hiring.
items.quote: So, 70 plus we are as of now, and we are I mean looking at the work orders, that we have probably will be reaching about 90 to 95 very soon in the coming days.

items.statement: Company holds one granted patent (transferred to company) and has one patent application in process; targeting one more research project completion in 1-1.5 years.
items.quote: Harsh, we have one patent right now, and we are in the process of filing another patent. So it will be two in numbers, and we are also targeting one research, to be initiated and completed within the next one year. So one or one and half years, so right now it is one that we have transferred on the company's name and one is in the queue.

items.statement: Management aims to reach INR 100 crores revenue in the next five years, citing need to scale team from 80 to ~300 people.
items.quote: I can tell you in the next five years, we have a lot of plans and I dream of, I can tell you to reach there because that is the magic figure we want to be.

items.statement: Dividend policy under consideration for the long term; no immediate payout expected as company is in growth phase.
items.quote: Definitely in the long run, sir, if I may take that liberty to answer you, definitely there would be plans, there are plans of dividends and other things. As the process itself is an evolving process. And since we also have a lot of expansion plans going on in our minds, it is not probably, it is too early probably to tell you about what kind of expansions we are planning.

items.statement: Marketing and investor outreach plan approved by board; building presence on LinkedIn, adding Twitter, and engaging agencies for branding.
items.quote: In fact, just about two days back, we presented the marketing plan to our board of directors also in the board meeting. And it's not only reaching out through social media, but also making our physical presence felt in the entire arena of our investors as well as our clientele. Networking is on our cards. And networking along with tie-ups with good agencies who could also take us to the next level

items.statement: No significant seasonality in revenue recognition as projects span 6-12 months, though order booking may have some bias.
items.quote: So in terms of revenue it is not that biased because what happens is the projects that you get are usually run through at least 6-8 months. So what happens is the revenue is distributed across the year and that is why in terms of booking the orders maybe there is a bias but in terms of revenue streams the bias is really marginal.

items.statement: Long-term CAGR has been 20% and company continues to grow double-digit as promised
items.quote: Our long term CAGR has been 20% in the past and we continue to grow by double digit as promised. We continue to deliver that which has been delivered in 24 also.

items.statement: Won largest ever single order worth 1510 crores from NMDC Data Center (Yotta) for execution in FY25
items.quote: Another very noticeable and moment of pride was our win, our largest ever single order worth 1510 crores, which we won from NMDC Data Center Private Limited, which is also popularly called as Yotta.

items.statement: No significant capital expenditure planned for FY25; only minor leasehold developments possible
items.quote: Ours is not a capital interest. Ours is not a capital expenditure side. Buying some few leasehold developments, which may, you know, happen because of the volumes increase or something like that otherwise we don't see any much of capital investment.

items.statement: Gross margins declined from 5.7% to 5.35% due to product mix shift; outlook around 5% industry standard
items.quote: So, our gross margins have come down from 5.7 to 5.35%. It's a combination of product mix and the, you know, sales cycles and product mix so the range normally what we give and the margins are in that range only

items.statement: Large data center projects have normalized margins but positive ROCE impact due to working capital structure
items.quote: In large projects, obviously margins are always constrained so I would only say at this stage that the margin for large projects will be normalized.

items.statement: AI-enabled PCs expected to drive high single-digit ASP increase and replacement demand in FY25
items.quote: Our gut feeling is that it should be high single digit ASP increase in the products on an average basis.

items.statement: Enterprise business grew ~70% YoY; embedded business grew ~92% YoY from small base
items.quote: Last year we had approximately 70% growth only in the enterprise business and in the coming year, we continue to maintain that momentum. On the embedded business which is our newer baby, we are just setting up the base and of course, we have a very small base right now but even in terms of size, we had almost 92% growth on a YoY basis

items.statement: Revenue split: 53% PES, 47% LIT in FY24; surveillance and visual display markets identified as meaningful growth areas
items.quote: Its 47 percent is LIT and 53 percent is PES.

items.statement: Inventory days at 54-55, above target 45-50 range; consciously working to reduce
items.quote: Right. So Aejas, this was a similar inventory levels that we had in, in the year of FY23. Usually, our average inventory cycle ranges between 45 to 50 days. We were hoping that this comes down further, but it has not come down and we are consciously working towards how do we bring this down.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of ~750 crores raised; debt-equity improved from 1.5x to 0.44x; ~50 crores IPO funds used for debt repayment in April
items.quote: With the IPO, with the public listing the capital that we raised for about 750 crores, 700 crores incremental capacity has been created. Most of this has gone into a working capital cycle purposes. Thereby our debt equity ratio falling from 1.5 times to 0.44 times.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded from A to A+ with positive outlook by CRISIL in March 2024
items.quote: Last but not the least, our credit rating in the month of March from Crisil improved from A to A+ with a positive outlook.

items.statement: Setting up India's first embedded lab in Bangalore; launching LOEM Make in India and visual display verticals in FY25
items.quote: We are setting up our own laboratory for embedded business where we can live demo the products and solutions so this embedded lab, the first ever in India will be set up in Bangalore.

items.statement: Forex risk managed via 45-day supplier credit, inventory repricing, and 20-50% forward booking of dollar exposure
items.quote: The way our business works is that we buy inventory on credit from all our suppliers. So usually what happens is that we have about 50-55 days of inventory, we get about 45 days of credit from all our suppliers on an open credit.

items.statement: Data center AI cloud installations just starting; more projects under discussion but too early to comment
items.quote: The data center AI Cloud data center installations and implementation have just started, so Sky is the limit but it was this was the 1st order that was finalized in India and we won this.

items.statement: Management reiterates confidence in delivering 25% EPS CAGR over next 3 years, consistent with guidance since 2022 JV with Vopak.
items.quote: The outstanding performance aligns with our guidance of achieving a 25% cumulative average growth in earnings per share over the next 3 years.

items.statement: Management expects FY25 logistics volumes of 5 million+ tons and distribution volumes to grow 25% YoY.
items.quote: I think if you take the run rate of the fourth quarter for logistics volume and slight improvement on that, I think, we should achieve 5 million plus for FY '25, if all things are normal as far as all other factors are concerned. Distribution volumes, we have always said that we expect a 25% increase from here on.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR4,500 crores by FY27 on track; Pipavav and Mangalore cryogenic LPG terminals expected Q1 FY26; additional 300,000 KL liquid capacity in FY25.
items.quote: You may recall that this time last year, we have set out the capex plan of about INR4,500 crores by FY '27, almost 50% of which comprised of these 2 cryogenic LPG terminals in Pipavav and Mangalore as well as the various liquid expansions in Haldia, Mangalore, JNPT, Kandla, and Kochi, which are proceeding on time and on budget.

items.statement: Ammonia terminal at Pipavav: 36,000 MT static capacity, ~INR500 crores capex, construction to start FY25 after permits, commissioning ~24 months.

items.quote: And we expect the capacity to grow next year also by almost 300,000 CBM. So it's more capex growth that is leading to revenue and EBITDA.

items.statement: Liquid division EBITDA margin improved to 46% YoY (INR396 cr vs INR272 cr) on new capacity and acquisitions; realization ~INR3,000/KL.
items.quote: We delivered the highest ever EBITDA at INR396 crores versus INR272 crores in the previous year, which is an increase of 46%.

items.quote: It has happened in distribution on account of procurement efficiencies, which we could get in this quarter. So the margins have improved in Q4 as far as distribution volumes are concerned.

items.quote: If you look at our presentation, the presentation talks about import of 25 million in 2034, 2035. Whereas in the current year, the imports of LPG have already crossed 20 million.

items.quote: For example, vegetable oil could be INR125 or INR150 a month, whereas a specialty chemical or an acid could be INR600, INR700, INR1,000. Could be 10x -- 8x, 10x.

items.statement: KGPL pipeline progress on track, expected to commission with cryogenic terminals by end FY25/Q1 FY26; no government delays reported so far.
items.quote: Again, KGPL is progressing well and is expected to come on line timed with our cryogenic, which is expected by end of FY '25 and Q1 FY '26. So we hope both to commence around the same time.

items.statement: Minority interest expected 15-20% of profit going forward; structure may change.
items.quote: But we expect minority interest to be between 15% to 20%, yes.

items.statement: Final dividend INR2/share recommended; total FY24 dividend INR6.50/share (650% of face value).
items.quote: the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR2 or 200% per share of the face value of INR1. The company has already declared and paid two interim dividends of INR2 in February 2024 and INR2.5 in August of '23 for the financial year ended 31st March. And therefore, the total dividend for the full year amounts to INR6.50 per share or 650% for every share of face value INR1.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin guidance of 10% to 12%
items.quote: Hence, we are cautiously optimistic of the coming quarters and of achieving our target guidance EBITDA of 10% to 12%.

items.quote: We are on track with our investments in Mahad and Baroda, which are at advanced stages of commercial production.

items.quote: So, the effective contribution of the hydrogenation facility as well as the Maha d facility would start kicking in from Q3 of financial year '24-'25. Or you can safely say that from Q1 of '25-'26 is when we will have the real contribution of these two plants in our top line

items.statement: Asset turnover for Mahad greenfield around 1.2x, brownfield expansion around 1.5x
items.quote: Asset turnover ratio for actually Mahad is a Greenfield. So, if I compare the cost of the plant with the top line of that plant, it would be around 1.2. And from the other side of business, we are expecting around 1.5.

items.statement: New plants expected to hit 60% to 80% capacity utilization in first year of operations
items.quote: Based on the feedback that we have received from our customers, we are pretty buoyant about capacity utilization hitting anywhere between 60% to 80% in the first year of operations.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin at 9.65%, up from 4.76% YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA margins stood at 9.65% as compared to around 4.76% in the corresponding period of the previous year.

items.statement: Gross margins recovered to pre-COVID levels of 34-35%, EBITDA still 400-500 bps below
items.quote: I think the gross margin achievement was primarily driven by a lot of business process re-engineering and so the material consumption etc are all kind of adding up to that contribution.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals demand regularized, price realizations improving daily
items.quote: However, I am glad to inform you with cautious optimism , w e have seen that demand is coming back in a regularized way and price realizations for the specialty chemicals is improving by every passing day.

items.statement: Fragrance and flavor division seeing healthy growth from new customer acquisitions globally
items.quote: We have seen healthy and profitable growth in terms of increased sales and improved profitability for this division in the year '23-'24. This growth has been led by way of new customer acquisitions across all geographies that we operate in globally and improved profitability.

items.statement: Camphor and terpene chemicals face continued pricing pressure due to excess capacity and supply exceeding demand
items.quote: We feel that this challenge in camphor powder and terpene chemicals will continue in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Chinese camphor production finding its way into India adding to oversupply
items.quote: I think just to add to what Dharmil just said, you also have a third element where there is a lot of camphor that's produced in China which also will have a tendency to kind of find its home in India.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity improved to 0.30x as of March 2024 from 0.34x previous year despite capex
items.quote: Net debt-to-equity ratio improved as on 31 March 2024 is 0.30x, as compared to 0.34x in the previous year. This has improved despite our investment in the CAPEX.

items.statement: Operating cash flow of Rs 142 crores in FY24 vs negative Rs 22 crores in FY23
items.quote: The net operating cash flow was Rs. 142 crores as compared to minus 22 crores in the FY '23.

items.statement: Interest cost expected at Rs 17-18 crores for FY25, depreciation Rs 21-22 crores standalone plus Rs 4-5 crores for new capex consolidated
items.quote: So, interest cost for the next financial year, we are expecting around 17 to 18 crore, and depreciation, we can assume around, for the current side, means for the standalone side, will be around 21 crore, 22 crores, and for the consolidated side, it will go up with the new CAPEX, say 4 to 5 crore more.

items.statement: Product mix remains roughly one-third each across three divisions, minor quarterly variations
items.quote: So, I think, Dhwanil, we will continue to be one -third, one -third, one -third, minor sub-aberrations happening in a few quarters, depending on one of the division having a little bit more or a little bit less, but we are pretty confident that in the few quarters from now, we should stay in the same configuration.

items.statement: TMD order book stands at Rs 3570 Crore for execution plus Rs 300 Crore export order book
items.quote: Currently, we hold an order book to the tune of Rs 3570 Crore, which are lined up for execution and an export order book of around Rs 300 Crore.

items.quote: We have, over the last 3-4 quarters, seen a downtrend in order intake which is reflected in the order book question on hand and this trend continues as of now.

items.quote: Our internal planning is that we have to be sitting tight for two quarters and save everything what we have got.

items.quote: During the last quarter, we have put in another 5 MW of solar capacity, taking our total installed capacity to 53 MW of renewable power.

items.quote: In the month of May 2024, we have taken a price revision for machines, which was on a hold for 2 years.

items.quote: The reason we have seen that our margins have come down closer to a single digit margin is that we have invested in capacities but not fully getting utilized.

items.statement: ATC order book upwards of Rs 200 Crore executable over next 18 months
items.quote: The order book for ATC continues to be upwards of Rs 200 Crore, which are executable for the next 18 months.

items.statement: Invested Rs 20 Crore in ATC machines earlier this year
items.quote: We have invested earlier this year, around Rs 20 Crore. into ATC, in terms of machines alone.

items.statement: MTD revenue mix remains 75:25 to 80:20 traditional vs machining centres; new VMC models driving growth
items.quote: It is still hovering between 75:25, or 80:20, depending on whichever quarter we take, depending on the projects we supply to, for that quarter.

items.statement: MTD capacity utilization at 65% with 35% headroom; continues adding capacity ahead of demand
items.quote: Our capacity utilisation is still in the range of 65%. So, we still have about 35% capacity available for utilisation in this particular division.

items.statement: Global economic challenges causing weak export demand expected to persist for couple of quarters
items.quote: The global economic challenges remain, and hence resulting in weak demand. This, we see as a business challenge for the exports market as well, for a couple of quarters.

items.statement: TMD operating 5 days/week in May 2024 due to low capacity utilization; foundry also reducing working days
items.quote: We have also announced a reduction in the number of working days in the month of May 2024 and currently, TMD is working 5 days because of lower capacity utilization.

items.statement: TMD active order book Rs 2300 Crore of total Rs 3520 Crore; order inflow FY24 ~Rs 700 Crore vs ~Rs 1300 Crore prior year
items.quote: The active order book within this is around Rs 2300 Crore. And the order flow during the current year was closer to Rs 700 Crore.

items.quote: In a very limited manner, we have put it on test runs. I should perhaps come back to you in another two quarters, once the commercial launch is announced.

items.statement: India added slightly less than 2 million spindles in FY24
items.quote: I think the spindles added during the current year is little bit less than, in India, it is a little bit less than 2 million spindles.

items.statement: MTD manufacturing for DMG Mori scaling from one to couple of machines; contributes ~5% of MTD turnover
items.quote: With respect to the manufacturing, yes, we are manufacturing for DMG and we have one machine, which is slowly scaling up to a couple of machines.

items.quote: So, next year's turnover should be around ₹5,000 Cr, +-5%.

items.quote: Investment is under consideration proposals have been made, but we are evaluating this proposal and once it is approved by the board, we will be going for some additional investment for the modernization of machines for balancing of the plant.

items.statement: Positive export enquiries but low conversion to bulk orders due to price challenges
items.quote: There is a positive flow of enquiries for export sales. However, at the same time, the conversion rate to bulk is very low due to extreme challenges in terms of prices.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 4.6%, FY24 EBITDA margin 3.2%
items.quote: In terms of EBITDA, which measures our operational efficiency, we saw an impressive rise from ₹22 Cr in Q3FY24 to ₹54 Cr in Q4FY24, with an EBITDA margin of 4.6%.

items.statement: Kaapas project generating ₹6-8/kg premium over peers
items.quote: It is abo ut ₹6/kg to ₹8/kg plus. So, you can expect good amount of profit, but it all depends only this project execution is not sufficient

items.statement: Yarn prices down ~10% YoY in FY24; Mélange down 25%

items.statement: PTA and MEG prices expected to decline, aiding production costs
items.quote: Prices for PTA and MEG are expected to decline, which could positively impact production costs.

items.statement: Textile exports grew 7% YoY in first two months of 2024
items.quote: Encouragingly, the positive trend has continued into the first two months of 2024 with exports growing by 7% YoY.

items.quote: The acquisition enlarges RSWM's footprint, cementing its standing in the spinning and fabric industry by incorporating substantial capacity: 80,016 spindles, 720 rotors, 12 tonnes per day of knitted fabric, and its processing.

items.statement: Risk Management Committee reviews risks twice yearly; Grant Thornton reviews compliance monthly
items.quote: The Company like RSWM is doing for risk management is that we have the Risk Management Committee which includes Directors, CFO and all Stakeholders like Business Head, Business Head - Yarn, Business Head - Denim, Business Head - Mélange, Business Head - Knitting and then Company Secretary and lastly Chief Information Officer. All kinds of risks are discussed and if any new risk is identified, it i

items.statement: Potential risk of increased cheap polyester fabric dumping in FY25
items.quote: However, there is a potential risk of an increase in the dumping of cheap polyester fabric.

items.quote: The RSWM management is pleased to inform the investors about the value creation on its investment in equity shares of Bhilwara Energy Limited, through unrealized mark to market gain of ₹138 crore on fair valuation.

items.statement: Expects FY25 growth similar to FY24 with Q1 slow due to elections, improvement after June
items.quote: The growth of FY '23-'24 is something that we are looking forward to also in the upcoming year. The first quarter could be a little slow because of the election effects.

items.statement: Annual capex expected to continue in INR 400-600 crore range
items.quote: on an average, we've had a capex of between INR 400 crores to INR 600 crores -- INR300 crores to INR 600 crores, if I can be broade r year -on-year. And this is a trend that we will continue

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 12.5% in FY24 from 12.1% in FY23
items.quote: EBITDA as a percentage of total revenue improved from 12.1% to 12.5%.
