items.quote: Gross profit margin for the current year stood at 37.1% reflecting an increase of 490 basis points year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Capex cycle ending; FY25 budget Rs 50 cr (incl. concluding capex); maintenance capex ~Rs 25 cr/yr
items.quote: For this year, we have a budget of Rs. 50 crores. That includes the concluding CAPEX and a normal ongoing CAPEX will be about Rs. 25 crores.

items.statement: FY25 capex will be well below depreciation; no new capex plan
items.quote: This year itself will be well within the depreciation. Our depreciation number would have definitely gone up, is also going up. And the CAPEX for the current year, the plan that we have it will be much below the depreciation number.

items.statement: Target to become debt-free by end of FY25
items.quote: this year? Rajendra Gandhi: This year h opefully before the end of the year we should be very close or aspirationally we should be debt free

items.statement: Appliances grew 33%, cookware 33%, induction cooktops 63% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: The biggest growth for us has come in from appliances which is 33% . O n the non-stick cookware, the growth has been 33% again or the cookware category, it's not exactly nonstick. Overall, the cookware category has grown by 33% for us and in the quarter our induction cooktop we have grown by 63

items.statement: Current demand environment not great; no input-cost disruption this year unlike last year
items.quote: On the current times , I can tell you that on the demand , particularly we are not in the summer products like fans or coolers but overall, the business is going through not great demand times.

items.statement: Input costs stable; passing on cost reductions to consumers; protecting gross margins
items.quote: This year we have not experienced that and we believe that there is a lot of learning that has happened and we will be cautious enough to protect our margins at the gross margin level.

items.statement: Retail expansion: 25-30 stores/quarter; COCO capped at 171; incremental stores COFO model
items.quote: we believe that we will be able to expand our number of stores by 25 to 30 every quarter.

items.statement: Maiden dividend of Rs 2.5 per share recommended
items.quote: I am also pleased to share that our board has recommended our first maiden dividend of Rs. 2.5 per share.

items.statement: ECL provision of Rs 4.7 cr in Q4 FY24 is extraordinary; not expected to recur in FY25
items.quote: I think it i s an extraordinary provision that we have made. And in fact , that has giv en us more comfort on our receivables

items.statement: Manufacturing share of revenue 91-92%; SKAVA merged with LED and deprioritized; modular kitchen manufacturing outsourced
items.quote: We are currently between 91 % and 92%, the total contribution from our revenue is coming from the manufactured products within the factories of Stovekraft.

items.statement: Target EBITDA of at least INR 300 crores in FY27
items.quote: In 2024, we have taken significant steps to lay a foundation for accelerated growth in coming years, with the target of achieving an EBITDA of at least INR 300 crores in FY27.

items.statement: Expect faster growth in revenue and EBITDA in FY25
items.quote: We are optimistic about FY25 anticipating faster growth in both revenue and EBITDA and the impact of many of our initiatives should be visible from onwards.

items.statement: Ad Tech business expected to return to growth from Q2 FY25
items.quote: We are backing that Q2 onwards of this year. We should be able to achieve our growth status on the Ad Tech.

items.statement: Plan to complete at least a couple of gaming studio acquisitions by Q2 FY25
items.quote: At this point of time, we at least have 4-5 ongoing diligences with various companies and we hope to get at least a couple of them across the finished line by Q2 of FY25.

items.statement: Core gaming businesses should generate 25-30% margins with room to increase
items.quote: We believe that core gaming businesses should generate 25%-30% kind of margins and there is enough room for us to increase our margins.

items.statement: Focus on acquiring core gaming IPs similar to WildWorks and Animal Jam for US monetization
items.quote: one key focus is core gaming IP s, very similar to what we did with WildWorks and Animal Jam, which is playing out pretty well for us and we think we can double down over there

items.statement: Expect FY25 to be much stronger for Esports given FY24 initiatives
items.quote: We personally expect FY25 to come back very strongly on Esports and are very bullish.

items.statement: Media rights growth slowed due to OTT funding crunch and TV channel issues
items.quote: The OT T players, given the start up funding crunch have struggled to raise capital and therefore have kind of slowed down media spends and also everything that is going on with the TV channels and the large media companies that kind of slowed down that process

items.statement: Raised INR 950 crores equity capital in FY24, net cash balance ~INR 1,450 crores
items.quote: This year, we have arisen successfully between the parent entity and our subsidiaries INR 950 crores of equity capital marking our largest fundraise to date and resulting in a net cash balance of approximately INR 1,450 crores.

items.statement: M&A deals will be predominantly all-cash to reduce equity issuance
items.quote: So, I think there will be predominantly all cash deals at this point of time. We want to reduce the amount of equity we issue unless it is really needed.

items.statement: Plan to bring core gaming IPs to parent level via mergers or direct IP purchase for cash flow efficiency
items.quote: the way we are looking at approaching this is a hybrid approach where we start bringing in some of our core gaming IP s at the parent level. This would happen through either mergers of existing subsidiaries or direct IP purchase in new M&A that we do

items.statement: New Animal Jam game expected alpha in 3-4 months, beta by end of FY25
items.quote: When we say new game, we mean something different, which is an entirely new game bein g developed by the team and that is something that we expect to take into alpha in about 3-4 months and beta by the end of the year

items.statement: Kiddopia ARPU increased ~1% QoQ in Q4 FY24 despite lower UA spend
items.quote: Lower user acquisition spending led to a higher rate of subscriber base decli ne in this quarter, while ARPU increased by around 1% quarter-on-quarter in Q4

items.statement: Playground Season 3 had 24 million viewers, revenues at least 50% higher than Season 2
items.quote: Season 3 had 24 million viewers. So, I think we are starting to achieve a scale that is worth looking at. And a lot of sponsors as well as Amazon, Mini TV have come in again in season 3 to generate significant revenues. I don't immediately have exact revenue numbers contributed, but I think they were at least 50% higher than season 2.

items.statement: AI task force created to build playbook for studio optimization and player engagement
items.quote: We have AI task force internally that is focusing on many innovative ways of using AI, testing it out on a couple of our studios with intent to create a playbook that can be replicated across everything else we do.

items.statement: RMG acquisitions not waiting for regulatory clarity, GST is clear, active conversations with large players
items.quote: On the R MG side , we are not waiting for any regulatory clarity, like you have right away mentioned, GST is already quite clear going forward and we are active plea in conversations with a couple of large players in that space to do something

items.statement: Industry expected to see double-digit revenue growth in FY25
items.quote: Anticipating a robust performance, the consumer durable and electronic industry is poised for a double-digit revenue surge in F Y'25

items.statement: Capex of Rs 2,500 per sq ft for a 10,000 sq ft store
items.quote: How we would do the math is we say approximately for taking a 10,000 square feet store , we will look at a CAPEX investment around Rs.2,500 a square feet. So that would be around 2.5 crores for making up the store

items.statement: 14 stores in pipeline for Delhi NCR over next 8-12 months
items.quote: So we already have like 14 stores in pipeline today in Delhi NCR region for the next 12 months, right?

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to remain similar to FY24 levels
items.quote: So, I think we would look at a similar number also going forward.

items.statement: Gross margin blended ~15%; mobile/IT 7-8%, large appliances 17-18%
items.quote: So for blended number, it would be what you see on a balance sheet around 15% and the lowest I would tell you would be around 7% to 8% for IT, mobile as a category and the larger appliances would be upwards of say 17 %, 18%.

items.statement: Cooling products ~15% of blended revenue in Jan-Jun period
items.quote: Overall blended to be around 15%.

items.statement: Mobile revenue share may rise 1-2% from current ~43%
items.quote: I would look at that going up by one or two more per cent in the coming time, but it will not drastically change from here on going forward.

items.statement: Targeting 30+ store openings in FY25, 10 in Q1
items.quote: So we would be doing around 30-plus stores in this financial year, out of which we have already opened six in the first quarter itself and then another five are getting ready which are due opening in the next 30 to 40 days.

items.statement: SSG target 9-10% for mature stores, blended 15%+ including new stores
items.quote: So for those stores, we will look at a comfortable number of 9% to 10%, and including the newer store opening, we will look at because depending on this quarter , we open the store. So, we will look at a blended growth of around 15% -plus comfortably.

items.statement: Uncontrollable costs from credit card penetration and NBFC fees
items.quote: especially now with just like payments, credit card penetration going up, NBFC costs going up. So these are all costs that we actually can't control because they are directly linked to the mode of payments and all.

items.statement: Inventory investment ~Rs 2.5 cr per 10,000 sq ft store
items.quote: And then another 2.5 crores of inventory. And this inventory would be majorly for the displays of stock and then a little bit towards the backup stock for over the counter product delivery from the same store .

items.statement: North cluster breakeven at ~Rs 35 cr net sales per store for 5-6% pre-Ind AS EBITDA
items.quote: So North cluster will give us that number upward of 35 crores average per store net of GST.

items.statement: North cluster margin trajectory to stay similar until stores mature in couple of years
items.quote: Margins will all remain the same more or less, because we'll be adding up of new stores as well for this coming year as well. So expansion in Delhi or that region is going to be heavier than other regions.

items.statement: Small appliances degrowth due to shift to ready-to-make products
items.quote: in the kitchen appliance category, we see a steep degrowth is because of the utilization of the product, because now everything is like ready-to -make idli maker so people are now actually picking up ready -to-make rather than cooking or making that dough at home.

items.statement: Financing mix 65% credit/financing, 35% UPI/cash across markets
items.quote: So the total blended would be around 65%: 35%, 65% being through credit card, payment financing or the financing activities on the floor versus 35% through UPI , direct payments and cash payments.

items.statement: Geographic expansion 50:50 North vs South, focusing on underpenetrated areas
items.quote: Right now, it will be more of 50 :50 mix up North and down South , because there are a lot of markets that we don't even have a store here.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guided at 8% to 10%
items.quote: So this year, we will not see the full impact of the recovery steps that we are taking. And therefore you know it will be 8% to 10% topline growth for FY25.

items.statement: FY26 expected to return to 15%-20% CAGR trajectory
items.quote: I feel, I mean the conclusion that, it's not a feeling it's a conclusion of our analysis that we will pretty much, get back on the track, of 15% CAGR.

items.statement: Export order book annualized value INR75-80 crores with eight part numbers across Mexico, US, Portugal
items.quote: But as of now, on an annualized basis, if I look at the RFQ volumes, the value of that order is about INR75 crores to INR80 crores, depending on the volume that you consider.

items.statement: New business order wins have lifecycle revenue of INR900+ crores, including INR390-400 crores export with North American Tier 1s
items.quote: The orders we have won have a lifecycle revenue of INR 900 plus crores. Of this, we have export business with marquee Tier 1 North American. So not just one BorgWarner, but their peers as well.

items.statement: Commitment to maintain EBITDA above 20% range and target minimum ROIC of 18%
items.quote: The commitment of the company is to sort of maintain EBITDAs above the 20% range and ROIC all our quotations everything is done to achieve minimum ROIC of 18%.

items.statement: IPO capex of INR170 crores, INR45 crores deployed to date, FY24 capex spend INR78 crores
items.quote: Out of the IPO process of capex of INR170 crores, till date we have deployed INR45 crores and capex spent for FY '24 was INR78 crores.

items.statement: Headwinds from four major OEMs (Mahindra, Tata EV, MG Motors, Mahindra Defense) to continue for first two quarters of FY25
items.quote: The headwinds that caused this dent in the last two quarters of FY24 we expect that to continue for the first two quarters of FY25.

items.statement: Asymmetric dependence on Mahindra transfer case business; lost INR35 crores top line in transfer case segment
items.quote: It is interesting to note that we lost about INR35 crores top line in the transfer case. So it's not as if we had not anticipated uncertainty with our major customer, Mahindra.

items.statement: Export business brings decidedly better margins than domestic business at component level
items.quote: Now when it comes to actually delivering a proprietary product the margins are of course the best, but even otherwise at the component level compared to the domestic business there is no doubt that overseas business brings decidedly a better margin.

items.statement: Strategic alliance with Toyota Group parts distribution company for opportunities in India and Southeast Asia with Japanese OEMs
items.quote: The visit was hosted by the parts distribution company of the Toyota Group, with whom we have a long -term strategic alliance. And working with them, we are looking at opportunities both in India and Southeast Asia with Japanese OEMs.

items.statement: Three-wheeler EV transmission development underway with significant OEM and startup ecosystem; not yet in budget/long-term plan
items.quote: So, I can tell you that, in the three wheeler segment, we are, working with all the stakeholders there, we are in touch with the vehicle engineers, who are advising, these companies.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR2.60 per equity share (face value INR5) for FY24
items.quote: Finally, to conclude, the Board of Directors at its meeting has recommended final dividend of INR2.60 per equity share of face value of INR5 each for FY'23-'24.

items.statement: Management targets 18-20% top-line growth and 15-20% bottom-line growth for FY25, with a conservative estimate of 15% and optimistic of 20%.
items.quote: we will want to continue to grow at about 18 % to 20% in terms of top line. And in the same way with our mix of gold versus diamonds stud ratio and the other products, we will also want to ensure that our bottom line also grows approximately between 15 % to 20%.

items.statement: Management aims to improve EBITDA margin towards 8% from current 7.3% by increasing stud ratio 100-150 bps annually.
items.quote: our EBITDA margin is at 7.3% that we have seen, and we will work on increasing it towards 8%, that's what we are saying, that is going to be our endeavor.

items.statement: Average capex per store is Rs 6,000-7,000 per sq ft, averaging Rs 2.5 crore per store; most stores are leased, not owned.
items.quote: on an average around Rs. 2.5 crore is our CAPEX per store, there are stores w here we have incurred Rs. 1.6 crore also, there are stores which have got Rs. 1.6 crore and Rs. 1.2 crore and Rs. 2.5 crore, there are multiple ranges, but average is around Rs. 6,000 per store, per square feet

items.statement: Export revenue grew from Rs 70 crore to Rs 187-188 crore in FY24; export gross margins are 6-7%.
items.quote: export last year was Rs. 70 crore to be precise and this year we have done exports around Rs. 187 crore to Rs. 188 crore. So, as you are aware export business gross margins are usually lower, let's say 6% to 7% range.

items.statement: Gold prices rose from ~Rs 57,000 to ~Rs 67,000 in FY24, impacting consumer behavior and shifting demand to lighter diamond-studded jewellery.
items.quote: the way it has worked out in the previous financial year, which has moved from ~Rs. 57,000 in the beginning of the year to about Rs. 67,000 by the end of the year

items.statement: Volume growth flat in recent period due to high gold prices; value growth driven by price increase. Wedding jewellery demand remains inelastic.
items.quote: in terms of value till Akshaya Tritiya, the value growth we can talk about 15% odd, but in terms of volume, we have not seen much of growth happening. So, people are taking a little bit of time to get used to the new gold prices.

items.statement: Stud ratio increased 100 bps to 11.4% in FY24; target 100-130 bps annual increase to offset gold margin pressure.
items.quote: our stud ratio is 11.4% as on date. And you are all aware that our fellow friends have had a bigger share in terms of their stud ratio and the diamond jewellery sales. So, even if we do a 100 to 150 basis point jump in the stud ratio that will create an upward pressure on the margins and the EBITDA.

items.statement: Competitive intensity increasing with more discounts and aggressive campaigns from peers, pressuring margins; expected to stabilize in 4-5 years.
items.quote: the competitive scenario is increasing, we have our fellow jewelers who are also working towards , trying to acquire new customers. And in that competitive scenario, there are more offers and discounts and aggressive campaigns that are happening and that is what is leading to this whole, downward pressure on the margins.

items.statement: Gold metal loan share increased from 55% to 61% of borrowing; target 75% to reduce finance cost.
items.quote: last year it was around 55% and has improved to 61% as of March 24, we propose to take it to around 75%.

items.statement: Plan to add 15-20 stores in FY25 (8-10 COCO, 8-10 franchise); 70-80% in East and North India.
items.quote: we are looking at about 8 to 10 Company owned, Company operated stores and 8 to 10 franchisees these are the thought process with which we are working for the new financial year. so about adding between 15 to 20 odd stores in the coming year.

items.statement: Old gold exchange share rose from 25% to 32% of business, indicating shift from unorganized to organized sector.
items.quote: our old gold exchange with our customers has grown substantially, two years back it was about 25% of the overall business,, but today we see 32% of the overall business is happening through the exchange of old gold.

items.statement: New customer acquisition ~45-50% of transacting customers; repeat buyers ~55%. New customer growth rate 5-10% YoY.
items.quote: we had a total number of customers that transacted was 5,54,000 and out of that new customer was 2,72,000. So, approximately 45% to 50%, that's how one has to look at it. And the repeat buyers were the remaining 2,80,000 odd, so around 55%.

items.statement: Launched Marygold savings scheme (6-9 month tenure) with fixed and flexible options to help consumers manage high gold price volatility.
items.quote: we have launched the Marygold scheme, in which a consumer can keep accumulating their money, save it with us over a period of six months or nine months and then they can buy it at the end of the tenure and there is a flexible option and a fixed option.

items.statement: Dubai store inaugurated on Akshaya Tritiya; global expansion is long-term (5-6 years) after East/North and West/South focus.
items.quote: the store in Dubai we did the puja and the auspicious beginning on the Day of Akshaya Tritiya, store in Dubai is under I wouldn't say the initiatives, the plan, the consumer connect, all those things are under process and right now there is nothing substantial to talk about

name: Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd

items.statement: Confident of sustaining 29% revenue growth and 35% EBITDA growth in years ahead
items.quote: We feel quite confident in sustaining this growth for the years to come.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion CAPEX estimated at Rs 60-65 lakh per bed for 450 beds across Noida Extension and Greater Noida
items.quote: So, the CAPEX that we have taken for the expansion of our existing Brownfields because it is not a Greenfield expansion, it is Brownfield. So, we feel 60 lakhs to 65 lakhs per bed CAPEX is required in terms of our both Noida Extension and Greater Noida Hospital coming up.

items.statement: Acquisition CAPEX estimated at Rs 60-70 lakh per bed for existing facilities
items.quote: As far as the CAPEX per bed is concerned, see if you look at it recently, we acquired the hospital in Faridabad, and it is when we expanded and we add medical equipments to it. So, we are paying roughly around Rs. 150 crores for a bed capacity of close to 200 beds, so coming to the CAPEX for bed of 60 lakhs to 70 lakhs roughly.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to remain sustainable at current ~27% level for next 3-4 years despite new hospital additions
items.quote: EBITDA margins, we are quite good in terms of EBITDA margins are concerned and we expect the margins to be sustainable because even though new hospitals are coming up, but there is still lot of occupancy growth that is going to happen in our existing hospitals of Greater Noida and Noida Extension.

items.statement: Cash patient schedule of charges revised annually with ~6-8% impact
items.quote: So, I think roughly I would say around 6%-7% can make an impact on the cash patient, 6% to 8% kind of.

items.statement: International patient revenue targeted to reach double-digit contribution in overall revenue in coming years
items.quote: We feel that in the years to come international patients should be contributing close to a double-digit contribution in our overall revenue and we are confident at this time.

items.statement: Case mix shifting toward super specialties (oncology, transplant, robotics) driving ARPOB growth; Noida Extension ARPOB expected to touch Rs 40,000
items.quote: I am quite confident that in the coming quarters this ARPOB in Noida Extension will even touch Rs. 40,000.

items.statement: Rs 70 crore frozen by income tax since October 2023; expected to be released within FY25
items.quote: We expect that in this financial year, that thing should be behind our back and this block money will be given back to us.

items.statement: Government receivables elevated at ~40% of revenue due to election-related delays; expected to normalize significantly in coming quarters
items.quote: We are in touch with the department and expect receivables to come down significantly by the coming quarter.

items.statement: Faridabad hospital (200 beds) operational since May 12, 2024; expected to ramp up occupancy faster than Jhansi
items.quote: We feel that because the health insurance is already there, some star doctors are there, this hospital should ramp up very soon and we are quite confident about the geographic area about where the hospital is located.

items.statement: Plan to acquire one hospital per year through FY26; targeting North India (UP, MP, Haryana, Bihar border)
items.quote: This strategic move with the purchase consideration of INR 1,160 million underscores our commitment to growth through inorganic mode and is in line with the commitment to acquiring one hospital each year through Financial '24 to '26.

items.statement: Greater Noida adding 200 beds focused on international patients; Noida Extension also has expansion scope
items.quote: Furthermore, we are strategically developing the infrastructure of the additional 200 beds at our Greater Noida location, the focus on catering to international patients.

items.statement: Faridabad hospital may drag margins initially but consolidated EBITDA margins expected to remain sustainable due to occupancy ramp-up in existing hospitals
items.quote: Yes, quite sustainable because the existing other hospitals that we still have the occupancy to ramp up, there the EBITDA margins will grow. So, in the overall consolidate level group, the margins would be sustainable.

items.statement: Government payer mix at ~40% of revenue; expected to decline as cash/insurance and international segments grow faster
items.quote: It will come down. See, today we have occupancy to ramp up right, we can take it, but one if given a choice between a cash and insurance patient and if you have restriction on the number of beds, then priorities always given to other segments.

items.statement: Management targets revenue of Rs. 900-1,000 crore by FY27 with EBITDA around 10%.
items.quote: We feel that we can achieve 20% growth easily. When we enter Maharashtra, we may get a growth of over 20% that year. You can calculate. We believe that we will see the company at Rs. 900-1,000 crores.

items.statement: FY25 capex estimated at Rs. 45-50 crore for Gujarat and Maharashtra combined, funded from internal accruals.
items.quote: Around Rs. 45 crore capex that I have been saying. We will incur Rs. 45 to 50 crore capex this year as well.

items.statement: Maharashtra Unit 8 Phase 1 capex estimated at Rs. 40-45 crore, completion by Q4 FY25; full project Rs. 100 crore over 4-5 years.
items.quote: Phase 1 capex, including the purchase of land and civil work, is estimated to be around Rs. 40-45 crores and is expected to be completed by quarter 4, 2025.

items.statement: IBC Line 1 at Unit 7 operating at 50% capacity; Line 2 to be ordered once utilization crosses 70-75%.
items.quote: At Unit 7, we have already commissioned Line 1 for IBC in July '23, which is currently operating at 50% capacity. We plan to order Line 2 IBC very soon, as soon as we cross 70-75% of the capacity.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to improve to 10-11% in FY25 from 9.1% in FY24 as raw material prices bottom out.
items.quote: We are expecting it to be between 10% to 11%.

items.statement: Management sees strong demand recovery in chemical sector driving volume growth across all three verticals.
items.quote: This year we see an opportunity in the chemical sector also, and the HDPE sector also. This year the entire industry is hoping to be good, because chemical sector is also recovering at the same time the HDPE demand is coming from them.

items.statement: FY25 volume mix expected: IBC 36-37%, HDPE Drum ~43%, MS Drum 11%, others ~10%.
items.quote: IBC would be around 36% to 37% and around 43% would be from Polymer. The revenue will keep switching over like this. Priyank Parekh: Ok and 10% others will still remain? Bijaykumar Agarwal: Yes 10% is nominal so it would be around 10

items.statement: Inventory loss of ~Rs. 5 crore for FY24 due to 45-day inventory lag during falling raw material prices.
items.quote: I assume that my inventory loss on my stock would have been around Rs. 5 crores for the whole year.

items.statement: Capex to be funded entirely from internal accruals; company aims to maintain net debt zero.
items.quote: We expect to continue maintaining a healthy balance sheet and capex is expected to be funded from internal accruals and cash balance, to maintain net debt zero balance.

items.statement: Maharashtra Unit 8 operations expected to start by December 2024 (Q4 FY25), adding capacity across all three product lines.
items.quote: We will start operations there in December, although I have been told September. We have ordered machines for that location, and starting everything may take 2-3 months. We may see the benefit of this in our volumes for 1 or 2 months.

items.statement: Target SSSG of 2-3% positive for FY25 with EBITDA margin improvement
items.quote: So going ahead, our target is to retrieve the SSSGs at least to a positive of 2% to 3% along with the implementation plan that we already initiated.

items.statement: Plan to add 90,000 sq ft retail area in FY25, majority in Tamil Nadu under Varamahalakshmi format
items.quote: As per the plan, we aim to open additional store capacity of close to 90,000 square feet in this financial year. Majority of it would be coming in the Tamil Nadu area and with our brand Varamahalakshmi Silks.

items.statement: Additional store area expected to generate INR300-350 crores incremental turnover in FY25
items.quote: So additional store area , in the normal course itself, should give at least another INR300 crores to INR350 crores of turnover.

items.statement: Q4 FY24 gross margin at 40.97% vs 39.77% last year; EBITDA margin ~17% in Q4
items.quote: Our gross margin stood at 40.97 compared to last year of 39.77. Our PAT for the quarter stood at 28.73 compared to last year's of 20.24, which has grown by about 41.95 percentage.

items.statement: Store-level margins: Varamahalakshmi 33-34%, Mandir similar, KLM 24-25%, Kalamandir at company average
items.quote: Store level margins for Varamahalakshmi should be in the range of about 33% to 34%. While KLM, it would be in the range of about 24% to 25%.

items.statement: Revenue per store FY24: Varamahalakshmi ~INR45-46k/sqft, Mandir ~INR44k/sqft, KLM INR14k/sqft
items.quote: is co ntinuing to be approximately 45,000 to 46,000 at a company level. Tamil Nadu would be slightly higher and the is Mandir continues to be almost on the same range about 44,000 per square feet. KML has shown a slight improvement, 20,000 per square feet there. And KLM currently is at INR14,000 rupees per

items.statement: Saree industry growing at 8% CAGR; Tamil Nadu equals Andhra+Telangana combined in consumption
items.quote: If you take that as a metric, a few of the highlights that I would like to highlight at this point of time is in the overall saree consumption, the SSSG, I mean, the CAGR growth is around 8% CAGR growth that saree as an industry sees.

items.statement: Sarees 69.5% of revenue (pure silk >25%, mixed silk 35-40%, Banarasi, fancy); non-saree 30% (lehenga, kurta, men's/kids occasion wear)
items.quote: So though SSKL has about 69.5% sarees and another 30% coming from other categories, if you just focus on sarees alone it's growing at an 8% CAGR.

items.statement: Negative operating cash flow in FY24 due to INR170 cr creditor reduction to gain cash discounts; benefits expected in 2-3 years
items.quote: you would have seen that in the cash flow statement, the reduction in creditors has been to the extent of about INR170 crores, of which a part of it was used from GCP and the entire year's generations were deployed for this.

items.statement: Inventory write-offs ~1% annually per bank surveillance audits; will report as separate line item from FY25
items.quote: Broadly, we have realized that this amount is in the range of about plus or minus 1% on an annual basis. We are planning that from this year onwards, we would declare it as a separate line item.

items.statement: Active customer base 6.5 million; 53-54% repeat purchase rate in trailing 12 months
items.quote: We have an active customer base as of today around 6.5 million and are growing strong as we expand. Our contribution coming from the loyal customer base also continued this season. We still continue to hold our loyal customer base of about 53% of our repeat purchases.

items.statement: FY25 store additions: ~25,000 sq ft by June, ~50,000 sq ft by H1 end, balance in H2; all Varamahalakshmi format
items.quote: We would be putting up another 25,000 sft in June in VML format itself. And by half year end, we should be completing the expansion of approximately plus or minus 50,000 square feet and the balance in the second half.

items.statement: 95%+ full-price sales company-wide; Varamahalakshmi 100% full-price, no discounting
items.quote: More than 95% of our entire sale is full price sale. We do not believe in end of season sale or discounting in a timely manner or a seasonality basis.
